Invariance of log plurigenera in families of compact Kähler manifolds

Let $(X_t,B_t)$ be a smooth proper family of pairs with Kähler fibres, where the boundary has relative simple normal crossings and real coefficients in $[0,1)$. We show that for every $m\ge1$, every section of $mK_{X_t}+\lfloor mB_t\rfloor$ extends locally over the base. In particular, the log plurigenera are locally constant, and for $B_t=0$ we obtain the deformation invariance of the plurigenera $P_m(X_t)$. Since the total space need not be Kähler, we run the minimal model program on the central fibre, using the work of Hacon-Wang and Hacon-Xie, and extend its steps over a disc. The obstruction to lifting a jet vanishes along the fixed part determined by the final model, and so it is square-integrable for the weight in the extension theorem of Cao-Păun. As an application, if the adjoint is pseudoeffective on one fibre, then the pair has a relative good minimal model near each point of the base and a relative canonical model over the whole base.
An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone

We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $G_N$. We promote its canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in $G_N$ and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in $G_N$ yields a logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.
Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions

We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.
Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists

We show that the Werner state $ρ= (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $ρ$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.
Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras

In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetildeΛ$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $Λ$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$.
 When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.
Sums of Kloosterman fractions and applications

We obtain improved bounds for bilinear and trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, building on the works of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec and Bettin-Chandee. Our results use the spectral theory of automorphic forms, and save $N^{1/12} A^{1/3}$ over the trivial bound when $M = N$ and $A$ is small. In the exceptional Maass spectrum, we rely on a new large sieve inequality with averaging over the levels, which may be of independent interest. Applications include an asymptotic for the second moment of the zeta function twisted by a Dirichlet polynomial of length $T^{0.532}$ (improving Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill's $T^{0.515}$ and Dong-Robles-Zeindler's $T^{0.518}$), as well as an improved level of distribution for unbalanced convolutions (improving results of Fouvry-Radziwill, Wright, and Dong-Robles-Zeindler).
On the Distribution of Prime Factors of $\lfloor αn^2 \rfloor$
Cati Alexandru; Johannes Borgwardt; Benjamin Faltin; Giorgos Petritakis

Let $α> 0$ be irrational. We show that $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ obeys a Gaussian distribution. That is, for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, the random variable $(ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Additionally, we fully describe the distribution of $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ for a positive rational $α$.
Unbounded DiPerna-Lions commutators for Osgood-Sobolev vector fields
Leonardo Franchi; Carl Johan Peter Johansson

In this paper we show that there exists a regime of Osgood-Sobolev vector fields in which the DiPerna-Lions scheme cannot be applied despite the recently proved well-posedness and propagation of regularity in arXiv:2607.28118. For Osgood-Sobolev vector fields we also show that the propagation of regularity proved in arXiv:2607.28118 is sharp and derive lower bounds on mixing.
Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching

A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $σ^2/Δ^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.
Pairing Powers of Pythagorean Pairs II
Lorenz Halbeisen; Norbert Hungerbühler; Arman Shamsi Zargar

Let $(a,b,c)$ be a pythagorean triple, i.e., $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Then $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$ are hypotenuse-leg pairs (hl-pairs), i.e., pairs $(c,d)$ of positive integers such that $c^2-d^2$ is a non-zero square. An hl-pair $(c,d)$ is called a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if there is a pythagorean pair $(k,l)$, which is not a multiple of the pythagorean pair $(d,\sqrt{c^2-d^2})$, such that $(c^hk,d^hl)$ is again an hl-pair. To each hl-pair $(c,d)$ and each $h\geq 1$ we assign the elliptic curve $Γ_{c^h,d^h}: y^2=x^3+(c^{2h}-d^{2h})x^2-c^{2h}d^{2h}x$ and show that its torsion group is $\Bbb Z/2\Bbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and that $(c,d)$ is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if and only if $Γ_{c^h,d^h}$ has positive rank over $\mathbb Q$. In this case there are infinitely many such pythagorean pairs $(k,l)$, not multiples of each other. Moreover, every hl-pair is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $1$ and a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $3$, and we give sufficient conditions for degree $2$. The two cases $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$, where $a=m^2-n^2$ and $b=2mn$, are worked out separately.
Floquet Decomposition: Floquet Multipliers and Time-Periodic Modes from Period-Sampled Snapshot Data

Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) fits one constant linear operator to a sequence of snapshots. When the dynamics, or the view of them, vary periodically, as in a parametrically excited flow or a rotating structure seen in a fixed plane, no such operator exists, and stability is decided by the Floquet multipliers, the eigenvalues of the map over one period. In the paper that introduced DMD, Schmid observed that snapshots sampled at the period of an oscillatory flow would identify the Floquet matrix. We develop that observation into a method and analyze it. The Floquet decomposition (FD) applies DMD to fixed-rate data subsampled once per period; the ensemble Floquet decomposition (EFD) stacks the snapshots of each period into one column, giving one set of multipliers and phase-resolved modes. For linear time-periodic systems both are exact: FD when the measurement at one instant determines the state, EFD when the measurements over one period do---so EFD succeeds with partial measurements. EFD and Hankel (delay-embedded) DMD use the same data matrix with different shifts between columns. With $p$ samples per period, Hankel-DMD returns each Floquet mode as a carrier with sidebands, a comb of $p$-th roots of its multiplier, which the period shift collapses onto the multiplier. The methods are verified against known multipliers; outside their hypotheses, on nonlinear or noisy data, the estimated moduli are biased and are not decay rates. Measurements of velocity, scalars, and acoustic pressure in a swirl-stabilized combustor illustrate the choice of period, rank, and data scaling.

The smallest possible surface area of a convex translational tile of $\mathbb R^n$ approaches $\sqrt{2}$ times that of a ball of equal volume as $n\to\infty$. For the lower bound, we combine Gaussian smoothing with the Milman-Neeman multi-bubble theorem. For the upper bound, we use Siegel mean value theorem to average over lattice Voronoi cells. Our method also yields convex $\mathbb Z^n$-tiles whose orthogonal projection onto any hyperplane has volume $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, answering a question of Naor and Regev.
Weakly Pointed Fusion $Π$-supercategories over fields of characteristic not two

We study a class of weakly pointed fusion $Π$-supercategories over a field $k$ of characteristic not equal to $2$, with unit $\mathbf 1$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf 1) = k$. Assuming the existence of a Brauer--Wall reference category over $k$, we classify these categories up to monoidal equivalence. We show that Brauer--Wall reference categories exist for $k = \mathbb C, \mathbb R$ but not for $k = \mathbb F_5$. For each finite group $G$, we also study a product of these categories equipped with a $G$-grading and define a group $\mathcal T_k(G)$, giving an explicit formula for the multiplication in terms of group cochains for $k = \mathbb C$ and $\mathbb R$.
Strong Ill-Posedness for the Surface Quasi-Geostrophic Equations in $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$
Elaine Cozzi; Nicholas Harrison; Zachary Radke

We establish ill-posedness of the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in Sobolev spaces $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every integer $k \geq 3$. This includes the scaling critical space $W^{3,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We build on ideas from (arXiv:2610.04872); in particular, we use a theorem of Bonami and Poornima to construct a basic building block, or packet, which obeys a linear evolution approximating that of the perturbation of the background solution to SQG. The Bonami-Poornima theorem ensures that this packet has both small initial $W^{k,1}$ norm and large $W^{k,1}$ norm at positive times. We then implement a process known as many packet dilution, which allows one to construct an initial perturbation as a sum of sufficiently many packets to dilute the effect of the nonlinear term. This initial perturbation leads to the desired norm inflation.
 To establish instantaneous blow-up of the $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norm, we also prove a local well-posedness result in the critical Sobolev-Lorentz space $W^{2,(2,1)}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This result gives a uniform lower bound on the existence time for solutions with bounded $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ data, even though the solutions' $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms may become arbitrarily large in arbitrarily short time.
Extensions of congruent monotileable (and amenable) groups
Paulina Cecchi-Bernales; Emir Molina; Cristóbal Rivas

A monotile of a countable group $G$ is a finite subset $F \subseteq G$ that tiles $G$, namely $G=\bigsqcup_{c\in C} c F$, for some set of centers $C\subseteq G$. The group $G$ is called congruent monotileable (CM) if it admits an exhaustive sequence of monotiles $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each $F_{n+1}$ is teselated by $F_n$. If moreover $G$ is amenable and the sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is Folner, we say $G$ is congruent monotileable amenable (CMA).
 In this work we observe that the classes of CM and CMA groups are stable under group extensions satisfying a certain technical condition, which we call $stepwise$ $monotileability$, and which is a weaker version of the notion of $X$-$monotileability$ introduced by Dikranjan $et al$. Our condition also includes central extensions previously considered by Gao, Jackson, Seward for CM groups, and by Cecchi Bernales, Cortez for CMA groups. We show that this condition is satisfied by semidirect products of the form $G\wr H$, provided $G$ and $H$ are CM/CMA groups, and also by extensions of locally finite groups by CM/CMA groups. This furnishes new examples of CM and CMA groups. In particular, we provide the first examples of finitely generated CMA groups which are neither solvable nor residually finite.
Exponential integrability of SLE Minkowski content

Let $0<κ<8$, $d=1+κ/8$, and $q=2/(2-d)$. Let $μ$ be the $d$-dimensional Minkowski content measure of either chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ in $\mathbb H$ from $0$ to $\infty$ or two-sided whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ through $0$. We prove that there exist constants $c_κ,C_κ\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \mathbb E\exp\left\{c_κ\left(\frac{μ(D)}{(\operatorname{diam} D)^d}\right)^q\right\}\le C_κ\] for every deterministic bounded Borel set $D$ of positive diameter in the corresponding domain. The exponent $q$ in this moment bound is optimal in both settings. We also show that, almost surely, $μ(B(z,r))=O\bigl(r^d(\log(1/r))^{1/q}\bigr)$ as $r\downarrow0$, locally uniformly in $z$.
Adaptive Control Barrier Functions for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems

Control barrier functions (CBFs) have emerged as a flexible and efficient approach for enforcing dynamic safety constraints. In this paper, we consider a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with singular perturbations and develop an adaptive CBF framework for such systems to enforce safety constraints on both the slow and fast subsystems in the overall singularly perturbed nonlinear system with uncertain parameters. We first develop a robustness property showing that if an adaptive controller for the slow subsystem satisfies the slow CBF condition with an appropriate safety margin, then for sufficiently small values of the singular perturbation parameter $\varepsilon$, the slow subsystem remains within an $O(\varepsilon)$-neighborhood of its safe set. We then consider the more general case of safety constraints on both the fast and slow subsystems and provide conditions under which joint slow-fast safety is achieved despite the parametric uncertainties. The reduced-order slow model and the slow and fast CBF conditions are evaluated using an online parameter estimate and the parameter mismatch between the estimated and true reduced-order models is addressed via a state-dependent robustness margin in the CBF inequalities. To illustrate the proposed framework, we present simulation studies for two systems with parametric uncertainties: a synthetic two-time-scale fourth-order example system and a unicycle with a fast turn-rate actuator and an obstacle avoidance safety constraint.
Real equiangular lines in dimensions 18-20 and sharp fixed-angle bounds
Valjakas Djaljapayan; Zhen-Qi Liao; Wei-Hsuan Yu

In collaboration with OpenAI's GPT-6, we prove that the maximum numbers of real equiangular lines in dimensions 18, 19, and 20 are $N(18)=57$, $N(19)=72$, and $N(20)=90$, respectively. We reduce the upper bounds to paired lattice points in sections of even unimodular lattices of rank twenty-four. Root-system estimates, exact certificates, and Golay-code arguments bound the sections. In the Leech lattice, generalized Hamming weights of a binary evaluation code give sharp bounds attained by nested sections. At prescribed cosine $1/q$, we also show that $N_{1/q}(d)=d+7$ for explicit intervals of consecutive dimensions for each odd $q\ge319$, and $N_{1/q}(d)=d+23$ on such intervals for each odd $q\ge5599$. Regular graphs in repeated Seidel blocks vary the cosine while preserving nullity, and a coherence bound proves optimality. Symmetric conference matrices give a further sharp family at quadratic irrational cosines.
On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks

We study Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Szép products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Szép factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Szép actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.
Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters

In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.

We prove formulas describing the behavior of Miyazawa's degree invariant of knotted spheres and real projective planes in the 4-sphere under satellite operations. As an application, we show that every deform-spun real projective plane admits infinitely many topologically but not smoothly isotopic copies. In particular, we produce an infinite exotic family of irreducible real projective planes containing Hughes-Kim-Miller-Nahm's counterexample to the Kinoshita conjecture.
Sharp constant in 2D critical fermionic Hardy inequality

We study the large-$N$ behavior of the optimal constant $κ_N$ in the two-dimensional fermionic many-particle Hardy inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^N -Δ_i \geq κ_N^{(2)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^2}, \] understood as a quadratic-form inequality on antisymmetric wave functions. We prove that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)κ_N^{(2)}=4, \] thereby proving a conjecture of Frank, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Solovej. The proof combines a dyadic Fefferman-de la Llave representation of the Coulomb kernel with separate estimates for squares of low and high particle occupation. A trace inequality controls the low-occupation regime, while sums of Neumann eigenvalues yield the sharp bound in the high-occupation regime.

We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.
We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.
The Vinogradov system in finite fields and two-source extractors with arbitrarily small min-entropy rate

Fix $k\ge2$ and $1/(k+1)<ρ\le1$. Let $q=p^n$, where the prime $p$ is fixed and sufficiently large in terms of $k,ρ$, and $n$ tends to infinity through prime values. We show that for every $A\subseteq\F_q$ with $|A|\ge q^ρ$, the Vinogradov system of degree $k$ in $2s$ variables has at most $|A|^{2s}q^{-k/2-η}$ solutions in $A$. Here the integer $s$ and the saving $η>0$ depend only on $k,ρ,p$. At $ρ=1/(k+1)$ an example rules out every saving $η>0$ in this moment estimate. For $k=2$ the author previously proved the analogous estimate over prime fields. We deduce a power saving for the double sums of $e(xy+(xy)^2+\dots+(xy)^k)$ over any two sets of size at least $q^ρ$, where $e$ is any nontrivial additive character of $\F_q$. Choosing $k$ sufficiently large gives a polynomial two-source extractor with exponentially small error at every fixed positive min-entropy rate. The proof of the moment estimate uses the theorem of Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao on Marton's conjecture and a bound for the intersection of the moment curve with an affine subspace over $\F_p$.
Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
Valentina Astore; Martino Borello; Alain Couvreur

Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.
Oleinik estimate for a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit

In this article, we establish an Oleinik type estimate for $2\times2$ systems of hyperbolic conservation laws in a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit. More precisely, we consider the parabolic approximation with vanishing viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon u_{xx}$ ($\varepsilon>0$) for the Temple class of hyperbolic system of conservation laws and for these approximate solutions we obtain an Oleinik type estimate uniformly with respect to the viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$. This extends the Oleinik inequality for scalar conservation laws with viscosity to the system. Subsequently, we prove that these approximate solutions converge via the process of vanishing viscosity limit to a global weak solution of the limit strictly hyperbolic system provided that the initial data is small in $L^\infty$. To do this we implement the vanishing viscosity method of Bianchini and Bressan [Indiana Univ. Math. J. 2000] with $L^\infty$ initial data which requires new tools as an local in time Oleinik estimate (obtained by employing a suitable maximum principle and a normal form argument) and a localization argument. In particular we need to introduce appropriate weight functions which satisfy a Bellman equation to get new localized transversal interaction estimates.
Slow information spreading in quasi-periodic quantum spin chains

We investigate the suppression of information propagation in a weakly interacting quantum spin chain subject to a quasi-periodic external magnetic field. Using a finite-order normal-form construction, we establish a localized barrier in the interior of the chain that inhibits information propagation and derive a quantitative bound on the commutator of observables supported at opposite ends of the chain.
A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
Ali Barki; Shubham Gupta; Yaozhong W. Qiu

We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(Δ+ 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |ξ|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 dξ,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
Supercritical Nodal Solutions on Annuli: Symmetry Breaking and Multiplicity
Alireza Khatib; Olimpio H. Miyagak; Somayeh Mousavinasr

We establish existence and multiplicity results for nonradial sign-changing solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=a(|x|)|u|^{p-2}u$ on annuli in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\geq4$, $a$ is a positive radial coefficient, and $p$ may exceed the Sobolev critical exponent. For each decomposition $N=m+n$, with $m\geq n\geq2$, we minimize the energy on a nodal Nehari set within a signed cone of angularly nondecreasing, $O(m)\times O(n)$-invariant functions. Whenever $2<p<2(m+1)/(m-1)$, the minimum is attained, and every minimizer is a classical solution with exactly two nodal domains. A cone-preserving auxiliary Dirichlet operator and a two-parameter energy deformation recover the full equation from the constrained minimization. We prove that these minimizers are nonradial if $(p-2)β_Ω>2N$, where $β_Ω$ is the optimal Dirichlet Hardy constant associated with the weight $|x|^{-2}$. Under a common admissible exponent range satisfying this condition, different orthogonal decompositions yield distinct solution pairs $\{\pm u\}$. An explicit lower bound for $β_Ω$ provides supercritical regimes on sufficiently thin annuli in which the nonradiality and multiplicity results apply.
PrO Filtering via Kernel Mean Embedding Dynamics
Linfeng Wang; Nikolas Nüsken; Chris. J. Oates

Filtering methods are routinely deployed with misspecified state-space models, where Bayesian filters can diverge and become overconfident. Predictively-oriented (PrO) filtering is a recent, hyperparameter-free alternative that was demonstrated to outperform (generalised) Bayesian filtering methods when either the dynamical model or the measurement model is structurally misspecified. This can be attributed to \emph{hedging} behaviour: when an observation conflicts with the forecast, the PrO update places mass near both. Yet existing implementations of PrO filtering rely on unimodal (Gaussian) approximations, whose ability to effectively hedge is limited. This paper develops the first nonparametric, particle-based implementation of PrO filtering. The key obstacle, that PrO filtering distributions are only implicitly defined, is overcome by constructing a path from the predictive to the PrO filtering distribution whose rate is available in closed form, enabling the use of kernel mean embedding dynamics for measure transport. The resulting algorithm requires only simulation from the dynamical model and evaluations of the likelihood, with neither importance weights nor the predictive density. Moreover, as we prove, the number of pseudo-time steps it requires does not grow with the outlyingness of the observation, in contrast to transport along the Bayesian tempering path. An empirical assessment shows substantial improvement over Gaussian variation of PrO filtering in challenging nonlinear examples where Gaussian approximation is unreasonably limited.
On the Distance Properties of Huffman Sequences
Parker Huggins; Alphan Sahin; Elza Erkip

In this letter, we study pairwise distances between sequences with a common aperiodic autocorrelation function. First, we show that pairwise distances are determined by a ternary signed pattern encoding the relative zero flips between spectral factors. Then, for Huffman sequences, we prove that Dihedral symmetries of the zeros preserve pairwise distances, and we further derive lower bounds on the minimum distance. The results in this letter offer a starting point for designing codes with a fixed autocorrelation. These codes are relevant in integrated sensing and communication.

We develop a linearization theory for completely Lipschitz mappings between operator spaces. Motivated by the classical theory of Lipschitz-free spaces, we introduce a completely Lipschitz-free space and show that completely Lipschitz mappings admit a canonical linearization as completely bounded operators on this space. We provide several equivalent descriptions of this operator space, extending to the noncommutative setting the classical constructions of Arens--Eells, de Leeuw, and Dixmier--Ng. In particular, we obtain a molecular description, a quotient representation of an operator $\ell_1$-space, and a realization as the closed linear span of evaluation functionals. Our framework applies over both the real and complex scalar fields; in the real case, we first establish some operator space results needed to carry out the constructions. We also show that our notion of completely Lipschitz mapping encompasses the previously introduced extensions of Lipschitz mappings to operator spaces. These results provide a unified framework for studying Lipschitz phenomena in the setting of operator spaces and establish the corresponding free operator spaces as a natural tool for their linearization.
Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks

In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.
Gregory J. Galloway; Eric Ling; Argam Ohanyan

We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.
Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction

We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $μ$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $μ+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.
Monoid Representation of the Determinants of the Adjacency Matrices of 1-joined Path Graphs
Daniel Pinzon; Daniel Pragel; Joshua Roberts; Zack Marshall; Olivia Strain

Following previous work by these authors, this paper explores all labeled path graphs joined by 1 edge where the labeling contains the information on how to join that graph. The algebraic structure that this operation has on the determinant of the adjacency matrix of the graph gives a finite monoid of matrices under matrix multiplication. We completely characterize the monoid using the representation theory discussed in Khovanov et al(2024). Finally, we demonstrate how these results can be used to find general formulas for the determinants of chains of 1-joined labeled paths.
The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees

We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.
On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules

We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property.
 By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.
Territorial Conflict as a Cellular Automaton: Frozen Domains and Active Fronts in a Risk-Derived Local Rule

We formulate the attack and fortification rules of the game Risk as a synchronous cellular automaton on a graph, with battles resolved by exact dice odds. We prove, and verify in Lean, that for the default exchange ratio the rule has radius 6, or 5 for deterministic battles with a positive attack threshold, both attained; that its deterministic form is irreversible except at the highest attack thresholds without growth and with fortification absent or inactive; that without troop growth it freezes in finite time; and that the dynamics near an interface is locally determined. The coupling of the ownership field to a troop field separates frozen domains from active fronts: with a positive attack threshold, saturated domains cannot be conquered, while interfaces with heterogeneous troops keep fighting. In 14252 runs, with attractors classified operationally in Wolfram's scheme, raising the attack threshold takes the system from dominance by one faction to a frozen fragmented partition. The share of the largest faction drops between the same two threshold values at every size up to L=128, in a step about 0.5 wide under a continuous threshold (L=64-96), whereas the probability of complete consolidation is a size-dependent crossover governed by saturated minority domains. Long-period attractors combine spatially fixed local oscillators; apparent class-IV gliders are artefacts of index-ordered tie-breaking. Straight fronts stayed within two cells of their initial position for up to 500,000 steps, over which they are one-dimensional automata with non-recurrent, incompressible dynamics and positive Lyapunov speeds, constant for L>=48. Compared with mean-field and random-regular-graph controls, the lattice lengthens conflicts about twentyfold and clusters conquest: a cell next to a fresh conquest is about five times as likely as average to be conquered next, against 1.1-1.5 in the controls.
Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families

We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, Ω_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber. This extends the case of rationally connected fibrations from [Bur26]. We further introduce higher Chow-theoretic notions of singularities.
On the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups
Liudmila V. Ivanova; Viachaslau I. Murashka; Alexander F. Vasil'ev

Recall that a class of groups $\mathfrak{F}$ is called $D_\mathfrak{X}$-closed if it contains every group $G = MN$ where $M$ and $N$ are normal $\mathfrak{F}$-subgroups of $G$ and $M\cap N\in \mathfrak{X}$. We prove that a hereditary formation of $ω$-soluble groups is an $n$-multiply $ω$-local formation if and only if it is a $D_{\mathfrak{N}^n_ω}$-closed formation. As corollaries we obtain the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about saturation of hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups and its extension to the class of all $π$-soluble groups, as well as the criterion for a formation of soluble groups to be $n$-multiply local.
The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
Ilon Joseph; Ivan Novikau; Michael R. Montgomery; Joanna Slawinska; Dimitrios Giannakis

We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.
The positive-sphere variant of Tingley's problem for $C^1([0,1])$

Let $C^1([0,1])$ be endowed with the norm $\|f\|=\|f\|_\infty+\|f'\|_\infty$, and let $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ be the part of its unit sphere consisting of nonnegative, nondecreasing functions. We prove that every surjective isometry of $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ is the identity and has a unique surjective real-linear isometric extension to $C^1([0,1])$.
Time-optimal travel driven by two vector fields on a Riemannian manifold
Erasmo Caponio; Dario Corona; Ebtsam H. Taha

We study minimum-time travel on a Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ for a kinematic model in which finitely many drift fields contribute additively to the velocity, after independent rescaling of their components parallel and orthogonal to a chosen unit direction $u$. The velocity is then $\mathcal Y_x(u)=(η(x)+h_x(\widehat Z_x,u))u+\widehat W_x$, $u\in UT_xM$, for two effective vector fields $\widehat Z$, $\widehat W$ and a self-propulsion speed $η\geq0$. Let $F$ be the gauge of the radial hull $\mathcal B_x=[0,1]\cdot\mathcal S_x$ of the velocity set $\mathcal S_x=\mathcal Y_x(UT_xM)$. Where $η>0$, we characterize when $F$ is a Finsler metric and give two-sided estimates and representation formulae for it; where $η=0$ and $\widehat Z\neq0$, we recover the Randers, Kropina and strong-wind regimes of Zermelo navigation. Examples include Matsumoto's slope metric, traction-modified slope models, and alternative models for wildfire propagation and microswimmer navigation. Since $F$ need not be a Finsler metric, we treat the minimum-time problem with tools from differential inclusions. For distinct endpoints, the inclusions defined by $\mathcal S_x$ and $\mathcal B_x$ give the same infimum travel time, and so does the convex hull of $\mathcal B_x$ under local controllability at the terminal point. When $F$ is finite, the infimum is attained if $(M,h)$ is complete, $\mathcal Y$ is bounded and each $\mathcal B_x$ is convex. When $F$ is a Finsler metric on $\{η>0\}$, the set $\{η=0\}$ cannot be reached from $\{η>0\}$ in finite time and, on $\{η>0\}$, the minimum time is the Finsler distance; if moreover $(M,h)$ is complete and $η$ is bounded, $F$ is forward and backward complete and the minimum time is attained by geodesics. We also compute the support Hamiltonian directly from the velocity law, for every $η\geq0$.
On the Convergence of Discrete-Time Primal-Dual Algorithm for Distributed GNE Seeking
Weijian Li; Lacra Pavel; Panos J. Antsaklis; Hai Lin

We investigate the convergence of a discrete-time distributed primal-dual algorithm for generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) seeking in a class of noncooperative games with nonlinear coupling constraints. We establish semi-global convergence of the algorithm under a fixed stepsize, in the sense that convergence can be guaranteed from any prescribed compact set of initial conditions by choosing a sufficiently small stepsize. Under a diminishing stepsize sequence, we further establish global convergence when the constraints are globally Lipschitz continuous. For the special case of affine constraints, global convergence is also guaranteed under a sufficiently small fixed stepsize. Finally, we extend these convergence results to a fully distributed GNE seeking algorithm in a partial-decision information setting, where each agent only has access to the actions of its neighbors. These results complement existing convergence results for continuous-time primal-dual dynamics, and provide new convergence guarantees for the discrete-time counterpart in distributed GNE seeking.

Let \(k\) be a field and \(V\) a finite-dimensional rational representation of the additive group \(\GG_{a,k}\). We show that the ring of invariants \(k[V]^{\GG_a}\) is finitely generated in every characteristic, extending Weitzenböck's classical theorem beyond characteristic zero.

We study the truncated moment problem on the one-dimensional full integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, seeking necessary and sufficient conditions for a prescribed sequence of $n$ real numbers to be $\mathbb{Z}-$representable, i.e. to be the sequence of the first $n$ moments of a probability measure supported on $\mathbb{Z}$. Building on the approach developed in 2017 in Infusino et al. for the truncated moment problem on the non-negative integers, we establish a complete characterization of $\mathbb{Z}-$representable sequences for every truncation order $n$. From this result, we derive an inductive and computable $\mathbb{Z}-$representability criterion. More generally, we also investigate the relationship between the truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem and the truncated Hamburger moment problem, seen as its continuous counterpart.
Prevalence of the periodicity of maximizing measures
Zelai Hao; Illya Koval; Zhiqiang Li

For a continuous map $T\colon X\rightarrow X$ on a compact metric space $(X,d)$, we say that a function $f\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ has the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ if its time averages along forward orbits of $T$ are maximized at a periodic orbit. In this article, we establish the Hunt--Ott conjecture (cf.~\cite{HO96a,HO96b}), that is, the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ is prevalent (in the sense of Hunt--Sauer--Yorke) in the space of Lipschitz functions with respect to a standard metric for subshifts of finite type. This result is a strengthening of \cite[Theorem~A]{BZ16} and \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DLZ24}, confirms the prediction mentioned in the ICM proceeding contribution of Bochi (\cite[Section~1]{Boc18}) suggested by experimental evidence.
Left-Invariant Kundt Structures on Almost Abelian Lie Groups
S. El Bourkadi; M. W. Mansouri

We study left-invariant Kundt structures on almost abelian Lie groups. We establish algebraic existence criteria and characterize the admissible real Jordan forms according to the signature of the Abelian ideal. We then characterize the Kundt pairs defining pp-waves and plane waves in arbitrary dimension, with particular attention to recurrent and parallel null directions. Examples in dimension four illustrate both plane and non-plane pp-wave geometries.
Recursive Word Conditioning for Higher-Dimensional Partitions: Exact Enumeration and Complexity

Let $p_d(n)$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional partitions of weight $n$. We develop an exact enumeration method operating on recursively parsed partition words (which are shown to encode $d$-dimensional partitions), beginning with an elementary interior-part decomposition of ordinary partitions. Conditioning on an interior word block separates the preceding and succeeding nested blocks. For higher-dimensional partitions, transversely re-parsing the preceding words permits the same conditioning operation to be iterated. Recursive containment and joins carry effective floors across the cuts, while a nonnegative excess permits exact truncation and pruning. The resulting procedure is a complete row-conditioning algorithm. For every fixed $d\ge3$, we prove that it computes $p_d(0),\ldots,p_d(N)$ using at most $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)}\log(N+2))\bigr)$ arithmetic operations. A diagonal refinement replaces the final row-conditioning stages by coupled interlacing chains of ordinary-partition words and sharpens the bound to $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)})\bigr)$. The algorithms count constrained completions through reusable weight-indexed coefficients rather than enumerating finished partitions. Exact computations with these algorithms reach weights 100, 50, 45, 40 and 35 in dimensions 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, respectively. On a single 2.1\,GHz core the program computes $p_3(0),\ldots,p_3(100)$ in under four hours and each of the tables in dimensions 4--7 in under 30 minutes.
On the Density of Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle

Let $N(a)$ denote the number of occurrences of the integer $a>1$ in Pascal's triangle, and set ${\mathcal E}_H=\{a\geq3:N(a)>2H\}$, $A_H(x)=|{\mathcal E}_H\cap[1,x]|.$ For every fixed $K\geq2$ we prove the expansion $A_1(x)=\sum_{k=2}^{K}(k!x)^{1/k}+O_K\!\left(x^{1/(K+1)}\right).$
 Consequently, the Dirichlet series ${D}_1(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_1}a^{-s}$ extends meromorphically to $\Re s>0$, with simple poles precisely at $s=1/k$, $k\geq2$, of residue $(k!)^{1/k}/k$.
 For every $H\geq2$, $x\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $A_H(x)\le A_2(x)\leq\exp\left(\frac{2\log x}{(\log\log x)^{1/4}}\right)\ll_{\varepsilon} x^{\varepsilon}.$
 Hence $D_H(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_H}a^{-s}$ is holomorphic for $\Re s>0$ when $H\geq2$, and $λ({\mathcal E}_1)=1/2, λ({\mathcal E}_H)=0\quad(H\geq2).$
 Here, for a set $S\subseteq {\mathbb N}$, its exponent of convergence is $λ(S)=\inf\left\{σ>0:
 \sum_{n\in S}n^{-σ}<\infty\right\}.$ We also determine the logarithmic-order counting law for the classical Lind--Singmaster family of coefficients of multiplicity at least six.
From NP-Hardness to Exact Tractability Through Sample Abundance

Additional observations can make exact optimization tractable without changing the objective or feasible set. We establish this phenomenon for noisy parity fitting, a worst-case NP-hard problem, with uniformly sampled rank-one sign tensor entries, independent fair factor signs and independent errors. For fixed interaction order $k\ge3$, $n$ signs per block, logarithmic mean degree and known channel biases, $O(n/(\log n)^{1/(k-2)})$ further readings of the same source suffice with high probability for exact optimization in $O(n\log^2 n)$ worst-case work. The leading coefficient is sharp for weak recovery by depth-$O(\log\log n)$ local estimators with independent reading marks. A common signed-field law determines the gain over the generating source, the number of tied optima and the dimension needed for later reweightings. The geometry of the remaining coordinates determines the sharp radius of local verification for high-scoring assignments with high probability.
Low-degree hardness rules out eigenvalue tests but not eigenvector tests

We study what low-degree hardness implies for spectral tests, with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) as the null distribution. We show that, once a fixed amount of Gaussian noise is added, it rules out every test based on eigenvalues, but not tests based on eigenvectors. For eigenvalues, if the low-degree advantage vanishes at logarithmic degree, then the joint law of the noisy eigenvalues converges to that of the GOE in total variation. For eigenvectors, we construct planted distributions with vanishing low-degree advantage whose eigenvalues follow the GOE law exactly at every noise level, yet whose noisy eigenvectors still distinguish them from the GOE. A single eigenvector can suffice. After a small amount of noise, a polynomial-time test that uses only the span of a fixed fraction of the top eigenvectors also succeeds, even when the low-degree advantage vanishes at a prescribed polylogarithmic degree.
 To prove the eigenvalue result, we split the noise into three increments. The first uses the low-degree assumption to establish eigenvalue rigidity. The second couples the two spectra through Dyson Brownian motion and applies homogenization to obtain a transport estimate. The third uses Gaussian smoothing to convert this estimate into closeness in total variation.
Tensor products of finite groups without compatibility conditions are finite

It has been an open question whether Inassaridze's tensor product $G\otimes H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative, and, as a consequence, we prove that the low dimensional nonabelian homology groups $H_i(G,A)$, $i=0,1$, are finite whenever $G$ and $A$ are finite. We achieve this by introducing a much more general tensor product $G\bt H$, defined for groups acting on themselves and on each other by arbitrary automorphisms, with no compatibility conditions, and subject only to the two defining relations of the nonabelian tensor product. We prove that $G\bt H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. Since the nonabelian tensor product of Brown and Loday, Inassaridze's tensor product and the box-tensor product are all quotients or special cases of $G\bt H$, this brings the finiteness results for all these tensor products under one umbrella.
Characterisations of symmetric Birkhoff--James orthogonality via numerical ranges

Birkhoff-James orthogonality in a normed space is in general not symmetric. For a complex Banach space $\mathscr{X}$ of dimension at least $2$, we prove that the following assertions are equivalent: Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $\mathscr{X}$ is symmetric; the spatial numerical range of every operator on $\mathscr{X}$ coincides with its reverse numerical range, defined by reversing the orthogonality; $\mathscr{X}$ has the simultaneous zero inclusion property, that is, $0$ lies in the closure of the numerical range of an invertible operator exactly when it lies in that of its inverse; $\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{X})$ has the analogous property for the algebra numerical range; and a simple inequality for supporting functionals holds. This confirms a conjecture of Ghosh. We also introduce the asymmetry constant $R(\mathscr{X})\in[1,2]$, as the supremum of the norms of the projections $I-x\otimesξ$, where $x$ is a unit vector and $ξ$ is a supporting functional at $x$. We show that $R(\mathscr{X})^{-1}$ is the radius of the largest ball around the identity on which the simultaneous zero inclusion property holds, and that every number in $[1,2]$ is the asymmetry constant of some two-dimensional $\ell^p$ space.

We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex Rényi multi-entropy.
Toward a human-friendly proof of a polynomial bound for the Directed Grid Theorem
Victor Campos; Allen Ibiapina; Raul Lopes; Rodrigo Nogueira; Ignasi Sau

The Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015] states that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph of directed treewidth at least $f(k)$ contains a cylindrical grid of order $k$ as a butterfly minor. Their function is not elementary, and Hatzel, Kreutzer, Garlet Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] improved it to a tower of exponentials of height $22$, by a proof in three stages through paths and cycles of well-linked sets. In this paper we prove each stage with a polynomial bound, so that $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial of degree $20\,031\,568$. As a consequence, Younger's conjecture, proved by Reed, Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas [Combinatorica, 1996], holds with a polynomial bound: for the polynomial $f$ that we construct, every digraph without $k$ pairwise disjoint cycles has a feedback vertex set of size at most $(k-1)f(k)$. In fact, beyond cycles, we obtain polynomial packing-covering bounds for every strongly connected digraph that is a butterfly minor of a cylindrical grid.
On the equivariant Heegner point main conjecture and refined conjectures of Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer type

In 1992, Darmon formulated refined conjectures of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer type for Heegner points, and proved the ``order of vanishing'' part of his conjectures by a development of Kolyvagin's Euler system arguments. In this paper, for good ordinary primes split in the underlying imaginary quadratic field, we prove the $p$-part of the ``leading coefficient formula'' conjectured by Darmon, as well as its derived strengthening by Bertolini-Darmon.
 Our method, which also offers a novel perspective on earlier results, is based on the formulation and proof of new equivariant anticyclotomic main conjectures, including an equivariant extension of Perrin-Riou's Heegner point main conjecture.

Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.
Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schrödinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials

We consider the Schrödinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.
Non-archimedean generalisations of the Kuznetsov formulas

In this paper we develop non-archimedean analogues of the Petersson-Kuznetsov formulas. Specifically, choosing a particular test function on either the geometric or spectral side of the formula, one may express the other side in terms of integral transforms. Such transforms involve representation theoretic Bessel functions attached to irreducible unitary admissible representations of $\text{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.
Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations

We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate.
 For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $κ$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $κ<0$.
 The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.
Boundary Observability for a Class of Degenerate Kolmogorov-Type Equations in a Cylindrical Domain
Dong-Hui Yang; Mengze Gu; Yuanzhi Zhou; Ghadir Shokor

This paper investigates the boundary observability for a class of multi-dimensional degenerate Kolmogorov-type kinetic equations in a cylindrical domain $Ω= \mathbb{T}_{x_1} \times (0,1)_{x_2}$. The model features a horizontal drift term $x_2^γ\partial_{x_1} \varphi$ coupled with a boundary-degenerate diffusion operator $\partial_{x_2}(x_2^α\partial_{x_2} \varphi)$ acting solely on the velocity variable, where $γ= 1$ and $α\in (0,1)$. By leveraging the structural advantages of the cylindrical domain, we establish an analytical framework based on the method of separation of variables. Crucial Carleman estimates tailored to the degenerate dual operator are derived to capture the subtle dissipation effects under the influence of the transport term. Consequently, by virtue of a uniform a priori estimate, we establish the quantitative boundary observability inequality for the state function.
A Garnett--Jones estimate for matrix weights

For an \(N\times N\) matrix \(A_p\) weight \(W\) on an averaging basis, set \(M_p=\max\{1,p-1\}\), \(1\leq p<\infty\). At rate \(1/M_p\), the operator-norm exponential moment of \(\log W\) centered on each basis set is bounded by \(2[W]_{\mathbf A_p}^{1/M_p}\). With scalar Garnett--Jones constant \(G\), the BMO distance from \(\log W\) to bounded Hermitian functions is at most \((2N^2-N)GM_p\), uniformly in the characteristic. Power weights on intervals show the sharp order in \(p\). Conversely, a uniform distance bound for scalar \(A_2\) logarithms gives the scalar property with the same constant. Under a uniform small-BMO condition this is equivalent to scalar \(A_2\) decomposition. The estimates apply to cubes and axis-parallel rectangles on \(\R^d\) and \(\T^d\). For rectangles with \(d>1\), the scalar quadratic estimate bounds the distance by \(\sqrt{2N^2-N}\,C_d M_p\), where \(C_d\) depends only on \(d\). The rectangular BMO distance is comparable to the critical exponential scale.
The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected

We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Doğan and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026).
 To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019).
 Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.
Cyclic polynomials in mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type spaces

The proof combines exact subharmonic duality with holomorphic realization at the original Gaussian weight. We characterize the elements of finite order in the Riordan group over the complex field by providing explicit conditions on their entries. We further derive consequences for the Lagrange subgroup and the group of formal power series under composition, obtaining a characterization of finite-order series and a constructive description of the solutions to associated functional equations.
Simultaneous ruin probabilities for Brownian risks with a deterministic splitting time

We consider two Brownian risk processes which coincide up to a fixed time and subsequently evolve with correlated increments. For a finite time horizon after the split, we derive the exact asymptotics of their simultaneous ruin probability as the initial reserves tend to infinity proportionally. The terminal correlation separates the two asymptotic regimes for the ratio to the joint tail at the terminal time. In the remaining regimes the ratio equals two, with a Gaussian factor in the endpoint tail at the transition. We also obtain asymptotics on intervals of length of order $u^{-2}$ near the terminal time and an exponential limit law for the first simultaneous ruin time, conditional on ruin by the horizon.

For every finite subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The Lagrangian contains an auxiliary field, which leads to an irregular secondary constraint. On the branch that reproduces the KP equation, all constraints are second class, and the Dirac brackets give the known Hamiltonian and Poisson operator. We confirm these results by the Faddeev-Jackiw method. Then, we consider fields periodic in the first spatial coordinate. In this case, the zero modes of the derivative operator lead to an additional secondary constraint on the mean of the potential. This constraint replaces the inverse derivative by its zero mean counterpart, and the resulting Hamiltonian is in accordance with the one of Reiman and Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii, up to normalization conventions. We also relate our results to an existing quantization of the KP equation, for which the potential Lagrangian provides an action.
Parameter selection procedures for model reduction of a parameterized wave propagation in damaged material

In this work, we consider a parameterized version of the classical wave equation that models wave propagation in damaged material. We apply model order reduction to the wave equation using a reduced basis method with the POD-Greedy algorithm. The success of the model order reduction highly depends on the parameter set used in the POD-Greedy algorithm. For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $α(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $α(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. We also prove reconstruction of partially deleted forward neighborhoods and determine the support, signs, and multiplicities of the corresponding upper Möbius transform. Rigidity of submanifolds under extrinsic curvature pinching

We investigate the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds whose curvature operator is bounded below by a nonnegative constant, under pointwise pinching conditions involving the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to many earlier results, we allow equality in these conditions without imposing additional assumptions on the mean curvature or restricting the fundamental group of the submanifold. Allowing equality reveals geometric and topological phenomena excluded by strict pinching. We establish classification theorems in all dimensions $n\geq4$, describing the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of such submanifolds. Our results also provide substantial information about the extrinsic geometry of the immersions, including precise conclusions concerning relative nullity, Dupin principal normals, and total geodesicity. As applications, we derive rigidity and sphere theorems for submanifolds of space forms and construct families of examples showing that the pinching conditions do not, in general, imply extrinsic rigidity. These results extend and refine several known rigidity theorems by providing a classification of the equality cases in a general ambient setting.

The cell wall is modelled as a collection of load-bearing cross-sections, with random number of cross-links in each such cross-section, around a fixed degree of cross-linking. We prove that the Lévy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.
A Finite Automaton Translating Geometric Addresses into Dynamical Itineraries on the Basilica

Fractals are generally known for their self-similarity and repeating patterns. One way to produce fractals is via the dynamics of functions from the extended complex plane to itself. These fractals are known as Julia sets. In this paper, we explore how methods from symbolic dynamics and computation theory can be used to describe where points on the basilica Julia set might be located depending on their dynamical orbit under the polynomial function $f(z)=z^2-1$.

Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence

Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories.

Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mariño conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces.

More precisely, we perform a past dependent pruning of a Crump-Mode-Jagers tree with immigration and obtain an explicit formula for the conditional intensity of the point measure charging the birth times of the individuals. We thereby provide the first embedding of a genealogical structure within a nonlinear Hawkes process, and obtain as a byproduct a new coupling with an upperbounding linear Hawkes. We finally study the impact of adding periods of infinite inhibition after each event of a supercritical Hawkes process. In particular we show that depending on the existence of a delay for this infinite inhibition, the process can exhibit either linear or exponential growth of the number of events with time. We obtain explicit criteria for both behaviors depending on the reproduction function, the delay and the length of these inhibition periods.
A consequence of the classical Lindelöf Hypothesis for the density of zeros of general Dirichlet series

Supposing the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function we prove that the density hypothesis holds for Res>3/4 for a large class of Dirichlet series. The first result of similar type was reached by Gábor Halász and Paul Turán in 1969.
Sharp entanglement and decay thresholds for fractional elliptic operators

For perturbations extending to infinity, this wave construction yields two-dimensional counterexamples with smooth compactly supported inputs and coefficient fields converging to the identity in every fixed unweighted $C^k$ norm. Finally, for a known underlying operator, a single exterior measurement determines the number, orders, and coefficients of the fractional terms, together with a continuous potential.

We formulate a fluid approximation of this system and show that optimal admission, routing, and eviction are governed by endpoint-specific shadow prices for computation and memory together with session continuation values. On 16 H200 GPUs, PARK raises output throughput by $24.2\%$ over the strongest baseline ($336.9\%$ over round robin) on turn-intensive SWE trajectories and by $40.0\%$ over the strongest baseline ($63.3\%$ over round robin) on generation-intensive Terminal-Bench trajectories. We construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler metrics on the complement of a smooth anti-canonical K3 divisor in a compact Kähler threefold, assuming that the normal bundle of the divisor is nef and big. Such a metric exists in every Kähler class whose exceptional periods are positive. We use a generalized Gibbons-Hawking ansatz to construct an approximate model on the normal bundle. When the normal bundle contracts an ADE configuration, this model combines an expanding Ricci-flat orbifold K3 metric with ALE metrics whose exceptional periods remain fixed. After improving the model by a finite iteration and transferring it to the divisor complement, we apply the Tian-Yau-Hein existence theorem.
On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$

Local models are used to model, étale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein. On one hand, this gives the analogous information for integral models of Shimura varieties for unramified unitary groups with parahoric level structure, and on the other hand also results in certain natural matrix equations defining non-Gorenstein singularities.
Stable finiteness and combination theorems for Hughes-free embeddings
