We show that all group algebras of Higman's group and Deligne's group are stably finite. We also study when the Hughes-free embeddability property is closed under taking graphs of groups, and give a positive answer when the edge maps are retractions or injective on Abelianisations. As a consequence we obtain that fundamental groups of graphs of torsion-free Abelian groups, graph products of locally indicable Hughes-free embeddable groups, and fundamental groups of graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups are Hughes-free embeddable.
Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields

We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.
Large deviations for integrated exponentials of Gaussian Volterra processes - application to variance options
Antoine Jacquier; Mugad Oumgari; Dan Pirjol; Lingjiong Zhu

We prove small-time large deviations for the normalised time integral of the exponential of a Gaussian Volterra process, and complement it with a central limit theorem and moderate deviations. As an application, we obtain short-maturity asymptotics for out-of-the-money and at-the-money variance options in rough volatility models, as well as implied volatility expansions which we validate numerically.
Pietsch's favourite problem on singular traces
Gustavo Araújo; Daniel Pellegrino; Joedson Santos

In 2023, A. Pietsch formulated twenty-seven open problems concerning traces on operator ideals. We give an affirmative answer to Problem 16, which Pietsch singled out as his personal favourite, by constructing a nonzero bounded singular spectral trace on the weak Weyl ideal over the class of all Banach spaces.
Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags

We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.
A second-order relaxation system for a degenerate-parabolic quasilinear fourth-order rimming-flow equation with critical spectrum

For a spectrally critical nonlinear degenerate-parabolic PDE of fourth-order, describing a capillary-driven fluid flow in a rotating cylinder, we propose a second-order relaxation system of parabolic-elliptic type. For positive initial data, we prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the relaxation system. Thereby, the lifespan of the approximate solutions turns out to be independent of the relaxation parameter. Moreover, we prove convergence of non-negative weak solutions of the relaxation system to weak solutions of the original equation on compact time intervals. We classify positive steady states of the relaxed system, prove a stability result yielding global strong solutions, and show that the long-time dynamics remain consistent under the relaxation limit.

We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

Building on the semantic information theory of Niu-Zhang and the classical information hiding theory of Moulin-O'Sullivan, this paper establishes an information-theoretic framework for information hiding under semantic communication. The classical hiding model is extended to a two-layer structure (semantic host, syntactic host, syntactic composite signal, syntactic received, semantic received) bridged by synonymous mappings f_s, f_x and the inverse mapping f_y^{-1}, subject to four distortion constraints: syntactic transparency, semantic fidelity, syntactic perturbation, and semantic destruction. The capacity is cast as a Stackelberg game with the hider moving first and the payoff J(Q,A) = I(U~; Y~ | K) - I(U~; S~ | K), yielding the single-letter maximin C^s = max_Q min_A J(Q,A), whose achievability and converse follow from random coding and joint typicality decoding. These results clarify that semantic hiding is not unconditionally superior to classical hiding. Binary, ternary, and Gaussian examples confirm the degeneration under one-to-one mappings and the capacity loss under coarsening.

The previous bounds were 19/27 $\approx$ 70.37%, due to Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek and to Bui and Heath-Brown (2013), and 84.77\%, due to Chirre, Gonçalves and de Laat (2020). Montgomery's pair correlation argument rests on a pointwise consequence of the explicit formula: at a zero of multiplicity $m\ge2$, a Dirichlet polynomial $J$ over prime powers of length $T^ψ$, $ψ<1$, is forced to have real part at most $-a<0$. The mollified derivative $ζ'(ρ)M(ρ)$ of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek vanishes there. Both facts are used at the same zero, in a single least-squares inequality. The new analytic input is the mixed moment $\sum_ρζ'(ρ)M(ρ)J(1-ρ)$ with $J$ much longer than the mollifier. We evaluate it under the Riemann Hypothesis alone; the long prime sum stays in the numerator and the mollifier variable is the modulus, so the barrier at $T^{1/2}$ does not arise. A second-order version of the argument gives $0.70736$. We show that no second-order certificate of this type can exceed $0.7073646063$, and pass this ceiling with fourth moments of short Dirichlet polynomials and with mixed moments against products of a bounded number of primes. All constants are certified in exact rational arithmetic.

We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Whether it has the Sperner property is open. We show that for every pair of adjacent levels, the smaller one can be matched into the larger one by parent--child pairs, except possibly for the pairs $(j,j+1)$ with $(28n-36)/39<j<(13n+5)/18$ (for small $n$ the window is slightly smaller still). This window has width about $n/234\approx0.0043\,n$. The largest level lies near $n/(2\ln2)\approx0.7213\,n$, which we prove using the law of the block sizes of a uniformly random ordered set partition of $[n]$, and for $n$ large it falls inside the window. Since the level sizes are log-concave, Hall's condition for all pairs would make $\OP$ Sperner. The proofs use explicit weights on the parent--child pairs; they reduce to a finite inequality between pairs of adjacent blocks. We explain why the simplest weights fail exactly at the boundary of a much larger window, and report computations supporting Hall's condition inside the window: exactly for $n\le14$, and by equalizing flows for every window pair with $n\le25$.
Square-root comparison, Turnpike, and exact semidefinite feasibility

Given positive integers $a_i,K$, put $S=\sum_{i=1}^k\sqrt{a_i}$. We construct a realizable Turnpike instance in which the minimum spacing of distinct distances and the smallest nonzero addition residual are both at most $|S-K|$ when $S\ne K$. With approximation oracles, one three-distance realizability query decides $S\le K$. For unordered lists of radical sums with nonnegative rational coefficients, a polynomial-time substitution by integers preserves every normalized ruler. We give the classical reduction of square-root comparison to exact semidefinite feasibility in both threshold directions. The comparison enters through numerical separation and marked sorting; the integer recoding needs no such comparison for unordered reconstruction.
Viscosity solutions for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms
Russell Schwab; Son N. T. Tu; Olga Turanova

We address global well-posedness for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms. This naturally results from establishing the comparison principle for viscosity solutions and existence via Perron's method. There are many earlier results for similar equations, and our work attempts to give a unified approach and improve upon some recent examples. There is a natural juxtaposition of earlier results in the usual framework of viscosity solutions which rely on a min-max structure, with some more recent implementations coming from the free boundary literature in which a min-max is not apparent initially, but does appear a posteriori due to certain rigid structural constraints. Here we give a presentation that combines ideas from both situations. The most important feature of the operators in our equations is what we call the global comparison property. This is combined with a natural local Lipschitz assumption on the operator defining the equation.
Convergence of Residual-driven Adaptive Kernel-based Multilevel Approximation

Kernel-based multilevel methods combine compactly supported radial basis functions with a residual correction scheme and are known to converge linearly in the number of levels. In this paper we study an adaptive version of the multilevel method, in which the interpolation on each level only uses those sites at which the residual of the preceding level exceeds a given threshold. Although this method has been proposed some time ago and converges in all numerical tests, a convergence proof has been missing so far. We close this gap. We derive an a priori error bound, an a posteriori error bound valid for arbitrary point selections, and extend the analysis to penalized least-squares approximation and to target functions outside the native space of the kernel. For a variant with an additional check-loop per level, we show convergence with the rate of the classical multilevel method. We illustrate our findings with three numerical examples.
On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic

Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $σ\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(σ)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $σ$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.
Existence of complete singular solutions of the Yamabe equation at prescribed points
Zheng-Chao Han; Qinfeng Jiang; Hua-Yang Wang; Jingang Xiong; Lei Zhang

Let $(M^n,g)$ be smooth, connected and closed, with $n\ge3$, and let $P$ be a prescribed nonempty finite set. We characterize the conformal classes $[g]$ that admit a complete metric of positive constant scalar curvature on $M\setminus P$. Such a metric exists precisely when $Y(M,[g])>0$ and either $[g]$ is nonround or $|P|\ge2$. In a nonround positive conformal class, the metrics can be chosen with Fowler asymptotics and arbitrary fixed ratios of their small asymptotic neck sizes. As the neck sizes tend to zero, every sequence of these metrics has a subsequence converging smoothly away from the punctures to a smooth Yamabe minimizing metric. The construction allows degenerate Yamabe minimizers and arbitrary curvature jets at the prescribed points. For nonempty closed singular sets $Λ\subset M$ with empty interior, we also announce the same existence criterion with the additional requirement that the Bessel capacity $C_{1+2/n,n/2}(Λ)$ vanish.
Nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase

In this paper, we construct smooth nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase $(n-2)π/2$ for every $n\ge4$. Together with the nonquadratic example in dimension two and Warren's example in dimension three, our construction shows that the supercritical condition $|θ|>(n-2)π/2$ in the Bernstein theorem proved by Yuan is sharp in every dimension $n\ge2$.
Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
Jory Griffin; Jens Marklof; Tariq Osman

Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by Götze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.
Selecting $2 \times 2$ submatrices with optimally bounded inverses

For a matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ ($n \ge k$) with orthonormal columns, the Goreinov--Tyrtyshnikov--Zamarashkin (GTZ) conjecture asserts that there exists a $k \times k$ submatrix $U_I$ with $\|U_I^{-1}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}$. The conjecture remains open for $3 \le k \le n - 3$. The existence of such a submatrix in the case $k = 2$ was proved for $n=4$ by Nesterenko (2023) and recently for general $n$ by Sengupta and Pautov (2026). In this paper, we give a short, elementary, constructive proof of a weighted strengthening of this result, which yields a single-pass streaming algorithm that selects a row pair satisfying the $\sqrt{n}$ bound in $\mathcal O(n)$ operations and $\mathcal O(1)$ auxiliary memory. We further give an explicit matrix representation of all equality cases for $k = 2$ characterized by Nesterenko (2026) and use it to construct a single matrix family on which standard selection strategies (including global and local maximum-volume selection, Bischof--Stewart pivoted QR, column-pivoted QR, and LU with partial pivoting) simultaneously fail to attain the $\sqrt{n}$ bound.
StePPO: Adaptive Step-Size Control for Initial-Value Problems Using Proximal Policy Optimisation
Milan Koumans; Nicola Pezzotti; Tristan S. W. Stevens

ODE solvers are used to model, simulate, and analyse continuous-time systems found in many signal processing applications. Time integration of these initial-value problems is traditionally performed using adaptive embedded Runge--Kutta methods. For proper time-step selection, adaptive solvers accept or reject each candidate step according to a local error estimate. Their efficiency is therefore controlled by the rule that selects the next step size. Classical proportional--integral--derivative (PID) controllers are computationally inexpensive per decision and reliable, but their reactive design can lead to costly numerical solves near stiff transitions. We formulate step-size selection for parametrised IVPs as a Markov decision process and train a continuous-action policy using proximal policy optimisation. The policy processes its observation signals using a deep network while maintaining the embedded solver logic. We evaluate on a decay function, the Van der Pol system, and the Brusselator system at matched tolerances, and compare against a standard PID controller and a multi-scale DeepONet network. We find that the proposed learned policy remains within prescribed error tolerances while reducing the required number of solve steps by up to 60%, achieving a wall-clock time reduction of 58%, for both in- and out-of-distribution settings.
On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties

For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five. Finally, we complete Ein's classification of smooth nondegenerate complex projective varieties with smooth projective dual. The list consists of smooth quadrics, the Segre varieties $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^m$ with $m\ge2$, the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$, and the spinor tenfold in $\mathbb P^{15}$.
The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C

We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.
Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
Buse Şen; Aras Selvi; Jean Pauphilet; Daniel Kuhn

Decisions under uncertainty increasingly rest on fragmented evidence, such as samples from related but different populations, privacy-protected summary statistics, or complementary statistical descriptions of the same data. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) can fuse such evidence by constructing one ambiguity set per source and hedging against all distributions in the intersection of these sets. This fusion approach is less conservative than aggregating the sources into a single ambiguity set, but it is computationally demanding. Exact reformulations grow exponentially with the number of sources, and even deciding whether the intersection is nonempty is NP-hard. We show that fusion DRO admits an exact reformulation in which the ambiguity sets are coupled only through functional Lagrange multipliers. Restricting these multipliers to affine decision rules yields upper bounds that decompose across the ambiguity sets, are exact for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references, and provably dominate aggregation-based relaxations such as Minkowski sums and balls around mixtures. The approximations admit finite conic reformulations in important special cases and subgradient methods for weakly convex losses, which makes fusion DRO applicable to neural network training. In portfolio, newsvendor, and binary classification experiments, the affine approximation stays close to the exact value wherever the latter is computable, scales far better than exact methods, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample.
The Monge Optimal Transport Barycenter Problem with Adaptive Features

The data-driven Monge optimal transport barycenter problem seeks a map $y=T(x,z)$ that minimally perturbs an outcome $x$ while removing its statistical dependence on covariates $z$. Numerical implementations approximate the independence constraint through finite-dimensional test-function spaces, making the effectiveness of dependence removal sensitive to the choice of features. This article develops a procedure whereby the features themselves are optimized throughout the procedure. In particular, we adopt a feature space for $f$ consisting of Gaussian radial basis functions (RBFs) with adaptive individual centers and bandwidths. Synthetic experiments show that while fixed nonlinear RBF features can capture dependence structures that are poorly represented by linear features, adapting the RBF centers and bandwidths can further improve dependence removal within a limited feature space and achieve residual dependence comparable to that obtained with a larger fixed basis. We further extend the formulation to multidimensional covariates and evaluate its applicability to real-world problems, including removing age-related dependence in biomedical measurements and dependence on temperature and humidity in bike-sharing demand.
Backpropagation as Dirac-bracket dynamics of dissipative training
Nicolaus Linneu Holanda; Ivan Eugenio Cunha

Gradient-based training of a parametric model is the motion of a damped particle in the potential set by the loss. Using the Bateman-Galley doubling of the degrees of freedom, which gives dissipative systems an action principle, we write gradient flow, the heavy-ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method as Hamiltonian systems. We show that, within this Hamiltonian description, backpropagation is Dirac evolution. The activations of a feed-forward network are treated as coordinates of phase space, and the layer equations as constraints. These constraints are second class for every architecture, and Hamilton's equations with the resulting Dirac bracket reproduce training with the exact gradient of the loss, although the Hamiltonian contains only the cost of the network output. The Dirac bracket of an activation with the momenta of the parameters is its Jacobian, the inverse of the constraint matrix contains both the forward and the reverse modes of automatic differentiation, and the errors propagated by backpropagation are the Lagrange multipliers of the layer constraints: the constraint forces of a kinematic chain under the load of the cost. These results hold in the full doubled phase space, not only in the physical limit. The network's part of the constraint algebra is the same for every optimizer, Nesterov's look-ahead adds one layer of momentum-dependent constraints that couple the two copies of the doubled system, and gradient flow is obtained by constructing the Dirac bracket in stages. We confirm these statements numerically to machine precision and train a network by integrating the Dirac flow of its constraints, with no backward pass in the computation.

We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.
Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
D. H. Zhao; J; Zhang; S. S. Yang; L. W. Liao

Let $\varphi$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^\varphi g+1$$
 has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Brück's conjecture.
Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
Hao-Chung Cheng; Li Gao; Shi-Bing Li; Hongsen Qiu

We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.
Functional Factor Graphs and the Functional Sum-Product Algorithm
Kuranage Roche Rayan Ranasinghe; Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu

We propose a generalization of factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm (SPA), widely used in the estimation of data, channel state information and sensing parameters, to unknowns that are functions, such as waveforms, time-varying channels and continuous-aperture array currents, which must otherwise be sampled first. In order to mitigate the challenge that functions have no probability density functions (PDFs), the proposed scheme measures densities relative to the prior of each function, not to the flat reference implicit in every PDF. Messages then become likelihood ratios, and the factor-node rule an average over the priors, still exact on trees. For Gaussian models, the proposed functional SPA (FSPA) is Gaussian belief propagation (GaBP) with kernels in place of matrices and a grid-independent convergence condition, whereas scalar GaBP on grid samples provably slows down under refinement, as information hops from sample to sample. Simulations in a multi-user detection setting confirms the latter, and shows that sampling first can also fail for smooth priors.
Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem

Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. In this paper, we construct a solution with a free boundary point of frequency 3.
Exact Lyapunov spectrum and localization length of the multichannel disordered Schrödinger equation

We consider the multichannel Schrödinger equation, describing the evolution of $N$ transverse modes in a finite width wire, in the presence of a Gaussian white noise potential in the unitary symmetry class. For arbitrary energy $E$ and disorder strength $T$, we compute exactly the set of Lyapunov exponents $\{ γ_n(E,T) \}_{1 \leq n \leq N}$ which define the decay rates of the wave functions. In the large energy regime, we recover that the Lyapunov exponents are equally spaced, as predicted by the so-called DMPK approach. However we show that this property breaks down at arbitrary energy, giving rise to a richer Lyapunov spectrum. We also uncover a direct relation between the localization length, given by the inverse of the smallest Lyapunov exponent, and the density of states. Our derivation relies on the analysis of matrix stochastic differential equation for a modified Riccati matrix.
Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
Konstantin Riedl; Justin Sirignano; Konstantinos Spiliopoulos

Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.
Optimal \texorpdfstring{$(1,1)$}{(1,1)}-Criss-Cross Deletion-Correcting Codes with Linear-Time Encoder and Decoder
Zhiqiang Li; Yubo Sun; Gennian Ge

We consider a $q$-ary $n\times n$ array subject to a $(1,1)$-criss-cross deletion, which removes one row and one column. We first derive a sphere-packing type lower bound on the redundancy of codes correcting such deletions. For every $q\geq 2$ and $n\geq 27$, the redundancy is greater than $2n+2\log_q n-2$. For fixed $q$, it is at least $2n-1+2\log_q n-o_q(1)$ as $n\to\infty$. We then present two code constructions. The first construction achieves redundancy $2n-1+2\log_q n+o_q(1)$ by selecting a largest syndrome class. It matches the lower bound up to a vanishing term and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time decoding. The second construction has redundancy $2n+2\log_q n+O_q(1)$ and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time algorithms for both encoding and decoding. For fixed $q$, these running times are linear in the number of array entries.
Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
Marcela Cárdenas; Francisco Correa; Nicolás Salazar

We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.
Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls

We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity.
 The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.
Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
Miquel Barcelona; Joan Gimeno; Marc Jorba-Cuscó

We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincaré maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space.
 For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests.
 Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.
Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers

Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions. For a fixed positive semidefinite integral form on a box of radius $H$, with a linear term of coefficients $O(H)$, the algorithm computes all level counts simultaneously in $O(H^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit operations when $H=O(\sqrt m)$ and the facet offsets have $O(\log(2m))$ bits. A signed decomposition into orthogonal simplices gives this bound. For fullerenes we use deterministic $O(m^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work to construct an index of $O(m\log(2m))$ bits. With this index a rank costs $O(m\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work, uniformly in the rank. Two families of recuts let energy descent escape self-contacts in the slit polygon. The decoder then writes the graph from its selected period in $O(m)$ arithmetic word operations.

We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.
Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry

We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.
The singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
Mohameden Ahmedou; Lina Wu; Lei Zhang

We compute the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. We assume that the kernel of the Paneitz operator consists of the constants. In each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the Euler characteristic and the conical orders. We match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. A localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. For generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. Assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. If the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. At one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. On the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.
Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling
David Krame Kadurha; Alessandro Zocca; Sandjai Bhulai

Multistage stochastic programs (MSPs) with discrete decisions are hard to solve due to the curse of dimensionality, non-convex value functions, and scenario trees that grow exponentially with the horizon. We develop a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework for MSPs in which a neural network predicts scores for the part of the decision that drives the state transition. Under structural conditions that make this sub-decision enter the stage objective linearly, the network is trained on labels from offline single-scenario problems, using the Fenchel-Young loss with perturbed optimizers, which need only an optimization oracle. We apply the framework to repair scheduling in power networks under stochastic, time-varying component failures, with and without a per-stage repair budget. On a synthetic 5-bus network and on the IEEE 14-bus network at two repair-cost scales, the learned and baseline policies are compared on common evaluation paths. Without the budget, DFL is the cheapest policy on the 5-bus network; on the 14-bus network it does not outperform a near-sighted model-predictive control (MPC) baseline, but it beats repairing every failed component at the higher scale. Under a binding budget, DFL is the cheapest policy evaluated on both networks and at both scales, 14% to 23% below the next-best policy. On the 5-bus network, the mean cost of DFL is 1.7% (without the budget) and 1.8% (with it) above the exact optimum computed by dynamic programming. Within days of computation, sample average approximation yields costlier policies than DFL and the repair-everything heuristic, and stochastic dual dynamic integer programming remains far from convergence. DFL computes its decisions about as fast as the trivial heuristics and orders of magnitude faster than MPC. Since these conditions are not specific to power networks, the framework extends to other MSPs that share this structure.
Homogenization with Shape-Evolving Microstructures: A Two-Phase Membrane Problem

We study a diffusion problem in a highly heterogeneous periodic medium (characterized by a small scale parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll1$) where small inclusions are separated from the surrounding connected area by solute-impermeable membranes. These membranes are allowed to grow and deform under surface tension and osmotic pressure (driven by the concentration difference across the membrane). We prove existence of weak solutions on a time interval which is independent of the microscopic scale via a Schauder fixed-point argument by establishing spatial boundary Hölder estimates. For the homogenization limit $\varepsilon\to0$, we establish strong compactness of the outer concentration via time translates and then derive a stability estimate for the driven inner cell problems. The limit couples a macroscopic conservation law, with shape-dependent effective diffusion, to inner diffusion and membrane motion in each cell.
Structure-preserving finite element method for the 2D MHD-$α$ turbulence system
Patrick E. Farrell; Mingdong He; Kaibo Hu

We propose a structure-preserving finite element method for the two-dimensional MHD-$α$ turbulence model, which filters the transport velocity at a length $α$ while retaining the ideal invariants of the original MHD equations, with the energy replaced by an $α$-dependent energy. The scheme preserves mass conservation and the magnetic Gauss law pointwise and satisfies discrete dissipation laws for the energy, the cross helicity and the mean square magnetic potential, which reduce to exact conservation in the ideal limit. The discrete systems are solved by an augmented Lagrangian preconditioner with monolithic geometric multigrid, observed to be robust with respect to the filter width $α$ and the Reynolds numbers, and to the mesh size for small time steps. The scheme converges at the optimal rates and agrees with a Fourier pseudo-spectral direct simulation of the original MHD equations at the large scales. In under-resolved flows, the unfiltered scheme has no numerical dissipation and accumulates energy at the grid scale. Filtering relieves this accumulation and a larger $α$ gives a more compact spectrum. Long-time simulations reproduce selective decay, including relaxation toward the Arnold-type bound and the inverse cascade of the mean square potential.
Galois scalar extension of simple Lie algebras
Alfonso Di Bartolo; Francesco Paolo Di Fatta; Gianmarco La Rosa

We investigate the behaviour of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras under finite Galois field extensions. Given a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a finite Galois extension $\mathbb{K}/\mathbb{F}$ of degree $n = [\mathbb{K}:\mathbb{F}]$, we prove that if $L$ is isomorphic to a $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ viewed as an $\mathbb{F}$-algebra, then the scalar extension $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $n$ copies of $S$. Furthermore, for cyclic extensions of order a prime number, we show that if no such $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ exists, the extended algebra $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ remains simple. This framework provides a general mechanism to transfer structural and classification results across different ground fields. In addition, we examine the centroids of simple Lie algebras, proving that the dimension of the space of centroids is invariant under finite field extensions. As an application, we explicitly determine the structure of the spaces of centroids for simple Lie algebras over finite fields.
Morse theory and a degree formula for the resonant singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds
Mohameden Ahmedou; Lina Wu; Lei Zhang

We develop Morse theory for the singular Paneitz equation at resonant mass on closed four-manifolds with conical orders between minus one and zero and Paneitz kernel consisting of the constants. Under nondegeneracy of the reduced interactions and nonvanishing of the leading mass-defect coefficients, we classify the critical points at infinity by the sign of these coefficients. We compute their indices and their contributions to the relative homology of sublevels. The topology of very low sublevels is determined by weighted barycenters of strictly smaller total weight and by the negative Paneitz eigenspace. These results yield strong Morse inequalities and a Leray--Schauder degree formula at resonance, which also applies when genuine solutions are degenerate. On the round four-sphere with two conical points, the Morse inequalities give existence on an open set of data for which the degree vanishes.
Non-Intrusive Least-Squares Reduced Basis Methods: Black-Box Snapshots and Exact Residual Certificates

For a parametrized linear first-order system, the least-squares functional at a conforming pair is the squared norm of the residual of the continuous problem, and it can be computed exactly. In this paper, we use this least-squares residual as the error certificate of reduced basis methods whose snapshots are computed by black-box solvers. The output of the solver is first made conforming by a reconstruction, and a flux is recovered by least-squares if the solver does not provide one. The online reduced problem minimizes the least-squares functional over the product of the space spanned by the snapshot fluxes and the space spanned by the snapshot potentials. It needs no inf--sup condition on the reduced spaces, and its certificate needs no stability constant. We discuss second-order elliptic equations, the Stokes equations, where only the velocity of a black-box solver is used, and linear transport equations with a moving inflow boundary. In the numerical experiments, the snapshots are computed by least-squares, conforming, nonconforming, stabilized, finite volume, and finite difference solvers. With adaptive meshes and the same tolerances, the greedy algorithm stops at the same or nearly the same reduced dimension for all solvers that accept a mesh.
Stability of separable solutions to a fast diffusion system

We study a Dirichlet fast diffusion system with symmetric linear cross-loss terms on a bounded smooth domain. A coupled Rayleigh quotient captures the variational structure of the coupling and is nonincreasing along sufficiently regular positive solution pairs. Under the common extinction and regularity hypotheses, this monotonicity and the energy identity yield upper and lower bounds \[ C^{-1}(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)} \le \|(u(t),v(t))\|_{L^{p+1}(Ω)} \le C(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)}. \] In the Sobolev subcritical range, a Lyapunov functional for the rescaled system yields a sequence of times $t_j\uparrow T^*$ along which the rescaled pair converges strongly in $H_0^1(Ω)\times H_0^1(Ω)$ to a nonnegative classical stationary solution pair. The integral lower bound excludes the trivial limiting pair, while the coupling with $α>0$ ensures that neither limiting component is identically zero. As a further property of the stationary system, we show that proportional components of a nontrivial nonnegative solution pair must coincide. We also construct a positive diagonal stationary solution pair by constrained minimization. Scalar upper comparison and a Bénilan--Crandall-type estimate for smooth positive diagonal solutions provide complementary links with the scalar fast diffusion equation.
Ultrarank and ideal structure of uniform Roe algebras
Liang Guo; Jin Qian; Qin Wang

In this paper, we study the ideal structure of the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ for a coarse disjoint union $X = \bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} X_n$ of finite metric spaces, with a focus on ideals lying between the compact ideal $\mathcal{K}$ and the ghost ideal $\mathcal{G}$. To analyze these ideals, we introduce a nonstandard invariant called the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank of an operator, which is stable under compact perturbations and completely characterizes principal ideal inclusions in the block-diagonal Calkin algebra. Using the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank as an obstruction to ideal inclusion in $C^*_u(X)$, we construct an ideal between $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ that cannot be written as the intersection of any geometric ideal and the ghost ideal. On the positive side, when the averaging projection $P$ belongs to $C^*_u(X)$, we prove that the closed two-sided ideal $\langle P \rangle$ generated by $P$ equals $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if every ghost operator has finite ultrarank and $X$ has zero-density Property A, and we classify all closed two-sided ideals of $C^*_u(X)$ in this case.
Optimal bounds for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-constant-power error-correcting cooling codes
Shuangqing Liu; Qianfei Zhang; Shikang Yu; Menglong Zhang; Lijun Ji

High temperatures have dramatic negative effects on interconnect performance. In a bus, whenever a wire changes its state from ``0'' to ``1'' or from ``1'' to ``0'', Joule heating causes the temperature to rise. Constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes, introduced in [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 66 (2020), 4804--4818], are coding schemes that can simultaneously control the peak temperature and the average power consumption of on-chip buses while providing error-correction capability for transmitted information. This paper establishes a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes for $t<w-3$ by some graph-theoretic techniques and the probabilistic method, and constructs several new families of optimal CPECC codes using the asymptotic existence result for GDDs. For $t\geq w-3$, this paper also provides a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes by some hypergraph-theoretic techniques, and several new families of CPECC codes attaining the resulting upper bounds using RBIBDs. The previous upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes in [arXiv:2608.08742] is a special case of our upper bound.
Haizhong Li; Yao Wan; Yijia Zhang

Chord integrals are moments of chord lengths and translation-invariant averages of dual quermassintegrals. In this paper, we prove their Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $q\in[1,n+2]\cup\{n+3\}$, with equality precisely for homothetic bodies. A transfer from symmetric dual quermassintegrals to covariogram level sets gives, in dimension two, the full range $1\leq q\leq5$. For every $0<q<1$, we establish the same inequality for simplices and an explicit factor version for all convex bodies. On the other hand, rectangular perturbations give counterexamples for every $q>n+1+β_*$, where $β_*\in(2,3)$. As consequences, we obtain Minkowski inequalities and uniqueness results for chord measures. We also prove Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for affine-section integrals and mixed Riesz energies.
The Functional Batch Conjecture And Its Extension To All Finite Fields
Isaac Barouch Essayag; Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy

We prove that the code whose servers store all $q^s-1$ nonzero linear combinations of $s$ information symbols over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a functional batch code with list size $(q^s+q-2)/2$: every list of $(q^s+q-2)/2$ requested nonzero linear combinations, repetitions allowed, can be recovered from pairwise disjoint sets of at most two servers. This holds for every finite field and every $s\ge1$, and the list size cannot be increased, even if recovery sets of any size are allowed. For $q=2$ the statement is the functional batch conjecture for the binary simplex code, in its stronger form with recovery sets of size at most two, and it follows from the conjecture of Balister, Győri and Schelp on perfect matchings of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with prescribed differences, which was proved by the second author in a separate paper. We also determine the minimum length of a functional batch code with $s$ information symbols over $\mathbb{F}_q$: it is $m(q^s-1)$ for the list size $m(q^s+q-2)/2$, for every $m\ge1$, and, for odd $q$, it is $2(q^s-1)/(q-1)$ for the list size $(q^s-1)/(q-1)+1$.
On Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners and their properties
Chen Greif; Jörg Liesen; Justus Ramme

Bramble and Pasciak (Math. Comp., 1988) discovered a preconditioning method for linear algebraic systems in saddle point form, which under certain conditions transforms a symmetric indefinite saddle point matrix into a nonsymmetric matrix that is positive definite in some non-standard inner product. Thus, the method "removes" the indefiniteness of the problem, while retaining the property that the preconditioned system can be solved using an optimal Krylov subspace method with three-term recurrences. Since this well-known method has some limitations, several variants with potential improvements have been proposed in the literature. In this paper, we attempt a systematic assessment of the mathematical properties and practical efficiency of Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners. Our goal is to close some gaps in the understanding of these techniques. We identify and analyze the three main methods in this context, highlighting a variant that offers additional flexibility but has received little attention to date. We perform detailed spectral analyzes of the preconditioned matrices and illustrate our theoretical results on several numerical examples.
The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation

We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.
Polynomial identities and primitivity in double extension regular algebras of type (14641)

We determine which members of the twenty-six families of double extension regular algebras of type $(14641)$ in the Zhang--Zhang classification satisfy a polynomial identity. Retaining the scalar twist parameter, we compute the PI degree for twenty-one of the twenty-two families with PI members and give three possibilities for the remaining family. We establish exact primitivity criteria for the nondegenerate members of eight families and show that sixteen families have no primitive members. The proofs use monomial data, normal subalgebras and crossed products of quantum tori. Twisting by a root of unity preserves the PI property, whereas finite order of the double-extension determinant is necessary but not sufficient for an algebra in the list to be PI.
On some problems regarding a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula

In \cite{FT23}, we introduced the group-theoretical function $f(G) = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{H \le G} |\Aut(H)|$ for a finite group $G$ and posed three open problems concerning its values on noncyclic groups. In this note, we provide complete solutions to all three problems.
Four Classes of Few-Weight Linear Codes over $u\mathbb{F}_q+u^2\mathbb{F}_q+u^3\mathbb{F}_q$ from Simplicial Complexes
Lan Deng; Zhao Hu; Nian Li

In this paper, we construct linear codes over the commutative non-unital ring $u\mathbb{F}_q+u^2\mathbb{F}_q+u^3\mathbb{F}_q$, where $u^4=0$, using simplicial complexes in $\mathbb{F}_q^m$ and their complements. For codes defined by two arbitrary nonempty simplicial complexes, we determine the lengths and $\mathbb{F}_q$-dimensions. When each complex has a single maximal element with nonempty proper support, we use an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear Gray map and exponential sums to determine the parameters and Lee weight distributions of four classes of codes. These classes have two, at most five, at most four, and at most eight nonzero Lee weights, respectively. Puncturing the Gray images yields projective codes with dual minimum distance three. Using the Griesmer bound, we obtain families of distance-optimal projective codes, including a binary family whose lengths exceed the bound by three. The Gray images are Euclidean self-orthogonal for $q=3$ and for $q=2$ under an additional condition, and Hermitian self-orthogonal for $q=4$. We also give sufficient conditions for minimality of both the Gray images and the projective codes.
Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
Hermen Jan Hupkes; Petr Stehlík; Vladimír Švígler; Jialing Yu

We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs. As the diffusion strength increases, the waves end up moving in the same direction irrespective of the bistability. This direction is determined solely by the underlying structure of the heterogeneous tree. Our techniques also lead to sharper results for the homogeneous setting.
Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe

We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions and integrals. We prove that the associated period map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto a bounded, convex planar domain whose rational points parametrize the conformal equivalence classes of closed extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants. We conclude with a study of the global geometry of closed extremals.
Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number

We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element. By the criterion of Marche and Wolff, this proves Goldman's ergodicity conjecture for $g\ge 3$ and Euler numbers $e$ with $0<|e|\leq g-1$.
List coloring degenerate graphs with requests
Rajat Adak; L. Sunil Chandran; Shiwali Gupta; Tomáš Kaiser; Subrahmanyam Kalyanasundaram; Rogers Mathew; Saraswati Girish Nanoti; Suraj Kumar Sahoo; Umesh Shankar; Joel M. Thomas

We prove three results on the flexible list coloring of $d$-degenerate graphs. Following Dvořák, Norin and Postle [J. Graph Theory 2019], a graph $G$ is $(k,ε)$-flexible if for any assignment $L$ of lists of size $k$ to its vertices and any choice of requested colors by a set $\widehat V$ of the vertices from their respective lists, there is an $L$-coloring satisfying at least $ε|\widehat V|$ of the requests. The complete graph on $d+1$ vertices shows that if all $d$-degenerate graphs are $(k,ε)$-flexible for some list size $k$ and satisfaction ratio $ε$, then $k \geq d+1$ and $ε\leq\tfrac1{d+1}$.
 Our results concern values at or near these extremes. For list size $d+2$, we improve the satisfaction ratio from an inverse exponential to an inverse polynomial function of $d$. For satisfaction ratio $\tfrac1{d+1}$, we prove that it is achievable for list size $2d$ as well as $\left\lfloor(d+2)\left(2-\tfrac1e\right)\right\rfloor$ (which is less than $2d$ for $d\geq 9$).
Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds

In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $ρ_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $ρ_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).
Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on vector bundles II: the non-simple case

In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system on the space of Fubini-Study metrics on a polarized compact Kähler manifold. Sano proved that if there exists a balanced metric for the polarization, then this dynamical system always converges to the balanced metric provided that the automorphism group is discrete (\cite{S}).
 In \cite{DKLR}, Douglas, et.\ al., conjecture that the same holds in the case of vector bundles. In \cite{Se}, we proved their conjecture under the assumption that the bundle is simple. In this note, we remove the simplicity assumption. The main tool is Thompson's metric on the space of Hermitian inner products on the space of holomorphic sections, with respect to which the generalized $T$-operator is non-expanding.
A Counterexample to Single-Control Null Controllability of Stochastic Heat Equations

We disprove the conjecture that a single localized drift control suffices for null controllability of stochastic parabolic equations with bounded adapted coefficients. On a bounded interval with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we construct a deterministic, nonnegative smooth noise coefficient supported at positive distance from the control interval. One fixed nonzero smooth initial state cannot be driven to zero almost surely at any positive time by any progressively measurable control with finite expected $L^2$ energy. The proof uses products of Brownian increments in the adjoint terminal data to keep the initial pairing bounded away from zero while the observation norm tends to zero. On the flat torus, the construction yields counterexamples in every Gevrey class of order $s>1$ whenever the complement of the control set contains an open ball. Thus Gevrey regularity above order one cannot replace analyticity as a general sufficient condition for null controllability.
Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree

We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support of $N=n+k+1$ monomials, and we study the topological degree of $F$ on the positive orthant. In a previous paper we computed this topological degree in terms of signs of maximal minors, under a half-space condition which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. Here we use these formulas, together with their translation on the Gale dual side, to bound the topological degree. Our main result is a Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree, which is as simple as the classical one: for two variables, the absolute value of the topological degree is at most half the number of cyclic sign changes, at the vertices of the Newton polygon, of the coefficients of any linear combination of the two equations, and similar statements hold in any dimension and on the Gale dual side. Our second result is a fewnomial bound: for generic exponents and coefficients, we get $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the maximal number of facets of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $N$ vertices, and this bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Our third result is a symmetry: using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible values of the topological degree is the same for the parameters $(n,k)$ and $(k,n)$.
Localizing spectra and pseudospectra of a class of unbounded operators on Hilbert space
Andreas Buchinger; Marko Lindner; Mattes Wittig

We use a localization technique to bound and approximate the spectrum and the pseudospectra of a certain class of possibly non-normal, generally unbounded but closed operators on $L^2(X)$, where $X$ is either a) a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group $G$, not necessarily Abelian, with identity, a proper metric, and a left Haar measure or it is b) a uniformly discrete subset of $G$ with the counting measure. We treat the discrete and continuous cases b) and a) simultaneously. Our results yield computable subsets and supersets of the pseudospectra of $H$ that converge to the corresponding pseudospectrum in Attouch-Wets distance as the size parameter $L$ in our localization procedure goes to infinity. We illustrate our findings with unbounded band operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and with Schrödinger operators with $L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ potentials acting on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.
Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
Christopher Chalhoub; Jeroen S. W. Lamb; Martin Rasmussen

We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.
CLT for Linear Spectral Statistics of sample covariances of superimposition of Separable Covariance Components

Suppose $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ are $p\times n$ random matrices with entries having zero mean and unit variance and $p/n \to c \in (0,\infty)$. We construct the sample covariance matrix $S_n = \frac{1}{n}XX^*$ where $X =\sum_{r=1}^K X_r$, where $X_r = A_r^\frac{1}{2}Z_rB_r^\frac{1}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $A_r,B_r$ are sequences of positive semi-definite matrices of dimensions $p\times p$ and $n\times n$, respectively that are are simultaneously digaonalizable within themselves. As an extension of our previous work related to the L.S.D. of such classes of matrices, we show that the linear spectral statistics arising from the spectra of $S_n$ have Gaussian limits under assumptions of fourth moment bounds on the entries of $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and convergence of the joint spectral distribution of $\{A_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and $\{B_r\}_{r=1}^K$ to probability distributions over $\mathbb{R}_+^K$ with compact support.
Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts

For a finite dimensional semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the multiplicity $c_{λμ}^ν$ of an irreducible $V(ν),$ inside the tensor product $V(λ)\otimes V(μ),$ of two highest weight irreducible representations can be realised as the dimension of the Kostant--Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan multiplicity space inside $V(λ)$, $V(μ)$ or $V(ν)$. A result of Panyushev and Yakimova shows how to split the multiplicity space for $c_{λλ}^ν$ inside $V(ν)$ into symmetric and alternating parts when $V(λ)$ is self-dual. For finite-dimensional semisimple or symmetric Kac--Moody, we extend this to Kostant--Kumar modules $K(λ,w,λ)=\mathfrak{Ug}(v_λ\otimes v_{wλ})$ when $w=w^{-1},$ and for all dominant weights $λ.$ We show that the multiplicities of an irreducible in the symmetric and alternating parts of $K(λ,w,λ)$ are given by the dimensions of the eigenspaces of the Tits lift $\widetilde w$ of $w$ on the multiplicity space corresponding to eigenvalues $\pm 1$. This recovers the result for the full tensor product by letting $w=w_0,$ the longest element of the Weyl group. In type A, we also discuss connections to a combinatorial interpretation due to Carré and Leclerc in terms of domino tableaux.

We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, μ)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, μ)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, μ)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, μ)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, μ)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.
Pettis integrability of $L^1$-functions in locally convex spaces

In this article, for a Hausdorff locally convex space $E$, we investigate conditions under which every Lusin-measurable $L^1$-function $γ:[0,1]\to E$ is Pettis integrable. We show that this property on $E$ is local and equivalent to $E$ being absolutely summable and satisfying the metric convex compactness property. Via examples, we show that these two properties are independent. Moreover, we establish sufficient conditions, for a Lusin-measurable weakly integrable function with values in the topological dual $E'$, to be Gelfand integrable.
The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality

Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincaré duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordström, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and Lê, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in Lê's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.
Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective

Variational principles have played a fundamental role in the development of modern mathematics, physics, and scientific computing. From the principles of least action in mechanics to the calculus of variations and the variational formulation of partial differential equations, they have provided a powerful framework for understanding complex problems and designing reliable numerical methods. In recent years, Machine Learning has introduced a new computational paradigm, in which highly expressive nonlinear function spaces and large-scale minimisation problems play a central role. In these notes, we explore the connection between these two frameworks. We develop a variational and numerical-analysis perspective on Machine Learning algorithms, focusing in particular on their formulation as nonlinear minimisation problems. We investigate how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness acquire new interpretations in this setting, and how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can govern the behaviour of neural-network approximations. This perspective provides a mathematical framework for understanding existing ML algorithms while also suggesting new approaches to their design. In particular, alternative and strongly coercive variational principles can lead to more stable, reliable, and potentially more efficient computational methods.
Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
Kanhaiya Lal Chaurasiya; Vaskar Halder; Prajyot Patil; Gaurav Navnath Shinde; Debashish Das; Akshay Joshi

The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.
Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields

We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $Γ$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $Γ$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $Γ$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.
The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs

A $Γ$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $Γ$. Fix a finite abelian group $Γ$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist. The result previously appeared only in the author's 2009 PhD thesis. This proof uses a reduction to unbreakable graphs and recent structure theorems for graphs drawn on a surface, and was found with the help of AI.
A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials

The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results

We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory.
