We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[
 E(ρ,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ρ(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ρ$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring. For $\ell\geq3$, this number is four when $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ and three otherwise. These results answer two questions of Aharoni, Holzman, Howard, and Sprüssel.

Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras

We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres.
 We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. The proof takes, among the labellings that order vertices by non-increasing degree, one minimising the sum over edges of the products of the endpoint weights.

We study mean field games (MFGs) on the torus with non-degenerate diffusion, in a regime (no monotonicity) where multiple solutions exist for the same data. Our main result gives a sufficient condition for a closed multifunction to be a value multifunction, namely, it must satisfy a dynamic programming principle formulated on proper time subintervals, expressed as invariance of its graph under the forward operators generated by equilibria of the game. This replaces the global requirement that each value be produced by a solution of the forward-backward system on the whole time interval by a local, time-consistent condition together with closedness, which carries the terminal condition. We reformulate solutions of the mean field game in terms of relaxed equilibria, show that the closure of a value multifunction is again a value multifunction, and prove that the forward operators compose as a semigroup. A latent index $J\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ is drawn from a prior $π$. Conditional on $J=j$, a gambler observes random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ drawn independently from a non-negative component distribution $F_j$. We study the space of fundamental symmetries of a real or complex Krein space in finite or infinite dimension. After recalling the equivalence of the associated Hilbert norms, we describe two global operator parametrizations and their relation. The space is realized as a Banach symmetric space under $m(J,J')=JJ'J$. Its canonical connection is the tangential projection of the flat derivative in the real Banach space of Krein-self-adjoint operators. This yields explicit formulas for geodesics, parallel transport, transvections, and curvature. The positive square roots $(JJ')^{1/2}$ implement both isometries between the associated Hilbert spaces and geodesic transvections. A proof of their intertwining property in an earlier publication is corrected.
Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains

Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
Vadim Kaloshin; Illya Koval; Daniel Tsodikovich

We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

We prove that deciding whether a positive integer is abundant is equivalent to complete integer factorization under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

We prove a polynomial-degree-robust ($p$-robust) saturation property for conforming finite element approximations of the Poisson equation on shape-regular triangular meshes. Previously, a $p$-robust saturation estimate for the spectral method on a square was proved in [C. abla^2h+hσ) &=fh^{p-1} igl(h^2+|

Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number

We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,μ)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.
Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps

We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $σ_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |λ|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.
A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n

For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].
Rigidity of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics at Isotropy Order $n-6$

We classify linearly full, irreducible, totally unramified conformal minimal two-spheres of constant Gaussian curvature in the real Grassmannian $G(2,n;\mathbb R)$, or equivalently in the complex hyperquadric $Q_{n-2}$, whose finite isotropy order is $n-6$, where $n\geq7$. We remove the additional polynomiality assumption on a Frenet norm in the earlier classification of Li and Jiao. An exterior-product norm identity reduces the problem to the multiplicity of the irreducible polynomial $1+zw$; a further divisibility argument handles the boundary dimension $n=7$, including isotropy order one. The dimension $n$ is necessarily odd, and the immersion is congruent, after a conformal reparametrization, to the second member of a Veronese sequence with its prescribed real structure. Its curvature is $2/(5n-13)$ in the Grassmannian normalization. An explicit model in $Q_5$ illustrates the boundary case and its harmonic sequence.
On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn

Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $ν^{es}\otimesν^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.
Semantic Tanner-Graph Decoding for LDPC Codes
Wenjing Wei; Chentao Yue; Branka Vucetic; Yonghui Li

Conventional low-density parity-check (LDPC) belief propagation (BP) decoding operates on a Tanner graph, with no factor describing the source structure. This paper proposes a semantic Tanner graph for LDPC-coded text transmission and develops semantic-factor-aided BP (SF-BP) decoding. The source text is tokenized into discrete tokens, which are then mapped to binary messages for channel coding. For each token, the proposed graph introduces a semantic factor connected to the corresponding information-bit variable nodes forming the token. A fine-tuned language model assigns this factor a posterior distribution over all possible token symbols in the alphabet at each token position. During SF-BP decoding, semantic-factor and LDPC parity-check messages are combined at their shared variable nodes for message passing. Simulation results show that SF-BP significantly improves the block error rate (BLER) and Sentence-BERT similarity (BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) compared with conventional BP. For example, SF-BP reduces BLER from approximately 1 to 6.51 x 10^-6 and increases Sentence-BERT similarity from 0.21 to 1 - 1.26 x 10^-6 for the (1248, 1040) LDPC code at 4 dB.
Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups

We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.
Two-type thinning with alternative leader rate for random partition structures

A dust-free random partition structure with infinitely many parts is a random sequence $(\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots)$ with $\mathsf{X}_1>\mathsf{X}_2>\dots>0$ such that $\mathsf{X}_1+\mathsf{X}_2+\dots=1$, almost surely. It is a model for thinning invariant random partition structures, where every one of the infinitely many parts $\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots$ are thinned IID at rate 1. We consider a 2-type thinning where the instantaneous leader is deleted with an alternative rate $1+r\geq 0$. Then we seek time stationary random partition structures. When $r =R\in \{0,1,\dots\}$ a solution is obtained by taking $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ and performing ``balayage,'' where balayage means simply excavating the first $R$ points. We find the solutions for all $r \in (-1,\infty)$, which we call $\mathrm{PD}^{(r)}(m,0)$. We motivate with an application, and we present graphical representations.
A general upper bound on broadcast function ${B(n)}$ using Kn{ö}del graph
Sirma Cagil Altay; Mohammadhossein Fakharan; Hovhannes A. Harutyunyan

Broadcasting in a graph is the process of transmitting a message from one vertex, the originator, to all other vertices. We consider the classical model in which an informed vertex informs one of its uninformed neighbours during each time unit. A broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a graph in which broadcasting can finish in ${\lceil \log_{2} n \rceil}$ time units from any originator. A minimum broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a broadcast graph that has the least possible number of edges, ${B(n)}$, over all broadcast graphs on ${n}$ vertices. This paper presents a new general upper bound on ${B(n)}$ for all odd ${n}$ except when ${n=2^{k}-1}$ for an integer $k$. In order to achieve this bound, a vertex deletion method is applied to Knödel graphs on ${n+1}$ vertices. To prove our result, we characterize all informed vertices in a Knödel graph after every time unit by applying the standard and reverse dimensional broadcast scheme with any cyclic shifts from an arbitrary originator. Furthermore, we completely resolve the open problem about the existence of minimum average time broadcast graphs.
Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension

We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions. We give examples in both the measure-theoretic and topological senses, showing that this entropy gap condition is sharp. We also present applications related to the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps.
Zhiyao Fang; Wenwen Zhang; Ying Xu; Qi Liu

Fabian, Godefroy, Hájek and Zizler [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{200} (2003), 301--323, Theorem~2] proved that at density \(\aleph_1\), generation by a space whose modulus of smoothness has power type \(p\), \(1<p\le 2\), is equivalent to \(\ell_p(Γ)\)-generation. We extend this equivalence to arbitrary density, with \(|Γ|=\dens X\), answering \mbox{Problem~291} of Guirao, Montesinos and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~127]. We characterize generation by superreflexive spaces and by their \(\ell_2\)-sums, and obtain \(\ell_{\min\{r,2\}}\)-generation for closed subspaces of \(L^r(μ)\), \(1<r<\infty\), including Hilbert generation for \(r\ge 2\).
Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals

Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

We consider complex elliptic curves \(E\) admitting a finite subgroup \(C\subset E(\mathbb C)\) of order \(n\) such that \(E/C\) is isomorphic to \(E\). % with the additional requirement that the invariant factors of (C) are unequal. We establish class-number counting formulas for the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases.

This leads to finite sets of admissible discriminants describing the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases with unequal invariant factors.

This provides an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work by \cite{CanepaGaba2014,CanepaGaba2019,CanepaGabaOlteanu2022} and its subsequent algorithmic extensions.

 The results provide an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work.
Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle

We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.
Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs

We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.
Reconstruction of Poisson Random Measures in the Variational Framework with Applications to Jump-Driven SPDEs

We establish a reconstruction principle for Poisson random measures arising in compactness arguments for jump-driven stochastic partial differential equations. A basic difficulty in such arguments is that, after a Skorokhod-type representation, almost sure convergence of the solution processes does not by itself identify the limiting stochastic integral, since integration with respect to a compensated Poisson random measure is not a pathwise continuous functional of the solution and the noise.

Starting from a tight sequence of approximating solutions in $D([0,T];H)\cap L^α(0,T;V),$ we construct, on the represented probability space, a time-homogeneous Poisson random measure with the original Lévy intensity and compensator, compatible with the limiting filtration, such that the limiting process solves the corresponding SPDE.

Together with a shifted dyadic approximation of the solution, the increments of the solution path over dyadic time cells approximate the compensated noise increments; since the time integral of the drift is continuous in $H$, no regularisation of the drift is needed. The jumps are then recovered by a measurable registration procedure, while injectivity of the jump coefficient permits reconstruction of the corresponding marks through a Borel inverse obtained from the Lusin--Suslin theorem. The reconstruction is performed simultaneously at all truncation levels; consistency of the resulting finite jump measures and a monotone patching argument yield a Poisson random measure with the full Lévy measure. Under the injectivity assumption, no enlargement of the represented probability space is required.
Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics

Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gröbner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators.

For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.
A Robust Optimization Framework for Energy System Capacity Expansion under Line Outage Uncertainty

Capacity expansion models are widely used in climate and energy policy analysis to find optimal investments in generation, storage, and transmission. As the share of renewable generation grows, these models rely more on transmission lines to balance supply and demand across regions. Transmission lines, however, can fail due to aging, extreme weather, or accidents. Models that represent outages as time-dependent events come mainly from electrical engineering and are applied to small-scale systems, as they quickly become computationally intractable for inter-regional capacity expansion. We develop a capacity expansion model in which the risk of line failures shapes the investments in all parts of the system. We formulate it as a two-stage, scenario-based robust optimization problem that samples time-varying outage scenarios from a Markov model and hedges the investments against the most severe ones. To solve the model, we propose a memory-augmented Benders decomposition algorithm combined with Monte Carlo simulation that can handle thousands of scenarios. The selected plan is then evaluated with an out-of-sample simulation to bound the Value-at-Risk (VaR) of its system cost. In a 25-node case study of Germany and its neighboring countries, the gap between the lower bound and the simulated VaR bound is below 1%. We compare the robust plans with a deterministic plan, which assumes all lines are always available, and with a reserve-margin heuristic, which requires local firm capacity to be above peak demand. Like the heuristic, the robust plans nearly eliminate loss of load in 1000 simulated outage scenarios. Their mean system cost is within 0.2% of the deterministic plan and about 4.5% below the heuristic. Instead of adding more generation capacity, the robust approach mainly changes the type and location of capacity, for example, by spreading storage across the network.
Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion

The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.
A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics

We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.
From Limit Theorems to Mixing Limit Theorems

Following the work of Gouëzel, we give an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of a result of Arana-Herrera and Forni, which provides a general method for upgrading limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems to mixing limit theorems.
Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries

We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity.
 We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon).
 Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.
Random walk on an induced component of the uniform spanning forest
Xinyi Li; Runsheng Liu; Yuval Peres

Let $T$ be the component of the origin in the uniform spanning forest of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and consider the induced graph $H$ obtained by retaining every lattice edge with both endpoints in $T$. Lyons, Peres and Sun (2020) showed that $H$ is recurrent if $d \ge 8$ and asked for which $d \in \{5,6,7\}$ this holds. We prove that simple random walk on $H$ is transient for $d=5$ and recurrent for every $d\ge6$. We also show that the quenched return probabilities to the origin satisfy $p^H_{2n}(o,o)=n^{-α_d+o(1)}$ a.s., where $α_5=4/3$ and $α_6=1$, while $α_7=4/5$ and $α_d=2/3$ for all $d\ge8$.
Concavity of cardinality-constrained interval stabbing and interval cover problems

We consider the cardinality-constrained interval stabbing problem, in which the goal is to maximize the total weight of intervals hit by at least one of at most $k$ selected points. Although this problem does not admit a simple greedy solution, we show that its optimal value is a concave function of $k$. We establish this result using a linear programming formulation whose relaxation always admits an optimal solution with integer values. This allows us to prove concavity for the original problem. We further extend the result to the related interval cover problem. These concavity properties provide a basis for applying Lagrangian optimization using algorithms for the corresponding unconstrained problems.
On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$

The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $Γ(Ω,q)$, where $Ω$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix. We then derive several significant properties regarding the symmetry, connectivity and girth of $Γ(Ω,q)$. Our results demonstrate that the connected components of $\{Γ(Ω_{m,n},q)\}_{2\leq |m-n|\leq 3}$ form a novel family of graphs with large girth in the sense of Biggs.
Exact Integration of ReLU-type Neural Networks for Solving PDEs

Existence and nonexistence results for a mixed local--nonlocal operator with a Hardy potential

The resulting survival bounds contain the Turnbull estimator, lie inside the bounds from all completions of the data and need no enumeration. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.

Extensive simulations across various noise distributions confirm that the proposed methods outperform classical LS and LAD estimators in both robustness and accuracy, often matching oracle MLE performance.
On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field

Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $Σ$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.
Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
Sergey E. Stepanov; Irina I. Tsyganok

We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal diffeomorphism directions, and give explicit self-similar flows. The normalized Ricci-flow velocity is an admissible Chen-Nagano variation for n > = 3, and the smooth Poincar'e theorem admits an equivalent formulation in terms of the existence of harmonic critical metrics
Michel Benaïm; Leo Hahn; Oliver Tough

We develop a general framework to show the convergence in distribution of non-irreducible Markov processes to invariant distributions supported on lower-dimensional subsets of the state space. In applications, these singular supports signal the emergence of distinctive long-time behaviours, such as the extinction of species in ecology and the concentration on laminar states in fluid dynamics. The proposed approach is made widely applicable by tailoring its assumptions so that they can be verified using the theory of stochastic persistence/extinction. We illustrate the framework by applying it to stochastic perturbations of the Lorenz and Rosenzweig-MacArthur models and to a general two-dimensional Kolmogorov system.
On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics

We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.
Lower deviations for the maximum of a branching random walk in a random environment in time: quenched versus annealed

We study lower deviations of the rightmost position in a supercritical branching random walk whose offspring laws are independent and identically distributed across generations. Every particle has at least one child, and displacements have a fixed law with finite exponential moments of all orders. For thresholds strictly between the lower endpoint of the step law and the speed of the maximum, the quenched lower deviation probability has a finite positive exponential rate precisely when the negative logarithm of the probability of a single child is integrable. We identify the rate by a variational formula. If a positive fraction of generations rule out single children and displacements are bounded below, the probability decays doubly exponentially. We compute its double-exponential rate in terms of the minimum offspring numbers, the lower endpoint of the displacement law, and the speed of the maximum. After averaging over the environment, the negative logarithm of the probability is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the generation number whenever single children are possible with positive probability. We obtain the exact exponential rate when the offspring mean is constant and the offspring second moments are uniformly bounded. With displacements bounded below, mixed environments thus yield double-exponential quenched decay and single-exponential annealed decay.
Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
Ji-Ho Jung; Seung-Hyun Nam; Si-Hyeon Lee

Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement. We then demonstrate that a strict quantum advantage persists even when the pre-shared entanglement is restricted to a single qubit pair and each user communicates only one classical bit. Using EACC protocols based on the geometry of qubit measurements, we establish this advantage for both asymmetric and symmetric hypothesis testing and every input alphabet of size $v \geq 3$ in the high-privacy limit. The ratio of the achieved error exponent to the optimal one under the LDP constraint is at least $5/4$ for all such alphabets and approaches $3/2$ as $v$ grows. These results demonstrate that quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing can persist under simultaneous constraints on entanglement dimension and classical communication.
Conjugation-preserving polynomial and rational interpolation for limited-memory matrix-function actions

Approximating $f(A)b$ for a large nonsymmetric matrix can require substantial storage if a long Krylov basis is retained. We develop polynomial and rational interpolation schemes that use a fixed number of large recurrence vectors and preserve conjugation symmetry. Starting from a prescribed scalar approximation region, the schemes organize real nodes and complex-conjugate pairs into Newton-like bases with real interpolation coefficients. The polynomial and single-real-pole recurrences use real arithmetic in the matrix-action stage; the multi-pole construction also exploits conjugate pole pairs. A conjugation-preserving AAA procedure supplies interpolation data for the latter. We establish the interpolation and basis properties and compare the resulting realizations with Leja, Taylor, and Krylov methods on matrices from differential equations, model reduction, and networks. The experiments demonstrate arithmetic savings relative to complex-arithmetic counterparts and identify the influence of shifted solves and orthogonalization requirements. The methods are intended for memory-constrained computations in which useful approximation-region information is available.
Model and higher-order structure-preserving scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies
Shuyan Ren; Kun Wang; Nianyu Yi

In this paper, we study the model and higher-order structure-preserving numerical scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies. By using a new variational analysis method, we first rigidly derive the nonnegativity for two solutions of the chemotaxis equations. Then, utilizing the finite element method with mass-lumping in space and the BDF scheme with the positivity-preserving extrapolation to deal with the nonlinear terms in time, we propose a high-order fully discrete framework for the chemotaxis equations by combining with the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) shift and the Lagrange multiplier method, which preserves the mass conservation of the discrete system and the nonnegativity of two approximation solutions. Moreover, apart from confirming the existence and uniqueness of the nonlinear equation generated by the Lagrange multiplier method, by classifying its structure in detail, we prove that the secant iteration method for this nonlinear equation is locally convergent. Finally, we show some experiments to verify the theoretical prediction and efficiency of the proposed scheme, including consistent simulations of the growth of the colonies under different nutrient concentration and agar hardness.
Geometric realization of the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in a partially ramified case

We construct a new family of algebraic varieties over a finite field, realizing the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in their compactly supported étale cohomology. The resulting representations have $L$-parameters which are induced from characters of a partially ramified field extension.
Weak monotonicity, Critical exponents, and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities on weighted graphs
Patricia Alonso Ruiz; Fabrice Baudoin; Li Chen

We study weak monotonicity of heat kernel and ball averaged functionals on weighted graphs, and the associated critical exponents. Under sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates, weak Bakry-Émery estimates for the semigroup are proved, with explicit values of the Hölder regularity exponent in the strongly recurrent case. Applications of the theory include Gagliardo-Nirenberg, Sobolev, Nash and isoperimetric inequalities on strongly recurrent graphs and their products.
Kelvin-invariant positive solutions for critical elliptic systems with repulsive interaction

In this paper, we consider the following critical nonlinear elliptic system with repulsive interaction: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δu_1 = μ_1 u_1^3 - β(x) u_1 u_2^2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr -Δu_2 = μ_2 u_2^3 - β(x) u_1^2 u_2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr u_1, u_2 \in \mathcal{D}^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^4), & \end{array} \right. \] where $μ_1, μ_2 > 0$ and $β(x) \in C(\mathbb{R}^4,\mathbb{R})$ is a nonnegative function. Assuming that $β$ is invariant under the map $x \mapsto -\frac{x}{\vert{}x\vert{}^2}$, we establish the existence of positive solutions to $(\mathcal{P}_β)$ that are invariant under the Kelvin transform subject to suitable assumptions. This result provides a critical counterpart to the work of Sato [Y. Sato, Nonlinear Anal. 234 (2023), 113302], who established the existence of an even ground state for the corresponding subcritical problem. Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the obtained solutions as $\|β\|_\infty \to 0$.
Policy and Value Iteration for Entropy-Regularized Stochastic Control
Yuling Jiao; Peiying Wu; Jerry Zhijian Yang; Ruizhe Zhang; Tao Zhou

We study finite-horizon entropy-regularized stochastic control with action-independent diffusion. To solve the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, we alternate between value and policy updates. Each iteration approximately solves a linear backward equation for the current policy, then approximates the Gibbs distribution defined by the resulting value gradient. We prove a uniform bound on the final policy's excess regularized cost. The bound assigns explicit, summable weights to the evaluation residuals and the Kullback-Leibler divergences from the updated policies to their Gibbs targets. Under the stated assumptions and with exact terminal data, vanishing errors in both steps imply uniform convergence to the optimal value. Two finite-horizon execution problems test value accuracy against a known solution and closed-loop performance when no exact solution is available. We also evaluate the iteration on a discounted infinite-horizon routing problem with twelve modes and an unregularized HJB benchmark in up to 10,000 dimensions.
Fixed-level profiles and fluctuations in age-dependent recursive trees

How many vertices of a growing recursive tree lie at a prescribed distance from the root? We compare two linear attachment rules. When an arriving vertex chooses a parent with probability proportional to its label, each fixed level eventually stops growing. We determine the limiting covariance kernel and the probability that a level will change again after time $n$. Writing $L_\infty(h)$ for its final size, we show that $2^{-h}L_\infty(h)$ converges in mean square as $h$ tends to infinity to a random variable with mean $1$ and variance $1/3$. Consequently the limiting variance of the level size is asymptotic to $4^h/3$. When parents are chosen with probability proportional to their age, each fixed level grows. Its centered fluctuations have a joint Gaussian limit whose covariance constants come from repeated logarithmic integration of attachment noise at the root. An exact finite-size calculation illustrates the difference between the limiting and finite-size variances.
Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation

Milk production during lactation is dynamically regulated by milk removal, yet quantitative models linking feeding or pumping schedules to subsequent production remain scarce. We develop a minimal model describing milk accumulation and production between removal sessions, and the stimulation of subsequent production through milk removal. We compare different assumptions about how stimulation depends on the amount of milk removed or the duration of removal, and consider two removal protocols: prescribing either the removed amount or the removal duration. When stimulation depends on the removed amount, declining production can reduce subsequent stimulation and reinforce the decline. This leads to a critical wait interval beyond which no repeated constant schedule can sustain lactation. If stimulation is inefficient for small removal amounts but more efficient at intermediate amounts, the model can exhibit bistability: depending on the initial conditions, milk production either persists or ceases. In contrast, duration-dependent stimulation does not permit a zero-production state under continued removal, but can generate non-constant long-term dynamics under certain conditions. We further show that maximizing milk removal per session need not maximize daily output, because increased removal competes with session frequency. The framework provides a basis for testing alternative feedback hypotheses against longitudinal data and for optimizing feeding and pumping schedules.
Duality of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions via inclusions

We study actions of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras on a unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$. We first define the Rokhlin property and approximate representability directly for an action $H\curvearrowright A$ and characterize these properties, under appropriate hypotheses, in terms of the corresponding properties of the canonical conditional expectation $E\colon A\to A^H$. Based on this characterization, we establish the following duality for a saturated action on a simple unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$ such that $A\rtimes H$ is simple:
 1. $H\curvearrowright A$ has the Rokhlin property if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ is approximately representable.
 2. $H\curvearrowright A$ is approximately representable if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ has the Rokhlin property.
 For separable $A$, we also identify these properties with the corresponding spatial formulations introduced by Barlak--Szab{ó}--Voigt, assuming saturation in the Rokhlin comparison. We present examples of Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions both with and without the Rokhlin property.
Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers

We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the invariant subring. Building on these results, we construct perfectoid towers arising from rational double points in mixed characteristic. We identify their tilts with the perfect towers arising from rational double points in positive characteristic of the same ADE type.
Total Curvature and Topology of Complete Euclidean Immersions: Heat Kernel and Boundary Morse Approaches

Two mechanisms relate the scale-invariant integral of the second fundamental form to topology at infinity of a complete Euclidean immersion. The first retains the mean-curvature potential in the Michael--Simon Sobolev inequality, establishes an ultracontractive estimate for the semigroup generated by $Δ+|H|^2$, and uses a vector-bundle Cwikel--Lieb--Rozenblum bound to estimate spaces of $L^2$-harmonic forms. Together with the theory of nonparabolic ends, this yields $e(M)\le 1+C_n\int_M|A|^n$ for arbitrary complete immersed $n$-manifolds, $n\ge3$. The second method, under the additional assumption of finitely many single-sheeted $C^2$-asymptotically planar graphical ends, uses a boundary Morse complex and the normal Gauss-map area formula to prove $\sum_j b_j(M;\F)+e(M)-2\le\TA(F)$. It supplies an explicit end coefficient and bounds ordinary Betti numbers. We provide proofs of both mechanisms, identify the exact role of their respective hypotheses, and discuss minimal and Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian specializations.
Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting

Gaussian useful-gain and mean-interference approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We extend a source-side thermal energy harvesting model with Poisson interference and certify two-sided outage bounds. In a tested environment, the combined required signal-to-noise ratio error has opposite signs at 20 and 24 elements per user. Under another power convention, mean or moment-matched Gamma-distributed interference can predict false feasibility with exact useful gain. In the Gamma case, the Gaussian gain approximation can mask this false feasibility. Propagated Chernoff bounds give sufficient designs. Results concern the specified model and tested regimes.
Universal Work Extraction from Individual Sequences by Finite--State Information Engines

We consider information engines that interact with a heat bath at temperature $T$, a work reservoir, and a tape carrying an individual (deterministic) sequence $x$ over a finite alphabet $\X$. An engine is a cascade of autonomous ratchets with fixed energy levels and detailed--balance dynamics, each processing segments of $m$ tape cells and having finitely many internal states. We prove a converse bound on the extractable work in terms of the empirical block entropies of $x$,and show that it is achievable \emph{universally}, by engines whose energy levels do not depend on $x$. The maximal work per symbol is $kT[\ln|\X|-\bar H(x)]$, where $k$ is Boltzmann's constant and $\bar H(x)$ is the asymptotic normalized aligned block entropy of $x$, which equals its block Lempel--Ziv complexity, and the minimal work needed to erase $x$ is $kT\bar H(x)$ per symbol. Underlying these results is a two--way correspondence with universal coding: energy levels define a code, and a suitably operated cascade extracts $kT$ times $\ln|\X|$ per symbol minus the code length; conversely, a fluctuation identity shows that every engine fixed in advance defines a code. Hence, converses of universal coding apply verbatim to engines; e.g., the optimal redundancy of memoryless universal engines is given by the Shtarkov sum.
Necessary conditions for the boundedness of directional maximal operators

Given a set of directions $Ω$, we investigate whether the associated directional maximal operator $M\_Ω$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$, for $p>1$. One can associate to $Ω$ a numerical quantity called its \textit{Perron capacity}. If the latter is finite, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for $p \geq 1$. In this paper, we generalize a method introduced by D'Aniello, Gauvan and Moonens to compute the Perron capacity of oscillatory sets of directions such as \[ Ω\_{\mathrm{cos}} = \left \{\frac{\cos (n)}{n}\,: n \in \NN^*\right \}. \] In a second part, using geometric arguments, we show that if the Minkowski dimension of $Ω$ is positive, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for a small range of $p>1$.
The irreducibility of tame character varieties

Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.

We consider stationary Lotka--Volterra competition-diffusion systems with any number of species and positive, possibly asymmetric competition coefficients. We study two settings with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions: a one-dimensional interval with constant drift, and radial solutions on a ball. In each setting we first determine when a prescribed ordering of species admits a segregated profile. Starting from such a profile, we construct a positive solution for every sufficiently large competition parameter $β$. The uniform distance from the profile is of order $\varepsilon=β^{-1/3}$, and the rescaled densities converge near each interface to a two-species model. Counting the admissible orderings gives a lower bound on the number of positive solutions. We also prove a non-approximation result when one directed competition coefficient is zero and the other species are suppressed on the interval or shell used in the proof.
Structure Preserving Iterative Solution of Linear Systems Arising in Gauss Collocation for port-Hamiltonian DAEs
Malak Diab; Andreas Frommer; Karsten Kahl; Stefan Maier; Nicole Marheineke

This work presents structure-preserving computational techniques for the pencil Padé approximation arising in the numerical integration of port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic equations (pH-DAEs) via the Gauss-Legendre schemes. We first extend the concept of the diagonal Padé approximation and introduce a generalized framework characterizing the $s$-stage Gauss method. We further examine its structural properties and the role of the full orthogonalization method (FOM) in approximating the discrete solution. Building on this, we analyze the iterative approximation of the pencil Pade approximation and establish conditions on the search space in Petrov-Galerkin-type approximations which guarantee that structure-induced properties, such as dissipativity or energy preservation, are inherited by the Petrov-Galerkin approximations. In particular, we show that FOM-based Krylov subspace methods preserve these properties iterate-wise. The presented results provide a new insight into the interplay between Krylov subspace methods and energy preservation in the numerical integration of pH-DAEs. Finally, we conclude with numerical examples illustrating the convergence and the conservation of the physical properties.
Global existence of small data solutions to 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations, II

For the 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation $\square u+\fracμ{t}\partial_tu=|u|^p$, where $t\geq1$, $μ>0$ and $p>1$, it is conjectured that the small data solution $u$ exists globally when $p>p_s(3+μ)=\frac{μ+4+\sqrt{μ^2+16μ+32}}{2(μ+2)}$ for $0<μ\le \frac{14}{5}$, and when $p>p_f(3)=\frac{5}{3}$ for $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, where $p_s$ and $p_f$ denote the Strauss and Fujita exponents, respectively. In our previous paper [Li Qianqian, Yin Huicheng, Global existence of small data solutions to 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations. Preprint (2026), arXiv:2607.04575], for $p>\max\{\frac{5}{3},1+\frac{2}μ\}$ and $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, the global small solution $u$ was obtained. In this paper, we establish the global existence of $u$ for the remaining range of $\frac{5}{3}<p\leq1+\frac{2}μ$ and $μ\ge \frac{14}{5}$. Therefore, the above 3-D conjecture for $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$ is solved.
Scattering for the defocusing two-dimensional NLS with an Aharonov-Bohm magnetic potential
Luca Fanelli; Vladimir Georgiev; Sandra Lucente; Nicola Visciglia

We study the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in two dimensions in the presence of an Aharonov--Bohm magnetic potential with noninteger flux. Working with the Friedrichs realization of the magnetic Hamiltonian, we establish global well-posedness for initial data in the weighted magnetic energy space. For mass-critical and mass-supercritical nonlinearities, we prove convergence of the interaction representation in the same weighted space, while in the mass-subcritical range we obtain scattering in the magnetic energy space. The proof is based on a magnetic lens transformation, which converts the original equation into a nonlinear equation governed by the Aharonov--Bohm harmonic oscillator on a finite time interval. Existence is obtained through truncation, compactness, and energy estimates, whereas uniqueness follows directly from the dispersive decay of the confined linear flow. This approach avoids derivative Strichartz estimates, which are delicate in the presence of the singular magnetic field.
PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
Michael Ruofan Zeng; Junaid Hasan; Xuanyu Yang; Emily Xia Meng; Henry Kvinge

There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on them, uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns from these trained models, and uses these patterns to formulate conjectures. Once an initial conjecture has been formulated, PatternMiner instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using calls to mathematical software. If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.
On Shepp's property in free probability
Wiktor Ejsmont; Takahiro Hasebe; Patrycja Hęćka-Jędraszczyk

We establish a free analogue of Shepp's theorem for freely independent standard semicircular elements. We show more generally that a family of self-normalized squared quadratic forms is free, and each has a standard Marchenko-Pastur distribution. The free analogue of Shepp's theorem follows by taking the coefficients of quadratic forms to be the three Pauli matrices. We also prove some new free analogues of Lukacs-type independence results. The key part of the proof is a construction of an equivalent and simpler operator model on a corner algebra compressed by a free projection.
$99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point

When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.
Near Optimal Pure Stepsize Adaptation Acceleration for Gradient Descent on Nonconvex Optimization

Existing accelerated first-order methods for nonconvex optimization typically rely on momentum or extrapolation, requiring auxiliary vectors beyond the current iterate and gradient. On the other hand, memory-free stepsize scheduling alone can accelerate certain convex problems, while no guarantee exists for nonconvex problems. This paper closes this gap by proposing Nonconvex Adaptively Clipped Chebyshev (NACC) gradient descent method, which achieves near optimal acceleration while keeping the vanilla gradient descent update. NACC combines an adaptive selection of reversed fractal Chebyshev stepsizes with an epoch-wise clipping mechanism to control the aggressiveness of stepsizes. For nonconvex problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients and Hessians, we establish a near-optimal $\widetilde O(ε^{-7/4})$ complexity. If the problem is convex in addition, then, without modification, NACC automatically achieves an $\widetilde O(ε^{-3/4})$ accelerated complexity. Importantly, NACC guarantees the standard quadratic sufficient descent at every iteration, even when the stepsizes are substantially larger than the conventional choice. These monotonicity properties further facilitate practical implementations that adaptively adjust the estimated gradient and Hessian Lipschitz constants, demonstrating significant advantages in numerical tests against the existing nonconvex acceleration benchmarks.
Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO

We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $α\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,α,θ}$ is bounded from below by $d$.
Counting solutions to sparse systems of congruences

We obtain new bounds and asymptotic formulas for the number of solutions to sparse systems of $n$ diagonal congruences modulo an integer $q$ in $s$ variables. In a large range of parameters, our results improve and generalise those of A. A. Karatsuba (1976). In particular, our lower bound on $s$, which guarantees the solvability of such systems, depends only on $n$, rather than on specific degrees as in the work of A. A. Karatsuba (1976).
Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
Junda Ying; Xinyu Wang; Peijie Zhou; Lei Zhang

Reconstructing the continuous time dynamics of cell state evolution from sparse snapshot observations can be formulated as an unbalanced optimal transport problem. To study such dynamics at a coarse grained cell type level, unbalanced optimal transport must be extended to discrete state spaces. Inspired by discrete flow matching, we extended the dynamic Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) problem to discrete spaces, and derived a closed form for its solution. For particularly large state spaces or more general models, we proposed an unbalanced discrete flow matching as a numerical approximation method, which provides a Markovian reconstruction of the optimal WFR flow. Our discrete WFR framework also stays stable across different coarse grain resolution. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and applications to real biological data supported the plausibility of the reconstructed dynamics.
A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Turán-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs

For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.

We describe the subcoalgebras and subbialgebras of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$, which lead to the introduction of the spectrum of a bialgebra. We also study the particular cases double bialgebras (bialgebras equipped with two compatible coproducts), firstly examining their connection to unital near-semirings or near-rings. Introducing a subbialgebra of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ obtained from the intersection with another Sweedler dual, we prove it is the terminal object in the category of double bialgebras. As a consequence, we show that the spectrum of any double Hopf algebra is a subgroup of the group of roots of unity. This imply that not any bialgebra can become double. We finally apply this framework to a bialgebra of graphs with a coproduct given by contraction and deletion of edges, relating its invariants to Bergman colorations of edges arising from graphical matroids.
The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface

We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.
Random dyadic shift scattering: scale-uniform deformation stability and phase-aligned Hilbert multipliers

Petermichl's theorem represents the Hilbert transform by averaging a single dyadic shift over dilations and random dyadic lattices. We study how the deformation stability of the lattice-averaged shift, and of a parameter-free feature map $Φ$ built from it in the spirit of Mallat's wavelet scattering, depends on the number $J+1$ of scales. For the Haar generator as well as compactly supported $C^1$ orthonormal wavelets, the covariance error under a deformation $f\mapsto f(\cdot-τ(\cdot))$ is $O((J+1)
orm{τ'}_\infty
orm f)$ without a $
ormτ_\infty$ term, because lattice averaging absorbs the translation part of $τ$ exactly. The deformation defect splits into a first-order Calderón commutator, bounded uniformly in $J$ by the $T(1)$ theorem, and a second-order remainder. On a single lattice, affine warps and $C^{1,δ}$ generators give a lower bound $c\,σ_\eps\sqrt{J+1}-C\eps$ for the defect, with an explicit constant $σ_\eps\ge0$ computed to be positive for sym4 and db4 at three values of $\eps$. Averaging over lattices turns the defect into a Fourier-multiplier quadratic form, yielding $J$-uniform bounds both for affine warps, with a logarithmic loss in the Haar case, and for $C^2$ warps with $C^{1,δ}$ generators, and hence a scale-uniform Mallat-type stability estimate for $Φ$. With the standard child pair, the Hilbert component of the averaged shift nearly cancels for smooth Daubechies-type generators; re-indexing the children by integers restores this component. For Haar and general warps, numerical computations agree with a conjectured $J$-uniform bound.
Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension

Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required.
 In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.
Certifying a Sufficient Gaussian Dependence Regime for Learned Weighted FDR Control

Learning hypothesis weights from informative auxiliary data can improve the power of multiple testing. Even when the weights are learned independently of the tests, the validity of weighted Benjamini-Hochberg depends on their joint distribution. We use reference observations to certify a sufficient dependence condition for one-sided Gaussian tests. An intersection-union test of uncertain correlation signs determines whether to apply weighted Benjamini-Hochberg or a prespecified fallback at an adjusted level. Under conditional separation of certification and testing, the procedure controls the false discovery rate (FDR) for every Gaussian correlation matrix satisfying the stated sampling assumptions and weight constraints. We establish a boundary obstruction to uniform certification and matching minimax sample-size bounds for worst-case pair sets and the all-pairs problem. In the parameter ranges of the matching bounds, the minimax sample size grows logarithmically with the number of checked pairs and quadratically with the inverse of their positive margin. For homogeneous Gaussian observations with known marginal variances, residual contrasts from the testing subjects provide an independent source of certification scores. Simulations with up to 4,950 checked pairs, comparisons under a common subject budget, and Gaussian designs based on correlations estimated from the Healthy Brain Network illustrate the trade-off between certification and detection power.
Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite bubbles

Let $k\geq 6$, $λ\in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $k$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with $\mathrm{Ric}_h > λ$. In this paper, we construct, for each given $ε>0$, a sequence of $(k+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(X\times\mathbb{S}^2 ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_ε,d_ε) $ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} > λ$, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_ε) \leq ε$, and $X_ε$ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. In particular, the sequence of Riemannian manifolds we construct have uniformly bounded topology, which improves the earlier examples of Hupp-Naber-Wang and Zhou.
Parallel sums of nilpotent elements: exact realization and structured eigenvalue splitting

We prove that, over every infinite field and for $m\ge2$, the parallel sums $N(N+C)^{-1}C$ of nilpotent $m\times m$ inputs with invertible sum are exactly the matrices of nullity at least two. Every positive split of the target nullity between the input kernels is realizable. Over $\mathbb{C}$, we determine the paired derivative image and characterize universal full matrix cancellation at nonzero residues. For analytic input paths, nilpotence is required only at the base. An adjugate identity forces the last two characteristic coefficients to be $O(\varepsilon^2)$, yielding sharp bounds $O(|\varepsilon|^{2/3})$ at nonzero three-dimensional nilpotent residues and $O(|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)})$ at nilpotent residues for $m\ge4$. At every base with residue of type $[m-1,1]$, $m\ge4$, we prove a generic splitting law, also with fixed input sum. For $m\ge5$, it has $m-2$ roots on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)}$ and two on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/2}$, separating the largest-root and spectral-gap scales. A separate sharpness family keeps both inputs nilpotent and two roots zero. At the nonzero nilpotent three-dimensional boundary, a finite coefficient criterion computes the splitting orders for each exceptional affine fixed-sum direction. For each such path, the punctured spectral gap is at least $c|\varepsilon|^3$ near zero for some $c>0$, and the exponent is optimal over this class. Over a nonzero unital ring with $2$ invertible, we construct two $3\times3$ matrix inputs, each of nilpotency index exactly three, with invertible sum. In the complex unital Banach case, the residue has spectrum ${0}\cup\tfrac12σ(Q)$ for every coefficient $Q$. With the common core allowed to vary, a complex matrix is a finite-Drazin Hua output if and only if its nullity is not one.
Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
Qian Chen; Qiang Zhang; Dongxiao Zhao

We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.
Dirichlet eigenvalues of Laplacian with potential on general graphs and Weyl limits in integer lattice spaces $Z^d$

In this paper, we first establish the existence of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian with a vertex weight on an infinite, connected and locally finite graph, via building compact embeddings of suitable spaces, when the weight decays faster at infinity than the optimal Hardy weight. In the particular integer lattice space $Z^d$, we apply a segmentation technique to estimate the mean Riesz potential over the entire space, thereby deriving estimates for the eigenvalue counting function and establishing the Weyl limit of the eigenvalues.
Nested Spherical Designs of Optimal Order

Zheng and Zhuang [22] showed that a spherical $t_1$-design $Y$ with $|Y|=M\sim t_1^d$ points on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$ can be extended to a spherical $t$-design by adding points, with a total of order $t^{2d+1}$, and asked whether the optimal order $t^d$ is attainable. We keep their construction and improve the estimate of the pairing of the given points against polynomials of unit $L^1$-gradient norm. We prove that, if the given spherical $t_1$-design is upper regular at scale $t_1$ (in particular if it is well-separated; such a design exists by Bondarenko, Radchenko and Viazovska [6]), then for $d\ge2$, every $N\ge C(d,K)\,t^d$ suffices to admit a point set $X$ with $|X|=N$, for all $t_1<t$, such that the multiset union $X\uplus Y$ is a spherical $t$-design; in particular $|X\uplus Y|\le C(d,K)\,t^d$. The proof combines the design property, which removes the low frequencies exactly, with an $L^1$ Jackson-type estimate and a sampling inequality applied on dyadic frequency blocks. Upper regularity turns out to be automatic for nested spherical designs of optimal order; that is, every spherical $t_1$-design with $M\le C_M t_1^d$ points extends to a spherical $t$-design with $N+M\le C(d)\,C_M\,t^d$ (with $C_M\ge1$), uniformly in $t_1<t$, without any separation hypothesis. Some control of local multiplicity is necessary for an extension of optimal order. We also show that the estimate of the pairing functional cannot be improved within this method; that is, for every point set of at most $c\,t^d$ points it is at least of order $t^{d-1}$, and for upper regular designs it is of exactly this order. Finally, we treat finite chains of nested spherical designs, and on the circle we remove a logarithmic factor from the general estimate.
Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
Dimitris M. Manias; Ismaila Muhammed; Dimitris A. Goussis; Haralampos Hatzikirou

Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification. A sparse-regression surrogate of the vector field is reconstructed from the data, and its Jacobian, estimated with a matrix-free Krylov method, is analysed with Computational Singular Perturbation diagnostics. The resulting fast-slow partition guides the learning of explicit SIM algebraic representations through regression, and the reduced model follows by restricting the dynamics to it. For a linear stochastic system, this regression agrees with the Mori-Zwanzig projection at leading order in the timescale ratio. We demonstrate the validity of the framework on an illustrative linear system, the Michaelis-Menten model, a biofilm growth model, and a five-dimensional target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model. The method accurately identifies fast variables, reconstructs slow invariant manifolds, and generates accurate reduced models. Furthermore, we map the performance boundaries of the framework under sparse sampling and measurement noise, showing robust recovery for low-dimensional systems and highlighting data-requirement limits in higher dimensions. These results demonstrate that interpretable multiscale reduction can be achieved directly from time-series data, without requiring explicit prior knowledge of the underlying fast/slow timescale separation.
On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)

We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bièvre and Torrésani.
Chuang Xu; Yanrong Yang; Andrew T. A. Wood

Principal component analysis (PCA) optimizes aggregate reconstruction accuracy but may represent heterogeneous groups unevenly.
