We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups. Similarly, we apply our theory to interpolation categories of wreath products, finite general linear groups, and finite affine groups. Our main technique is an explicit construction of objects corresponding to coordinate algebras using the calculus of relations that Knop's categories are based on.

In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.
Regenerative range for planar random walks

We consider a centred random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which consumes resources originally present at every site. After consumption, each resource regenerates independently with probability $p$ at each step. We study the number of resources consumed up to time $n$, which is denoted $C_n$. Letting $p=p_n$ depend on $n$ and supposing that the walk moves faster than the resources regenerate, $i.e.$ $p_n=o(1)$, we establish a Law of Large Numbers and a Central Limit Theorem for $C_n$. In particular, we identify a phase transition between a so-called fast regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrow\infty$, where the fluctuations of $C_n$ are Gaussian, and a slow regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrowλ\in[0,\infty)$, where the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and described by a weighted renormalized self-intersection local time of planar Brownian motion depending on the parameter $λ$.

We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8π^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperkähler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.
Hölder continuity of Green functions for Markov sets

Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb C^N$. We prove that its Green function (and consequently, the Siciak extremal function) is Hölder continuous if and only if the first derivatives of polynomials satisfy Markov's inequality on $K$. The implication from Markov's inequality to Hölder continuity of the associated Green function settles a longstanding open problem at the intersection of approximation theory and pluripotential theory. A Markov bound $An^m$ in degree $n$ gives every Hölder exponent below $1/m$. In one complex variable it gives the exponent $1/m$ itself. The proof compares the extremal functions of two neighborhoods of $K$. For $N>1$ we use Hörmander's theorem on holomorphic extension from a point. For $N=1$ the comparison follows from the maximum principle.
A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression

For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.
Winning and losing NoGo is PSPACE-complete
Kyle Burke; Alfie Davies; Craig Tennenhouse

We resolve an open problem of Burke and Hearn and show that the combinatorial game NoGo is PSPACE-complete on grids. This is the usual geometry the game is played on, including at the tournament at a 2011 Banff workshop. In addition to this result, we show that it is also PSPACE-complete under misère play on grids. We prove both of these results using reductions from Bounded Two-Player Constraint Logic. Finally, we show that it is PSPACE-complete under normal play on connected bipartite subcubic graphs.

We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.
Low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with singular bilinear interactions
Rémi Buffe; Alessandro Duca; Tristan Robert

We consider the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) $i\dt ψ-\dx^2 ψ= (u(t)\cdot μ) ψ+κ|ψ|^{2m}ψ,$ on the torus under the presence of singular, time-dependent bilinear external fields $(u(t)\cdot μ)$. We prove well-posedness in $H^s(\T)$ for low regularity indices $s>\max\big\{\tfrac12-\tfrac1m,0\big\}$ ($s>0$ when $κ=0$), under sharp assumptions on the singular potentials, covering both the linear and nonlinear cases. We establish small-time exact controllability in $H^{\frac12+}(\T)$ for a large class of states, by combining saturation techniques with the moment method. The result extends previous bilinear exact controllability results for linear Schrödinger equations, which are typically obtained in large time and under high regularity assumptions. Crucial to our approach is the role of the singular time-dependent potentials, which enable the recovery of controllability properties in small time and at low regularity, overcoming obstructions present in the smooth setting.
Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting

We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.
Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters

For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $φ_π\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(π)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.
Forms and polynomial covers in many variables

Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \ge 2$, and let $σ$ be the affine dimension of the singular locus of $F = 0$. We prove that the hypersurface $F = 0$ satisfies the smooth Hasse principle whenever \[ n - σ\ge 2^{d + 1} - 3. \] This is the first improvement in the order of magnitude of Birch's classical result. We also apply the method to the counting problem for polynomial covers $F(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = g(y)$, and give a condition on $n - σ$ under which Serre's conjectural upper bound holds and another condition under which the expected asymptotic formula holds.
Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle

We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.
Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data

In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. We assume that the shear viscosity $μ$ is a positive constant, the bulk viscosity $λ(ρ)\ge0$ depends on the density, and the heat conductivity takes the form $κ(θ)=κ_0 θ^α$ with $κ_0>0$. For a broad class of density-dependent bulk viscosities, we establish the global existence and large-time behavior of strong solutions for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. In particular, our results include the sublinear growth law $$ λ(ρ)=\fracρ{(1+ρ)^\varepsilon \log\log(e^e+ρ)}, $$ where $\varepsilon>0$ is a sufficiently small constant depending only on the domain, the initial data, and the physical parameters.

Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of Rödl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollobás, Erdős and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<α<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has density at least \(1-α\). For triples this recovers the sharp bound of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. For \(k\ge4\), this improves their general exponent to the optimal value \(1/(k-1)\) and answers a 1990 question of Erdős for which he offered a \$500 prize.
An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories

We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.
Coverage of THz Networks in Presence of Blockages and Scattering
Kaushlendra Pandey; Aman Pandey; Afaq A. Lone; Harpreet S. Dhillon; Abhishek K. Gupta

In this paper, we develop an analytical framework to study a cellular THz network that incorporates the effects of blockages, scattering elements (SEs), directionality, atmospheric absorption and noise. We first characterize the power incident on each SE and the power scattered towards the users, while considering the presence of blockages. Modeling the SEs via a Poisson point process (PPP), we derive the Laplace transform (LT) of the sum interference caused by the SEs at the typical user. We also characterize the sum interference caused by the interfering base stations (BSs). Using this framework, we derive the coverage probability (CP), the mean signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR), the rate coverage (RC) and the area spectral efficiency (ASE) at the typical user, and we validate them against a Monte Carlo simulation that retains the correlation of the incident power across SEs. The analysis reduces the design of the network to a few quantities that follow from the system parameters. We also identify various densification regimes highlighting two critical or corner values of BS density and show that the shape of the coverage versus densification curve along with the optimal density value depends on these two critical densities. We identify a critical SE density, via equating the mean SE interference with the typical cell edge signal strength, which marks the deployments in which scattering must be accounted for. Below this density, the SE interference has a small effect on the coverage, whereas above it, the coverage falls steeply. We show that the critical density does not depend significantly on the BS density. Result shows that, in heavily cluttered deployments with significant number of SEs, their interference must be accounted for to get accurate results.
The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation

How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\toρ\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-ρ)/(2-ρ)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $ρ=1$.
Alba González; Tejas Mittal; Andrew Wood

We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.
Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs

We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-Kähler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally products of two $3$-Sasakian manifolds. We construct compact examples for which these local decompositions are not global. Finally, compact normalized hyper contact pairs have finite fundamental group and are finite quotients of products of compact $3$-Sasakian manifolds, in contrast with normalized hyper contact--symplectic pairs, which may have infinite fundamental group.
DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
Ahmed Ellithy; Vishnu Kakkat; Stephen McCormick

Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.
Sharp estimates for incremental moments of inverse subordinators and approximation errors for time-changed stochastic differential equations
Ivan Biočić; Sixian Jin; Kei Kobayashi

This paper establishes precise upper and lower bounds for the incremental moments of general inverse subordinators. Such processes are used as random time changes to model subdiffusive phenomena. The upper and lower bounds provide the foundation for a general framework for analyzing numerical approximation of time-changed stochastic differential equations on deterministic time grids. We derive an upper bound for the approximation error and further prove that the resulting order of convergence cannot be improved in general.
Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields

We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|Γ|'$ $Γ$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $ν_{Γ,n,U}$, where $Γ$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|Γ|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $Γ$. The $Γ$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_Γ(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-κr^2-ζr}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $κ>0$, and $ζ\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $Γ$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $Γ$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $Γ$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $Γ$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $Γ$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $Γ$ (with multiplicity one).
Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk

For an isometry-invariant reproducing kernel $k$ on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{D}^d$, we consider its composition factors, analytic selfmaps $ϕ:\mathbb{D}^d\to\mathbb{D}^d$ such that $k^ϕ=k/(k\circϕ)$ is a reproducing kernel. Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^ϕ)$, we define the rank of $ϕ$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^ϕ)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Martín, and Vukotić, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $ϕ$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $ϕ$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szegő kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.
The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers
Gendo Kumoi; Hideki Yagi; Manabu Kobayashi; Shigeichi Hirasawa

Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise. Recasting decoding as a test over a Gaussian channel, we derive an upper bound from the union and Chernoff bounds and a lower bound from the nearest competing category and the Mills ratio. The bounds show that a large Hamming distance is both necessary and sufficient for reducing the excess error rate. The excess error rate stays bounded away from zero, by a constant that depends on the two largest posteriors and the noise level but not on the number of categories $M$, whenever the distance between the code words of the two most probable categories is bounded; for equidistant codes this distance is $d_{\min}$. Conversely, it is at most $M-1$ times a factor that is exponentially small in the minimum distance $d_{\min}$, and it vanishes whenever $κ\,d_{\min}-\ln(M-1)\to\infty$ for an explicit $κ$ (for general codes, under a posterior condition). For $n$-vs-rest codes with $n\geq2$, the upper and lower exponents coincide asymptotically, which determines the reliability function of ECOC in closed form. The results extend to correlated Gaussian noise with the Hamming distance replaced by an effective distance; when noise is shared at the level of categories, the effective distance stays bounded and the excess error rate does not vanish for any code. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. In a semi-synthetic setting, the measured decay agrees with the predicted exponent. On ResNet-50 features of CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet-1k, the excess error over a log-likelihood decoding reference decreases with $d_{\min}$ and, for larger $M$, levels off at a moderate distance, while codes with $d_{\min}=1$ degrade as $M$ grows.
$S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
Peter Jipsen; Erkko Lehtonen; Reinhard Pöschel

We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.
An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces
Francisco Gonçalves; Tuomas Oikari; Troy Roberts

We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.
Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry
Christa Cuchiero; Paul Peter Hager; Julian Pachschwöll; Luca Pelizzari

We develop series representations for solutions to general nonlinear controlled and stochastic Volterra equations in terms of two new types of signature, called geometric and Itô Volterra signature. These signatures collect the necessary iterated kernel integrals and satisfy (quasi) shuffle identities, which allow us to prove universal approximation results for Volterra path functionals. We then derive finite order expansions with precise remainder terms for both controlled and stochastic Volterra equations with possibly singular kernels, as well as expansions of their expectations. For the latter, we provide sufficient conditions for absolute convergence of the resulting series representation and verify them for polynomial Volterra processes. As an application, we propose a weak approximation principle for stochastic Volterra equations based on matching low-order expected signature coordinates of the kernel. Numerical experiments for Volterra-Jacobi processes demonstrate promising performance.
Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem

For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Apéry sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.
When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes

Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods. In the noiseless setting, where the binary classifiers output the true posteriors, we ask on which code matrices each decoder always agrees with the Bayes-optimal (MAP) class. For the sum decoder the answer is known: the code must be equidistant (James and Hastie, 1998). We answer the question for the product decoder. Two classes are compared through the votes of the columns on which they differ: the sum decoder decides by their sample mean, the product decoder by an M-estimator with influence function artanh, and each vote is the MAP margin plus a bias determined by the other classes alone. Our main theorem states that the product decoder is MAP-consistent if and only if, for every class pair, the columns on which the two classes differ are matched with the columns obtained by swapping the two classes (or their complements), and equivalently if and only if the code is a union of n-vs-Rest codes. Efficient equidistant codes are therefore excluded: Hadamard codes ($M\ge 8$), which meet the Plotkin bound with $M-1$ columns, have no such pairs, and for the Sylvester type the reversal margin can be at least a constant 0.0182 independent of $M$. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. On six real datasets with estimated probabilities, the product decoder is slightly more accurate when each column is calibrated, and the sum decoder is better when the calibration error differs across columns; in either case the decoders disagree only near ties.
A unified approach to logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequalities and logarithmic Minkowski problems for geometric functionals
Yude Liu; Xinbao Lu; Qiang Sun

We establish two general principles for geometric functionals, one for proving logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities and the other for solving the associated logarithmic Minkowski problems. For origin-symmetric convex bodies, we prove logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, spectral zeta functions, torsional rigidity, and chord integrals, along with their equality conditions. For each functional, we give the necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an origin-symmetric solution to the corresponding logarithmic Minkowski problem for even measures and prove uniqueness.
The Poissonian limit of a model inspired by the one-dimensional ERAP, and its application to satellite data
Matteo D'Achille; Jessie Levillain; Pascal Moyal; Achim Schlather

We consider a model of particle tracking in one dimension studied by Quarck in which $n$ independent random points of the interval $[0,1]$ are shifted by i.i.d. noise at a common scale $\varepsilon_n>0$. We prove that, if $\varepsilon_n=αn^{-2}+\mathbf{o}(n^{-2})$ for some $α>0$ when $n\to \infty$, then in the latter limit the total number of consecutive swaps in the shifted sample w.r.t. its order statistics converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with a parameter depending explicitly on the product of $α$, the mean absolute difference of the shifts and the $L^2$-norm of the density of points. We compare the statistical criterion implied by this theorem to numerical simulations based on real terrain maps, and discuss both its usefulness and limitations.
Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration

We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.
Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion

We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.
Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
Margaret H. Regan; Frank Sottile; Simon Telen

The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.
Perfect powers with small exponents from products of terms in progression

Let $k$ be a large integer, and let $\ell$ be an integer with $2 \leq \ell \leq (\log \log k)^{1/5}$. We determine all solutions to the Diophantine equation \begin{align*} n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)=y^\ell \end{align*} in nonzero integers $n,d,y$ with $d\geq 1$ and $\text{gcd}(n,d)=1$. We also prove results for generalizations where the product $n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)$ is ``almost'' a perfect power, rather than exactly a perfect power, and where some of the terms $n+id$ are dropped from the product.
Bounded Nörlund operators on Hardy spaces

We characterize the nonnegative Nörlund matrices that induce bounded operators on Hardy spaces. For $a_n\ge0$ and $a_0>0$, boundedness on one $H^p$, $1<p<\infty$, is equivalent to boundedness on every such space and to a single quadratic testing condition involving the ratios of the partial sums $A_n=\sum_{k=0}^na_k$. The testing constant is comparable to the squared $H^2$ operator norm, with absolute constants. No doubling or monotonicity assumption on the weights is required. The proof combines an exact vector-valued Hankel representation with square-function estimates and a geometric argument showing that the doubling-time endpoints have finite lacunary order. Equivalently, boundedness is characterized by a truncated quadratic block condition on the coefficients of $G_a(z)=\sum_n(a_n/A_n)z^n$. Within the bounded family, $G_a$ belongs to the Bloch space if and only if it belongs to $BMOA$, and this occurs exactly when $(A_n)$ is doubling.
The local Weil explicit formula and related structures

We study the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces constructed from the local Weil quadratic form associated with the Riemann zeta function. Wherever this form is positive definite, we prove a local explicit formula expressing the Weil distribution in terms of the discrete spectra of self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator. We characterize the Riemann hypothesis by the uniform boundedness of the diagonal values of the reproducing kernels. We then study the chain of de Branges spaces and recover the Hamiltonian of the corresponding canonical system explicitly from these kernels under local positivity, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. Finally, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study the asymptotic behavior of solutions of this system.
On the first eigenvalue of the infinity Fractional Bilaplacian

We study the first eigenvalue of the infinity fractional bilaplacian under hinged and clamped exterior conditions. On bounded Lipschitz domains satisfying a uniform exterior ball condition, we establish existence of minimizers for both problems. In the hinged case, we prove uniqueness up to multiplication by a nonzero constant and identify the minimizers with the fractional torsion function. In the clamped case, an $L^p$-approximation yields a minimizer satisfying a limiting fractional PDE-system with measure data. We also prove a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the hinged eigenvalue, and use its explicit expression to obtain double sided estimates for the clamped eigenvalue on a ball.
Triangle-free planar graphs need not be POSH
We show that a triangle-free planar graph need not be partial one-sided Hamiltonian. This disproves a conjecture of Felsner, Schrezenmaier, Schröder and Steiner.
Large-time existence for the gravity water waves equations

We provide a new well-posedness result on the gravity water-waves equations, i.e. the free-surface, incompressible and irrotational Euler equations, in the absence of surface tension. Our main contribution is to provide the existence of solutions, in high enough but finite Sobolev regularity, on a timescale that grows like the inverse of the non-linearity parameter. Our result is also uniform in the shallow-water parameter. The main difficulty is that we allow for the presence of a large (though not emerging) bathymetry.
A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--Bénard convection

We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--Bénard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0<σ\leq1$ in the temperature equation. For every deterministic initial temperature, we prove that \[ \underline{Nu}-1 \geq c(σ^3 Ra)^{7/192}, \] provided that \[ σ^3 Ra \geq C(1+\log(1/σ))^{192/7}, \] where $c,C>0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional Itô process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.
On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers

We prove unconditionally that the first-order theory of Presburger arithmetic expanded by a predicate for the primes is undecidable. Bateman, Jockusch and Woods proved this in 1993 assuming Dickson's conjecture. We use the counter-machine framework of Karimov, Nieuwveld and Ouaknine and their idea of using `arbitrary permutations', and the number-theoretic input comes from Hildebrand and Maier's 1988 proof that the limit points of $k$ consecutive normalised prime gaps have positive measure. We use a discrete version, which they obtain before limits are taken. The key lemma is that although Hildebrand and Maier's result does not seem to give arbitrary permutations of consecutive prime gaps, it gives arbitrary permutations for the differences $p_i - q_i$ for two finite blocks of consecutive primes $p_0 < \cdots < p_k$ and $q_0 < \cdots < q_k$. Moreover, with the same key lemma, we show that Presburger arithmetic expanded with the function that maps $n$ to the $n$th prime defines multiplication.
Traversing hyperplane arrangements with an affine objective

We give geometric constructions of directed acyclic graphs on the chambers of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement. Fix a nonconstant affine objective. At each chamber where it is bounded above, a choice of flag based at the optimal face determines $2^r-1$ outgoing edges, where $r$ is the codimension of that face. The optimal value of the objective weakly increases on each step, but not always strictly. Nevertheless, we show that every infinite directed walk in these graphs eventually reaches a chamber where the optimal value exceeds its starting value. Additionally, we show that if an affine objective is bounded above on a closed face of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement, then the supremum is attained, and the optimizer set is again a closed face, generalizing the classical result for polyhedra.
Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
Sascha H. Hauck; Nis-Luca van Hülst; Matthias Kabel; Dieter Jaksch; Nicolas R. Gauger

Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-Bénard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

In Pascal's triangle, the boomerang identities, which were recently introduced, combine and extend the well-known hockey-stick identities of the binomial coefficients by allowing additional terms. We show that the binomial transform of sequences in a ring play a central role in this context. Subsequently, we show several applications to Bell and Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Appell polynomials, as well as, to harmonic, Fibonacci, Lucas, and Stirling numbers.
Curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary

Let $γ\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a closed, embedded, connected, oriented $C^1$ submanifold in $\mathbb R^n$ of dimension $m-1$ where $2\leq m<n$. We prove that the area of any immersed $m$-dimensional submanifold with oriented boundary $γ$ is bounded in terms of its curvature energy, unless $γ$ lies in an $m$-plane. The problems leads to a weak formulation involving oriented curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary, and we solve a boundary-value minimization problem with obstacle in this class.
Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata

We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Plücker divisors. For the full Plücker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the Möbius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.
The Universal Frame Characterization of C*-algebras

We prove that a C*-algebra A is a C*-algebra of compact operators if and only if every Hilbert A-module admits a frame. This answers affirmatively the question of Amini, Asadi, Elliott and Khosravi (2017), arising from the problem of Frank and Larson (2002)
A robust Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme for intrinsic shallow water equations with wetting-and-drying transitions on locally discontinuous beds
Eduardo Abreu; Elena Bachini; John Pérez; Mario Putti

In this work, we extend the Intrinsic Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume method for the Intrinsic Shallow Water Equations (ISWE) to account for localized topographic discontinuities that influence flow patterns. The ISWE formulation is modified to incorporate these bottom perturbations without altering the global structure of the system. The numerical discretization is based on a Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme within an intrinsic geometric framework and consists of a Lagrangian evolution step followed by an Eulerian remapping onto a fixed reference grid. The combination of the intrinsic nature of the ISWE formulation and the dual Lagrangian-Eulerian structure of the proposed discretization yields a numerical method that naturally satisfies the three key properties essential for stability, accuracy, and robustness: well-balancing for preservation of the lake-at-rest equilibrium over irregular bathymetry; wetting-and-drying, enabling robust tracking of moving fluid boundaries; and hyperbolicity guaranteeing consistency with the system wave propagation and stability constraints. Numerical experiments on curved two-dimensional surfaces with localized bottom discontinuities demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the method, including accurate long-time velocity computations in near-dry conditions and transitions between wet and dry states.
Online V-Learning with Adaptive Longitudinal Data

Reinforcement learning methods for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes are increasingly applied in mobile health (mHealth), where treatment decisions are made continually. Luckett et al. (2020) proposed V-learning, which estimates an optimal policy from offline trajectories. In practice, mHealth policies are updated online. Batch updating, in which the policy is re-estimated after each block of new data, is a tractable middle ground between offline learning and updating after every observation. However, because each batch's treatment policy is estimated from data pooled across patients in earlier batches, the resulting data are adaptively collected and patient trajectories are dependent, a setting that offline theory does not address. We develop statistical theory for V-learning in this setting with varying, deterministic batch sizes. For each fixed batch, as the number of patients grows, we establish uniform consistency of the estimated value function, consistency of the estimated policy, a functional central limit theorem over the policy class, asymptotic normality of the estimated value of the learned policy, and a consistent variance estimator. To first order, the online procedure performs as well as an oracle that deploys the optimal policy after the first batch. With the number of patients fixed and the number of batches growing, the estimated value function and policy remain consistent under a persistent identifiability condition. In simulations, as the number of patients grows with the number of batches fixed, confidence intervals attain near-nominal coverage under adaptive assignment and the online procedure closely matches the oracle. With a small cohort followed over many batches, the learned policies improve steadily.
On the phase-space geometry for Riemann solutions: rank-one structure, implicit solutions and elusive transitional shocks

The effective flux function reduces a Riemann problem for a $2\times 2$ system of conservation laws to a scalar one, by lifting the wave curve. We show that the reduction rests on a rank-one property, namely that the Jacobian $\partial(u,\,v)/\partial(x,\,t)$ equals the product of the two wave strengths, up to nonzero factors, and vanishes identically for every self-similar solution. Hence the lifting needs no hypothesis for Riemann data, and for Cauchy data it survives exactly on an integral curve of an eigenvector field, where we give an implicit solution; off that curve the state path leaves it at a rate we compute. We then ask when an implicit closed-form solution exists for arbitrary data. For homogeneous quadratic fluxes these are precisely the systems linearly equivalent to two decoupled Burgers equations (the curve $a=1+b^2$ of the Schaeffer--Shearer normal form). Every such system loses strict hyperbolicity along a full line, so no model with an isolated umbilic point qualifies, among them the quadratic Corey model of three-phase flow. We close with a quadratic model in which a datum on a straight integral curve gives an exact solution with a stationary transitional shock, having one family nearly linearly degenerate at each end.
Efficient inferential models and their fiducial connections

Valid inferential models (IMs) provide frequentist calibration guarantees, but validity alone does not determine which construction is most informative. We study finite-sample efficiency through concentration risk, the expected volume under a possibility contour. For a smooth, fully identified association and a specified parameter-volume measure, a weighted Neyman--Pearson argument identifies the generalized fiducial density as the optimal score for minimizing cut volume subject to fixed-data auxiliary compatibility. The resulting maximum-specificity transform gives an explicit volume interpretation of the fiducial efficiency ceiling, which need not itself be sampling valid. We develop two approaches to valid construction. The first minimizes design-averaged concentration risk among single, data-independent auxiliary-compatible contours. The design measure prioritizes efficiency without requiring prior beliefs or restricting validity. The second localizes the parameter-volume score to candidate-specific contours, yielding a normalized, valid IM equivalent to sampling validification of the relative fiducial likelihood. A parallel sample-space construction recovers the ordinary likelihood-ratio IM; direct validification of the ceiling provides another repair. For the same association, exact, data-independent predictive contours share a common fiducial distribution as a saturating inner probability, while generating different calibrated confidence-region geometries. Design averaging thus selects an efficient member without changing the underlying fiducial law. Examples in a two-component measurement model and an exponential scale model illustrate the efficiency gains and show that sampling-valid repair can improve on the raw ceiling by leaving the fixed-data auxiliary-compatible class over which it is optimal.
Higher-Order Moments of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials

Stochastic Galerkin methods reformulate a differential equation with uncertain parameters as a deterministic surrogate system by writing the solution as a series of polynomial basis functionals and projecting onto the parameter space. Given correlated Gaussian parameters, Rahman (2017) established solution convergence when the basis functionals are multivariate Hermite polynomials (MHPs), which is the setting considered here. Each term of the original equation contributes coefficients to the surrogate system, which we call the $N$th moments, that are expectations of products of the basis polynomials. Since the parameters are dependent, the $N$th moments do not factor into one-dimensional expectations via tensorization as they do in the independent case; consequently, their values are typically determined numerically at a nontrivial and compounding cost. Namely, the number of $N$th moments that emerge grows combinatorially with parameter dimension and truncation order. In this paper, we first relate MHPs and slowly growing functions --- which are smooth functions whose derivatives of all orders grow at most polynomially --- in correlated Gaussian parameters. In doing so, we derive an expression for the $N$th moment of an MHPs in terms of $(N-1)$th moments that can be evaluated exactly, along with sufficient conditions for the $N$th moment to vanish. Numerical examples illustrate the benefit of evaluating such moments directly without numerical approximation and confirm that formula-predicted values match sampling-based estimates.
An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
Ruggero Carli; Andrea Carron; Luca Schenato; Marco Todescato

In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.
From hockey stick to boomerang via Appell polynomials

In Pascal's triangle, the hockey-stick identities are well known as certain sums over the binomial coefficients, e.g., lying in a fixed row or column of the triangle. We establish unified identities that are connected with Appell polynomials, from which the hockey-stick identities follow as a very special case. Subsequently, we derive several identities for (reciprocal) Appell polynomials yielding applications to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials. As a result, we obtain new identities for the Bernoulli, Euler, Fibonacci, and Genocchi numbers, as well as, power sums. This also leads to infinitely many recurrence relations for these numbers.

Very recently, Bóna introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials. We also show the strong q-log-convexity of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials and the asymptotic normality of the Boolean-Narayana numbers. A bijection between 0-1-trees and colored Motzkin paths is constructed, presenting an alternative interpretation of the Boolean-Narayana numbers.
The Kelvin--Hicks Formula from the Energy--Casimir Principle

The classical Kelvin--Hicks formula expresses the propagation speed of a thin vortex ring in an incompressible ideal fluid in terms of its circulation, distance from the symmetry axis, and core radius. In this paper, we rigorously derive this formula from a variational principle based on Arnold's energy--Casimir method, without prescribing any of these geometric or physical quantities a priori. We introduce a scale-invariant variational principle involving the energy, impulse, and $L^p$ Casimir invariants. For $1 < p < \infty$, we construct orbitally stable energy-maximizing vortex rings and investigate how their geometry depends on the Casimir exponent $p$. For sufficiently large $p$, the vortex rings have cores homeomorphic to a ball and converge to Hill's spherical vortex as $p \to \infty$. In contrast, as $p\to1^+$, the energy-maximizing vortex rings concentrate onto a circular filament of radius $e^{1/3}$, uniquely selected by the variational principle. After suitable translations and rescalings, their vortex-core profiles converge to an optimizer of the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Introducing an effective core radius $ε_p$ determined by the entropy of the vorticity distribution, we establish the Kelvin--Hicks formula \begin{align*} W_p = \frac{Γ_p}{4πR_p} \left(\log\frac{8R_p}{ε_p}-1+o(1)\right) \quad \textrm{as}\ p\to1^+, \end{align*} where $W_p$, $Γ_p$, and $R_p$ denote the propagation speed, circulation, and effective ring radius, respectively. In particular, the constant correction $-1$ is obtained for nonuniform vortex-core profiles without imposing any prescribed core structure.

CholeskyQR is an orthogonalization algorithm particularly well suited to modern computing architectures, but it may fail to produce numerically orthonormal columns when applied to ill-conditioned matrices. A customary solution is to first reduce the condition number of the input matrix by means of a preconditioner, and then apply CholeskyQR to the preconditioned matrix. We propose three mixed-precision techniques for constructing such preconditioners: mpSCQR, based on a shifted Cholesky factorization; mpEVDQR, based on the eigendecomposition; and mpLUCQR, based on a pivoted LU factorization. We prove bounds on the condition number of the matrix after mpSCQR, mpLUCQR, or a shifted variant of mpEVDQR has been applied. Our experiments compare the proposed preconditioners with existing deterministic and randomized alternatives. The results suggest that mpEVDQR and mpLUCQR can be substantially faster than traditional shiftedCholeskyQR, with mpLUCQR attaining performance comparable to that of the most efficient randomized preconditioners.
Sharp Casorati Inequalities for Pointwise Bi-Slant Riemannian Maps into Sasakian Space Forms

We establish Casorati inequalities for pointwise bi-slant Riemannian maps into Sasakian space forms with the characteristic vector field tangent to the range. The Sasakian structure imposes specific conditions on the second fundamental form, leading to refined inequalities for the normalized horizontal scalar curvature that also account for O'Neill's tensor. For proper pointwise bi-slant maps, equality in the two principal inequalities is characterized by the vanishing of the second fundamental form on the orthogonal complement of the characteristic direction in the range. We also derive corresponding inequalities for pointwise semi-slant, hemi-slant, and slant Riemannian maps and construct examples attaining equality.
Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
Changbo Chen; Bo Huang; Valery Romanovski; Linpeng Wang

This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gröbner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition with branch-wise triangular solving, thereby efficiently deriving necessary and sufficient conditions with enhanced computational flexibility and rectifying subtle classification errors in a class of Liénard systems. For Hopf bifurcations, extending prior work on necessary conditions [SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 34 (1997)] and sufficient conditions [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 182 (1994); J. Symbolic Comput. 30 (2000)], we establish a complete algebraic characterization via two equivalent formulations: one using Hurwitz determinants and subresultant sequences, and another derived from the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the real and imaginary parts of the characteristic polynomial. From the GCD formulation, we obtain a novel and, for the first time, complete semi-algebraic description of the transversality condition, yielding a decision procedure via triangular decomposition of semi-algebraic systems and heuristic real quantifier elimination. Our approach resolves cases beyond the reach of state-of-the-art polynomial-based methods, and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of our frameworks.
On Waring's problem for fourth powers

We prove that every sufficiently large integer $n$, satisfying $n\equiv 1,2,3,\dots,11\pmod*{16}$, can be written as a sum of $11$ biquadrates. In particular, $G^{\#}(4)\leq 11$. This improves upon $G^{\#}(4)\leq 12$ due to Vaughan in 1989.
A Dimension-Free Bound on the FDR of the Benjamini-Hochberg Procedure under Slowly Decaying Gaussian Correlations

The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure is proven to control the false discovery rate under independence and under positive dependence. Under arbitrary dependence, however, its guarantee deteriorates by a factor that grows logarithmically with the number of hypotheses. For Gaussian test statistics, it is unknown whether dependence can make the false discovery rate grow with the number of tests. We study this question when the correlation between two test statistics decays with the distance between their indices. We seek guarantees that hold uniformly over a wide class of correlation structures and over all configurations of the signals. We show that if the correlations decay at least as fast as a power of the inverse logarithm of the distance with exponent larger than one, then the false discovery rate of the original BH procedure is bounded by the nominal level times a factor that does not depend on the number of hypotheses. This factor grows only polylogarithmically as the level decreases. The result holds for both one- and two-sided tests, and the procedure uses no knowledge of the correlations. The class allows correlations of both signs. The required decay can be arbitrarily close to the inverse logarithm. The key technical tool is a truncated Hermite expansion of the exceedance indicators. It shows that their main fluctuations are common to all thresholds that BH may use. These fluctuations can be well controlled, while the remainder is too small to accumulate, which leads to a bound that does not inflate with the dimension.
Discretely self-similar solutions to coupled fluid systems with locally $L^2$ data

In this paper we present a systematic way to construct discretely self-similar solutions of fluid systems, including the viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics equations, the viscoelastic Navier-Stokes equations with damping, and the Oberbeck-Boussinesq system, for locally $L^2$ initial data which are not necessarily in the uniformly local $L^2$ space. The solutions satisfy local energy inequalities, local a priori bounds depending only on the $L^2$ norm of the initial data in a fixed ball (and, for the Oberbeck--Boussinesq system, on the force), and a limiting formula for the pressure.
An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups

By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.
Shared information governs multi-view planted matching

We study when the rows of $K$ shuffled views of the same $n$ objects can be matched, where each object is observed once in every view through a Gaussian feature vector with known covariance. For every fixed $K$, all views can be matched up to $o(n)$ errors if the shared information $J$ of one object's $K$ observations exceeds $(1+ε)\log n$, and not if it is below $(1-ε)\log n$; this can hold although no two views can be matched on their own. Below the threshold, two views can still be matched if some set of views containing both has shared information above $\log n$; otherwise every estimator, even one that reads all views, has vanishing overlap between them. Matching every row is governed by the weakest bipartition of the views: with weak correlations the threshold is $2\log n$ for the mutual information across it. For a weak common signal observed through independent noise, the two thresholds are $4/K$ and $4/(K-1)$ in units of $\sum_\ellρ_\ell^2/\log n$, which answers a question of Wee, Yang, Fan and Mao. Beyond weak correlations the bipartition condition is not sufficient: rare subpopulations impose a Rényi condition for every partition into at least three blocks. We conjecture that the two conditions together characterize exact recovery for Gaussian laws, and prove this for three views with equal correlations and in several further cases, in part with computer assistance. With equal correlations, layered screening attains $4/K$ for $K=3,4$ in $O(Kn^2d)$ operations, and for general laws a recursive decoder attains $J$. The almost-exact thresholds extend to known product laws and to objects observed in random subsets of the views.
Global regularities for the Dirichlet problem of Monge-Ampère type equations
Feida Jiang; Jiakun Liu; Jian Lu; Chuanlong Sun

We establish global a priori $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ estimates for elliptic solutions of the Dirichlet problem for cost-generated Monge-Ampère type equations under the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang condition A3w, assuming continuous and Hölder continuous right-hand sides, respectively.
Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
Niels Martin Møller; Andreas Savas-Halilaj; Knut Smoczyk

In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $π$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $π$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.
The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks

$K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.

Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.
Matthieu Fradelizi; Auttawich Manui; Mark Meyer; Maud Szusterman; Artem Zvavitch

It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.
Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties

We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.
An intrinsic kinematic wave model with conservative fluxes for overland flow on curved terrain

Kinematic wave models, the simplest surface flow models, route overland flow by gravity alone and there is no pressure or inertial term to redistribute flow when the resulting velocities misroute it. Computed from piecewise-linear elevation data, this velocity jumps across the edges of the mesh: two neighboring cells can push water into each other, and the scheme can hold water in ponds that the terrain does not contain, or concentrate it where the data do not. We formulate the model intrinsically on the bed surface, with the depth normal to the bed as unknown, and obtain a single-valued edge velocity, in the unique edge frame of the intrinsic geometry, by correcting the raw cell field with the star-based conservative flux of Larson and Niklasson. Because the field is derived from data rather than from a Galerkin solution, the local problems are solvable only with a compatible load, the weak discrete divergence of the field being corrected, which for the slope is a discrete mean curvature of the terrain. With a Neumann boundary, every element is conservative, and the corrected field reproduces the cell average of the nodal divergence of the raw field, plus the divergence resolved inside the curved cells. Since any single-valued flux conserves mass, the correction is about consistency and robustness: the steady state of the upwind scheme solves an M-matrix system exactly when every cell drains to an outlet, and spurious ponds are closed classes of a transfer directed graph, computable before any simulation. Four rainfall tests, from a plane to a real catchment, are designed to verify the difference in storage and timing between the intrinsic and the classical form, the effect of the mesh on the consistency of the edge velocity, the robustness at a degenerate stationary point, and the application to terrain data.
A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
Romain Bourneuf; Pierre Charbit; Samuel Coulomb; Stéphan Thomassé

We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.
Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings

We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.
Finite-time blowup in the inviscid GOY and Sabra models

For the inviscid GOY and Sabra shell models with zero boundary conditions at the lowest shells, we construct strong solutions with finitely supported initial data whose vorticity amplitudes blow up in the supremum norm in finite time, at the self-similar rate $(T-t)^{-1}$. The blowup is stable under small perturbations of the initial data in the same norm, including complex-valued ones. Guided by the work of Mailybaev, we use a travelling wave of the renormalized equations to obtain blowup in the original variables. We construct such a wave for the equations extended to all integer shells, decaying in both directions. We then show that the dynamics near this wave contract once the directions generated by time-translation and phase symmetries are removed by adjusting the symmetry parameters at each step (a modulation argument). This yields blowup solutions on the positive shells satisfying the original boundary conditions. Computer-assisted interval arithmetic is used to establish the existence of the travelling wave and the contraction estimate needed for the modulation argument.

Using the Riemann hypothesis for the nonprincipal character modulo four, we disprove Fujii's first conjecture on exponential weights and prove his second conjecture on iterated weights by Mellin convolution [Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A Math. Sci. 64 (1988), 260--263]. Further, we unify the two conjectures through a two-parameter family of Mellin kernels and prove that the prime race exhibits a phase transition.

We study the hyperbolic $p$-barycenters $C_p$, $0\le p\le\infty$, of $n$ points $α_1,\ldots,α_n$ in the hyperbolic plane. For $0<p<\infty$, $C_p$ minimizes the sum of the $p$th powers of the hyperbolic cosines of the distances to the points. At the endpoints, $C_0$ minimizes the product of these cosines and $C_\infty$ their maximum. The center map $p\mapsto C_p$ is real analytic at every finite parameter. A point $P$ is the center for every parameter exactly when, at each positive distance from $P$, the unit directions to the points at that distance sum to zero. If the map is nonconstant, the equation $C_p=P$ has at most $n-2$ solutions in $[0,\infty]$ for each $P$, and at most $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ when the points lie on a geodesic. Finite solutions are counted with multiplicity, and the endpoint contributes one if $C_\infty=P$. Each bound is attained in arbitrarily small disks, with prescribed finite parameters and multiplicities, and with or without the endpoint. The proofs use exponential sums over distance shells, a variation-diminishing property of the radial-weight kernel, and the Hobby--Rice theorem. For the upper-half-plane roots of a totally complex real binary form, $C_0$ is Julia's zero and $C_1$ is the hyperbolic zero. Their coincidence forces the center map to be constant in degrees at most six, but counterexamples exist in every even degree at least eight. We obtain the same bounds on the number of distinct parameters for Riemannian $L^q$ centers, the minimizers of $\sum_i d(P,α_i)^q$ on Hadamard manifolds for $1<q<\infty$.
Cenk Aydin; Giovanni Caiolo; Chiara Giardino; Mara Gruß; Mikael Häglund; Elena Hoster; Christian Stump

The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.
