The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties. First, we give two sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of the eccentricity matrix of a connected graph, which generalize some previously known results. Then, we show that the eccentricity matrix of every unicyclic graph of girth $3$, $5$ or $7$ is irreducible and provide a unicyclic graph whose eccentricity matrix is reducible for every odd girth $g\ge 9$. On the other hand, we also provide a class of unicyclic graphs of odd girth, whose eccentricity matrices are always irreducible. Additionally, we find the inertia of eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs in which the trees attached to the cycle are nontrivial and have equal heights. Moreover, we characterize the graphs in this class whose E-eigenvalues are symmetric about the origin. Finally, we obtain necessary conditions for the invertibility of the eccentricity matrix of a unicyclic graph.
Alessandro Zuccotti; Cedric Münger; Chien V. Le; Paul Olyslager; Kristof Cools

Among the integral equations for scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects, single-source integral equations (SSIEs) provide the advantage of having only a single electric or magnetic current unknown. A well-conditioned SSIE can be obtained by appropriately combining the interior and exterior Calderón formulas. The condition number of the resulting operator appearing in the well-conditioned SSIE remains bounded at low frequencies. However, SSIEs still suffer from low-frequency cancellation, causing loss of significant digits in the solution, the right-hand side, and the system matrix. In this work, we apply a rescaling strategy based on quasi-Helmholtz projectors to the well-conditioned SSIE. Primal and dual space projectors are required since both primal and dual spaces are used to discretize the SSIE operators. We show that the solution of the rescaled SSIE is immune to catastrophic cancellations at low frequencies. Numerical experiments corroborate the method by testing the accuracy of the radiated field for extremely low frequencies.
On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
James Cruickshank; Csaba Király; Bernd Schulze; Shin-ichi Tanigawa

Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jordán and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.
A Proof of the Balister-Győri-Schelp Conjecture on Perfect Matchings with Prescribed Differences

We prove the conjecture of Balister, Győri and Schelp on perfect matchings with prescribed differences. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $d_1,\dots,d_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with repetitions allowed. The space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ can be partitioned into pairs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ with $x_i+y_i=d_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_i d_i=0$.
Aerodynamic Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres in Very Low Earth Orbit: Exploiting Lift for Short Warning Times and Reduced Orbital Decay
Paul J. Haufe; Fabrizio Turco; Friedrich Tuttas; Zeno Pavanello; Stefanos Fasoulas; Roberto Armellin

Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO, below $450\,\mathrm{km}$ altitude) offer promising mission capabilities for future spacecraft, but increasing traffic and the presence of orbital debris create collision risks that pose a particular challenge for satellites without conventional propulsion. Aerodynamic drag, resulting from interaction with the residual atmosphere, has been shown effective for performing collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs). However, short warning times remain challenging, and current methods do not exploit aerodynamic lift forces that enable out-of-track manoeuvres, which could help enhance control authority and mitigate drag-induced orbital decay. This work addresses both gaps by developing and evaluating two complementary optimisation methods: a heuristic approach using reachable set analysis to determine minimum lead times, and a direct shooting method to limit the increase in orbital decay due to the manoeuvre. Analyses using data derived from real conjunctions show that achieving a sufficient reduction in collision risk in the considered scenarios is feasible with lead times lower than one orbital period. Results also show that lift-based manoeuvres outperform drag-only approaches, with modest lead time reductions and more pronounced benefits in limiting orbital decay. Performance sensitivity to variations in control authority due to the type of gas-surface-interaction, altitude, and the encounter geometry is characterised. The methods and results presented highlight the potential of aerodynamic CAM for short warning time scenarios, contributing to sustainable operations in the increasingly congested VLEO environment.

Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $ω\in Ω_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

Under the Riemann hypothesis and the linear independence hypothesis, the set of such $x$ has the same logarithmic density as the set on which $π(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.

The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.

This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We prove that a decomposition exists if and only if all such equivalence classes have the same cardinality, and we explicitly construct the coordinate transformation together with the matrices of the observable and unobservable subsystems. The observable subsystem is shown to be the quotient graph obtained by contracting each class into a single vertex. These results are further generalized to BCNs, for which an algorithm and an illustrative example are provided.

Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We consider the heat-diffusion semigroup related to expansions with respect to an orthogonal system emerging by taking arbitrary finite tensor products of classical Hermite, Laguerre and Jacobi polynomials. Tang, Adaptive mesh methods for hyperbolic conservation laws with bound-preserving flux limiters, arXiv:2602.12580] to two dimensions within the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework. Full-wave simulation of three-dimensional time-harmonic Maxwell problems over hundreds of wavelengths leads to indefinite systems with tens to hundreds of billions of unknowns. We present a matrix-free three-grid solver for such systems and its implementation on GPUs and CPUs. The solver is built on an interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization on the Yee grid, whose compact face and edge filters keep the phase error small at 6 points per wavelength, and it applies the same compact stencil on all three grids: an unshifted intermediate-grid correction is preconditioned by a complex-shifted auxiliary cycle, so that one preconditioner application performs a fixed number of stencil sweeps and reductions with storage linear in the number of unknowns. The socle of the last term in a minimal injective resolution II

Let $R$ be a Gorenstein ring with left and right self-injective dimensions $n$. We prove that the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $_RR$ has an essential socle. It answers an open question of Iwanaga and Sato. As a consequence, we get that for any left $R$-module $M$ with injective dimension $n$, the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $M$ also has an essential socle.
Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks

The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. An adaptive finite element method for the interior problem of Helmholtz equations with generalized transmission boundary conditions
Zhe Zhu; Lei Lin; Wei Yang; Tao Yin

This paper proposes a new adaptive finite element method for solving the interior transmission problem with generalized transmission boundary conditions (GTBCs) involving a surface Laplace-Beltrami operator. A $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity technique relying on a lifting operator is established to show the well-posedness of the variational problem in appropriate nonstandard Sobolev spaces. Then both the a priori error estimates and a posteriori error estimates including the upper bound and local lower bound of the finite element discretization are constructed. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the adaptive finite element method. Extension and high efficiency of the proposed method for the computation of the interior transmission eigenvalues for the problem with GTBCs are also discussed numerically.
Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems

We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $Λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter black holes. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $π_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.
Hardy and BMO spaces for the Laplacian with drift

We study Hardy and BMO spaces associated with the Laplacian with drift. We define an atomic Hardy space $H^1$ whose atoms satisfy cancellation against constants and linear functions in directions perpendicular to the drift. We prove the John--Nirenberg inequality, Hardy--BMO duality, equivalence of finite and infinite atomic norms, and interpolation theorems. We show that the Riesz transforms and their adjoints are bounded from $H^1$ to $L^1$ and from $L^\infty$ to BMO. Moreover, we prove that the cancellation conditions are optimal, but the Riesz transforms do not characterize $H^1$. We also characterize the $L^p$ boundedness of their commutators, $1<p<\infty$, in terms of local BMO.

We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

We provide a complete classification, in a \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, of all hydrodynamic states and external forces for which a local equilibrium distribution constitutes an exact solution to the Boltzmann kinetic equation. We demonstrate that the temperature \(T\) must be spatially uniform, that the velocity field is the sum of a rigid translation, a radial expansion or compression, and a rigid rotation, and that the external acceleration must be conservative, though time-dependent within a reference frame that translates and rotates along with the fluid. The density profile is then determined by the external potential, while its temporal dependence is governed by any temperature function \(T(t)\) that can be generated through an appropriate adjustment of the external acceleration. We recover the classic ``harmonic breather'' and obtain solutions involving static forces that exhibit algebraic cooling, similar to Haff's law, despite the occurrence of elastic collisions. Our classification identifies the exceptional circumstances under which local equilibrium is exact and provides rigorous criteria for evaluating kinetic and hydrodynamic approximations.
A sharp form of Welsh's log-concavity inequality for chromatic polynomials

Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge 1$, and let $P_G(x)$ be its chromatic polynomial. In the early 1970s, Welsh conjectured that $P_G(k)^2 \ge P_G(k-1)P_G(k+1)$ holds for any positive integer $k$. This conjecture was also independently proposed by Brenti in 1992, while in 1997, Seymour disproved it for $k=6$ by constructing an infinite family of graphs of sufficiently large order as counterexamples. In 2005, Dong, Koh and Teo conjectured that $P_G(x)^2 \ge P_G(x-1)P_G(x+1)$ holds for all real $x\ge n$. In this paper, we prove that the inequality holds for all real $x\ge n-1$. Equality holds if and only if $n\ge 2$, $G$ is complete, and $x=n-1$. Moreover, the bound $x\ge n-1$ is best possible for every $n\ge 2$.

For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $π\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections. A positive algebraic kernel and an explicitly solved variational problem give the pressure with logarithmic error $O(n^{2/3}\log^{2/3}n)$. This determines the total exponential growth, the location of every mode, a full large-deviation principle, and limiting structural densities. At activity $z=t/n$ with fixed $t>0$, we also prove a $\operatorname{Poisson}(19t/4)$ limit and coefficient asymptotics uniform for defects $q=o(n^{1/3})$.

Solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations over finite fields is a central problem in algebraic cryptanalysis, commonly approached using Gröbner basis algorithms. The complexity of Gröbner basis computation depends on the algorithm employed and is governed by the solving degree, defined as the maximum degree of the polynomials processed during the computation. Estimating this quantity is therefore crucial, and several bounds in terms of the degree of regularity have been established in the literature. In this work, we investigate the effect of Buchberger's criteria on the elimination of redundant pairs, and prove that the solving degree of a Gröbner basis algorithm combining linear algebra with Buchberger's original algorithm is bounded above by the degree of regularity defined by the leading forms of the involved polynomials. This result provides a rigorous justification for using the degree of regularity in complexity estimates for Gröbner basis algorithms, thereby supporting a common assumption in algebraic cryptanalysis. We refine the complexity analysis by establishing bounds on the number of pairs that must be processed. These bounds improve upon published complexity estimates, with particularly significant gains in certain parameter ranges.
Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras

We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). The intensities guaranteeing reflection positivity of loop-soup vertex occupations on every reflection-symmetric finite graph with positive semidefinite cross-conductance matrix of rank $r$ form the real Wallach set $\W_r$. For the renormalized occupation field on the massless planar Dirichlet strip, the exact set is $\bigcap_{r\geq1}\W_r=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$.

We study finite-time shock formation in a nonlocal traffic flow model with Arrhenius look-ahead dynamics. For the constant interaction potential, we derive a time-dependent lower bound for the minimum slope and obtain a sufficient condition with logarithmic dependence on the magnitude of the minimum initial slope. For the linear interaction potential with look-ahead distance $γ$, we show that the condition $u'_0(x_0)>\frac{1}γ$ at a single point is sufficient for shock formation, which is independent of the minimum initial slope. The affine Beltrami fiber over a closed hyperbolic surface has a quadratic normal response whose least vertical $L^2$ energy equals the tangent norm dual to the hyperbolic cotangent supremum norm. We prove this calibration using a curvature identity and exact localized responses. Its strictness determines the energy measures of near-minimizers and, under an amplitude constraint, gives a positive excess with an explicit quadratic lower coefficient when the supporting differential has nondegenerate maxima. Pointwise Poincar'e barycenters of representatives in one fiber give a nonlinear realization: equal-weight pairs attain prescribed small outputs exactly, and their creation energy approaches the calibrated norm if and only if the output scale is negligible relative to the squared amplitude bound. We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.

For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $Γ(q,ξ)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $ξ\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(ξ),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$. For $q=4$, these cases yield the well-known icosidodecahedral and dodecadodecahedral graphs, respectively. Then we determine the distance distributions and full automorphism groups of the covers and prove that, for fixed $q$, two covers are isomorphic if and only if their defining parameters lie in the same Frobenius orbit. Nonexistence of positive entire solutions to systems of semilinear elliptic inequalities

Consider the system $Δu \geq p(x)g(v)$, $Δv \geq q(x)f(|\nabla u|)$, with $u>0$ and $v>0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq2$, $f,g\in C[0,\infty)$ and $p,q\in C(\mathbb{R}^n)$. If $f,g$ are non-decreasing and convex, using a comparison argument we prove a sufficient Keller-Osserman type condition for the nonexistence of entire solutions. This result is sharp for a wide class of systems. Similar results are also shown to hold for systems without gradient terms.
Computing expectations associated with McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations via probability-flow ordinary differential equations

This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite full-dimensional configuration, and put $F_X(N)=\max_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^d, |S|=N}\#\{(\mathbf{v},λ)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty):\mathbf{v}+λX\subseteq S\}$. Elekes and Erdős posed the problem of estimating $F_X(N)$. In this article, we determine its exact value when $X$ is the vertex set of a simplex. For several other classes of configurations, we obtain sharp asymptotic bounds and exact extremal values. We also introduce binomial barcodes for order polytopes and a recursive criterion for their effectiveness. In particular, if $X$ is the vertex set of the three-dimensional cube, then, for $n\ge 1$, $F_X(n^3)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^3=\left(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\right)^2$.
Exact Last-Iterate Bounds and Optimal Stepsizes for Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent

Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent minimizes the sum of an $L$-smooth convex function $f$, known through unbiased stochastic gradients of bounded variance, and a nonsmooth convex function $R$, known through its proximity operator. We derive the exact worst-case value of the expected objective gap of its last iterate, for every predetermined stepsize schedule in a broad class, which contains all the schedules with stepsizes at most $3/(2L)$. This extends to the composite setting a recent result of Grimmer and Shen for the smooth case $R=0$. The value is the sum of an initial-error term and of one term per iteration, which is the price of the noise injected at this iteration, damped by the stepsizes that remain after it. The upper bound is proved with a simple potential, the Moreau envelope of the objective with a smoothing parameter proportional to the remaining stepsize sum, and it is attained by an explicit instance. The formula shows that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable with a constant stepsize, and it gives the exact price of the proximity operator, relative to the smooth case. It also makes the choice of the stepsizes a tractable optimization problem: for a uniform variance bound $σ^2$, the best schedule is unique, decreasing, and computed by a scalar search, and it is minimax optimal among all predetermined schedules, unless the noise level is low. Asymptotically, the minimax value $M_T$ after $T$ iterations satisfies $(Dσ/M_T)^2=T+\log T+C_\star+o(1)$, where $D$ is a bound on the initial distance to a solution and $C_\star\approx1.768$ is a universal constant; unlike in the smooth case, $L$ plays no role at this order. Stefano Capparelli; Arne Meurman; Mirko Primc

The purpose of the present paper is to establish three combinatorial Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Although their motivation comes from the representation theory of affine Lie algebra of type $A_2^{(2)}$, our proofs are entirely combinatorial and analytic. They follow the automata-theoretic approach introduced by Takigiku and Tsuchioka in their proof of Nandi's conjecture and adapt it to the present setting.

The equation features a reaction term $f$ satisfying a one-sided Lipschitz condition and a bounded, globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient $σ$. Solutions are constructed in a scale of weighted continuous function spaces. Under an additional dissipativity condition on $f$, which covers reaction terms of the form $f(u)=u-u^{3}$, we prove that the transition semigroup admits an invariant measure on some weighted space $C_ρ$. This constitutes the first step toward a complete ergodic theory for dissipative stochastic heat equations on unbounded domains, a setting that has so far remained largely open in the literature.

After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product $Nγ$ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size $a$ from $\{0,1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$ goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate $O((Nγ)^{-1/2})$ if $a\in \{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

On the number of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact star graphs

In this paper, we consider the number and the shape of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact symmetric star graphs with Dirichlet condition at the exterior vertex and Kirchhoff condition at the central vertex.

For any convex polytope $C$ containing the origin, we use the KL exponent $0$ to show that the full-step manifold proximal point iterates for minimizing the support function of $C$ over $\mathcal{S}$ stabilize at a critical point in finitely many steps.
Similarity classes of $5\times5$ matrices over local rings of length two
Himadri Mukherjee; Gunja Sachdeva; Adeep Varghese

Let $R$ be a commutative local principal ideal ring of length two whose residue field has arbitrary characteristic. Prasad, Singla and Spallone classified similarity classes in $M_n(R)$ for $n\leq4$ by using module extensions. We extend their classification to $n=5$. We determine explicit extension-orbit representatives and stabilizers for the partitions $(3,2)$, $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,1,1,1)$. We prove that every orbit contains exactly one of the listed representatives. Together with the known primary cases, these results give all similarity classes in $M_5(R)$ and their centralizers. We also determine representatives and stabilizers for the family $(m+1,1,1,1)$ for every $m\geq1$. When the residue field is finite, we obtain the sizes and total number of similarity classes.
A proof of the toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs

As a measure of the connectivity of graphs, Chvátal \cite{Chvatal} introduced the concept of toughness. For integers $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2k+1$, the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ has all the $k$-subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ as its vertices, and two vertices are adjacent if they are disjoint. Cioabă and Wong~\cite{CW} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,2)$. Park et al.~\cite{Park} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,k)$ when $k=3,4$ and $k\geq5$ for large $n$. They \cite{Park} proposed a conjecture for $k\geq5$ and other values of $n$. In this paper, we resolve this conjecture.
From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling

Nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) models are the central statistical models of pharmacometrics, where they support dose selection, individualized dosing and regulatory decisions in drug development. Statistically, NLME modeling is a marginalized likelihood problem. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) solve such problems with a neural network encoder that amortizes the approximation of the intractable posterior distribution, and allow the integration of AI components into NLME modeling. This paper provides the convergence analysis of the VAE-NLME algorithm. First, its version for the evidence lower bound (ELBO) is proven to converge almost surely to the set of stationary points of the ELBO, without assuming that the encoder is trained exactly. Second, the final VAE-NLME algorithm trains the encoder on the ELBO by gradient-based optimization and uses it as proposal for importance-weighted sufficient statistics. It converges almost surely to the set of stationary points of the marginal log-likelihood, without any assumption on the training of the encoder. Thus, it combines the fast gradient-based training of VAEs with the limit of maximum likelihood estimation.
AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
Miguel A. L. Marques; Irene D'Amico; Stefano Pittalis

The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.
The pair correlation of $αn+β\log n$ modulo one
We show that for any non-Liouville irrational $α$ and for any real $β\ne0$, the sequence $\left(αn+β\log n\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ has Poissonian pair correlation modulo one.
A Sylow reduction for isomorphisms of Cayley graphs on abelian groups of cube-free order
Tingzeng Wu; Liang Qin; Yong Yu; Xing Gao

The isomorphism problem for Cayley graphs is one of the fundamental problems in algebraic combinatorics. Dobson studied this isomorphism problem and asked whether, assuming that the group generated by the left regular representation and its conjugate under an isomorphism admits a complete sequence of normal block systems, the isomorphism problem for Cayley digraphs on a finite abelian group of cube-free order can be reduced to the corresponding problem on its Sylow subgroups. We answer this question affirmatively. We first prove that color-preserving isomorphisms preserving the fiber partition on direct products $A\times H$ of abelian groups of coprime orders, where $|H|$ is a prime or the square of a prime, have a product decomposition property. Applying this property successively to the Sylow subgroups of a cube-free-order abelian group $G$, we show that if two colored binary Cayley structures on $G$ are connected by a color-preserving isomorphism $f$ for which $\langle G_L,f^{-1}G_Lf\rangle$ admits a complete sequence of block systems, then they are also connected by a color-preserving Sylow coordinate isomorphism. This yields the corresponding Sylow reduction for solving sets.

We study local embeddability of $C^*$-algebras into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ as an analogue of QWEP in the LLP/WEP picture. We characterize this property by an analog of CP-stability, an approximation property for finite-dimensional operator systems. We show that local embeddability, together with an amenable trace, implies a tracial local lifting property. Combining this observation with the cohomological obstructions of Ioana, Spaas and Wiersma, we prove that the full group $C^*$-algebra $C^*(\SL_3(\Z))$ does not locally embed into $C^*(\F_\infty)$. We obtain the same conclusion for the full $C^*$-algebras of two hyperlinear groups constructed by Thom. To our knowledge, the only previously known obstruction to local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ was due to Junge and Pisier.
Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras

In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $σC^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $σC^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that: - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $σ$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $σ$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property. - The category of $σC^*$-algebras and $σ$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable. - $σC^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property. - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $σ$-additive assignments from a $σ$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $σ$-normal completely positive maps between $σC^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $σ$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.
A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
Weisz Ferenc; Guangheng Xie; Dachun Yang

We characterize the increasing sequences $(ν_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{ν_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $ν_j$. Divide each $ν_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{ν_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(ν_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.
Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics

We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical pair with $X$ of Fano type, $-(K_X+B)$ nef and coefficients of $B$ in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all $ε$-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of $ε$. We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral $\Q$-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.
The first moment of symmetric cube $L$-functions

We establish a power saving asymptotic formula for the first moment of symmetric cube central $L$-values over Hecke--Maass forms in short spectral windows. As applications, we prove quantitative non-vanishing, an almost-all Lindelöf bound, and almost-all decay of cubic periods. We also prove the corresponding first moment asymptotic for central derivatives in the holomorphic weight aspect. Our proof begins with an application of the Kuznetsov formula, followed by a first Poisson summation and stationary phase analysis. The key observation is that a periodic cubic factor can be separated from the resulting oscillation and incorporated into the arithmetic sum, allowing a second application of Poisson summation to yield further cancellation.
Exact Solutions and a Critical-Damping Threshold for a Nonlinear Transport-Wave Equation

Linear stability theory does not determine whether a small disturbance in a physical system decays or grows without bound when the disturbance has finite size and the damping varies in time. We address this question for the nonlinear damped transport-wave equation $u_{tt}+cu_{xt}+γu_t=λu(u_t+cu_x)e^{-γt}$, a constant-coefficient case of a model introduced in previous work. Combining the method of characteristics with a Riccati reduction, we reduce the equation exactly to a first-order ordinary differential equation at each point and solve it explicitly. For a natural class of initial data, the solution has a critical damping rate $\gc$, given in closed form in terms of the initial data: for $γ<\gc$ the solution blows up in finite time, and otherwise no finite-time singularity occurs. A similar result holds for time-dependent damping and for power-law feedback. Applications to shock formation in the damped Burgers equation, gelation with decaying reactivity and frictional heating under a moving band are presented.
Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements

We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type. As an application, we show that every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines admits a realization whose complement has no $2$-dimensional CW model.
Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
We prove that the Simons cone in $\mathbb R^8$ minimizes the fractional perimeter $P_s$, under compact perturbations, whenever $s$ is sufficiently close to $1$.
From Horner's rule to neural networks

Horner's rule is usually taught as an efficient algorithm for evaluating a polynomial. Read as a recurrence, however, it is also a small computational graph: an input is propagated through intermediate states, while parameters enter locally. This note follows that elementary observation from polynomial evaluation to polynomial fitting. The equation $Va\simeq y$ then unifies least-squares approximation, interpolation and overparametrisation as different regimes of a fixed representation. Neural networks are introduced as the next step: the representation itself becomes parametrised and is learned from data. The purpose is pedagogical rather than encyclopaedic. It offers a numerical route into machine learning, using approximation, linear algebra and optimisation as familiar entry points.
Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
Dror Aiger; Sariel Har-Peled; Goran Žužić

Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

We give a short proof of Bourgain's slicing theorem with the explicit bound $L_K\leq\sqrt{5/π}$ for every convex body $K$. The argument combines the strong thin-shell inequality obtained from the moment-measure method of Chen and Klartag with an entropy estimate along Eldan's stochastic localization. The proof uses neither $M$-ellipsoid theory nor the reverse Santaló inequality.
Morten Nielsen; Gabriele Peluso; Mikkel Hviid Thorn

We show that $L^p$-boundedness for magnetic pseudodifferential operators is equivalent to $L^p$-boundedness of non-magnetic pseudodifferential operators for $p\in[1,\infty]$, regular magnetic fields and classical Hörmander symbols $S_{ρ,δ}^m$ with $0<ρ\leq 1$ and $0\leqδ<1$. As a corollary we get $L^p$-boundedness for $1<p<\infty$ of magnetic pseudodifferential operators when $ρ>0,0\leqδ\leqρ\leq1,δ<1$ and $m\leq-d(1-ρ)|1/2-1/p|$. Moreover, we give a bound on the operator norm in terms of the magnetic field and symbol.
Breaking Resonance: Square-root acceleration for Metropolis-adjusted randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a fixed integration time can fail to mix because of resonances, and randomizing the integration time removes them. We prove that Metropolis-adjusted HMC with velocity Verlet and random integration times mixes from a warm start in a number of transitions that does not depend on the condition number, for every integration-time law satisfying a Fourier condition that we call non-resonant; uniform, exponential and triangular laws are examples. For a target density proportional to $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$, where $U$ is $m$-strongly convex with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian and $κ=L/m$, the number of gradient evaluations needed to reach a fixed total variation accuracy is, up to constants and logarithmic factors, $\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}\,(d/m)^{3/4}$. This is the first square-root condition-number bound for this sampler beyond Gaussian targets. The proof converts relative-entropy contraction of the unadjusted proposal into a conductance bound for the adjusted chain, and shows that the integration-time law enters only through its characteristic function. Hessian regularity cannot be dropped for a fixed step size: without it there are targets in the class for which the cost is at least of order $κ^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic factors, even from a warm start.

Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.
The Orientable Genus of Generalized Corona Graphs

The generalized corona of a graph with a family of graphs, one for each vertex, is obtained by joining every vertex of the base graph to all vertices of its own copy of the corresponding graph; the corona of Frucht and Harary is the case in which all graphs in the family are equal. Each attached copy meets the rest of the graph in a single vertex, so additivity of the orientable genus over blocks reduces the genus of a generalized corona to the genus of the base graph plus the genera of the graphs obtained from the attached graphs by adding a dominating vertex. We study this last quantity through faces that meet every vertex, and we determine it for complete graphs, balanced complete bipartite graphs, wheels, prisms, antiprisms, the Petersen graph (value 2). The Petersen case follows from a face-length criterion. We also obtain bounds under edge addition, a formula for iterated coronas, a criterion for two coronas taken in opposite order to have the same genus, and we show that the corona is not associative with respect to the genus.

We study an exterior-algebra analogue of classical invariant theory for linear, symplectic, and orthogonal groups, with particular emphasis on integral constructions and positive characteristic. The theory presented here is rather different from the classical one developed by us in DeConcini Procesi 1976 . In fact, the present theory is based on good filtrations and on a surprising divided-power structure on the algebras of exterior invariants. We also include a short characteristic-zero treatment of the corresponding First and Second Fundamental Theorems via the exterior Cauchy identity; these known results motivate the integral theory.
Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term

This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(α\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(α\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.
Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
Ke Tan; Chong-Jun Li; Xu Guo

Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML scheme with linear completeness. By using linear displacement field constraints to reconstruct the corresponding columns of the transition matrix, we ensure that the resulting numerical shape-function space contains the space of linear polynomials. We derive error estimates and establish convergence results of the improved scheme in the H1 and L2 norms. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate that the improved PIML achieves optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.
Harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms and deformations of branched covers of special Lagrangians
Siqi He; Jacek Rzemieniecki; Thomas Walpuski

This article introduces the notion of a non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-form on a manifold $X$ in terms of immersed submanifolds of $T^*X$ and develops a deformation theory extending Donaldson's work on harmonic non-degenerate $\mathbf{Z}/2\mathbf{Z}$ $1$-forms. More precisely, the universal moduli space of harmonic non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-forms is shown to be a tame Fréchet orbifold whose projection onto the space of Riemannian metrics is a submersion and whose fibres are locally parametrised by their periods. The proof relies on Hörmander's subelliptic estimates and the Nash--Moser submersion theorem. As an application of this analytic framework, harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms on a special Lagrangian are shown to control deformations of its branched covers, extending work of He for multiplicity two.
Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas

We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.
Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator

Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations. When the modulation is slow compared with the libration frequency, the phase states follow adiabatically. As the two frequencies become comparable, this approximation breaks down and the driven libration resonates with the intrinsic one. This nonadiabatic regime is examined for a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping. The averaged equations describe a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics, whose homoclinic loop is derived in closed form. The phase states persist as invariant tori supporting quasiperiodic motion. Their stability and period-doubling bifurcations are captured by a damped Mathieu equation, in which the modulation contributes to both parametric stiffness and parametric damping. A Melnikov analysis yields explicit thresholds for separatrix splitting and the onset of homoclinic intersections, which are corroborated by numerical computations of the invariant manifolds. Numerically it is revealed that these intersections arise well before sustained chaotic motion develops. The fate of the parametric oscillation depends markedly on the resonance condition: modulation at the libration frequency destroys the invariant tori and quenches the oscillation, whereas modulation at twice the libration frequency leaves it intact.
Weak oddness to resistance ratios in snarks

Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. If $G$ is not 3-edge-colourable, we call it a \textit{snark}. The \textit{resistance} of $G$, denoted $r(G)$, is the minimum number of edges which can be removed from $G$ in order to render $G$ 3-edge-colourable. The \textit{oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any 2-factor of $G$. The \textit{weak oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω'(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any even factor of $G$. In their comprehensive survey paper on measurements of uncolourability in cubic graphs, Fiol et al. conjectured the following two statements for a snark $G$: $ω(G) \leq 2r(G)$ and $ω'(G) \leq 2r(G)$ \cite{FiolMazzuoccoloSteffen2018}. Previously, we disproved the former by proving that the ratio of oddness to weak oddness, and hence the ratio of oddness to resistance, can in fact be arbitrarily large \cite{Allie2019}. In this paper, we prove a slightly stronger version of the latter: $ω'(G) < 2r(G)$. The proof centres around substructures in $G$, given a minimal colouring $f$, which we call \textit{meta-Kempe chains}.
Commutator syzygies and pure resolutions over central polynomial rings with division-ring coefficients
Hoang Anh Tu; Huynh Viet Khanh

Let $D$ be a division ring and let $A=D[x,y,z]$ with central indeterminates. For positive integers $p,q$ and $a,b\in D$, put $f=x^p+az^p$ and $g=y^q+bz^q$. We compute their left syzygy module and the minimal graded free resolution of $A/(Af+Ag)$. This quotient has projective dimension two if $ab=ba$ and three otherwise. In the latter case, it has finite length and total Betti numbers $(1,2,2,1)$, with a pure resolution of type $(0,d,3d,4d)$ when $p=q=d$. These tables do not occur over polynomial rings over fields. If $D$ is finite-dimensional over its center $K$, the Betti tables of modules of finite length over $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and left modules of finite length over $D[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ generate the same rational cone for every $n\ge1$. In three variables, the semigroup over $K$ is properly contained in that over $D$ when $D$ is noncommutative.

We investigate semirings induced by join-semilattice (meet-semilattices) with a degenerate multiplication on all the subset that excludes the multiplicative unity. The way those semirings are defined enables a big impact of the semilattices we start with on the associated semirings: many of their order-theoretic properties reflect in algebraic properties of the induced semirings. This enabled constructing examples of semirings with desired properties as well as providing counterexamples to wrong claims in old and recent papers/preprints. In particular, we construct families of examples of semirings induced by non-modular join-semilattices for which the lattice of subtractive ideals is non-modular disproving a claim of Henriksen who introduced this important class of ideals of semirings.
Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral

The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior minimiser and makes any such solution the unique global minimax, and we prove interior attainment for $K \le 11$. A certification algorithm audits a candidate mixture in multiple-precision arithmetic, using a proved bound on the number of extrema as its completeness test, and three search pipelines reach $K = 9, 10, 11$, the last with certified worst-case error $1.26 \times 10^{-11}$. A signed $K = 22$ mixture carries a relaxed certificate at $3.605 \times 10^{-15}$. In causal mediation with a binary outcome, the certified sum replaces a biased Taylor expansion and stochastic integration with one closed-form evaluation.
Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
Maciej Gałązka; Jaewoo Jung; Hyunsuk Moon

We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.
Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models

Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Chiara Gambicchia; Matteo Novaga; Matteo Talluri

In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.
On the bounds of path-unique subgraph of De Bruijn graph

The De Bruijn graph is a directed graph G(n, m) such that V = (Zn)m and there is an edge from A to B iff A deletes the first coordinate equals to B deletes the last coordinate. Based on the background of achieving DNA labeling with minimum labels, we consider the De Brujin graph and its path-unique subgraph with maximum edges. Motivated by the work of Lutwak--Xi--Yang--Zhang on the chord measures, we introduce the $(s,q)$-chord measures arising from variations of a new family of geometric invariants, called the $(s,q)$-chord integrals. These vector fields are continuously differentiable except for a finite number of points on the boundary. Our approach identifies a form of h-principle and a close analogy with Nash's construction of smooth isometric embeddings.

The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics

Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. Polar Carleson zeto set preventing Dirichlet cyclicity

The work of Chen, Fang and Guo shows, finally, that the Brown-Shields conjecture is false. In this note, we construct a polar Carleson set E on the unit circle T which has the property that any Hölder continuous function in the Dirichlet space vanishing on E is non-cyclic.

In this paper, we study observability inequalities for the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation associated with the operator $H_m=-\partial_x^2+|x|^{2m}$, where $0<m\leq1$. Exceptional points (EPs) in complex elastic materials signify the coalescence of compressional and shear modes and bound a frequency gap where waves become evanescent. While their effects on wave propagation have been extensively studied, the physical mechanisms underlying their existence remain elusive. In this Letter, employing a transfer matrix formulation combined with Bloch's theorem, we demonstrate that the gaps bounded by EPs in layered media originate from destructive interference between the compressional and shear wave fields. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the following eighth moment estimate holds \[ \int_{[0,1]^2} \left|\sum_{n=1}^N b_n \exp(2πi(nx+n^3y))\right|^8 dxdy \ll_{\varepsilon} N^{1/2-1/47500+\varepsilon} \left(\sum_{n=1}^N |b_n|^2\right)^4. \]

The proof of nonexistence for the remaining types is based on \cite{VB22} and \cite{Tu}. This paper completes the investigation undertaken in~\cite{VB26}.

For integer $k\geq2$ and power $q$ of prime $p$, the algebraic bipartite graph $D(k,q)$, proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko in 1993, is $q$-regular, edge-transitive and of girth at least $k+4$. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.
An Exposition of Gerstenhaber's Proposition 1: Elimination of Coboundaries in Formal Deformations

Gerstenhaber's foundational work on formal deformations of associative algebras relates the first non-trivial term of a deformation to the second Hochschild cohomology group. In the proof of Proposition~1 of his 1964 paper, a leading Hochschild $2$-cocycle which is a coboundary is successively removed by formal changes of variables. If this elimination terminates after finitely many steps, no limiting argument is required, but the possibility that coboundaries continue to be eliminated indefinitely is left largely implicit in the original treatment. This expository note makes that limiting argument fully explicit for deformations over $K[[t]]$ of a fixed associative $K$-algebra $A$. We use the $t$-adic topology on the relevant spaces of formal power series and formal endomorphisms, establish completeness and the continuity of composition, inversion and the action on formal multiplications, and show that an infinite sequence of successive changes of variables assembles into a single, well-defined formal equivalence. This yields a complete, self-contained proof of the classical result and its rigidity consequence.
Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
Yida Xu; Baichuan Mo; Zhengzhong Ricky You; Yuan Zhou; Hao Yi Ong; Zuo-Jun Max Shen

Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching. To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.
Sameer Chavan; Zenon Jan Jabłoński; Il Bong Jung; Jan Stochel

We characterize subnormality of $B$-operators $T=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}V&E\\0&S\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ on $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\mathcal{H}_2$, where $V$ is an isometry, $V^*E=0$, $S$ is subnormal, and $S|E|=|E|S$. We determine when $T$ admits compactly supported signed elementary measures and express them explicitly in terms of the elementary measures of $S$. Requiring the signed elementary measures of $T$ to be positive yields a complete measure-theoretic characterization of the subnormality of $T$. If $E$ is injective, $T$ is subnormal if and only if it is a contraction. In the general case, the subnormality of $T$ is equivalent to the contractivity of its restriction to $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\overline{{\mathcal R}(|E|)}$. We also obtain equivalent criteria involving the Taylor spectra of $(S,|E|)$, its minimal normal and minimal quasinormal extensions, and the corresponding pairs of moduli. These results extend the characterization previously known for a quasinormal lower-right entry.
Rigidity for semiconvex entire solutions of Hessian quotient equations
Guohuan Qiu; Jin Yan; Xingchen Zhou; Ruixuan Zhu

We prove that every smooth admissible semiconvex entire solution of $σ_k(D^2u)/σ_l(D^2u)=1$ in $\mathbb R^n$, where $0\le l<k\le n$ and $k-l=1$ or $2$, is a quadratic polynomial. The proof uses a shifted Legendre transform and interior Hessian estimates for Hessian quotient equations to reduce the problem to equations of lower order. We then conclude by induction on the order of the equation.
Spontaneous Synchronization in Cellular Circadian Clocks

We study a population of identical cellular circadian oscillators, each a four-species transcription--translation feedback loop of the type analysed by Wang and Peskin, coupled by the exchange of cytoplasmic mRNA with a shared, well-mixed bloodstream at rate $ε$. Simulations started from uniformly random phases show a collective damping of the mean rhythm followed by spontaneous synchronization. We show that the blood compartment tracks the population mean on the time scale $1/[N_c(ε+δ_m)]$, and that the population means obey the single-cell equations with a correction proportional to the variance $σ_{pn}^2$ of nuclear protein across cells; the correction is accurate only near synchrony. Deviations from the mean obey a linear system with periodic coefficients, whose leading Floquet exponent $-κ(ε)$ is the asymptotic synchronization rate. Using the fact that the four first-order stages of the feedback loop commute, we prove that $κ(ε)=ε/4+O(ε^2)$ on the limit cycle in the large-population limit. Numerically computed exponents agree with the decay rates measured in simulations to within $0.2\%$ for $5$ to $400$ cells. The approach to synchrony from an incoherent state is slower than $κ$, and at the weakest coupling tested the population remains in a two-cluster state. With intrinsic molecular noise, uncoupled cells lose their autocorrelation within about ten cycles, whereas coupled cells retain it and sustain a Kuramoto order parameter of $0.68$ to $0.93$.
Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation

We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$. The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are real-analytic and strictly convex. The principal innovation of the article is the use of a slide resampling that preserves the conditioned law. The slide acts by cutting the long finite connection at a given $\pmb{\ell}$-height and relocating the upper piece by a random shift. The mass gap is obtained by a delicate analysis of an iterated version of the slide operation along a positive density of attempted heights.
Wave interactions for the two-dimensional self-similar Euler equations of nonconvex gases

Gases with nonconvex equations of state may differ significantly from polytropic ideal gases; for example, rarefaction and sonic shocks may occur. This paper studies a 2D Riemann initial-boundary value problem for the potential flow equations with a nonconvex equation of state. We construct global-in-time self-similar solutions by analyzing eight distinct types of wave interactions, including composite waves consisting of a sonic/double-sonic shock coupled with one or two fan waves. Three main difficulties arise in studying these wave interactions: the self-similar potential flow system is of mixed type, with its type at each point determined by the local pseudo-Mach number; the sonic or transonic nature of the shocks is not known a priori; and sonic singularities arise on sonic shocks. To overcome these difficulties, we proceed as follows. First, we introduce a density-dependent invariant region and apply the maximum principle to establish the hyperbolicity principle of the 2D self-similar Euler equations. Second, we establish a priori estimates for the shock types by differentiating the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions along the shocks, comparing the shock and acoustic speeds, and using the Oleinik-Liu entropy condition. Finally, we employ the hodograph transformation together with regularization to handle the various singularities on sonic shocks. These wave interactions serve as building blocks for more complicated 2D Riemann problems and as benchmarks for numerical algorithms for nonconvex conservation laws. We also propose several open problems.
Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory

We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations.
