Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.
Cardinal Transfer Events for Infinitary Logic with Infinitary Quantification
Assuming the existence of a certain theory $Φ$, we solve the Gap-$n$ problem for more than one predicate. This will be done for infinitary logic with infinitary quantification.
Unit Lattices of Totally Complex, non-CM $D_4$-Octic Number Fields

Given a number field, we can endow the unit group of its ring of integers, modulo torsion, with the structure of a lattice. Included in the study of the distributions of these lattices is the classification of shapes of unit lattices arising from $D_4$-quartic number fields with signature $(2,1)$. We extend this work to rank 3, by investigating the shapes of lattices arising from the unit groups of totally complex, non-CM $D_4$-octic number fields. In particular, we show all such unit lattices have automorphism group $D_4\times \mathbb{Z}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$, yet none correspond to Gram matrices whose entries are all algebraic.
A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
Siyad Rahman Mandottil; Neela Nataraj; Ricardo Ruiz-Baier

This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.
Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles

The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3πk/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.
Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds

Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^β$ Poincaré inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $λ(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-β}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.
Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
Matthew Harper; Joshua O'Connor; José Sánchez Menchén; Angie Wu

The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials. We also discuss behavior of our formulae under connected sums. We give formulations for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of even powers of the Garside element $Δ_3\in B_3$ and a closed formula for the invariant on positive $3$-braids, resulting in a formula for the invariant on all $3$-braids.
Semisimple-Unipotent Decomposition and the Exact Order of a Linear Cellular Automaton over F_2

We study the linear cellular automaton on the cyclic graph $C_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by the local rule $v_i(t+1)=v_{i-1}(t)\oplus v_i(t)\oplus v_{i+1}(t)$ (Wolfram's Rule 150 under periodic boundary conditions). Identifying the configuration space $V_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $R_n = \mathbb{F}_2[x] / \langle x^n - 1 \rangle$, the evolution operator corresponds to multiplication by $G(x)=1+x+x^{n-1}$. We re-derive the invertibility criterion $3\nmid n$, classify periodic and transient behaviour, and prove that Hamming weight is non-monotone for every $n\ge3$. We then factor $x^n-1$ via the Chinese Remainder Theorem and separate semisimple contributions governed by finite-field multiplicative orders from unipotent contributions governed by Frobenius squaring. We determine the exact local unipotent orders and obtain a closed-form global order $r(A)$: $r(A)=2^{m-1}$ for $n=2^m$ with $m\ge2$, while for $n=2^m q$, $q>1$ odd and $3\nmid n$, $r(A)=2^m\operatorname{lcm}(m_2,\ldots,m_r)$. The theory is illustrated by $n=5,7,8,16$ and computationally verified for small dimensions.
Why $(4x(1-x))^{3/4}$ approximates the binary entropy so well: a proof of Topsøe's convexity conjecture

Write the binary entropy as $h(x) = u^{g(x)}$ with $u = 4x(1-x)$. Topsoe (2001) proved the sharp bounds $1/\ln 4 \le g \le 1$, i.e. $u \le h \le u^{1/\ln 4}$, and conjectured that the effective exponent $g$ is convex. We prove this conjecture. In the variable $s = (1-2x)^2$, $g$ extends to a Pick function on $\mathbb{C} \setminus [1,\infty)$ with an explicit positive density on the cut, so that $g(x) = \sum_n γ_n (1-2x)^{2n}$ with $γ_n > 0$ and $(γ_n)_{n \ge 1}$ a moment sequence. Pinelis's monotonicity theorem, Topsoe's power-type bounds and the optimality of their exponents follow as corollaries, together with a classification of all exponents $α$ for which $u^α$ bounds $h$. The proof is by hand except for one inequality in one real variable on a bounded interval, certified by interval arithmetic. As an application we give sharp, certified constants for the approximation $h \approx u^{3/4}$: $-0.0065493 \le u^{3/4} - h \le 0.0080004$ on $[0,1]$.
Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes

A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=Ω(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$. The lower bound improves the exponential base $(9/5)^{1/4}=1.15829\ldots$ of Körner and Marton. It comes from a random system of overlapping local constraints, in which every position is read two or three times, followed by thinning and the deletion of nearby pairs and of the remaining triples that violate trifference. The required estimates reduce to finitely many inequalities, which we verify rigorously by computer. The upper bound improves our earlier bound $O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)$.

In this article, we give characterisation of crossed homomorphisms of Leibniz superalgebras as Maurer-Cartan elements of an associated graded Lie algebra. This characterization enables us to develop a cohomology theory for crossed homomorphisms and to apply it to their formal deformation theory. We show that the infinitesimal of a deformation is a 1-cocycle and that linear deformations are classified by such cocycles. Furthermore, we introduce the category of crossed homomorphisms between two fixed Leibniz superalgebras.
A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor

We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.
Variational Thresholds and Multiplicity for a Nonlocal r-Laplacian Logistic-Type Problem

This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $λ$: \[ \begin{cases} -Δ_r u - \displaystyle\int_Ω K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +λ|u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_ΩQ(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in Ω, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partialΩ. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $λ$. For $λ\ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(λ<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehatλ^*<λ^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(λ^*<λ<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with positive energy, yielding two distinct nontrivial weak solutions. The same holds at \(λ=λ^*\), where the global minimizer has zero energy. In a left neighborhood of \(λ^*\), two distinct nontrivial weak solutions persist, a local minimizer and a mountain-pass critical point, both with positive energy and the latter at a strictly higher level. For \(λ<\widehatλ^*\), only the trivial solution exists. Finally, as $λ\to 0^-$, the norm of the global minimizers blows up. Along subsequences, selected nonnegative mountain-pass solutions converge strongly in $W_0^{1,r}(Ω)$ as $λ\to 0$ to a nontrivial nonnegative weak solution of the problem at $λ= 0$. The associated mountain-pass levels converge to the same limit from both sides of zero, and the corresponding solution norms also converge to a common value.
Counting solutions to Euclidean Fermat equations
Niven T. Achenjang; Santiago Arango-Pi{ñ}eros; Sameera Vemulapalli

A solution $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^3-\{(0,0,0)\}$ to a Fermat equation \begin{equation} \label{eq:abstract-gfe} Ax^a + By^b + Cz^c = 0 \end{equation} is called \emph{primitive} if $\gcd(x,y,z) = 1$. In the \emph{Euclidean} regime (that is, when the Euler characteristic $χ= \tfrac{1}{a} + \tfrac{1}{b} + \tfrac{1}{c} - 1$ is zero), the equation above defines a smooth genus one curve in a weighted projective plane. We study these models and provide an asymptotic formula for the number of primitive integral solutions with bounded height.
Classification of fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system

We study fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system with four reaction exponents, in which only one component diffuses. For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.
Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base

We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.
Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization

The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.
Local Reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up

We give four regularity criteria for the forced Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The first is an $\dot H^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local Reynolds number $|v|^2/(ν|ω|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $M(t)$ with $\int M^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. It rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. Two further $\dot H^1$ estimates use the Newton potential of $|ω|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the Lamb vector, so that the integral of $|ω|^2|v|^2$ cancels. The second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by $\int\|ω\|_{L^3}^2\,dt<\infty$. The fourth is a maximum principle for $\frac12|v|^2+λ|ω|$: vortex stretching is absorbed by viscous dissipation, and the pressure is controlled by a weighted local estimate. It requires a bound on $|v|^2/(ν|\nabla v|)$ only at maximum points where the velocity part dominates. We show that the forced finite-time blow-up recently constructed by OpenAI violates each hypothesis, and that the violations locate its mechanism: inflow down the centripetal pressure gradient, at the same order as viscous dissipation.
On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
Stephanie Chan; Peter Koymans; Nick Rome; Tim Santens

We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.
Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
Minchan Jung; Dimitrios S. Georgiou; Augustinos D. Saravanos; Evangelos A. Theodorou

Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.
Distributed Time-Varying Resource Allocation in Open Networks

We consider the problem of distributed resource allocation over a team of agents whose active membership changes over time. Each agent's allocation evolves according to its own temporal dynamics, while a shared equality constraint couples all active agents at every instant. For the case of quadratic local objectives, we show that the optimal solution is characterized by a linear system whose coefficient matrix couples a block-tridiagonal temporal structure with a block-diagonal Laplacian capturing the time-varying communication graph. Building on this structure, we develop a distributed forward-backward sweeping algorithm in which each agent resolves its own temporal coupling through a local forward-backward sweep, while the shared resource constraint is resolved through a distributed consensus iteration that is feasible at every iteration. Under a mild diagonal-dominance condition on the temporal coupling, we establish that the optimal allocation at any fixed time converges geometrically to a stationary solution as the horizon grows, and that our distributed algorithm tracks this limit at a matching geometric rate. These results justify a memory-efficient variant of the algorithm in which each agent retains only a bounded window of past history, with the resulting approximation error decaying exponentially in the window size. We validate these theoretical guarantees through numerical simulation, confirming the predicted convergence rates under dynamically changing team membership.
Pan Shun Lau; Nancy De Menzelthe; Tin-Yau Tam

We study the wedge and projection multiplicities of a point in the $k$-numerical range $W_k(A)$ of a complex matrix $A$. The representatives are decomposable wedges of orthonormal $k$-frames and rank-$k$ orthogonal projections, respectively. For $1\le k<n$, put $r=\text{dim}_\mathbb{R}\text{span}_\mathbb{R}\{I_n,H,K\}$, where $H=(A+A^*)/2$ and $K=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. We prove that every $ξ\in\text{relint} W_k(A)$ satisfies $p_{A,k}(ξ)=n^2-r+1$ and $w_{A,k}(ξ)=\binom nk$. We determine both multiplicities at every boundary point of $W_k(A)$, including non-exposed points. For complex symmetric matrices we establish lower bounds for both real multiplicities, including singular interior fibers, and obtain exact formulas for boundary points, line ranges, and commuting symmetric parts. We also relate the two multiplicities by quadratic inequalities.
On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families

Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.
Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles

We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.
A Hereditarily Atomic Domain without ACCP

An integral domain for which every subring is atomic is said to be hereditarily atomic. Every hereditarily atomic cancellative commutative monoid satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals (ACCP), but it remained an open question whether every hereditarily atomic domain satisfies ACCP. We construct a hereditarily atomic domain which does not satisfy ACCP, answering this question in the negative. This domain is an overring of the ring of integer-valued polynomials $Int(\mathbb{Z})$, and its subrings that fail ACCP are precisely those of finite additive index.
Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values

We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.
Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data

This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
Brian M. Cho; Michael Lindon; Nathan Kallus

The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework accommodates arbitrarily dependent decisions, data-dependent trajectory termination, dynamically generated hypotheses, and quality measures defined after the trajectory concludes. We construct upper and lower bound estimators and confidence sets for agent quality with statistical guarantees that hold uniformly over agent trajectory distributions and establish instance-wise sharpness of our estimator class. We demonstrate our methods with a case study comparing the success of Claude Opus and Claude Haiku in improving the runtime of an open-source Python package.
An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus

We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".
Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
Grzegorz Biskowski; Marcin R. Piatek; Franco Ferrari

We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UEA regular multivariate time series benchmarks specifically when class-discriminative information is purely geometric.
The Work of Mathematical Production in the Age of AI

The emergence of powerful artificial intelligence has unsettled the relationship between mathematical production and the human intellectual activity that mathematical artifacts have traditionally documented. We argue that mathematical practice cannot be adequately understood through the production of mathematical knowledge alone, and distinguish four interrelated dimensions of inquiry: knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out. Building on Kitcher, Dewey, and subsequent philosophy of mathematical practice, we develop an expanded framework incorporating the cognitive and computational capacities of mathematical communities, their conceptual organizations, provisional investigative models, and the role of unsuccessful inquiry. We propose reconceptualizing artificial intelligence as a manifestation of physically organized computation whose mathematical behavior itself can become an object of experimental investigation. This perspective motivates a program of \emph{natural mathematics}, by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition. Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.
Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules

There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$ when $μ$ is obtained from $λ$ by adding one to a part of $λ$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $λ$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^λ$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^λ$ to $\mathcal{S}^{λ'}$.
An easy proof of transience of one-dimensional Rademacher walk with power weights
Using a version of a local limit theorem, we provide an easy proof that the Rademacher random walk with step sizes $n^α$, $α>1/2$, is transient.
Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang

Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, χ_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, André, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.
Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation

We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.
Dispersive estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
Adam Black; David Damanik; Jake Fillman; Giorgio Young

We prove dispersive estimates for limit-periodic operators that are super-exponentially well-approximated by periodic operators. The key ingredient is a sharp enhanced convexity statement for the density of states of periodic Jacobi matrices. This statement implies log-convexity of the density of states and hence is a strengthening of existing results on the convexity of equilibrium measures. We expect that it will be of interest and use outside of this work. We also construct almost-periodic discrete Schrödinger operators with purely singular continuous spectrum whose unitary groups enjoy recurrent dispersive motion: on one subsequence of time scales, the unitary group has a dispersive estimate at a rate as close to the free rate as one desires, while on another set of time scales, the unitary group is as far from dispersive as possible. In fact, this behavior is generic within the class of limit-periodic operators.
Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
Federica Dragoni; Nicola Garofalo; Gianmarco Giovannardi; Paolo Salani; Dimiter Vassilev

We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $Ω\subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Korányi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $Δ_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $Ω\setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $ u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partialΩ, \quad u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partialΩ$, then $Ω$ must itself be a Korányi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it is an affine normalization of the fundamental solution of $Δ_{\mathbb{G},p}$.

We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gouëzel skew products [Gouëzel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.
Higher-symmetry selection rules for second- and third-harmonic radiation in the Bullough-Dodd model

We investigate nonlinear excitations of the discrete shape mode about a static complex soliton of the integrable Bullough-Dodd model. Extending the linear stability analysis to third order in the excitation amplitude, we construct explicit spatially localised corrections to the shape-mode oscillation and determine its nonlinear frequency shift using the Poincaré-Lindstedt method. Although both the second and third harmonics lie inside the continuous spectrum of the linearised fluctuation operator, the corresponding inhomogeneous equations admit exact localised particular solutions. We demonstrate that the nonlinear sources have vanishing on-shell overlaps with the scattering states at both harmonic frequencies, suppressing the corresponding radiative responses. We further investigate the role of integrability and show how a higher commuting symmetry of the Bullough-Dodd equation provides a perturbative selection-rule interpretation of these cancellations. Our results illustrate how higher integrable symmetries can constrain nonlinear resonances that are otherwise permitted by the linear spectrum.
Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program

I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.
Generalized Images and Multi-Index Transmutations for Brownian First Passage to Polynomial Boundaries

We study Brownian first passage to a finite polynomial boundary \[ F(t)=d+\sum_{j=2}^p c_jt^j. \] For every such boundary we construct a time-independent signed exterior image measure. After Brownian scaling its density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation whose kernel is the multivariate Wright series \[ \mathcal K_{\boldsymbolβ}(u,v) =\sum_{\bn\ne\mathbf0} \frac{\boldsymbolβ^{\bn}v^{|\bn|/2} (u-v)^{κ(\bn)-1}} {2^{κ(\bn)}\bn!Γ(κ(\bn))}, \qquad κ(\bn)=\sum_{j=2}^p(j-1)ν_j. \] An exact multivariate finite-difference cancellation yields exponential tail control of the image density. Consequently, on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian scale, its heat potential is the killed transition kernel and its boundary flux is the first-passage density. The image kernel is connected exactly with the differential transported-zero theory. A two-variable beta-moment transform carries its multivariate Wright seed to the entire constant-flux function associated with the polynomial boundary. Writing $K(\bn)=\sum jν_j$ and $W(\bn)=\sum(2j-1)ν_j$, we construct the graded spatial transmutation and prove the Laplace conjugacy \[ \Lap\A_{\bn}\Lap^{-1} =\frac{(-1)^{|\bn|}}{\bn!}k^{|\bn|} \left(-\frac1k\frac{d}{dk}\right)^{K(\bn)}. \] Thus the inverse transmutation generates the formal parameter expansion of the same first-passage problem. For $F(t)=At^2+Bt^3$ we also derive fifth- and eighth-order scalar annihilators and prove their exact rational factorization. Numerical experiments for two- and three-term polynomial boundaries independently agree with Durbin's equation to discretization accuracy.
Convergence rate of rescaled mean curvature flows over asymptotically conical shrinkers

We study how rapidly a rescaled mean curvature flow can approach an asymptotically conical self-shrinker. For a global normal graph with small $C^1$ norm and time-integrable $C^0$ norm, we prove that every nonzero solution has a leading asymptotic term given by an eigenfunction of the linearized operator $L$. In particular, a global graph $u$ with $e^{kt}\|u\|_{C^1}\to 0$ for every $k$ must coincide with the shrinker. We also construct a nonzero local graph over an immersed asymptotically conical shrinker with $C^2$ super-exponential decay in every bounded subset. This flow is defined on expanding open graphical domains. The example illustrates how rigidity fails in the local graphical setting.
Uniqueness Results for Static Asymptotically Locally Hyperbolic (ALH) Manifolds

We give uniqueness results for related classes of static asymptotically locally hyperbolic (ALH) manifolds. As an application, we give examples of one ended hyperbolic manifolds with boundary that are not optimal for the Positive Mass Theorem or for the Riemannian Penrose Inequality
Matrix Criteria for Mordell--Weil Ranks of Quartic Twists of $y^2=x^3+x$ with Root Number $-1$

We study the Mordell--Weil ranks of quartic twists $E_a:y^2=x^3+ax$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with global root number $-1$. For $D$ a product of $n\ge2$ distinct odd primes, a $2$-isogeny descent yields unconditional rank bounds for $E_D$, $E_{-D}$, and $E_{-2D}$ in terms of matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by additive Legendre symbols. Under suitable congruence and matrix-rank conditions, these curves have rank at most one, and rank one assuming the Mordell--Weil parity conjecture. For $E_{-2D}$, an additional explicit square condition establishes rank one unconditionally. Our results extend earlier two-prime criteria to arbitrary numbers of prime factors and further to fourth-power-free coefficients $H=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i^{e_i}$, where $e_i\in\{1,3\}$.
Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis

Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $Π_1^0$ statements about $ζ(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, Gödel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. The self-referential result converts a digital encoding framework with any uniform proof-compression principle for RH into an immediate non-constructive refutation of RH. Given that, with human input and computer assistance, $\mathsf{RH}$ has been formally verified in the Lean theorem prover strictly within constructive logic, this contradiction does not refute $\mathsf{RH}$. Instead, it falsifies $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$. We conclude by isolating the exact proof-theoretic obstruction---Pudlák's lower bound on bounded reflection proofs---showing why the analytic regularity of $\mathsf{RH}$ cannot compress logical self-reference, and exposing the limits of applying the Law of Excluded Middle to uncomputably bounded searches.
Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
Benjamin Budway; Makiko Sasada; Mykhaylo Shkolnikov

We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.
Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
Wolfram Bauer; Zhicheng Han; Zhipeng Yang

Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carathéodory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.
Cyril Morluyan Cordor; Anthony M. Bloch; Eitan Geva

Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.
Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras

We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.
Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
Ziheng Cheng; Xin Guo; Ben Hambly

In-context learning (ICL) enables transformers to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without updating their parameters. However, theoretical guarantees for transformers remain limited in general, and elusive in particular when target responses depend nonlinearly on the evolution of observed paths. We establish an ICL framework for path space, using path signature features. Building on the universal linear approximation property of signatures, we construct explicitly a causal softmax transformer with two attention heads per layer that emulates in-context Lasso. Under sparse signature approximation and suitable moment and concentration conditions, we establish finite-sample prediction error bounds. Our analysis goes beyond the IID data setting in the existing ICL theory, allowing dependence among demonstrations and the query. Experiments on in-context sparse recovery, nonlinear path regression, execution-cost prediction, and financial payoff inference demonstrate robustness to changes in observation grids and adaptation to unseen market environments. Across these prediction tasks, transformers with signatures match or outperform vanilla transformer baselines with substantially fewer trainable parameters, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of signature-based ICL.
Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length

When is an image ellipse the outline of a given ellipsoid with semi-axes $a <= b <= c? For a camera with square pixels, zero skew and known principal point, we show that it is an outline at focal length $f$ exactly when a cone ratio kappa(f), computed from two eigenvalues, is at most a/c; the middle semi-axis b plays no role. With f unknown, the admissible focal lengths form an interval; whether it is empty is decided by the smallest cone ratio over $f$, which, when attained, is obtained from an explicit quartic. The interval is bounded above only when the principal point is closer to the long axis of the ellipse than to its short axis. Thus one ellipse can rule out ellipsoids that are too round, never ones that are too elongated, and none if the principal point is unknown. Simulations and 45 Cassini images of Saturn's moons support the test.

We characterize order-theoretic disjointness of two elements $a$ and $b$ in the self-adjoint part of a $C^*$-algebra $A$ via the condition $aAb = \{0\}$ and the trivial intersection of closed two-sided ideals generated by $a$ and $b$. As a consequence, we show that disjoint complements coincide with the self-adjoint parts of annihilator ideals. We also prove that $A$ is commutative whenever every pair of algebraically orthogonal positive contractions in $A$ is disjoint. Finally, we establish corresponding commutativity criteria involving projections for real rank zero $C^*$-algebras.
Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples

Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.
Localization and homogenization of anisotropic fractional energies

We study the joint limit of localization ($s\uparrow1$) and periodic homogenization ($\varepsilon\downarrow0$) for anisotropic fractional energies with $p$-growth and oscillating kernels. We prove that the $Γ$-limit is governed by the single parameter $θ=\lim\varepsilon^{p(1-s)}$, and that its density is the convex combination $θ\mathcal{A}^* + (1-θ)\bar{\mathcal{A}}$ of the homogenized and the averaged densities. This shows that the picture recently obtained for quadratic energies also holds for every $p$ and for anisotropic kernels, with no regularity in the oscillating variable; the approach is different, and is based on convex duality. A nonlocal version of the duality argument gives the limit as $s\uparrow 1$ for a fixed kernel under weak assumptions, correcting a previous proof by the authors.
RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations

There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$, where $L(λ)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(λ)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.
Analysis and Optimal Approximation of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations with Unbounded Control Operators

In this work, we present new results on the well-posedness and approximation of the operator-valued Riccati equations that arise in the context of control systems with unbounded control operators, e.g. interior point and boundary control systems. We first prove that the Bochner integral form of the operator-valued Riccati equation is well-posed even if the control operator is unbounded. We then leverage the favorable structure of the Bochner integral form to prove that the error of approximate solutions are bounded by the approximation error of the process $C_0$-semigroup. This general result then leads to the correct prediction of optimal error estimates for the finite element approximation of the Riccati equation. The analysis is carried out on both the time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations and our numerical convergence study on the weakly damped wave process and the thermal process with delta function actuation operators corroborate the results of our analysis.
Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation

We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.
The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes

A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $χ^{-4/3}$, where $χ$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.

We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|Δ_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - δ}$ for any fixed $δ> 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.
Andrew Osborne; Rhine Samajdar; Andrew A. Houck

The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves

Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.
Farzan Vafa; Puskar Mondal; L. Mahadevan

Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.
Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
G Conant; J Freitag; C Terry
We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).
Fuzzy vectors from first and second moments: Affine consistency, carrying and sparsest realizations

When the probability law of a random vector cannot be identified, its mean and possibly singular covariance can often still be elicited. We consider fuzzy vectors with compact convex cuts as mathematically tractable representations of such a moment pair, and ask how they must be designed to rely only on this information. We postulate two modeling desiderata, independence of the choice of origin and basis, and invariance under embeddings into a higher-dimensional space. Under these requirements alone we show that, in every ambient dimension, every level set of the fuzzy vector must be a Mahalanobis ellipsoid centered at the mean. Its complete specification then amounts to the choice of a radial profile for each covariance rank. We call a fuzzy vector a carrier of the moment pair if at least one of its random-set selections has exactly the given mean and covariance. For an ellipsoidal fuzzy vector of rank $p\ge1$ with radial profile $ρ$, carrying is equivalent to $\int_0^1ρ(α)^2dα\ge p$, and equality characterizes the inclusion-minimal carriers within the fixed-shape Mahalanobis class. A discrete random vector with the same mean and covariance and the fewest equally weighted atoms has its atoms on a regular simplex in Mahalanobis coordinates. Completing this simplex under the rotations left free by the moments yields the minimum-volume crisp ellipsoid in the state space that carries them. The ellipsoidal representation also encodes interaction through the covariance matrix.
Rupture and far-field profiles for Hénon-type MEMS elliptic equation with pressure

Motivated by membrane touchdown in electrostatic microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) under external pressure, we study the Hénon-type elliptic equation $Δu=λ|x|^αu^{-p}+F$, $u>0$, where $N\ge2$, $λ,p>0$, $α>-2$, $F\in\mathbb R$, and $α<2p$ if $F\ne0$. Near the origin, we construct positive radial rupture solutions with $u(0)=0$ for $F\ne0$ and infinitely many non-radial but asymptotically radial ones for every $F$, and derive expansions to arbitrary order. On exterior domains $Ω_{R_0}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:|x|>R_0\}$, with no condition at the origin, we establish existence and uniqueness of positive solutions on $[R_0,\infty)$ for radial initial value problems with $u(R_0)>0$ if $p\ge1$, or if $F\ge0$ and $u'(R_0)\ge0$. We determine the leading behavior of all positive radial exterior solutions as $|x|\to\infty$ for $F>0$ and $F=0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$ and $α\ge0$. For possibly non-radial exterior solutions satisfying $u(r,θ)=A_\infty r^{σ_\infty}(1+o(1))$ uniformly in $θ$, with $A_\infty>0$ and $σ_\infty\in\mathbb R$, we uniquely determine the leading exponent and coefficient in all three pressure regimes, without derivative bounds on the remainder. Although pressure affects only higher-order terms near an asymptotically radial rupture point, its sign changes the leading-order behavior at infinity under the stated hypotheses. Local radial rupture solutions extend uniquely to $\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}$ for $F>0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$, with the classified far-field profiles under the corresponding hypotheses.
Idempotent generically stable measures in NSOP$_1$ groups

We prove the Idempotent Measure Conjecture for type-definable groups in theories whose Keisler randomization is NSOP$_1$. More precisely, every global idempotent frequency interpretation measure on such a group is the unique left-invariant and the unique right-invariant measure concentrating on its type-definable stabilizer. In particular, its support is a left-simple convolution semigroup and has a unique minimal left ideal. The announced theorem of Ben Yaacov, Chernikov and Ramsey that randomization preserves NSOP$_1$ (proof in the appendix) yields the corresponding conclusion for all type-definable groups in NSOP$_1$ theories.
Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories

We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.
Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game

Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual affine formulas with integer coefficients on residue classes. The same finite-state method extends four numerical tables of Zhang. We also give the entire augmented sequence for $c>\max S$ when the losing heaps of $S$ are exactly the multiples of a fixed integer.

A construction for a ternary perfect linear $2$-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy $r \geq 5$. The construction is recursive with seeds given for $5 \leq r \leq 7$. The construction of redundancy $r \geq 8$ is derived from a code of redundancy $r-3$ and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.
On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls

We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.
Bounds for the small Davenport constant of extraspecial groups of exponent three

Let $E_s$ be the extraspecial group of order $3^{2s+1}$ and exponent three. We prove $4s+2r+2\le d(E_s\times C_3^r)\le 4s+2r+3$ for $s\ge1$ and $r\ge0$. For $s\ge2$, the degree in the polynomial proof is optimal among weights depending only on group-element multiplicities modulo three. For $s=2$, we reduce the question in all ranks to an abelian subset-sum problem with a fixed set of forbidden values in a $77$-dimensional space. We show that this set, together with zero, contains no $76$-dimensional subspace. The equality $d(E_2\times C_3^r)=2r+10$ in all ranks is not established here.
Depth of leaves in closed linear $λ$-terms: exact recurrence, limit law and edge window

Let $K_n$ (resp.\ $D_n$) be the depth of a uniform leaf (resp.\ node) in a uniform closed linear $λ$-term of size $n$. A bijective \emph{grafting identity} yields an exact polynomial-time recurrence for the full depth profile. By the method of moments, $K_n/n$ converges in law to the density $3x/\sqrt{1-2x}$ on $[0,\frac12]$, i.e.\ $2K_n/n\to\Beta(2,\frac12)$, with $\mathbb E[K_n^r]/n^r\to3(r+1)!/(2r+3)!!$; likewise $1-2D_n/n\to\Beta(\frac12,1)$. A backward Markov chain gives the corresponding local limits for $k\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)n$. The limit density diverges at $\frac12$, and the profile has a second scale: a window of width $\sqrt n$ around $n/2$, which carries a fraction of order $n^{-1/4}$ of the nodes, at a density $n^{1/4}$ times larger than in the bulk. We prove that a single explicit function describes both regimes: uniformly in $d$, \[ n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(D_n=d)=g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}),\qquad n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(K_n=d)=\tfrac{3d}{n}\,g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}), \] where $g(y)=2^{-1/2}e^{-y^2}D_{-1/2}(2y)$ is a parabolic cylinder function. In particular $\mathbb P(K_n>n/2)\sim\frac34\,\mathbb E|Z|^{1/2}\,n^{-1/4}\approx0.6166\,n^{-1/4}$ with $Z$ standard Gaussian. The proofs rest on harmonic functions of the heat equation evaluated along the backward chain.

This AI-assisted article settles (partially) several conjectures coming from spline theory: Scherer--Shadrin conjecture on mirroring the sign patterns of polynomial derivatives is answered in the negative through a counterexample; the author's conjectures on the Lebesgue function of the orthoprojector onto spaces of polynomials multi-vanishing at an endpoint are answered in the affirmative; and Schumaker conjecture on interpolation with lacunary bivariate Bernstein polynomials is provided with solutions in a number of previously unknown situations.
A Boundary Comparison Method for Gaussian Fluctuations in Planar Euclidean Optimization

We develop a boundary comparison method for Gaussian fluctuations of optimization costs on planar random points, including traveling-salesman length, minimum perfect-matching length, and the Held--Karp relaxation. A local change can alter an optimal solution far from the modified points, making a direct decomposition into local contributions difficult. Our criterion requires the difference between the changes in the full and local costs caused by the same replacement to be controlled at the boundary scale, allowing a smaller-order $L^2$ excess. Under this condition, the centered difference between the total cost and the sum of independent cell costs vanishes in $L^2$. The multiscale argument shows that a nonvanishing variance of the cutting error would produce Gaussian tails incompatible with the boundary control. We obtain joint Gaussian limits for the three centered costs, using a conditional version for matching, and prove that the limiting covariance is positive definite in the Euclidean case. Convergence holds in quadratic Wasserstein distance for Poisson and fixed sample sizes. The results extend jointly to finitely many planar norms and to fixed sampling laws whose absolutely continuous component has a density positive almost everywhere on the square, with an arbitrary singular component.
Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I

We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-π^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.
Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
Andreas Chatziafratis; Guenbo Hwang; Georgia Karali

We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.
A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
Andrea Agazzi; David F. Anderson; Daniele Cappelletti; Lucie Laurence; Jonathan C. Mattingly

At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.
On the linearization of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation in $\mathbb{R}^N$
Massimo Grossi; Sérgio L. N Neves; Zoe Saudade Wynants

Let $u$ be a positive radial solution of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation $$-Δu=u^p \qquad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad p>\frac{N+2}{N-2}. $$ In this paper we classify the bounded solutions of the associated linearized operator $-Δw -pu^{p-1}w=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The resulting classification reveals the role of the threshold value $p=\frac{N + \sqrt{N^2 - 8N}}{4}$. In particular, above this threshold, the solutions are generated by the invariance of the problem under dilations and translations. Below this threshold, many new solutions appear, and their number tends to infinity as $p$ approaches the Joseph-Lundgren exponent and $N$ is large.
Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$

Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $χ=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.
Diophantine sets over global function fields

Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.
Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
