Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.
Double-dimer loops in the biased Aztec diamond converge to a diffeomorphic image of nested $CLE_4$

We superimpose two independent domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order $N$, with vertical weight $a>0$ and horizontal weight $1$. Represent each domino by the edge joining the centers of its two squares. The edges used by exactly one tiling form loops. After rescaling by $N^{-1}$, the full loop collection converges in law to the image of the nested conformal loop ensemble $\CLE_4$ under the diffeomorphism \[ w\longmapsto \frac{2(\Re w+\ii a\,\Im w)}{\sqrt{1+a^2}\,(1+|w|^2)} \] from the unit disk onto the liquid region of the rescaled diamond. Thus the bias rescales the horizontal and vertical coordinates of the unbiased limit. The topology of convergence records loop multiplicities and the order of traversal around each loop, up to reversal. Transfer estimates in the Krawtchouk basis control slab traversals and opposite crossings along entire sections, including where they meet the arctic ellipse. These estimates give tightness and, together with finite-puncture observables, identify the limit and rule out backtracking.
Hongyi B. Hu; Dung Nguyen; M. Amin Rahimian

We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $Θ\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.
Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
Bikun Li; Guo Zheng; Liang Jiang

Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.
Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$

We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.
Self-similar solutions for capillary water waves
Alvaro Carballeira; Gerard Castro-López; Eduardo García-Juárez; Javier Gómez-Serrano; Marcus Pasquariello

In this paper we prove the existence of self-similar solutions to the capillary water wave problem. In particular, this implies finite-time formation of singularities in the form of a corner, and retraction from a corner due to the time-reversibility of the equations. Unlike most self-similar smooth solutions, the solutions with $2/3$ time-length scaling are seen in experiments like pinch-off retraction, bubble bursting or jet formation. The proof involves a new argument through the regularization of the Hamiltonian and does not require the existence of an approximate profile. We believe this strategy has further implications in the construction of self-similar solutions of dispersive PDE.
Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm

We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=γ(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two. Interestingly, while Minimum Fill-in is fixed-parameter tractable in the number $k$ of added edges, Cop-Win Edge Completion, whose target class strictly contains the connected chordal graphs, is W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, even by $k+γ(G)$. We then give two lower bounds. The first, $\copfill(G)\ge 2n-m-b-c-1$, where $n,m,b,c$ count vertices, edges, nontrivial blocks, and components, is tight for partial 2-trees, giving a linear-time algorithm for the optimum value and a quadratic-time construction; for outerplanar graphs, an optimum completion preserving outerplanarity is found in linear time. The second, based on the cycle space modulo the subspace generated by triangles, gives $\copfill(G)=c-1+\sum_{i=1}^r(\ell_i-3)$ for block-cactus graphs with long cycle blocks of lengths $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$. We also show how the optimum behaves under disjoint unions and joins, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm for $P_4$-sparse graphs, including cographs, and exact formulas for complete multipartite graphs. In contrast to partial 2-trees and block-cactus graphs, an optimum cop-win completion can be much smaller than a minimum chordal one, already on complete bipartite graphs. Finally, we give FPT algorithms for $k+\mathrm{nd}(G)$, for the twin-cover number $t$ alone in time $2^{O(t^3)}n^{O(1)}$, and for $k+\mathrm{tw}(G)$.
Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted

We perform the complete light--cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $κ$--symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which is required to be nonvanishing and nontrivial in this limit for its consistency. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.
On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$

We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.
Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees

We study the Bergman projection $P_ω$ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_ω$, where $ω$ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_ω$ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $A^p_ω$ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $ω$ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_ω^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $L^p(ω) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $Ω\in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(Ω) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_Ω(\mathbb{D}) $.
Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions

We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli (2013); a proof of polynomial mixing remained one of the major challenges in the field. We prove this polynomial mixing time bound at all low temperatures. The key step is to establish fast mixing of the interface separating the plus and minus phases on a box with Dobrushin boundary conditions. In simpler models of height functions, polynomial bounds tend to rely on exact harmonic properties and connections to a discrete heat equation. However, the Ising interface exhibits microscopic defects that necessitate the development of a more robust method. We address this via a new multiscale approach to bound mixing times of general disordered random-walk bridges that homogenize to a Brownian bridge at mesoscopic scales. Another notable ingredient is a novel application of censoring to reduce the mixing time problem to proving only a weak Poincaré inequality, or warm-start mixing bound, allowing us to assume suitable regularity conditions on the interface and bubbles.
Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation

The use of one-bit quantized complex-valued data samples enables efficient distributed computation of an array data covariance. This reduced complexity covariance estimate can be used for adaptive beamforming, but requires careful diagonal loading and results in lower performance compared to a full-precision approach. Two main approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built out of complex one-bit data samples, and a ``hybrid'' cross-covariance between the one-bit data and the full precision data. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for the associated population and finite-sample matrices are derived and compared to the full precision results using tools from linear algebra and statistics. Many strong, well-separated interferers with low overlap with the signal of interest are assumed throughout, none of them dominant.
Modularity of Heegner Cycles and Arithmetic Inner Products on Kuga-Sato Varieties

For \(κ\ge2\), the principal part of a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight \(\tfrac32-κ\) determines a linear combination of codimension-\(κ\) Heegner cycles on a compact Kuga--Sato variety. We use isogeny correspondences to prove that every such combination vanishes in the Chow group with complex coefficients. These rational equivalences imply that the generating series of Heegner cycles is a Chow-valued cusp form of weight \(κ+\tfrac12\) at every level and for every compatible fundamental twist. We prove an arithmetic inner product formula for theta lifts on the modular curve \(X_0(N)\) and on higher-dimensional Kuga--Sato varieties. It expresses their height pairings in terms of central derivatives of quadratic twists of newform \(L\)-functions, with an explicit product of local operators on oldspaces. On each primitive newform line selected by the twist, the height of one projected Heegner cycle at a fundamental index with nonzero Fourier coefficient determines all pairings of projected cycles on that line. This specialization recovers the Gross--Zagier formula in weight two and the genus-character case of the Gross--Zagier--Zhang formula in higher weight.
A remark on cohomological and Chow decompositions of the diagonal
We construct a quartic double solid whose desingularization admits an integral cohomological decomposition of the diagonal but no Chow decomposition.
Standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart rings have unimodal $h$-vectors

We prove that the $h$-vector $(h_0,\ldots,h_s)$ of every standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart ring is unimodal, with a peak at position $\lceil s/2\rceil$. More generally, a standard graded Ehrhart ring has an alternatingly increasing $h$-vector if the radical of the ideal generated by the degree-one part of its canonical trace ideal contains the homogeneous maximal ideal. In characteristic zero or two, the generic Artinian reduction of each such ring has the strong Lefschetz property. We also prove unimodality for every standard graded nearly Gorenstein domain of dimension at least two with $h$-vector $(1,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, where $s\geq2$, provided that $h_1-h_s\leq1$. In the level case this $h$-vector is both concave and alternatingly increasing. If $h_1=h_s$, then $h_1=\cdots=h_s$.

We prove that the full group \(C^*\)-algebra \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) fails the local lifting property for all integers \(k,m\ge2\), and therefore disprove Ozawa's Strong Kirchberg Conjecture. Our proof is inspired by a construction of Ioana concerning Hilbert--Schmidt stability. We then strengthen this result by showing that \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) does not locally embed into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\). Consequently, the lifting property, the local lifting property, and local embeddability into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\) are not preserved under maximal tensor products.
Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices

Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.
A strict Neumann-Dirichlet eigenvalue inequality on planar domains

On simply connected, bounded planar Lipschitz domains it is known from our earlier work that the ($k+2$)-nd eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian cannot exceed the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. In this note we sharpen this statement by showing that this inequality is always strict. This was previously only known under additional assumptions.
Euler Characteristics of Perverse Sheaves on Complex Ball Quotients

Let $X=Γ\backslash\mathbb{B}^n$ be a finite-volume complex ball quotient with neat lattice. We prove that every nonzero algebraically constructible perverse sheaf on $X$ has positive Euler characteristic. More generally, we establish a criterion for strict positivity on smooth quasi-projective varieties whose logarithmic cotangent bundle is nef and admits an ample negative rational twist of the boundary divisor. For perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support, we give a lower bound in terms of the intrinsic geometry of $X$ for both proper and nonproper quotients. The bound depends on the systole of $X$ and tends to infinity with it. In particular, the minimum Euler characteristic among perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support tends to infinity as one passes to higher levels of any cofinal normal tower of finite covers. We also deduce lower bounds for the middle intersection Betti numbers of projective subvarieties and boundedness of supports with bounded middle intersection cohomology.
The Privacy Cost of Writing an Audit Receipt Before Its Context Is Known

An audit recorder must permit exact recovery with a small private index before it knows which questions a future reader will ask. A recursion on question partitions generates the decision trees, their eventwise costs and the price equations. A common-optimal-tree criterion explains when reduction to a fractional cover preserves the result. On uniform binary linear event spaces with four private roles, if every quartet is split evenly by some bit, optimal identification probability at expected follow-up budget $b$ is $(1+b)/2$. Otherwise it is $\min(1/2+b/3,3/4)$. We characterize all priors attaining the latter curve in its rising regime and derive a closed-form compiler for three binary fields. For a population tilted by one pairwise parity we obtain the full budget curve and a single recorder attaining it. On eight negotiated TLS suites the aligned populations allow a 60 percent follow-up rate at a 70 percent identification ceiling. A pairwise correlation with unchanged marginal field frequencies reduces that maximum to 40 percent. Across 960 local TLS sessions, the recorder recovered every negotiated suite using two private bits per session.

We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.
$K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line

Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $ω(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an étale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.
Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity

We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-Δu=|x|^{-γ}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0<q<1$, $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$ and nonnegative initial data $u_0\in C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $s\mapsto s^q$ is not Lipschitz continuous at the origin, the uniqueness of nonnegative solutions is a delicate issue. {For $u_0\not\equiv0$, it was known for small values of $γ$ and, more recently, under the additional condition $γ<N(1-q)$.} We prove that, for $u_0\not\equiv0$, uniqueness holds on the whole range $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$, which settles a conjecture of the authors. In fact, we establish a comparison principle between bounded subsolutions and supersolutions which are bounded from below by a multiple of the profile $t^{1/(1-q)}(|x|+\sqrt t\,)^{-γ/(1-q)}$. We then describe completely the set of nonnegative solutions emanating from $u_0\equiv0$: it consists of the trivial solution, of a unique positive solution $U$, and of the delayed copies $U(\cdot,(t-τ)_+)$, $τ>0$. The solution $U$ is radially symmetric and self-similar, it obeys {two-sided pointwise bounds by multiples of the same profile}, and it is the limit of the solutions with nontrivial data as the data decrease to zero. Finally, we show that $U$ describes the large-time behavior of every nontrivial solution. The proofs replace the singular Gronwall inequality used in earlier work by a quotient estimate which exploits the concavity of $s\mapsto s^q$ and requires no smallness condition.
A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula

We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.
Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
Ruben Lizarbe; Liliana Puchuri; Rudy Rosas

We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.
$\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces

We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.
Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up

Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^γy,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $γ\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a Bôcher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincaré condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\logρ$ term, $ρ=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $ρ^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.
A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
Gabriel Berk Pereira; Paul J. Goulart

First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. At fixed positive barrier parameter, matching the splitting metric to current barrier curvature equalises the primal variable corrections under the same regularisation and leaves a factor of two between the Moreau-slack corrections. With metrics frozen at a barrier solution, local analysis identifies when doubling improves (local) convergence and when the primal solve remains the bottleneck. Metric choices that simplify linear solves (eg make them diagonal) become Newton regularisations, exposing a shared convergence cost associated with computational convenience. Finally, a computable defect in the regularised Newton equations gives an accuracy-based criterion for reusing a splitting factorisation.
Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem

For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.
Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process

We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.
A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem
Sweta Chakraborty; Deepjyoti Goswami; Saumya Bajpai

This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results

We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed symplectic manifolds and fails on others, thereby defining a new symplectic rigidity invariant. We also introduce the non-displaceability width of a continuous map, defined as the infimum of the radii for which a non-displaceable thick fiber exists, and use it to obtain quantitative obstructions to uniform approximation by maps with small Poisson brackets.
A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint

We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.
Ilias S. Kotsireas; Huaning Liu; Arne Winterhof

We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.
Griffiths-Dwork Reduction For Smooth Hypersurfaces in Grassmannians

We give an explicit Griffiths-Dwork pole-order reduction algorithm for a smooth hypersurface $Z$ in a Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$. Under two arithmetic conditions on $k,n$, and the degree of $Z$, the residue construction describes the Hodge filtration on the middle cohomology of the complement in terms of the Jacobian ring. We explicitly characterize the required cohomological vanishings. As applications, we compute group representations on the vanishing cohomology of two symmetric hyperplane sections of $\mathrm{Gr}(3,10)$ and deduce maximal Picard rank for their associated Debarre-Voisin fourfolds. We also compute a Picard-Fuchs equation for a pencil of symmetric Gushel-Mukai fivefolds.
Sharp High-Dimensional Self-Normalized Central Limit Theorems

We study Gaussian approximation over all coordinate rectangles for coordinatewise self-normalized sums of iid centered random vectors. The Gaussian reference has the population correlation matrix, which may be singular. Under a fixed bound $K>1$ on the standardized marginal third absolute moments, uniform approximation over the corresponding moment class holds exactly when $d=o(\sqrt n)$ under arbitrary coordinate dependence. If $R_{jk}\le1-a$ for $j\ne k$ and a fixed $a\in(0,1]$, the necessary and sufficient condition becomes $\log d=o(n^{1/3})$. For marginal moment order $q\ge3$, we also allow the correlation gap $a_n$ to depend on $n$. For every fixed $0<β<1/3$, uniform approximation over the corresponding class in dimension $d_n=\lfloor e^{n^β}\rfloor$ holds if and only if $a_n\log n\to\infty$. Under arbitrary dependence, we determine the sharp error order $1\wedge\{d/n^{(q-2)/2}\}^{1/q}$ for every $q\ge3$ and $d\ge2$. At a fixed positive gap, we identify, for every $q>2$, the supremum of the decay exponents in uniform error bounds that allow fixed logarithmic factors. The proofs replace observations one at a time, keeping their contributions to both numerator and denominator in the same expansion. The resulting weights depend only on the retained sample, allowing the remainders to be controlled by marginal moments.
On the stress-bienergy tensor of conformal immersions and hypersurfaces

We study the stress-bienergy tensor $\bar S_2$ of a conformal immersion $ϕ:(M^m,\bar g)\to(N^n,h)$ with conformal factor $λ$, and we compute it, together with its trace and its divergence, in terms of $λ$ and of the second fundamental form of the associated isometric immersion. This gives a characterization of biconservative conformal immersions and, for hypersurfaces, we prove that $\mathrm{div}\,\bar S_2=0$ if and only if the tangent part of the bitension field vanishes. We introduce conformally biconservative hypersurfaces and show that a totally umbilical hypersurface of a space form is conformally biconservative with a non-constant conformal factor if and only if this factor is an isoparametric function satisfying an explicit ordinary differential equation. We illustrate this result with several examples, in which dimension four plays a special role. Finally, we study the equation $\bar S_2=0$: on a compact manifold of dimension $m\neq 4$, it forces the associated isometric immersion to be harmonic.
Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points

In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.
Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions

We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $ϕ^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.
Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs

Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist. On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.
Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space

We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by Pérez, Rodríguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(κ,τ)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $τ$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.
When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces

How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
Mohit Tekriwal; Het Mankad; Naifeng Zhang; Keita Teranishi; Sahil Bhola; Daisuke Uchida; Jean-Baptiste Jeannin; Franz Franchetti; Karthik Duraisamy; Jeffrey Vetter; Yohann Dudouit

Agentic AI tools have recently had success in mathematical reasoning. Both general purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, and specialized mathematics agents such as Aristotle, have been used for formalizing mathematical problems such as Fermat's last theorem, Erdős problems and several IMO level math problems. However, much of these efforts are concentrated in the pure mathematics domain, which benefits from relatively self-contained theorem statements, fixed mathematical representation and extensive support in existing formal libraries. Applied mathematics, on the other hand, presents additional challenges because the source may describe a computational procedure or modeling transformation rather than a declarative theorem. Our primary contribution is a cross-layer taxonomy of failure modes and an analysis of the form of expert feedback required at each layer to recover mathematical soundness. From these observations, we derive a workflow for recurring proof patterns and practical guidance for using AI agents while preserving mathematical soundness. We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.
Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity

The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.
Accurate Products, Inaccurate Inverse: Emulated FP64 BLAS in Blocked Triangular Inversion

FP64 emulation on integer tensor units now ships in cuBLAS and GEMMul8, and each emulated matrix product can be checked against an accuracy grade. We ask if a routine built from such products inherits their accuracy, and show that blocked triangular inversion, the core of LAPACK's inverse of a symmetric positive definite matrix, does not. Under fixed-precision emulation every product passes the grade-B error bound of Demmel et al., yet the inverse errs at 7.1e-2, against 2.0e-15 natively. The matrices are well conditioned after diagonal scaling, but the scaling spans 64 binades. The cause is one product, T = X22 L21, whose summed index carries both the diagonal scaling and its inverse, which a grade-B bound does not absorb. Computing those products natively restores native accuracy; leaving any one of them emulated does not. The pattern holds on four GPUs, and on real covariance matrices the fixed-precision routes lose up to about four orders of accuracy. Equilibration, a solve-based association and cuBLAS's automatic dynamic precision avoid the loss, and an exact error recurrence audits a completed run. On an RTX 4090 the fastest accurate emulated inversion takes 0.40 of cuSOLVER's time. Where each product's scaling falls decides if per-product accuracy carries over to a composite routine, and that is what builders of emulated libraries need to check.
Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
Hoang T. Nguyen; Deepjyoti Deka; Priya L. Donti; Varsha Pendyala; Nurali Virani; Wajid Muneer; Reetam Sen Biswas

This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.

Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $Ω$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. In Carnot groups, we show that pliability and the Lusin approximation property are preserved by quotient maps, and we deduce several applications. For instance, we show that, in free Carnot groups of step at least 3 with at least $2$ generators, every horizontal direction is non-pliable, the Lusin property fails in a strong sense, and there is a Lipschitz curve that is purely unrectifiable with respect to smooth horizontal curves. We investigate the geometric properties of free boundaries associated with nonnegative viscosity solutions to the infinity Laplace equation with strong absorption $$ Δ_\infty u=λu_+^m, \qquad λ>0,\quad 0<m<3. $$ We first establish a sharp distance-to-free-boundary regularity estimate with an explicit optimal coefficient, which coincides with the constant in the non-degeneracy estimate. As consequences, we obtain a sharp lower density bound of $1/2$ for the positive phase, a locally finite covering of the free boundary by Lipschitz graphs, and quantitative local estimates for its $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the question raised by Araújo, Leitão, and Teixeira (J. Funct. Anal. {\textbf 270} (2016), no. 6, 2249-2267). The underlying barrier mechanism also suggests possible extensions to more general equations.

We compute the ambient sectional curvature and obtain a formula for the intrinsic sectional curvature of nondegenerate surfaces in terms of their Gauss and mean curvatures. We provide a complete classification of cylindrical surfaces with constant intrinsic sectional curvature, covering all causal characters of $\mathcal{V}$ and of the rulings. For rotational surfaces whose axes are parallel to $\mathcal{V}$, we reduce the constant-curvature condition to an ordinary differential equation. Explicit solutions are obtained for null axes and, in the metric case, for surfaces with zero intrinsic sectional curvature.

Written in Lagrangian mass coordinates, the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations for a polytropic gas become a single second-order equation for the radius $r(t,m)$ of the shell enclosing mass $m$, with adiabatic index $γ>1$ and entropy profile $S(m)$. Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
Yuan Guo; Stefanus Jasin; Chen-An Lin

Organizations use large language models (LLMs) to classify jobs that differ in uncertainty and the cost of errors. Querying additional models may improve accuracy, but it also incurs fees and increases congestion at shared servers. We study congestion-aware adaptive routing (CAAR) policies that adapt model selection and stopping decisions to observed outputs while accounting for the steady-state congestion they generate. The objective is to minimize the long-run average cost of misclassification penalties, query fees, and holding costs. We can represent CAAR policies as a mixture of decision trees, and derive exact holding costs for first-come-first-served servers with exponential service times and processor-sharing servers with general service times. We formulate a convex optimization problem with unique optimal model loads. Congestion prices capture the marginal system-wide holding costs of additional queries and guide routing and stopping decisions through a Bayesian dynamic program. We characterize optimal stopping decisions and identify models whose information does not justify their cost. A column-generation algorithm computes optimal CAAR policies and provides an explicit optimality-gap bound. We also bound the additional cost of limiting cascade depth relative to full-depth CAAR. Finally, under a common query-depth limit, cascades with a predetermined model order can be arbitrarily more costly than optimal CAAR, even when the order is randomized and stopping decisions adapt to observed outputs. Numerical experiments distinguish the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design.
Quantum Approximation and Integration in Sobolev Spaces -- Low Smoothness

We study the complexity of approximation and integration in Sobolev spaces in the quantum setting of information-based complexity theory (IBC). Previous results have been obtained under the assumption that the embedding condition holds. Here we drop this assumption and use a quantum version of a previously developed stochastic discretization technique.
The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles

We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.

We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.
Gibbs-type allelic partitions of $Λ$-coalescents: a rigidity theorem

Let $Π^θ_n$ be the allelic partition induced by a $Λ$-coalescent with mutation rate $θ$ under the infinitely-many-alleles model. We characterise the finite measures $Λ$ for which the EPPF of $Π^θ_n$ is of Gibbs type: the only possibility is $Λ=c\,δ_0$, corresponding to Kingman's coalescent and the Ewens sampling formula. Starting from Möhle's recursion, we derive its EPPF form and organise the Gibbs constraints by the difference between sample size and number of blocks. Roman-Type Domination on Bisplit Graphs: Hardness and Inapproximability

Inspired by the structure and name of split graphs, bisplit graphs have three independent sets $I,A,B$, where every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, and vertices of $I$ may have arbitrary neighborhoods in the core $A\cup B$. Thus they have a complete bipartite core together with the remaining vertices, making them a structured setting in which to study how core size affects complexity. Mann and Fernau's construction already implies NP-completeness of perfect Roman domination on bisplit graphs with a singleton core side \citep[Theorem~20]{mann-fernau-pr}. Motivated by this result, we study all four Roman-type domination problems across further core-size regimes: we prove NP-completeness when one core side has size one or two, and when both sides have size at least three. For perfect Italian domination, even deciding whether prescribed core labels of total weight two can be extended is NP-complete on bipartite bisplit graphs. The $4^k$ Roman cluster-deletion bound is known; the other bounds follow from our dynamic programs. To our knowledge, the latter parameter has not previously been studied explicitly for domination variants.

The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

Let $μ\in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|μ|=1$, and assume that $μ$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_γ$ denote the Bishop quadric with $γ= 1/\sqrt{2+μ+μ^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $μ$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_γ$. We prove this conjecture.

We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.
Kennedy Obinna Idu; Francesco Paolo Maiale

We prove an a priori $C^{2,α}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side.

We define symmetric multiple zeta values, unified zeta functions, and finite zeta values in the Schur setting. We also show a vanishing property for a symmetric sum of finite Schur multiple zeta values, generalizing a result obtained by Hoffman for finite multiple zeta values.

We construct a positive solution of an exterior Dirichlet problem for a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian operator on each smooth strictly star-shaped domain whose boundary curvatures lie in $Γ_k$. We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.
A discontinuous Galerkin method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy model
Sweta Chakraborty; Deepjyoti Goswami; Saumya Bajpai

In this paper, we have analysed a discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for the coupled surface-subsurface flow, which is modelled by the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy (NSD) equations. While the DG method has been applied for the spatial discretization of both Navier-Stokes and Darcy equations, for time, we have employed the first-order backward Euler scheme. The fully discrete error analysis has been carried out for both velocity and pressure of the Navier-Stokes equations, and for the piezometric head of the Darcy equation, and optimal estimates have been derived. Our analysis relies on appropriate treatments of the nonlinear convective term from the Navier-Stokes equations, along with the interface conditions that couple the system. We have employed a modified Oseen operator on an appropriate DG setup along with the standard duality argument to derive optimal error estimates in the L2-norm for the unknowns, which are novel for the NSD equations within the DG framework and are supported by numerical simulations demonstrating the scheme's efficiency.
A Hitchhiker's Guide to LR B-Splines
Carla Manni; Francesco Patrizi; Hendrik Speleers

We review the theoretical foundations of locally refined (LR) B-splines, a natural extension of univariate B-splines to multivariate, locally refined, and generally unstructured box partitions. LR B-splines are defined using standard tools from B-spline theory, such as knot insertion, and retain key properties including locality, non-negativity, and a piecewise polynomial structure. Our presentation starts from the definition of spline spaces over box partitions and discusses the instability of their dimension formula due to the presence of a homological term. Conditions ensuring the stabilization of the dimension naturally motivate the construction of LR meshes and LR B-splines. We subsequently analyze the spanning properties of LR B-splines, with particular emphasis on completeness, linear dependence, and local linear independence. We also address known characterizations and refinement strategies ensuring that the resulting LR B-splines preserve the desirable properties of tensor-product B-splines.
Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks

We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $π_v/β_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(π_v/β_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.
Probabilistic well-posedness of dispersive PDEs beyond variance blowup II: quadratic nonlinear wave equation
Guopeng Li; Jiawei Li; Shao Liu; Tadahiro Oh; Nikolay Tzvetkov

We study the quadratic nonlinear wave equation (NLW), posed on the two-dimensional torus, with rough Gaussian random initial data beyond the variance blowup threshold observed by Okamoto and the fourth author (2021). By introducing a suitable vanishing multiplicative renormalization constant on the frequency-truncated Gaussian random initial data, we prove that the corresponding solutions converge in law to a solution to the stochastic NLW with zero initial data, driven by a Gaussian space-time noise whose temporal covariance at each spatial Fourier mode is given by the Bessel function of order $0$. We also show that the solution to the limiting equation almost surely blows up in a finite time, and that the convergence above holds on every compact time interval before the maximal existence time. %on the maximal time of existence. A main new ingredient is the analysis of the oscillatory covariance of the second Picard iterates. We identify the limiting covariance by averaging the leading oscillatory phase over the angular variable. In contrast to our previous work on the Benjamin-Bona-Mahony equation (2025), multilinear dispersive smoothing plays an essential role both in proving tightness of the second Picard iterates and in controlling the rough nonlinear interactions via paracontrolled analysis. The resulting gain of a quarter of a derivative persists in the limit, where it is reflected in the decay of the Bessel covariance.
Quartic hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{A}^3$ isomorphic to the affine plane

In 1975 Abhayankar and Moh have shown that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 all polynomial embeddings of the affine line into the affine plane are equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. For embeddings of the affine plane into $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose image is a hypersurface of degree 3, it is shown in arXiv:1912.02144 that they are also equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. We will consider the case where the image is a quartic hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ and classify all such hypersurfaces up to affine automorphisms.
Codimension two complements in hyperbolic products
Hyeran Cho; Jean-François Lafont; Nicholas Miller; Barry Minemyer

Let $M$ be a finite-volume locally symmetric manifold modeled on $\H^m \times \H^n$, and let $S$ be a compact, totally geodesic, codimension two submanifold of $M$ modeled on $\H^{m-1} \times \H^{n-1}$. In this paper, we initiate the study of manifolds of the form $N = M \setminus S$. In the case where $M$ is a product and $S$ is connected, we prove that such $N$ admit complete, finite-volume, $A$-regular metrics with non-positive sectional curvature. We also deduce some topological properties of $N$, and algebraic properties of $π_1(N)$. In the case where $M$ is irreducible, we show that $N$ admits {\it almost non-positive curvature}. Similar results hold for manifolds $X_d$, which are $d$-fold branched covers of $M$ ramified over $S$. Along the way, we show that there are infinitely many commensurability classes of such pairs $(M,S)$, and develop general curvature formulas for doubly warped product metrics, which may be of independent interest.
Closed-Form Formula for $d_{\mathrm{critical}}(a_0)$ in Large Fully Connected Power Grids

Kadloor and Santhi (arXiv:1011.4098) modeled cascading failures in a large fully connected power grid by a coupled four-variable recursion for the minimum surviving load $a_n$, the mean failed load $μ_{n-1}$, the redistributed load $\mathcal{D}_n$, and the stagewise failure probability $p_n$. They noted that the recursion was not tractable and identified the critical disturbance $d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ by simulation. We show that the recursion telescopes exactly into a one-dimensional monotone map $a_{n+1} = g(a_n)$. This yields the threshold in closed form: $1 - a_0 = d_{\mathrm{critical}}\,(1 + \ln(1 + 1/d_{\mathrm{critical}}))$, or explicitly in terms of the lower branch $W_{-1}$ of the Lambert W function. We prove a sharp dichotomy. For $d_m \le d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ the cascade halts with limiting load $a_0 + d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ at criticality and surviving fraction $1/(1 + d_{\mathrm{critical}})$. For $d_m > d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ a complete outage occurs in finitely many steps.
Higher-Order Minkowski Inequalities via Gradient-Weighted Hessian Potentials

We prove a sharp boundary inequality for exterior potentials of a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian equation under regularity, level-curvature, flux conservation, and radial decay hypotheses. The inequality bounds a power of the Newton flux by the normalized integral of $H_k^p/H_{k-1}^{p-1}$, and equality characterizes balls. After a conformal change of metric, two Newton-tensor divergence identities give comparisons between regular levels even when the slab between them contains critical points. For smooth strictly star-shaped domains with strictly $k$-convex boundary, a companion existence theorem supplies exterior potentials for $p$ close to one. We identify the limiting flux with the integral of $H_{k-1}$ and recover the sharp consecutive Minkowski inequality, including its equality case.
The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces

We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{N,s}$ such that for every measurable set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of finite positive measure, $$ \sup\Bigl\{\frac{1}{|Ω|}\int_Ωe^{α_{s,N}|u|^{\frac{p}{p-1}}}dx: u\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^N), u=0\text{ a.e. on }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΩ, [u]_{s,p}\le 1\Bigr\}\le C_{N,s}, $$ where $[u]_{s,p}$ is the Gagliardo seminorm and $α_{s,N}$ is the upper threshold found by Parini and Ruf for $N\ge 2$ and by Iula for $N=1$. Moreover, the constant $α_{s,N}$ is sharp. This answers two of their questions. We use a nonlocal version of Moser's one-dimensional lemma. The $p$-th moment of a translation kernel on the logarithmic half-line determines the sharp coefficient, and finiteness of the next moment characterizes the endpoint. We obtain sharp singular, whole-space, Adachi--Tanaka type, concentration-compactness and affine inequalities. When the Euclidean distance in the seminorm is replaced by the gauge of an origin-symmetric star body $K$, we determine the sharp exponent for each fixed $K$ and show that it exceeds the volume-normalized exponent unless $K$ is an ellipsoid. The same exponents are sharp for regional seminorms on bounded Lipschitz domains in dimensions $N\ge 2$. We prove attainment of the critical supremum on balls for $N\ge 2$ and $s$ close to one. In the Hilbert case $N=1$, $s=1/2$, we compute the concentration level of the singular problem on an interval using a sharp weighted logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Consequently, the critical supremum is attained for every singular weight $|x|^{λ-1}$, $0 < λ\le 1$.
Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system

This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.
A Classification of Low Genus Modular Curves

Let $G$ be an open subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\in G$. Associated to $G$, there is a modular curve $X_G$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ which parametrizes elliptic curves with $G$-level structure. We give a classification of modular curves with genus equal to a fixed nonnegative integer $g$. In particular, we show that all modular curves of genus $g$ lie in finitely many families of $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}}$-twists of modular curves. We also describe an algorithm for computing all families of modular curves of a fixed genus $g$ and use this to compute projective models for these modular curves. This algorithm has been fully implemented for $g \leq 12$. In an appendix with Yongyuan Huang and Rakvi, we describe two algorithms, one for computing rational functions on modular curves given as quotients of two modular forms of the same weight, and the other for computing models for the generic fibers of universal elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}_G$, where $G\subset \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an open subgroup satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\notin G$.
Eigenvalues of doubly stochastic matrices in large orders

For $1\le k\le N$, every point in the convex hull of the $k$th roots of unity is an eigenvalue of some doubly stochastic matrix of order $N$. Perfect and Mirsky asked whether any other eigenvalues occur. We prove that the union of these polygons is the whole region for every $N\ge450$. Our pencil-and-paper proof for $N\ge10^{30}$ starts with an eigenvector $v$ of Euclidean norm one. Place one unit of mass at each coordinate $v_j$. If $Av=zv$, row $i$ draws mass $A_{ij}$ from each mark $v_j$, so the mass it receives has centre $zv_i$. The column sums ensure that each mark supplies one unit in total. It follows that the sum of the row variances is $1-|z|^2$. Since the regular $N$-gon contains the disk of radius $\cos(π/N)$, an eigenvalue outside the polygons would force this sum below $\sin^2(π/N)$. We use this bound to compare permutations of the outer marks and to follow a randomly chosen mark through a quarter turn. To reach $450$, we count marks between concentric circles and verify a finite set of inequalities by computer. We also determine the regions in orders five and six by computer-assisted proofs. At order five the full region is obtained by adding to the polygons the segments from the origin to two conjugate arcs traced by roots of quartic polynomials. At order six the square, pentagon and hexagon give the whole region.
Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
Camilo Castro-Landolt; Rabsan Galib Ahmed; Graeme Smith

Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals $γ+\frac{1-γ}{d}$ for transmission probabilities $0<γ\le \frac{1}{2}$ and logical dimension $d$. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.
Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
Pierre-Emmanuel Caprace; Alex Loué; Andreas Thom

Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, φ_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $φ_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.
The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs

By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $α^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $α\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $α^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.
A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products

For a positive semidefinite matrix $X$, let $μ_k(X)$ be the minimum of the least eigenvalues of its principal submatrices of order $k$. For positive semidefinite $A,B$ of order $n$, we prove \[ μ_{i+j-1}(A\circ B)\geqμ_i(A)μ_j(B), \qquad i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\},\quad i+j-1\leq n, \] and characterize equality when the right-hand side is positive. The resulting symmetric least-eigenvalue bound \[ λ_{\min}(A\circ B)\geq \max_{1\leq i\leq n}μ_i(A)μ_{n-i+1}(B) \] recovers the classical Schur lower bounds at endpoint choices and can be exact even when both factors are singular. It is incomparable with the projection bound from a recent companion paper, and combining the two bounds can improve on both. The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $μ_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. Multifactor and Khatri--Rao consequences are also given.
The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums

Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.
A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT

We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.
The Exact Value of the Rankin Number gamma_{5,2}

The Rankin number gamma_{5,2} measures the exact upper bound for the squared determinant of the densest 2-dimensional sublattice of any 5-dimensional lattice of determinant one. We prove that gamma_{5,2}=16^{1/5}, attained by D*_5.
Coherent Recovery of Nested Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel Using Erasure Decoding and Quantization
Aditya Guhagarkar; S. Sandeep Pradhan; Achilleas Anastasopoulos

Motivated by quantum capacity results, we revisit nested binary linear codes for the quantum erasure channel through a packing-covering viewpoint: the outer code supports erasure reconstruction, while the inner code performs erasure quantization. We turn this perspective into two explicit decoder architectures.
