Architecture I requires no stabilizer-syndrome measurements and combines a classical peeling decoder and erasure quantizer with corresponding coherent quantum reconstruction and cleanup operations that disentangle the logical state from inaccessible erasure-environment branches. Architecture II goes one step further and implements erasure belief propagation directly through reversible ternary quantum gates, providing quantum state healing that reconstructs erased symbols while leaving unerased code states unperturbed. We establish sufficient conditions for exact recovery of arbitrary logical states, and illustrate both architectures using the Steane code, including explicit scheduling procedures and coherent quantum circuits.

For a Hermitian Wigner matrix $M_n$ and complex $α$ with $|α|\leq1$, we study the $α$-characteristic polynomial $\det_α(zI-M_n)$, which interpolates between the characteristic polynomial ($α=-1$) and the permanental polynomial ($α=1$). Assuming finite fourth moments off the diagonal and second moments on it, we show that this polynomial, normalized by its expectation, converges in distribution off the segment $\sqrt{-α}\,[-2,2]$ to the Wick exponential of an explicit Gaussian analytic function, with the same Gaussian modes for every $α$. As consequences, all zeros lie near this segment with probability tending to one, the empirical zero measure converges to a rotated semicircle law, and analytic linear statistics of the zeros satisfy a central limit theorem. We also show that $\det_α(zI-M_n)$ is approximated, with vanishing relative error, in terms of the characteristic polynomial of $M_n$ at a transformed point. The proof writes the $α$-characteristic polynomial as a polymer gas, which becomes asymptotically ideal after an exact resummation over matchings.
Trace-class perturbations of Voiculescu's free semicircular families
Minghui Ma; Rui Shi; Tianze Wang

Let $\{s_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ be the standard free semicircular family on the full Fock space $\mathcal H=\mathcal F(\ell^2(Λ))$, where $|Λ|\geqslant2$. For any family $\{K_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ of self-adjoint trace-class operators with $γ=\sum_{j\inΛ}\|K_j\|_1<\infty$, we prove that the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand $\mathcal P$ of the von Neumann algebra $W^*(\{s_j+K_j\colon j\inΛ\})$ is isomorphic to the free group factor $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_Λ)$. As an application, we show that the set of irreducible operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not dense in the trace-class norm. For each fixed $γ>0$, the possible values of the Murray--von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal P}(z_{\mathcal P}\mathcal H)$ form the interval $[1,1+γ)$, where $z_{\mathcal P}$ is the identity of $\mathcal P$.
Strong Subdifferentiability in Bochner Function spaces $L^{p}(μ, X)$

In this article, for $1\leq p<\infty$, we provide a characterization of strongly subdifferentiable points of $L^{p}(μ, X)$, when $X^*$ is separable and $μ$ is the Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$. For $f\in L^{p}(μ, X)$ with $\|f\|_{p}=1$ we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferetiable at $f$ if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable at $f(t)$ for almost every \(t\in[0,1]\) with $f(t)\neq 0$. Moreover, for a separable Banach space $X$, we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferentiable if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable.
Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
Zhenyu Du; Xiongfeng Ma; Vlatko Vedral; Jinzhao Sun

While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.
A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle

We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.
We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.
Information-Theoretic Generalization for Adaptive Learning Under Privacy and Fairness Constraints
Amirreza Zamani; Parastoo Sadeghi; Mikael Skoglund

Adaptive learners may update, select, and stop models after repeatedly examining the same data. Privacy and fairness constraints regulate this adaptation only selectively: they limit information about a private or sensitive coordinate, whereas task generalization depends on information about the coordinate on which loss is evaluated. We develop a unified information-theoretic framework for this mismatch. For a finite-alphabet pair $(A,B)$, we define directly the residual-information certificate $ h_ε(P_{AB})=\min\{H(B),H(B| A)+ε\}. $ A chain-rule transfer inequality converts a bound on $I(W;A)$ into an upper bound on $I(W;B)$, which can be inserted into a mutual-information generalization inequality. We first establish a transcript-level composition theorem for sequential learners. Conditional per-update information budgets add along the transcript, and the resulting certificate remains valid for history-dependent checkpoint selection, bounded stopping, and independent heterogeneous data batches. Under selective privacy, the learner observes $(X^n,Y^n)$, protects $X^n$, and incurs loss on $Y^n$. Under fairness, the learner observes $(S^n,X^n,T^n)$, limits dependence on the sensitive block $S^n$, compresses $X^n$, and incurs loss on $T^n$. The bounds expose the residual entropies $H(Y| X)$, $H(T| S)$, and $H(T| X)$ and the cumulative information cost of adaptation. We retain block and individual-sample bounds, task-compression refinements, per-output total-variation privacy, empirical-to-population demographic-parity transfer, and finite-alphabet information-parity transfer. FRL/EFRL/SFRL/ESFRL constructions study the tightness of the task-information upper bounds.
Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels

We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $Δ(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.
The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
Jun Gao; Oleg Pikhurko; Mingyuan Rong; Shumin Sun

The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.
The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces

We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.
Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds

Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ<γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ=γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $γ_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.
Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups

We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $σ$-local compactness, $σ$-compactness, the Lindelöf property, and left $ω$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindelöf property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.
Lessons from Chess: Mathematics in the Age of AI

The history of chess offers a perspective on the growing role of artificial intelligence in mathematics. We explore the parallels and limitations of this analogy and consider possible directions for mathematical research, education, and the public perception of mathematics.
On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}

For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_δ$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.
Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices

We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.
On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps

To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ is of class $k$. $\boldsymbol{4}$. For generic $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^k$, $Σ_{Q}$ contains $\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$ collections of ellipsoids of codimension $2$ consisting of degenerate parabolic points. $\boldsymbol{5}$. If $k>\ell$, the parabolic set in $Σ_{Q}$ (if any) is a union of hyperplane closed discs bounded by ellipsoids. $\boldsymbol{6}$. The above ellipsoids (items $4$ and $5$) are in bijection with the isolated singular points in $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$.
Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Ampère equation

We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Ampère density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(Ω)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(Ω\).
Yinji Li; Haoyuan Sun; Zhiwei Wang; Xiangyu Zhou

We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact Kähler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact Kähler manifolds.
A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
Harald Garcke; Yifei Li; Robert Nürnberg; Quan Zhao

We introduce a geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation for the $L^2$-gradient flow of a class of curvature-dependent energies of closed hypersurfaces, where the energy density depends on the mean curvature and the unit normal. A square-root auxiliary variable converts the geometric energy into a quadratic functional. Combining its evolution equation with a skew-symmetric treatment of surface transport yields a weak formulation whose energy law depends only on the normal velocity and is therefore independent of the chosen tangential motion. We construct monolithic nonlinear parametric finite element methods by coupling a common IEQ discretization with one of two geometric formulations that accommodate either the Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) tangential velocity or the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential velocity. Both fully discrete approximations satisfy an unconditional decay estimate for the discrete quadratic energy. We further extend the construction to anisotropic Willmore flow, and to $H^{-1}$-gradient flows. A variety of numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the introduced methods.
On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms

In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.
On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions

Let $κ$ be $λ$-supercompact for a regular $λ>κ$. We show that if $λ$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $κ$, $\diamondsuit(S^λ_{\geqκ})$ implies that every ${<}κ$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $λ$ is a projection of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $κ$-distributive projections of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $κ$-distributive forcings of size $λ$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.
Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent

Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $π$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.
Support-Constrained Local Randomizers for Robust Private Distribution Learning
Amirreza Zamani; Parastoo Sadeghi; Mikael Skoglund

Local differential privacy protects users before data collection, but full-support randomizers can be wasteful on ordered, metric, or semantic alphabets. We study support-constrained local randomizers for robust private discrete learning. Restricting reports to input neighborhoods reduces reporting distortion but creates support mismatch. Under range-restricted approximate local differential privacy, a relational guarantee weaker than ordinary all-pairs local differential privacy, we decompose the exact hockey-stick defect into support leakage and overlap excess loss. For line-supported sparse randomized response, we derive the exact defect, solve the joint privacy-distortion problem in closed form at each radius, and prove a privacy-imposed support lower bound. For distribution estimation, we obtain an exact finite-sample risk identity and show that the least-favorable law over any closed convex uncertainty set is a Euclidean projection. On cyclic alphabets, the uniform law is uniquely least favorable, nominal and minimax mechanism rankings coincide, and the minimax risk obeys spectral upper and lower bounds. This diagnoses why prior shift cannot alter the selected mechanism in a homogeneous cyclic experiment. We therefore introduce a boundary-normalized nonhomogeneous path family in which robust calibration changes the mechanism and reduces worst-case risk. We also derive exact cyclic privacy, robust privacy-range calibration, and precise conditions for safe context- or history-dependent channel selection. Sparse Laplace, Gaussian, staircase, and score-based mechanisms remain extensions of the same design principle. All numerical results use exact privacy and risk calculations with matched-guarantee baselines.

We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. A key analytical ingredient, of independent interest, is a pair of moment asymptotics, as $t\downarrow 0$, for the boundary local time of a reflected diffusion, extending known results for the unreflected case. Uniqueness in law of $\widetilde X$ among Feller REDs sharing the same interior dynamics is established through a resolvent/boundary-value-problem argument. The result extends the classical Itô-McKean construction of elastic Brownian motion to time-homogeneous diffusions, closing the gap between analytic and probabilistic treatments of elastic killing used in recent applied models.
A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
José Antonio Carrillo; Timon Gutleb; Andrea Medaglia; Yijia Tang

We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.
Jean-Baptiste Campesato; Jean-Philippe Monnier; Enrico Savi

Let $R$ be a real closed field. A Zariski-constructible subset of $R^n$, $\mathcal{ZC}$-set for short, is a Boolean combination of algebraic subsets of $R^n$. Euclidean closed Zariski-constructible subsets of $R^n$ are the closed subsets of a Noetherian topology finer than the Zariski topology of $R^n$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$. Let $U\subset R^n$ be a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set. We say that a function $f:U\to R$ of class $\mathcal{C}^k$ is a Zariski-constructible function, $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function for short, if its graph is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-set. For instance, regular and $k$-regulous functions on $R^n$ are $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions. We show that the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set is way richer, even for $k=\infty$, although $\infty$-regulous functions are just regular. Then, we extend the notion of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function over any $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. This paper is mainly devoted to the study of the geometric and algebraic properties of the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(X)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. From now on, assume that $k\in\mathbb N$. We show that $\mathcal{ZC}$-closed subsets $X$ of $R^n$ are exactly the zero loci of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $R^n$. We show that the Nullstellensatz holds in the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$, where $U$ is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open subset of $R^n$, and that this ring is radically principal. As a consequence of the Nullstellensatz, we prove that any $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$ extends to a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open neighborhood $U$ of $X$. Then, we translate our results into the language of sheaves of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed sets, from which we deduce a $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-version of Cartan's theorems A and B.
Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs

We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.
Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
Guangyi He; Damir Filipovic; Lukas Gonon

Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. Under bounded actions, a regular benchmark policy and exact empirical minimization, the expected objective gap to the benchmark policy is at most of order $N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{N(1+\log N)/n}$, with $N$ the feature width per output coordinate and $n$ the number of paths. At fixed sample size the two terms trade off in $N$, and balancing them gives $N\asymp\sqrt{n/\log n}$. Across a wide range of examples, estimated gaps generally decrease with width and sample size, and RFNNs show an advantage when simulated paths are limited. We also study Parsimonious Random Feature Learning (PRFL), which grows and prunes the random dictionary during training while training only the output coefficients. At matched retained width and training budget, PRFL improves on a fixed RFNN in the LQ and Heston comparisons, while the fully trained network remains best in those examples.
Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the quasilinear Lane-Emden equation

We study isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to $-Δ_pu=u^q$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $Δ_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<n$, and $n(p-1)/(n-p)<q<np/(n-p)-1$. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u(x)\sim K_{n,p,q}|x|^{-p/(q+1-p)}$ as $x\to0$, where $K_{n,p,q}>0$ is an explicit constant depending only on $n,p,q$. The result holds without radial symmetry or an a priori growth assumption. The proof combines a removability criterion with a rigidity theorem for positive solutions in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying two-sided power bounds. To handle the infinite $p$-Dirichlet energy at the singularity, we construct a continuous Steiner deformation that fixes all sufficiently high superlevel sets. The resulting energy comparison yields radial symmetry of the blow-up limits.
Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem

We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.
Shirley Xiaoqi Liu; Tirthankar Adhikari; Parthe Pandit

Precise asymptotic theory for M-estimators in high-dimensional settings is largely limited to convex or mildly non-convex formulations, yet non-convex loss functions as well as regularizers are widely used in practice. We study M-estimation in generalized linear models (GLMs) where the loss function or the regularizer can be non-convex. Under rotationally invariant design matrices in the proportional asymptotic regime, we analyze the problem through Vector Approximate Message Passing (VAMP), whose iterates are described by a low-dimensional deterministic recursion called State Evolution (SE). Existing proofs of SE require the proximal operators of the loss function and the regularizer to be Lipschitz, but a non-convex loss or regularizer can have a discontinuous proximal operator, and the usual Onsager terms in VAMP then miss the contribution of the discontinuities. Assuming that the proximal operators are special functions of locally bounded variation, we derive a correction to the Onsager terms using a distributional Stein's lemma. We prove that SE holds for the corrected VAMP. We apply the theory to analyze group sparse regression with an $\ell_0$-type penalty and to robust regression with the Cauchy loss.

We consider subgroups in $PU(2,1)$ generated by three involutions $I_1,I_2,I_3$ such that $I_2I_3$ has order $p$ and the elements $I_1I_2$, $I_2I_3$, $I_1I_3I_2I_3$ are all in the same conjugacy class of $PU(2,1)$. We show that these groups are discrete whenever $I_1I_2$ and $I_1I_2I_3$ are non-elliptic and we study the orbifolds at infinity. In addition, we show that for $3 \leq p \leq 9$ the complement of a symmetric cyclic chain of $p$ simple links admits a spherical CR uniformization.
A martingale proof of simultaneous convex and smooth renorming
Zhiyao Fang; Tingting Hu; Mengmeng Bao; Qi Liu

We give an affirmative answer to Problem 198 of Guirao, Montesinos, and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~90], also formulated by Pisier [\emph{Martingales in Banach Spaces}, Cambridge University Press (2016), p.~461]. Given equivalent norms with convexity of power type $p$ and smoothness of power type $q$, respectively, we construct a single equivalent norm with both properties using finite dyadic martingales. It can be chosen arbitrarily close to the given smooth norm in multiplicative distortion and preserves all linear symmetries shared by the two initial norms. The case $p=q=2$ with group invariance answers Problem 3.6 of Cabello Sánchez, Ferenczi, and Randrianantoanina [São Paulo J. Math. Sci. \textbf{16} (2022), 406--458].
Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set

We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly. Finally, we show that arbitrary vexillary permutations are encoded by excursions of the same walk model.
Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants

We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.
Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors

Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.
A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics

Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading. The proof uses a minimum argument for the global Morse remainder and requires no individual index exclusion. For odd $n\ge3$, we obtain a smaller, dimension-dependent strict bound when good iterates of Maslov-type index $-1$ are excluded. Irrational ellipsoids show that the multiplicity bound is sharp.
Irreducibility of Primitive Special Cycles in Locally Symmetric Spaces of Orthogonal Type

Let $L$ be an even lattice of signature $(n_1,n_2)$ with $n_1\geq k+1,n_2\geq 2$ and let $X$ denote the quotient of the symmetric space associated to $O(L\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{R})$ by the discriminant kernel of positive spinor norm. We show that primitive special cycles in $X$ of real codimension at most $kn_2$ are irreducible if $L$ splits off $k+1$ hyperbolic planes locally at every prime.
Automorphism groups of mixing shifts of finite type

We prove that nontrivial two-sided mixing shifts of finite type are flip conjugate if and only if their automorphism groups are abstractly commensurable. This resolves an outstanding question of Boyle, Lind, and Rudolph from 1988.
Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.
Distribution of Rademacher random multiplicative functions in short intervals, with proper normalization

We determine the limiting distribution of partial sums $\sum_{x<n\le x+y}f(n)$ of a Rademacher random multiplicative function over short intervals. Combined with the theorem of Soundararajan and Xu, our result gives a standard real Gaussian limit, with a suitable deterministic normalization, throughout $x^{1/5}\log x\ll y=o(x)$. This resolves the Rademacher extension raised by Harper, Soundararajan and Xu. The normalization is smaller than the standard deviation by a factor tending to zero when $\log(x/y)=o(\sqrt{\log\log x})$. As an application of our method, we also obtain a complex Gaussian limit for short interval sums twisted by a fixed primitive nonreal Dirichlet character.
Normalized Weyl Energy and the Differential Topology of Four-Manifolds

The Weyl functional $\int_M\|W_g\|^2\,dμ_g$ plays an important role in four dimensional conformal geometry. Using this functional, Chang, Gursky, and Zhang introduced an invariant of an admissible conformal class and a smooth invariant of the underlying manifold obtained by taking the infimum over all such classes. We use a normalization in which both invariants, denoted by $β(M,c)$ and $β(M)$, take values in $[0,1)$. We prove that every admissible four-manifold $M$ with $β(M)$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ up to reversal of orientation. At $β(M)=1/2$, this result and the conformal characterization of the Fubini--Study class confirm Conjecture~1.1 of Chang, Gursky, and Zhang. Among admissible four-manifolds with indefinite intersection form, we prove the corresponding stability of the diffeomorphism type of $S^2\times S^2$ near $2/3$. For the one- and two-point blow-ups of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we show that $β(M)$ lies strictly above the respective topological lower bounds of $2/3$ and $23/30$. These results lead us to ask whether $1$ is the only accumulation point of the values of $β(M)$ and whether, among simply connected admissible four-manifolds, $β(M)$ determines the diffeomorphism type up to reversal of orientation.
Categorical Torelli theorem for quintic threefolds
We prove that two smooth quintic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$ are isomorphic if their bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves are equivalent.
On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients

We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.
A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming

We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $ε$ in $(n^{ω+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)$ time, where $ω\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.
Symmetry breaking Poincar{é}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields

We construct Poincar{é}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{ö}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$π$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{ö}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{ö}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.
A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra; John Matos Ascona; Lizet Santa Cruz Calderón; Heraclio López-Lázaro

We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocities, it yields dissipativity with an explicit exponential decay rate, which cannot be obtained from the classical inequality of Henry. With it we prove the existence of the minimal pullback attractor in the universe of families of bounded sets, on the moving domain and then on the fixed rescaled reference domains. Finally, numerical simulations on contracting domains illustrate the effect of the boundary motion on cell aggregation.
Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon

Recently, L. Alpöge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.
Via a New LP Relaxation: Stronger Performance Guarantees for WSEPT, and an LP-Based Proof of Kawaguchi & Kyan
Maximilian von Aspern; Andreas S. Schulz; Eugenio Vairo

We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value. This bounds the integrality gap of the relaxation and gives a short, LP-based proof of the tight bound of Kawaguchi and Kyan on the performance of WSPT. We then turn to the stochastic version of the problem, in which processing times are independent random variables whose squared coefficients of variation are at most~$Δ$. A variance-corrected version of the new LP relaxation is valid for all non-anticipatory policies, and we show that WSEPT is within a factor $1 + (1 + Δ)/(3 + \sqrt{7 + 2 Δ})$ of it for $Δ\ge 1$, for any number of machines. This is $O(\sqrtΔ)$, whereas all previous guarantees for this problem grow linearly in $Δ$. Up to a constant factor, our bound matches the known $Ω(\sqrtΔ)$ lower bound for WSEPT. For $Δ\le 1$, we recover the best known bounds.
Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions

Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincaré returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings. The fixed-point bifurcation diagrams reveal the creation, destruction or annihilation of equilibria and non-monotonic changes in their number under asymmetric coupling. In representative asymmetric parameter slices, nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcations generate or terminate stable equilibria within intervals that also support periodic or chaotic running motion. The running dynamics exhibit period-doubling, period-cascading sequences and embedded periodic windows within chaotic regions, while the initial-condition scans resolve their coexistence with stationary states. These results connect the local equilibrium structure with the parameter-dependent organization and selection of dynamical regimes in the coupled-junction system.
Resolution of ladder representations for classical groups

Atobe has introduced ladder representations of the $p$-adic groups $\mathbf{Sp}(2n)$ and $\mathbf{SO}(2n+1)$, which contain the strongly positive discrete series and Mœglin's representations attached to irreducible Arthur parameters, and has expressed their characters as alternating sums of costandard modules. We show that all the coefficients of this formula are $\pm1$, with the sign given by the dimension of the orbit of the Langlands parameter, and that these representations have coresolutions of Cousin type by costandard modules, whose Euler characteristic is Atobe's formula.
Partition rank and analytic rank over finite field

We prove that the partition rank and the analytic rank of a tensor over any finite field are equivalent up to a constant depending only on the order of the tensor. The proof combines Milićević's theorem on dense multilinear varieties with the differential Schur complement of Moshkovitz and Zhu. The new ingredient is a method for approximately eliminating multilinear equations.
Learning and Dynamic Route Recommendation Under Unknown Traveler Compliance and Road Conditions
Yanru Guo; Siqian Shen; Ruiwei Jiang; Xi Jessie Yang

Route planning during evacuations and other large-scale egress operations is inherently dynamic: the planner's recommendations affect future congestion on the roads, influence whether travelers accept their guidance, and determine what the planner can learn from the travelers' actual route choices. In this paper, we consider stochastic dynamic route recommendation to many travelers over a finite horizon under uncertain compliance and road conditions. In each period, a planner assigns routes that lead different origins' traveler groups to safe destinations, and travelers either follow the recommendation or revert to a preferred route. We model compliance using a logistic model and learn its unknown coefficients from observed route travel. We also filter the state of road conditions from noisy telemetry, and use a performance state to capture how the quality of past route recommendation affects travelers' future compliance. To determine the route assignment policy, we formulate a finite-horizon, belief-state dynamic program, show that the information state is sufficient for optimal Markov control, and develop an approximation that combines compliance beliefs with proximal policy optimization (PPO) using a Dirichlet actor over feasible route shares. We conduct numerical studies on instances of Eastern Massachusetts highway network data under different uncertain road conditions and compliance behavior. We demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the PPO method and the value of dynamic adaptive solutions, against static routes. Our solutions reduce the mean and upper-tail costs of all travelers relative to myopic policy benchmarks, even when these benchmarks know the true compliance coefficients. Moreover, updating beliefs and the performance state dynamically also reduces the total cost under accurate, biased, and diffuse priors.
A variant of the Erdős--Gyárfás problem for $K_9$ and $K_{12}$
Luyi Li; Guiying Yan; Zicheng Ye

For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $K_n$ such that every copy of $H$ contains a color appearing an odd number of times. We prove that $r_{K_9}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ and $r_{K_{12}}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$. These bounds on $r_H(n)$ yield linear graph codes of density at least $\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ that avoid images of $K_9$ and $K_{12}$.
Fairness-optimized interlacing knots for even-degree periodic B-spline interpolation

Interpolating an ordered set of points by a B-spline curve is a fundamental operation in computer-aided geometric design. Most of the literature addresses open curves, where the Schoenberg--Whitney condition characterizes a nonsingular collocation matrix and averaging is the standard way to choose the knot vector. Periodic B-spline interpolation has received much less attention, and the open-curve algorithms cannot be transferred directly. No theoretical criterion is available for choosing the knots, and the few existing constructions, such as the shifting and energy methods, remain empirical, with neither a theoretical guarantee nor a supporting analysis. This paper addresses this gap for even degrees. We prove that for every even degree $p\ge2$ the periodic collocation matrix is nonsingular whenever the domain knots and the interpolation parameters interlace, in either of two admissible orderings, for arbitrarily nonuniform parameters. Rather than singling out one knot vector, this sufficient condition delimits an $n$-parameter family of admissible knot vectors and provides the theoretical foundation for knot selection that periodic interpolation has lacked. It also explains why the empirical shifting method is solvable, previously justified only by an incorrect diagonal-dominance argument. We then exploit the remaining freedom to place the knots by fairness optimization, which preserves admissibility at every iterate and leads to the methods Opt-R and Opt-L. On four closed shapes with irregularly distributed points these methods achieve a fairness comparable to the shifting and energy methods, improve on them in several cases, and offer guarantees that no empirical construction provides.
Gray II, Kähler Nullity and Ricci Flow on Generalized Flag Manifolds with Two Isotropy Summands
Lino Grama; Ailton R. Oliveira; Francisco V. Oliveira

We investigate Gray's second curvature identity, Kähler nullity, and homogeneous Ricci flow on generalized flag manifolds with two isotropy summands. We prove that every invariant metric satisfies Gray's second identity for both invariant almost complex structures. For the non-integrable structure, the Kähler nullity is trivial except at a distinguished metric ratio, where it coincides with the vertical distribution of a homogeneous fibration. This distribution is integrable and has totally geodesic leaves. For the integrable structure, the Kähler nullity exhibits a different behavior and need not be integrable away from the Kähler locus. Finally, we reduce the normalized homogeneous Ricci flow to an autonomous equation for the ratio of the metric parameters. The resulting dynamics identify two invariant Einstein directions and show that the Kähler--Einstein direction is attracting, while the other is repelling.
Certified Finite Element Error Bounds for Diffusion Equations with Measure-Valued Principal-Part Delays

We derive computable a posteriori finite element error bounds for diffusion equations whose highest-order spatial operator carries a non-negative measure-valued delay. Although the delay law is replaced by finitely many atoms in computations, the bounds measure the error with respect to the solution for the original law. An equilibrated Raviart--Thomas flux controls the spatial residual, and a transport estimate on the computed time reconstruction controls the delay-law residual without additional temporal regularity of the exact solution. A cumulative-mass representation preserves cancellation in this residual and allows a jump between the numerical initial state and the prescribed history. The constants are independent of the mesh aspect ratios and of the number of atoms, and inexact flux equilibration and errors in the elementwise residual means are included. We also give a quantile-based budget for the delay residual and a weighted finite-horizon bound beyond the mass-subcritical regime. Under an elliptic equilibration hypothesis, we prove a two-sided estimate for a combined error norm that includes the time derivative. On right-triangular meshes satisfying the maximum-angle condition, however, the lowest-order Raviart--Thomas estimator can exceed the combined graph error by a factor at least proportional to the aspect ratio. Numerical experiments on anisotropic meshes, including a law beyond the mass-subcritical regime, illustrate the behaviour of the residual indicators and the limitations of efficiency.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ with perfection $R^\infty$. We study whether coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R^\infty\cong S^\infty$ for some regular Noetherian local ring $S$. For a normal Noetherian local domain, coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R$ to be $p$-almost factorial, equivalently $R^\infty$ is a GCD domain; a finite regular extension $R\subseteq S$ with $S^q\subseteq R$ gives the uniform bound $q Cl(R)=0$. In the non-Noetherian direction, we construct, for every prime $p$ and every $d\geq2$, a perfect coherent local valuation domain of dimension $d$ that is not the perfection of any Noetherian ring. In the positive direction, we characterize coherence for affine semigroup local rings. Finally, we give an F-coherent ring without regular model.
Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.
An Alphabet-Size Bound for the Information Bottleneck Function

The information bottleneck function gives a measure of optimal preservation of correlation between some random variable $X$ and some side information $Y$ while compressing $X$ into a new random variable $W$ with bounded remaining correlation to $X$. As such, the information bottleneck has found many natural applications in machine learning, coding and video compression. The main objective in order to calculate the information bottleneck is to find the optimal representation on $W$. This could in principle be arbitrarily complicated, but fortunately it is known that the cardinality of $W$ can be restricted as $|{\cal W}|\leq|{\cal X}|+1$ which makes the calculation possible for finite $|{\cal X}|$. Now, for many practical applications, e.g. in machine learning, $X$ represents a potentially very large data space, while $Y$ is from a comparably small set of labels. This raises the question whether the known cardinality bound can be improved in such situations. We show that the information bottleneck function can always be approximated up to an error $δ(ε,|{\cal Y}|)$ with a cardinality $|{\cal W}| \leq f(ε,|{\cal Y}|)$, for explicitly given functions $δ$ and $f$ of an approximation parameter $ε>0$ and the cardinality of ${\cal Y}$. Finally, we generalize the known cardinality bounds to the case were some of the random variables represent quantum information.
Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity

We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincaré inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.
Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
Willian Cintra; Jônatas Peralta; Antonio Suárez

In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.
Statistics of Fundamental Fourier Coefficients of Cusp Forms

We study sign changes of Fourier coefficients of elliptic and Siegel modular forms in considerable generality. For any $N \geq 1$ and an arbitrary non-zero elliptic cusp form $f\in S_κ(Γ_1(N))$ ($κ\in \frac{1}{2} \mathbb{Z}$) with real Fourier coefficients, we show that a positive proportion of its non-zero Fourier coefficients change sign if $κ\geq 1$ is integral. If $κ\geq 1/2$ is half-integral, we get an almost optimal result. As applications, we establish quantitative sign-change results for `fundamental' Fourier coefficients of Siegel cusp forms of arbitrary degree $n$. These improve the previous best known results on the number of non-zero fundamental Fourier coefficients, even in degree $n=1$.
On the Unique Identification of Finitely Many Radial Heat Sources

In this work, we investigate an inverse source problem for the heat equation in $\R^d$ ($d\geq1$), in which the source is a finite positive linear combination of translates of a known real-valued radial Schwartz profile with nonzero total mass. Both the locations and strengths of the sources are to be identified from the observations of time traces at finitely many spatial points over an arbitrary nonempty open positive-time interval. For $d\geq2$, we prove that the sharp universal measurement threshold is $dN+1$: every set of $dN+1$ measurement points in affine general position uniquely identifies every source configuration with at most $N$ locations. For $d=1$, we prove that two distinct measurement points uniquely identify every finite source configuration, independently of the number of sources, and that this count is sharp. The analysis relies on an equivalence between equality of heat traces and equality of weighted distance measures, and then employs perpendicular-bisector hyperplanes to resolve geometric ambiguities. We also establish identification guarantees using $d+1$ measurement points: clustered designs under a reference-distance separation condition, adaptive designs for arbitrary configurations, and any fixed affinely independent design for almost every location configuration, uniformly over all positive strengths.
Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments

Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $ζ_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.
Equivalence of Cohen generics is hyperfinite

It is shown that the equivalence relation on Cohen generic reals over a countable model of set theory, where two are equivalent if they produce the same generic extension, is hyperfinite, answering a question of the author. The proof uses asymptotic separation and is a digestion of an argument originally produced by GPT-6.
On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
Suratno Basu; Abhirup Das; Umme Joinab; Rupam Karmakar

In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles. In view of the above, we study $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles on blow ups of certain $K3$-surfaces $(K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X)$. Finally, we provide a result concerning the $k$ very ampleness of certain uniform line bundles on the general blow up of product of curves $(K_X \not\cong \mathcal{O}_X)$.
Microlocal and global smoothing effect of variable coefficient ZK-type operators

In this work, we study the smoothing effect of a class of Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equations, which generalize the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to higher dimensions. Specifically, we consider linear evolution equations generated by ZK-type operators with variable coefficients, and we study both their microlocal and global smoothing effects under suitable conditions on the coefficients of the operator. Our analysis requires a detailed study of the geometric properties of the Hamiltonian flow associated with the operator under consideration. These properties allow us to prove a dispersive and a strong smoothing effect associated with the Cauchy problem in question: under suitable moment conditions on the initial datum, the solution becomes smooth in space for positive times in a finite time interval.
The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws

For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of arXiv:2611.30663 from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.
A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws

We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).
Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
Jan-Frederik Pietschmann; Carmen Tretmans; Nicola Zamponi

We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.
Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals

Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.
Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization

Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. An interference term becomes coherence at most with the probability of unambiguously discriminating its two reference states, a bound attained when there are no others and, for positive coefficients and nonnegative overlaps, exactly when the overlaps are probabilities of a random grouping. Maximal degree means conversion into a maximally coherent state with certainty, possible for up to three reference states but not in general. Each coherence measure gives its own degree; when two degrees order two superpositions oppositely, neither converts into the other with certainty, and we find such pairs already for two reference states, unlike in qubit coherence. For equal positive overlaps, in-phase superpositions are rigid: deterministic conversions that keep all components can only permute their coefficients. As the reference states merge, the degree stays bounded where widely used measures can diverge, and at every amplitude a rotation-symmetric cat state attains its maximum. Our results quantify superposition operationally and reveal conversion constraints created by nonorthogonality.
Alessio Baldelli; Francisco Lázaro; Davide Orsucci; Massimo Battaglioni

XYZ codes generalize the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework by adding $\sym{Y}$-type stabilizers to the usual $\sym{X}$- and $\sym{Z}$-type ones. We study XYZ codes whose three classical component codes are binary cyclic codes of odd length~$n$. Assigning disjoint sets of irreducible factors of $x^n-1$ to the three Pauli types fixes the number of encoded logical qubits and ensures that the row spaces of the three parity-check matrices intersect pairwise trivially. Then, a coprimality condition between the factors assigned to each type and the reciprocals of those assigned to the others guarantees the required orthogonality. Cyclotomic cosets give a complete and explicit description of the resulting family. We show that, for odd~$n$, a cyclic stabilizer code admits an XYZ representation with cyclic component codes iff its stabilizer generators are invariant, up to a phase, under the qubit permutation $i\mapsto 2i\bmod n$. By fixing the length and the dimension of the code, the proposed cyclic XYZ codes attain the best known minimum distance of stabilizer codes, exceed the minimum distance of the underlying CSS codes, and even exceed the linear-programming upper bounds for general CSS codes.
Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels

Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.
Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors

We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $θ$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(θ/2)\leq p\leq\cos(θ/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion left multiplication through Euclidean projection onto the zero-divisor cone.
Hyperbolicity and zero divisors in random graphical groups
Elena I. Bunina; Winston Lee; Alexei Miasnikov; Kyrylo Muliarchyk

We give a criterion for hyperbolicity of random groups presented by labelled graphs. On $n$ vertices, we prescribe the proportions of the possible sets of outgoing labels. For each generator, we choose a uniform matching between its occurrences and those of its inverse, independently across generators. We condition the graph to have girth at least $\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$ for sufficiently small $c>0$, and take the labels of closed paths as relators. The distribution of outgoing labels determines a matrix of turn weights. Suppose that each letter occurs as often as its inverse and with positive frequency, every vertex has degree at least three, and the entrywise square of the turn matrix has spectral radius less than one. We prove that, with probability tending to one as $n$ grows, the resulting group is torsion-free and non-elementary hyperbolic and admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space. On the same event, every path from a prescribed root to a different vertex has nontrivial label in the group. The proof uses the spectral radius bound to control repeated path labels in diagrams and a local-to-global argument to obtain a linear isoperimetric inequality.
