Applied to OpenAI's characteristic-two zero-divisor construction, the criterion recovers the hyperbolicity result of Mghirbi and Douglas.
On the work of Jacob Tsimerman

Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.
Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood

Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression. The likelihood is obtained by integrating a logarithmically growing Catoni-type score and exponentiating the negative integrated score, producing a proper location-scale density with a reusable normalizing constant and EM-compatible responsibilities. Although the induced density itself is lighter than exponential and has all moments, its likelihood score grows only logarithmically; this distinction yields a smooth residual-robust estimator that can be stably fitted when the data are generated from Laplace, Pareto, or even infinite-variance heavy-tailed error mechanisms. We derive deterministic tail envelopes, the location-scale decomposition of the normalizing constant, a rejection sampler, a lower-bounded mixing-weight update, a unique componentwise scale update, and a constrained generalized EM algorithm. The theory gives monotonicity of the observed likelihood and a local population-to-sample perturbation guarantee under standard compactness, contraction, and numerical-accuracy conditions. Simulations and applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations show that the method is a competitive smooth likelihood-based alternative to Gaussian and pseudo-robust EM procedures, especially in residual-outlier regimes, while also clarifying its limitations under high leverage and extremely adversarial contamination.
Structure Preservation of $2$-Wasserstein Barycenters on the Real Line with Applications to Log-Concave Distributions

We study to what extent the $p$-Wasserstein barycenter ($p$-WB) of arbitrary, not only finite, collections of distributions preserves their structure, focusing on shape constraints on the densities, such as monotonicity, unimodality, or log-concavity. This preservation is a generalized convexity property in Wasserstein space, which we call $p$-WB convexity. We investigate $p$-WB convexity of the families of $ϕ$-unimodal distributions: an absolutely continuous distribution $μ$ is $ϕ$-unimodal if composition with $ϕ$ turns a density into a concave function on the interior of the convex support of $μ$. This notion generalizes log-concavity and $s$-concave densities. We find a quantile representation of $ϕ$-unimodality and then use a novel closed-form expression of the quantile density function of the $2$-WB to decide on $2$-WB convexity. In higher dimensions or for $p\neq2$, we give counterexamples ruling out the $p$-WB convexity of $ϕ$-unimodal distributions. On $\mathbb{R}$ and for $p=2$, we characterize which $ϕ$ generate $2$-WB convex families. The family of log-concave distributions is $2$-WB convex, as is the family of distributions with $s$-concave densities if and only if $s\geq-2$. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
Kun Cheng; Changlong Shen; Leilei Zhang

A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.
Algorithms and topological invariants for dynamic systems. IV. Topological Equivalence of Functions and Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems

This is the fourth part of a series on algorithms and topological invariants for dynamical systems. We study the topological equivalence of smooth functions and of Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, and the discrete invariants, Reeb graphs and cell decompositions, that classify them. We recall the notions of topological equivalence and structural stability, introduce two equivalences of functions (with and without the order of the critical values) and show that simple Morse functions on closed orientable surfaces are classified by their Reeb graphs with vertex odering, while simple Hamiltonian flows are classified by Reeb graphs with marked edges. For the disc and for the sphere we obtain a recursive description and a generating function for the numbers of such trees, and compute the numbers of topologically non-equivalent simple Morse functions and Hamiltonian flows with a given number of saddles. We also describe functions with isolated, possibly degenerate, critical points by cell decompositions, and give an algorithm and computational results for functions with three critical points. In the first part (arXiv:2501.15657) we discussed the basic concepts of differential topology. In the second part (arXiv:2502.00506) we discussed the discrete topological structures used in the topological theory of dynamical systems. In the third part (arXiv:2502.09958) we constructed algorithms that recognize $2$- and $3$-manifolds in simplicial complexes and regular CW-complexes and determine the topological type of a $2$-manifold (connectivity, orientability, genus, number of boundary components).
Pierre-Emmanuel Chaput; David Dos Santos Ferreira; Valentin Féray

Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties. The proof involves the study of polyharmonic functions on the positive discrete orthant $\mathbb Z^n_{>0}$, and a relation with the co-invariant algebra of type $A$. We also provide a generalization connected to colored permutations, and discuss the analogue problems where $E=\mathbb C[T]_0/(T^\ell)$ for some $\ell >0$, and where $E$ consists of infinitely differentiable functions. Finding a complete description of algebraic solutions in these settings is still open.
Generic Strong Regularity and the Branson--Gover Conjecture
Wei-Chun Chen; Wei-Ting Kao; Chun-Kai Lien

On each closed smooth manifold of even dimension $2N\ge 4$, we prove that the Branson--Gover detour operators are strongly regular in every degree $k-1$, $1\le k<N$, on a $C^\infty$-open dense set of Riemannian metrics. Consequently, every de Rham cohomology class of positive degree below the middle dimension has a unique conformal harmonic representative for these metrics. On a connected manifold, the critical scalar GJMS operator has only constants in its kernel on an open dense set of conformal structures modulo diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, as conjectured by Canzani, Gover, Jakobson, and Ponge. The proof computes the principal symbol of a reduced metric Hessian that accounts for the motion of the kernel through a Green operator.
Fast Gradient-Based Framework for Spatial and Length Optimization of Geothermal Borehole Fields
Oliver Heinzel; Smajil Halilovic; Thomas Hamacher; Michael Ulbrich

Common analytical design tools for Borehole Heat Exchanger (BHE) fields size the total drilling length for a given layout but do not optimize the positions of the boreholes. We introduce a framework (OptiGeoS) for the simultaneous, gradient-based optimization of the borehole length and the continuous borehole positions under groundwater advection. It couples the Moving Finite Line Source model with local BHE equations and evaluates the temporal convolutions by Fast Fourier Transforms. The gradients with respect to the length and the positions are computed analytically. A flow-dependent Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation confines each borehole to its own cell, which enforces the spatial separation and provides advection-informed layouts. Under purely conductive conditions, the fluid temperature extremes of the forward model for a single borehole lie between those of EED and GHEtool, which differ by $0.32\,\mathrm{K}$. For a field of 120 boreholes, the hourly outlet temperature agrees with that of EED with an RMSE of $0.28\,\mathrm{K}$, while the peak temperatures deviate by up to $2\,\mathrm{K}$. For 25 boreholes simulated hourly over 20 years, one forward simulation takes less than $0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ and a full optimization about $8\,\mathrm{min}$ on a laptop CPU. In a case study with groundwater advection, the optimized layout requires $16.2\,\%$ less borehole length than a fixed grid. It reduces the length increase caused by the advected thermal plume from $20.9\,\%$ to $1.4\,\%$.
Optimal first eigenvalue estimates for positive holomorphic sectional curvature
Jiaxuan Fan; Mingwei Wang; Xiaokui Yang

Let $(M,ω_g)$ be a compact Kähler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature $\geq 2$. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplacian $Δ_d$ satisfies $$λ_1\geq 4, $$ and $λ_1=4$ if and only if $(M,ω_g)$ is holomorphically isometric to $(\mathbb{P}^1,ω_{\mathrm{FS}})$.
Weitzenböck curvature estimates in arbitrary degree and sectional-scalar curvature pinching

For each odd dimension $n\ge7$ we give an explicit constant $B_n<(n-1)/(n+2)$ such that a closed, connected, nonflat Riemannian $n$-manifold with $K_{\min}\ge B_n S_0$ is a rational homology sphere, where $S_0=\operatorname{Scal}/[n(n-1)]$. For example, $B_7=28/43<2/3$. This answers the question of Li, Matinpour, and Petersen about lowering the sectional curvature coefficient in the remaining odd dimensions. The same argument recovers their five-dimensional endpoint $B_5=10/19$. The proof starts with a four-frame inequality for two-forms. Contracting forms and averaging over hyperplanes propagates a Ricci-weighted estimate whose coefficient depends on the parity of the codimension. For an algebraic curvature tensor with nonnegative sectional curvature, we obtain lower bounds for the Weitzenböck curvature endomorphism in every degree. When the dimension and degree are both even, we classify all nonzero equality pairs for the sharp bound by powers of Kähler forms. For three-forms the optimal coefficient in the scalar curvature bound is $1/3$ in dimensions five and six and lies between $4/9$ and $5168/11253$ in dimension seven. On the cone of strongly nonnegative curvature tensors we determine the optimal coefficient in every degree.
Asymptotic approximation for a certain class of statistics associated with generalized urn models

The generalized urn model is defined in terms of a collection of random frequencies, which is treated as a collection of conditionally independent random variables given their sum. We consider a class of random variables that can be represented as series of functions of these frequencies. The general results concern asymptotic normality, estimates of remainder terms, and Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansions for such random variables. We then consider random variables defined in various versions of the generalized urn model. These models include the random allocation of particles of several types into finite or infinite numbers of cells, random sampling without replacement from a finite population, random coverage of a circle, random forests, and random permutations.
Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras

Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant. We establish several inequalities and equalities relating these weighted regularities to the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of derived Hom and derived tensor complexes. These results recover their unweighted counterparts and yield new relations involving the a-invariant for a fixed weight. Some of these results generalize the inequalities of Kirkman-Won-Zhang between weighted CM-regularity and Tor-regularity by allowing the weight to range over the entire plane R^2. We also give conditions under which these inequalities become equalities, thereby answering a question posed by Kirkman-Won-Zhang. We use weighted AS-regularity to study the Artin-Schelter regularity of A. Under mild conditions, we prove that the weighted AS-regularity of A vanishes if and only if A is an N-graded AS-regular algebra. This generalizes an unweighted result of the present authors and a weighted result of Kirkman, Won, and Zhang.
Nicolas Boullé; Diana Halikias; Samuel E. Otto; Alex Townsend

We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.
For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
Christopher J. Fewster; Christiane K. M. Klein

State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables $(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}$. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.
Cyclic changes of frame for designing non-retracing verification cases for numerical interface tracking

A forward-backward deformation test supplies an exact final interface, but retracing can allow errors from the two halves to cancel. We construct alternative tests by superposing a cyclic change of frame on the same base deformation. The frame returns to its starting pose, preserving the exact final phase and the deformation history up to rigid placement. A small returning translation can keep trajectories close to the retraced ones. A full rotation about a fixed centre or axis gives closed paths with nonzero winding for material labels that stay off that centre or axis. For incompressible base fields the transformed velocity is divergence-free. We construct discretely solenoidal face fluxes for geometric volume-of-fluid advection by circulating the transformed potential. In three TwoPhaseFlow benchmarks, with a shared time grid for each pair, a full-turn frame increased the final cell-average shape discrepancy in all 30 comparisons, with a median factor of 1.50. The fitted convergence exponent decreased in each of the six benchmark-reconstruction comparisons over the tested grids.
Norbert Hegyvári; Péter Pál Pach; Quanyu Tang

We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.
Cross Correlation of Binary Niho-type Sequences and Related Constacyclic Codes
Yuehui Cui; Jinquan Luo; Yongbo Xia; Qiuyi Zhang

Let \(q=2^m\), where \(m\ge3\) is odd, and let \(d=(q-1)(q+4)/6+1\). We study the cross correlation between a binary \(m\)-sequence of length \(q^2-1\) and its \(d\)-decimated sequence of length \(3(q-1)\). We prove that the cross correlation is exactly four-valued and determine its distribution explicitly. For shift decimated sequence, we obtain at most five cross correlation values and express their frequencies in terms of a specified cubic root count over \(\F_q\). We also determine the complete value distribution of the associated exponential sums. As an application, we construct \(q\)-ary constacyclic codes with parameters \([q+1,4,2(q+1)/3]_q\) and determine their weight distributions.
Approximate L_r-factorization of \ell_p-strictly singular operators on L_p
Gang Cai; Jinghao Huang; Yin Zhou

For \(1<p<2\), we study norm approximation of operators on \(L_p(0,1)\) by operators that factor through \(L_r(0,1)\), where \(p<r<2\). Using a sharp factorization estimate for finite diagonal blocks, we show that the corresponding norm-closed factorization ideals form a strictly decreasing chain as \(r\) increases. We also construct a strictly singular operator \(T_p\) at positive distance from the closed linear span generated by these ideals and all finitely strictly singular operators on \(L_p(0,1)\). In particular, \(T_p\) is \(\ell_p\)-strictly singular, yet its distance from the \(L_r\)-factorization ideals has a positive lower bound independent of \(r\). This answers a question due to Johnson and Schechtman in the negative.
Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons

Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $τ$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $τ$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.
Optimal XOR Lemmas for Information Complexity

Information complexity studies how much information the parties to a communication protocol must reveal to each other about their inputs to accomplish a given task. For a Boolean-valued communication problem $F$, let ${\rm IC}_ε(F)$ denote its information complexity with error $ε$, and let $F^{\oplus n}$ denote the XOR of $n$ independent instances of $F$. A fundamental question is whether information complexity obeys an XOR lemma, ${\rm IC}_{1/3}(F^{\oplus n})=Ω(n\cdot{\rm IC}_{1/(3n)}(F))$, which would match the trivial upper bound. Previous work either established the $n$-fold increase in information cost without the $n$-fold decrease in error (Bar-Yossef et al., FOCS 2002) or proved a lower bound with a subtracted penalty proportional to the input length of $F$ (Sawettamalya and Yu, STOC 2025). In particular, the question has remained open even for the XOR of $n$ or fewer copies of a function $F:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$. We completely resolve the question of XOR lemmas for information complexity, for every error $0\leε\le1/3$. For total functions $F$, we prove that ${\rm IC}_ε(F^{\oplus n})=Θ(n\cdot{\rm IC}_{ε/n}(F))$ unless $F$ has the degenerate form $F(x,y)=a(x)\oplus b(y)$, in which case ${\rm IC}_ε(F^{\oplus n})=O(1)$. For the richer class of partial functions, we obtain the characterization ${\rm IC}_ε(F^{\oplus n})=Θ({\rm IC}_ε(F)+n\cdot{\rm SIC}_{ε/n}(F))$, where ${\rm SIC}$ is the information complexity of protocols in which Alice and Bob privately output bits whose XOR is the answer. Finally, we prove an optimal distributional XOR lemma, for every function $F$ and every distribution. We obtain an optimal direct sum theorem to accompany each of our XOR lemmas. All implicit constants are absolute. Our work contributes a novel combination of information-theoretic and geometric techniques.
Signed Admissible Regions and 2-adic Area Obstructions for Perfect Triangles

A perfect triangle is a triangle whose sides, medians and area are all integers; whether one exists is an open problem. We study Buchholz's rational parametrization of triangles with two rational medians on the whole $(θ,ϕ)$-plane, allowing the generated side lengths to be negative. We factor its Heron polynomial $H(θ,ϕ)$ into ten explicit factors and show that the points whose componentwise absolute values form a triangle are exactly those with $H>0$; the points giving positive side lengths directly form three open quadrilaterals, one of which is the region used by Buchholz and Rathbun. Every triangle with two rational medians arises from sixteen signed parameter points, given by explicit rational functions. Rational area forces $H$ to be a square in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and the valuation and the unit part of $H$ yield parity and modulo-8 conditions in three valuation ranges. Since a triangle is excluded as soon as one of its sixteen parameter points fails a test, these conditions exclude infinite families of signed admissible parameters, including non-integral ones. The conditions are necessary only and do not settle the existence of perfect triangles.
Combining Physical Layer Security and Symmetric Encryption to Secure Rate-Splitting Multiple Access
Bastian Loss; Mohammad Parvini; Ahmad Nimr; Gerhard Fettweis

The demand for increased spectral efficiency (SE) in downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems has led to the development of various multiple access techniques. Among these, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) can improve SE over space division multiple access (SDMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by splitting each user's data into common and private parts. The common parts from all users are then encoded into a single common message, which is transmitted alongside the private messages using an RSMA-specific precoder. Recent results showed that the precoder can be modified to enable physical layer security (PLS) by integrating secrecy rate constraints into the design. However, this approach only secures the private messages, while the common part of each user remains unprotected. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid-PLS RSMA scheme that symmetrically encrypts all user data and embeds key information within the PLS-secured private messages. Additionally, the RSMA precoder is adapted to ensure that the private messages are sufficiently sized to carry the key information. The precoder design is formulated as a non-convex SE maximization problem and solved using successive convex approximation (SCA). Analytical and numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed hybrid-PLS RSMA can significantly improve SE compared to partially secure RSMA and secure SDMA, when complete user data security is required.
Non-Perturbative Analysis of Resonances by a Contraction Mapping on Complex Domains

In this paper, we consider a perturbation problem of embedded eigenvalues for an abstract Friedrichs--Lee Hamiltonian and analyze its spectral properties. By deforming the contour and constructing a contraction mapping on complex domains, we prove the existence of resonance poles.
Uniform Ionization Bounds in Molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker Theory

We study the molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker theory. For each fixed number $K$ of nuclei, we prove that every minimizer of mass $N$ satisfies $N\leq Z+C_K$, where $Z$ is the total nuclear charge, and $C_K>0$ is independent of the nuclear charges and positions. This answers the molecular large-charge ionization question posed in [R. L. Frank, P. T. Nam and H. Van Den Bosch, CPAM, 2018]. For $N\geq Z$, we also compare the screened potentials and electronic radii of Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker minimizers with those of the corresponding neutral molecular Thomas--Fermi minimizers and establish a uniform bound on the ionization energy.
Complex Oscillation and Non-Oscillation Results of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations

In this paper, we investigate oscillation and non-oscillation results of second order differential equations \begin{equation} f''+(H_1e^z+H_2e^{αz}+q)f=0,\tag{+} \end{equation} where $H_1,H_2\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, $0<α<1$, and $q$ is an entire function of order less than $1$. First, we show that if equation (+) has a zero-free non-trivial entire solution, then either $α=1/2$ or $α=3/4$, which settles the Problem 9 posed in \cite{HITW}. Second, we prove that if either $q$ is transcendental, or $α=(2m-1)/(2m)$ for some integer $m\geq 2$ and $q\equiv 0$, then every non-trivial entire solution $f$ of $(+)$ satisfies $λ(f)=\infty$.
Newton iterations and semi-Lagrangian schemes for mean field games of controls

We study Newton methods for second-order mean field games of controls (MFGC), in which agents interact through local averages of their controls. We prove local quadratic convergence of full Newton iterations, and of Newton iterations on reduced unknowns, near stable classical solutions. Stability holds under weak control interaction and under an infinitesimal monotonicity condition of Lasry--Lions type. We propose a semi-Lagrangian (SL) scheme for second-order MFGC, in which the average-control relation is solved by a convergent Chebyshev iteration, and two matrix-free solvers: a full Newton--SL method with block Gauss--Seidel preconditioning, whose spectrum we characterize in the absence of control coupling, and a reduced Jacobian-free Newton--GMRES method whose density iterates are nonnegative and mass-preserving by construction. We also construct an exact, time-dependent, coupled MFGC solution for use as a benchmark. In the experiments, the reduced solver converges quadratically in its final iterations, also in a strong-alignment test in which full Newton updates lose positivity. On the benchmark, the SL scheme and a finite-difference scheme both converge at first order with errors of comparable size, and our SL implementation is faster.
Fedor Kuyanov; Michael Drmota; Mikhail Skopenkov; Alexey Ustinov

We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying integral representations. They are applicable in several other situations as well.
Morita equivalence classification for irrational noncommutative solenoids

Given a prime integer $p$, we define a $p$-angle to be an element of the $p$-solenoid ${\mathcal S}_p$ or equivalently an element of $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{Q}_p$ modulo $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$. Noncommutative $p$-solenoids, or equivalently $p$-rotation algebras, are $C^*$-algebras defined by a $p$-angle in the same way as non-commutative tori or usual rotation algebras are defined by an angle. We give a complete classification, in terms of their $p$-angles and in the irrational case, of these $C^*$-algebras up to strong Morita equivalence, but also the associated groupoids up to Morita equivalence; more precisely, we obtain the following classification result: two irrational $p$-angles define strong Morita equivalent noncommutative solenoids if and only if they define isomorphic dimension groups if and only if they are congruent modulo $GL_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/p])$ if and only if they define Morita equivalent groupoids. This generalises, with a different proof, the classification up to isomorphism, previously obtained by Latrémolière and Packer. We also give a geometrical construction of projective $C^*$-modules in terms of proper $G$-spaces which exhaust the dimension group up to a shift and implement all relevant Morita equivalences by groupoid equivalences.
Michael Feischl; Jörg Nick; David Niederkofler

We introduce an explicit time-stepping scheme for ODEs, together with a residual-based a posteriori error estimator. Using this estimator, we show a new approach to proving optimality and linear reduction of adaptive algorithms for time-dependent problems that works in $H^1(0, t_{\rm end})$ and $W^{1,\infty}(0,t_{\rm end})$ norms, does not require quasi-orthogonality, and poses no restrictions on the marking parameter $θ$. The key idea is to use the Lipschitz continuity of the semi-discretized operator to obtain a stronger form of estimator reduction. Numerical experiments illustrate the benefits of this explicit scheme coupled with adaptive refinement over uniform time stepping for classical evolution problems, regularized dynamical approximation, and neural ODEs.

Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{é}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.
No coexistence in the two-type Richardson model when one side is stronger than the other
Gideon Amir; Dor Elboim; Gady Kozma

We study the two-type Richardson model in two dimensions. We prove that there is no coexistence of the two species when their infection rates are different, establishing a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m and Pemantle from 1997. In our proof we analyze a second order approximation of the infected region and use a Mermin--Wagner style argument to push the strong type out of the weak one.

The main purpose of this paper is to introduce and investigate strongly meet continuous posets. It is shown that a poset is strongly meet continuous if and only if the Scott closure of the set of elements way below each element coincides with its principal ideal. Moreover, the Scott topology of every strongly meet continuous poset is shown to have a basis consisting of Scott open filters, and a countable strongly meet continuous dcpo that is not continuous is constructed. For posets with the one step closure property, strongly meet continuity is equivalent to continuity. Further, a poset is continuous if and only if it is strongly meet continuous and its Scott space is core compact. As a consequence, every core compact strongly meet continuous dcpo has a sober Scott space.

Let $G_d(n,p)$ be the graph formed by joining pairs of $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ within a radius chosen to give edge probability $p$. For each fixed integer $K\ge0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, we prove that at $np=\log n+K\log\log n+t$, the probabilities of $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity both converge to $\exp(-e^{-t}/K!)$ uniformly over all $d=d(n)\ge3$. This is the same limit as in the Erdős--Rényi graph. Moreover, as the radius increases on a single sample, the first radii for minimum degree at least $K+1$, $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity, and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity coincide with probability tending to one uniformly over $d\ge3$. To our knowledge, this is the first critical-window law for connectivity in a random geometric graph that holds uniformly from fixed dimensions to dimensions growing arbitrarily with $n$.
Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport

Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.
The limit shape of uniform random antichains in $[0,1]^d$

For each $d\ge2$, we study $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, conditioned to form an antichain: no point is strictly smaller than another in every coordinate. We prove that the point cloud converges in Hausdorff distance to the closure of the hypersurface \[\mathcal S_d=\left\{\mathbf x\in(0,1)^d: \sum_{i=1}^dΦ^{-1}(\mathbf x_i)=0\right\}\] in probability as $n\to\infty$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The proof also shows that the antichain probability $a_n$ satisfies $\log a_n=-\frac{n}{d-1}\log n+β_d n+o(n)$ for a finite constant $β_d$. We identify the limiting empirical distribution and hence the limiting permuton of uniform random $d$-dimensional permutations avoiding a single pattern of size $2$.
Derivation of BCS functionals and gap equations from quantum many-body fermionic system
Xuwen Chen; Jiahao Wu; Zhifei Zhang

We consider 3D single-species spin-$1/2$ Fermi systems with general dispersion relation and general attractive interaction initially inside a finite box. Up to some critical temperature $T_c$ determined by the interaction and system size, we establish, for the expected discrete BCS gap equation, existence of positive maximal solution. We then prove the uniqueness of nonzero (not identically zero) nonnegative solution. That is, any nonzero nonnegative solution, if exist or obtained via other methods, must equal to the positive maximal solution. Building on such a well-posedness result and assuming quasi-freeness, we prove the emergence of the $SU(2)$ symmetry of the finite system. Finally, letting the system size tend to infinity, we prove the emergence of the continuous BCS functional and gap equation for which we also have the uniqueness of nonzero nonnegative solution, and the convergence of the critical temperature. In particular, our work also implies there is a positive energy (hence mass) gap for aforementioned Fermi systems for $[0,T_c)$, any nonzero nonnegative solution for the gap equations are from the many-body system it suppose to describe, and the Cooper divergence of the density of states from a finite to an infinite system.

Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, γ)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This construction is compatible with the eigendecomposition associated with the surface multi-grading on sutured instanton homology.
Normalized solutions of critical biharmonic equations on bounded domains

We study the critical biharmonic equation with clamped boundary conditions and prescribed $L^2$ norm on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$. For every sufficiently small mass, the constrained energy admits a local minimizer. We also obtain a second solution for masses in the closure of a measurable set having positive measure in every interval adjacent to zero. This holds on arbitrary smooth bounded domains when $N\ge8$ and, when $N=5,6,7$, under a condition involving the first clamped eigenvalue and a cutoff quotient. Explicit sufficient conditions are given and verified on balls. The proof combines a quantitative monotonicity argument with a norm estimate excluding loss of compactness.
The Hlawka-Schatten inequality: an exposition of recent progress

We give an expository account of recent progress on a question of Audenaert and Kittaneh concerning a Hlawka-type inequality for Schatten norms of matrices. We review the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality and explain the motivation behind understanding the so-called Hlawka-Schatten inequality. We present an elementary $2 \times 2$ construction showing that no finite constant satisfies the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for the trace norm, and explain Esa's proof that a dimension-independent constant exists for every $1 < p < \infty$. We also discuss the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for diagonal matrices and subsequent developments thereof on Prove2Me. Our aim is to make the mathematical ideas behind these AI-assisted results accessible, and to clarify their relationship with the available Lean formalizations.
A preconditioned Reconstructed Discontinuous Approximation for Darcy flow
Ming Cui; Yanxiang Gao; Ruo Li; Qicheng Liu; Fanyi Yang; Shuhai Zhao

In this paper, we develop an efficient numerical method for Darcy flow based on the reconstructed discontinuous approximation (RDA). The key contribution is a mesh-robust piecewise-constant preconditioner for arbitrarily high-order RDA discretizations of Darcy flow. The method discretizes the Darcy equations by a stabilized discontinuous Galerkin scheme in coupled velocity-pressure form, with RDA spaces for both velocity and pressure. Function spaces of this type can achieve arbitrarily high-order approximation accuracy while retaining only one degree of freedom per element. We establish an optimal-order error estimate in the energy norm and a suboptimal error estimate in the L2 norm. Benefiting from the property that the number of degrees of freedom of the RDA space is independent of the approximation order, we can construct a simple and efficient preconditioner based on piecewise constant functions for algebraic systems arising from arbitrarily high-order discretizations. We further prove a mesh-independent spectral equivalence between the preconditioner and the original algebraic system, so that the convergence of the GMRES residual does not slow down under mesh refinement. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed preconditioning method.
The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras

AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.
Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane

A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $α$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $α$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$. Call a $5$-subspace of $H$ a $β$-flat if all its blocks pass through one point, its focal point. We show that at least $41$ points of $H$ are not focal points of $β$-flats. Consequently $\mathcal{D}$ has at least $85$ non-$α$-points, at most $42$ $α$-points, and at most $22$ $α$-points in every hyperplane.
The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent

We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls or pairs of equal balls with diverging separation, with both alternatives realized by minimizing sequences. For $\mstar<m\le3\mstar/2$, only the separated pair occurs and the infimum is twice the energy of a half-mass ball. We also obtain the first-order change in interaction energy with respect to the exponent along subsequences of near-minimizers as $s\to1$ and $m\to m_*(1)$.
Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points

A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber. The convergence is uniform over compact sets disjoint from the tropical hypersurface, independently of the arguments of the point coordinates. When the chamber is nonempty and its index is an interior lattice point, the limit is the classical linking number of the oriented chamber boundary with the limiting logarithmic point. A plane cubic illustrates both this interpretation and its failure on a tropical wall.
The $H^p$-Corona theorem on bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary

For $0<p\le2$, we solve the $H^p$-Corona problem on bounded pseudoconvex domains $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$ with $C^2$ boundary, obtaining the bound $C_Ωδ^{-q-1}|\logδ|$, where $q=\min\{n,m-1\}$ and $m$ is the number of generators. The range of $p$ is sharp even on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain admitting a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function and having only one weakly pseudoconvex boundary point.
Free-boundary minimal varifolds I: zero boundary mass

Let $V$ be a $k$-varifold in a compact Riemannian manifold $M^n$ with smooth nonempty boundary, where $2 \le k < n$. Assume that $V$ is stationary with free boundary and almost minimizing modulo two in every sufficiently small relative annulus about each point of $M$. We prove that $V$ is integral and that the trace of the boundary second fundamental form on $T_x V$ vanishes at $\|V\|$-almost every boundary point. On all of $M$, the first variation is $δV = ν\,σ$, where $ν$ is the outward unit normal and $σ$ is a nonnegative measure on $\partial M$ singular with respect to $\|V\|$. A strict sign for the trace on all tangent $k$-planes at each boundary point forces zero boundary mass. For hypersurfaces in ambient dimensions three through seven, strict mean convexity gives smoothness and proper embeddedness. In every bounded smooth Euclidean domain $Ω$, we obtain $\|V\|(Ω) \ge c_{Ω,k}\|V\|(\overlineΩ)$ with $c_{Ω,k} > 0$. For smooth connected free-boundary minimal submanifolds in $\overlineΩ$, assuming a volume bound and a common annular almost minimizing condition at a fixed scale, then their first Dirichlet eigenvalues uniformly bounded above.
Local limit theorem for the Kemperman's oscillating walk
Andrew Elvey Price; Marc Peign{é}; Wachtel Vitali

We study the asymptotic behaviour of the local probabilities of the so-called oscillating walk on the latttice Z; this class of discrete time Markov chains was introduced by Kemperman. Our main result is a local counterpart of the convergence of a properly rescaled oscillating walk towards the corresponding skew Brownian motion. In particular, we show that the approximation of local probabilities by the density of the limiting distribution may fail in the points which are not far from zero.
On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations

We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.
Scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map and applications to Kähler reduction

Suppose that a compact and connected Lie group acts holomorphically on a Hodge manifold, and that the action linearises to the associated Hermitian ample line bundle. Assume that zero is a singular value of the associated moment map. The spaces of global holomorphic sections of powers of the line bundle decompose over the finite dimensional irreducible representations of the group. The main goal of this paper is to study the scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map. As an application, we discuss the quantization of the singular reduced space: the behaviour of invariant sections along the singular strata, the failure of the asymptotic unitarity of the Guillemin--Sternberg map near the singular strata, and the number of invariant sections concentrated near a singular orbit.
Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold

We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $Λ(m)=(36π)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation argument for critical minimizing sequences. All results hold for arbitrary finite-perimeter competitors, without connectedness or boundary regularity assumptions.
Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data

Let $Ω=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.
Endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules in special characteristic

We classify the division algebras that occur as endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank in special characteristic which cannot be defined over a finite field. The classification is in terms of the center of the algebra and its local invariants. Together with the known results in generic characteristic and over finite fields, this gives a complete description of the endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank.
Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities

We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.
Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms

Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<χ<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-χ,χ]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<χ<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $χ$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.
Backward Error and Scaling in Level-Based ILU(k) and IC(k) Preconditioners

We analyse the effect of rounding errors and diagonal scaling on level-based ILU($k$) and IC($k$) preconditioners. Because the sparsity pattern is fixed in advance, the computed factors are those that the incomplete factorization produces, in exact arithmetic, for a nearby matrix, and the deviation of the preconditioned matrix from the identity is bounded by an incompleteness term plus a rounding term. When no shift or pivot modification is needed, scaling leaves the iterates unchanged in exact arithmetic but can change the quantities in this bound by orders of magnitude. For IC($k$), we bound the change in the preconditioned eigenvalues caused by rounding by a multiple of the Skeel condition number of the incomplete factor, which does not depend on the scaling, and we show that after Jacobi scaling the entries of the factor are bounded, so that in half precision a breakdown can be detected before any overflow. Experiments in double, single and half precision illustrate the theory.
OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective

This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.
Principal spectral theory of time-periodic nonlocal advective cooperative systems and its applications
Hao Wu; Xiangdong Fang; Wan-Tong Li; Wenjie Ni

We develop a new spectral theory for time-periodic nonlocal cooperative systems with advection on bounded intervals, allowing asymmetric dispersal kernels. By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincaré map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. For spatially homogeneous coefficients, we establish the limit of the principal eigenvalue as the interval expands to $\mathbb R$ and identify it as the minimum of the principal Floquet exponents of the associated exponentially weighted periodic systems. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solutions either converge to a unique positive time-periodic solution or vanish as time tends to infinity. We also prove convergence of positive periodic solutions as the interval expands. For the Cauchy problem on the whole real line, we characterize the leftward and rightward spreading speeds, which may differ for asymmetric dispersal kernels, and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for accelerated spreading in either direction. In particular, under irreducible coupling, accelerated spreading in one component induces accelerated spreading in all components in the same direction.
Sierpiński Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals

Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Eroğlu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.
How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges

After causal discovery, a confidence interval for a total effect valid uniformly over the model class must pay for structural uncertainty. We measure this price by the worst-case ratio of expected length to that of the efficient interval knowing the graph, for linear Gaussian models with a known superset of the adjacencies and k-triangle faithfulness. The global price is of order sqrt(n) once one edge can be malignant, so we study it locally, near a generic distribution with one edge absent. Our main result classifies this weak edge by Meek closures. It is benign if deleting it leaves the effect identifiable in the resulting MPDAG and Markov equivalent explanations agree; the local price is then bounded, and otherwise, for small k, of order sqrt(n). At benign edges the price is of order R+K, with R a ratio of efficient lengths and K a cross-model constant. It equals one, so that honesty is free, exactly when K = 0, generically decided by a d-separation. For two Markov classes it is determined within a factor 3.40, and its upper bound is approached without knowing the base point or the weak edge. A further graphical condition gives the rate uniformly in a second edge's margin.
Existence and multiplicity of radial solutions for higher order logarithmic and infinite mass Schrödinger equations
Chen Huang; Rong Li; Junren Luo; Xian Zhang

We study radial solutions of the Schrödinger equation $-Δu+V(x)u=g(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$, where $V$ is radial and $g(t)/t\to-\infty$ as $t\to0$. In this infinite-mass case the energy functional is not finite on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. First let $g(t)=t|\log|t||^{α-1}\log|t|$ with $α>1$. We only assume that $V$ is continuous and bounded from below. So $V$ may change sign, and it need not be coercive or have a limit at infinity. We obtain a nontrivial radial solution and a sequence of radial solutions whose energies tend to infinity. To do this, we add the term $λ|u|^{p-2}u$ with $1<p<2$, find critical points of the perturbed functional by minimax methods, and let $λ\to0$. The infinite-mass structure gives the compactness in this limit. Next let $g$ be odd, with a power bound near zero and at most critical growth at infinity. Let $V$ be bounded, with a smallness condition on $(x\cdot\nabla V)_+$. We combine the Pohozaev identity with an augmented symmetric minimax method and obtain infinitely many pairs of radial solutions. A negative critical power term is allowed.
Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
Hanzhi Bai; Xinyu Hu; Kaidi Liu; Guanghui Wang

Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{Ω_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{Θ_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in the affirmative a question posed by Mubayi and Suk. As a second application of our theorem, we show $r_k(k+1,3;n)=2^{Θ_k(n^{k-2}\log n)}$, which, together with a new stepping-up lemma developed in this paper, further yields $r_k(k+1,t;n)=\twr_{t-1}(Θ_{k,t}(n^{k-t+1}\log n))$ for every fixed $k\ge6$ and $4\le t\le k-2$, where $\twr_1(x)=x$ and $\twr_{j+1}(x)=2^{\twr_j(x)}$. Here $r_k(k+1,t;n)$ denotes the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-subsets of an $N$-vertex set contains either $k+1$ vertices spanning at least $t$ red edges or a blue clique of order $n$. As a third application of our theorem, we show that $r_k(F_{\ell,k,d},n)>2^{Ω_{k,\ell,d}(n^{k-d-2}\log n)}$ for all fixed integers $k\ge4$, $1\le d\le k-3$, and $\ell\ge2k+1$ with $k\nmid\ell$, where $F_{\ell,k,d}$ is obtained from the $k$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$ by deleting $d$ consecutive edges.
Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow

We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\).
MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization

Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.
The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds

We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.
Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic

We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_λ$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $λ^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.
A construction of proper Jordan schemes of rank $5$

Let $q$ be a prime power such that $m=q^2+q+1$ is a prime satisfying $m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. We construct a proper symmetric Jordan scheme of rank $5$ on $2m$ vertices using a Singer difference set with parameters $(m,q+1,1)$ and the Paley graph on $m$ vertices.

Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

Let $a,b\in\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)$ with $a\neq 1$, and let $s$ be chosen uniformly in $A_n$. We show that the probability that $\langle a, bs\rangle$ is insoluble tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly in $a$ and $b$. More precisely, this probability is at least $1-O(n^{-1/24})$. The proof combines a bound in terms of the support of $a$ with estimates on permutations lying in transitive subgroups of the symmetric group.
Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error

Subentropy gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of ensembles of pure states. We prove its subadditivity for arbitrary bipartite states in finite dimensions and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. This relation strengthens a conjectured comparison with conditional min-entropy. Its inverse gives the strongest universal lower bound on the error determined only by conditional subentropy and the number of labels. Both main results follow from a comparison of conditional subentropy with the average subentropy of measurement posteriors, valid for mixed signal states and every finite measurement. We characterize all equality cases in these two results and bound posterior deviations near equality. We also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, including the exact constant when the quantum marginal is fixed. A determinant inequality strengthens subadditivity and proves strong subadditivity for classical distributions, while an exact counterexample shows that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states. Lean 4 proofs of all theoretical results are available at https://pratikpatil.io/lean/subentropy/
Synchronisation under quasi-periodic forcing of circle diffeomorphisms with two attracting and two repelling fixed points

We study the dynamics of circle diffeomorphisms, which have exactly two attracting and two repelling fixed points, under quasi-periodic forcing. For sufficiently small forcing, such a system exhibits uniformly hyperbolic behaviour. The results focus on systems with larger forcing, where every orbit intersects the basins of attraction of both attracting fixed points infinitely often. For such quasi-periodically forced circle diffeomorphisms, we identify a set of parameters of positive measure for which the corresponding skew-product systems admit a unique attracting and a unique repelling invariant graph, which capture the dynamics of Lebesgue almost every point on $\mathbb{T}^2$. Further, we show that both continuous invariant graphs and invariant graphs that are discontinuous on a dense set can occur within the same class of forced circle diffeomorphisms, for different quasi-periodic rotations on the base.

We study the support of the optimizer $π_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. The construction is indexed by smooth balanced periodic seeds satisfying a simple characteristic condition at a nonzero initial value. A local inverse, followed by an exact correction of the full vector remainder, yields estimates with a fixed loss of derivatives. A smoothing iteration then eliminates the actual return error on a fixed open set of positive radius while retaining the seed as the leading nonlinearity.
Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES

Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. Consequently, the region of spacelike slopes is nonconvex, making the preservation of spacelikeness more delicate. We identify a natural geometric condition that overcomes this difficulty: the closed convex hull of the initial slopes is compactly contained in the spacelike region. We prove that the convex hull is preserved along the flow, yielding uniform spacelikeness and uniform acausality. For initially $C^{1,α}$ graphs, we establish global existence and uniqueness, without assuming convexity or initial curvature bounds. If the initial perturbation vanishes at spatial infinity, we further prove smooth and uniform convergence to the prescribed affine spacelike line, without rescaling. Remotest Operator Control String-Averaging Methods in Feasibility-Seeking
Yair Censor; Ariel Nisenbaum; Simeon Reich

The string-averaging (SA) method is a versatile algorithmic scheme for solving feasibility-seeking problems. It partitions the index set of all constraints into subsets of indices, called strings, allowing the user to apply operators successively along each string separately, and thus in parallel. The end-points of all such string operations are convexly combined to create the next iterate. Due to its flexible framework, SA is not restricted solely to this procedure; however, this characteristic applies only to the simultaneous step, while the sequential one is restricted to operator compositions. To permit alternative strategies in the latter, a novel algorithmic structure termed the Skeletal SA is introduced. Although its convergence is not established, it serves as a foundational "parent" structure that unveils unexamined SA algorithmic structures, as well as other known methods, obscured by standard compositions. This method favorably handles the common fixed point problem (CFPP), which requires finding a point within the intersection of finitely many constraint sets whose intersection is nonempty. However, remotest operator control SA (ROC-SA) methods have remained unexamined in this context.

In a nonlinear two-state model, the quadratic remainder estimate holds uniformly over terminal threshold events. We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $Δ$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $Δ$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.

The rate is governed by whether the squared modulus of the dominant non-Perron root is smaller than, equal to, or larger than the Perron root. This result quantifies the approach to the common cohort limit and distinguishes the present cohort-level question from first-order Perron convergence alone.
Products of translates: bounds and constructions
Sian Fang; Danqing He; Xinyu Zhu

We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(α)}$ for some $c(α)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^α$ with $α<1$.

Soobin Cho; Panki Kim; Renming Song; Zoran Vondraček

Let $D$ be a $C^{1, η}$ open set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{B}: D\times D\to (0, \infty)$ a symmetric Borel function which blows up at the boundary of $D$. Let $\overline{X}$ be a conservative purely discontinuous Markov process on $\overline{D}$ with jump kernel $\mathcal{B}(x,y)|x-y|^{-d-α}$, $0<α<2$. In a recent paper, we obtained two-sided estimates on the transition density of $\overline{X}$. In this paper, we consider the process $X$ obtained by killing $\overline{X}$ upon approaching the boundary of $D$ or by a critical potential. We obtain sharp two-sided estimates on the transition density of $X$. The estimates capture the interplay between the blow-up rate of $\mathcal{B}$, the geometry of $D$, and killing.
A High-Order Geometry-Conforming Selective Discontinuous Galerkin Method and Its Error Analysis for Elliptic Interface Problems on Curved Domains

We develop and analyze a high-order geometry-conforming immersed finite element (GC-IFE) method for elliptic interface problems on curved domains. The method uses a triangular mesh that conforms to the outer boundary but need not fit the internal interface. Groups with dual classes of subgroups
E. Ingrosso; M. Trombetti; A. Zitouni

We completely characterize insoluble groups whose subgroups are pronormal or pronormalize every subgroup. We also completely describe $p$-groups with this property, and prove many structural results in the soluble case (for example, such groups are always of length at most $3$ and have Sylow towers).
IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow

The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. We study normal-play subtraction games with one globally shared pass. An expansion of the subtraction set is pass-equivalent if it leaves the pass-available Sprague--Grundy sequence unchanged. We show that pure periodicity of the ordinary sequence, together with an eventual translation identity for the pass-available sequence, forces every pass-equivalent expansion to preserve the ordinary sequence. We extend this result to sets in short intervals. An exact recurrence certificate also exhibits a three-element set for which pass-state rigidity fails.
Raoof Zare Moayedi; Mohammad Hossein Yassaee; Javad B. Ebrahimi

We give polynomial-time algorithms for Gaussian multi-sampling under approximate $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differential privacy, with optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors. Their joint distribution is $α$-close in total variation to $P^{\otimes m}$. Our lower bounds hold even for dependent outputs under the same joint accuracy guarantee, showing that exact independence incurs no additional sample cost beyond logarithmic factors. The single-sampler of Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis [COLT 2025] uses $\widetilde{O}(d/\varepsilon)$ input samples. Running it on a separate input dataset for each of $m$ outputs therefore costs $\widetilde{O}(md/\varepsilon)$ in total. Our approach builds on the stable weighted statistics of Brown, Hopkins, and Smith [COLT 2023], also used for Gaussian single-sampling by Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis. To control privacy loss when the entire batch shares these statistics, we compare the joint output densities and obtain a privacy bound that scales with the square root of the batch size. The stability step downweights influential records and can reject the entire batch. Both actions can make the outputs dependent. Our correction restores exact independence while preserving differential privacy and joint accuracy.

We prove the folklore conjecture on maximal central sections of the cube in every dimension and codimension. The maximizing sections are exactly the products of diagonals of disjoint coordinate blocks whose sizes differ by at most one. This determines the sharp volume in the cases left open by Ball's 1989 bounds. In fixed dimensions, the logarithmic volume deficit controls both the direction and the displacement of an affine section linearly, with optimal exponent. We also obtain the sharp uniform bound on projection densities for independent real random variables with bounded densities.
