We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$. Using the imported arithmetic relative-image identification, we construct a reflection pairing and derive the completed functional equation with positive root number. We also give a canonical Frobenius-equivariant splitting of the fibrewise compact-support/parabolic sequence by separation of weights and examine the comparison on open coordinate-zero divisors. The statements do not assume global arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or a higher-codimension wild-boundary exchange. An explicit source-and-dependency ledger distinguishes results imported from the companion papers from deductions established here.
Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.
Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based

We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.

For positive integers $M$ and $N$, consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n\in[M,M+N)}χ_p(n)$, where $χ_p$ is the quadratic character modulo $p$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}+\varepsilon}$ for any integer $r\geq 2$ and any real $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Booker, who showed (under size restrictions on $M$, $N$, $p$ and $r$) that $\lvert S(M,N)\rvert \leq α(r)N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}}(β(r)+\log{p})^{1/2r}$, where $α(r)$ and $β(r)$ are given in (Booker, 2006). We show that when $M$ is not too small compared to $N$, we can improve $β(r)$ by a fixed amount. If $M$ is also not too large compared to $N$, we can further improve $β(r)$ by an amount proportional to $\frac{M}{M+N}$.

Recently, a particular type of defining set is being used to get $Lee$-weight distribution over a particular type of ring. However, little work has been done on mixed alphabets. Therefore, in Section 3, we investigate the $Lee$-weight distributions associated with various kinds of defining sets, labelled A to J, for code constructions over the mixed-alphabet ring $R=Z^α_2 Z^β_4$, where $α$ and $β$ are positive finite integers. Using Parseval's identity, we determine the cardinalities of the defining sets A to J. We further establish several new results concerning 2-$Lee$-weight and 3-$Lee$-weight distributions.
Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
Chenlin Gu; Tom Hutchcroft; Xiaoran Li

It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $σ(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $μ(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $μ(p)$ known as the time constant. By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open seven-dimensional coordinates are deferred to the outermost layer, all positions of the same type across all layers can be pooled per record and filled jointly via grouped binary-flag nodes. This paper investigates the uniqueness issue of Chern connections from the Cheng-Yau type estimate point of view. A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
Agnese Barbensi; Daniele Celoria; Lavender Marshall; Finn Thompson

Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type.
GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces

In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

This formula arises as the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling limit of a zero-temperature Brownian last-passage identity from our earlier work on the O'Connell-Yor polymer. To pass the coalescence probabilities to the limit, we show that two paths sharing an optimal exit almost surely lose total weight if they must stay disjoint before reaching it. We construct two exact embedded special Lagrangian germs with the same unique multiplicity-one tangent cone, the Harvey--Lawson cone in $\mathbb C^9$. A quadratic obstruction and a corrected cubic obstruction yield the distinct sharp $C^1$ convergence rates $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1}$ and $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$, respectively. We also prove Jacobi nonintegrability of the Harvey--Lawson cones in $\mathbb C^8$ and $\mathbb C^9$, and realize the sharp rate $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$ at the eight-dimensional cone.

We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. Unlike classical Fujita problems, regular solutions exist globally, so the relevant dichotomy concerns boundedness versus grow-up. We identify the critical exponent $q_c=N/(N-1)$ for $N\geq 2$, with $q_c=\infty$ for $N=1$. For stationary forcing, every solution grows at least linearly on a fixed ball when $1<q\leq q_c$. In two dimensions, solutions tend to infinity locally uniformly for every $q>1$, with an explicit logarithmic lower bound. For $q=2$, the Cole--Hopf transformation relates the exact growth rate to the spectrum of $-Δ-w$. Conversely, when $N\geq 3$ and $q>q_c$, bounded solutions exist for sufficiently small nonnegative data and forcing. We also establish growth criteria for time-dependent forcing, including decaying profiles.
H(n)-Gordian graphs of knotoids and their quotients: Gromov hyperbolicity

In this paper, we study $H(n)$-moves on knotoid diagrams and the corresponding $H(n)$-Gordian graphs. We establish that the $H(n)$-Gordian graphs of knotoids are not Gromov hyperbolic. We also consider quotient graphs of the $H(n)$-Gordian graph of knotoids by the following knotoid invariants: the height of a knotoid, the span of the affine index polynomial, the $y$-span and $z$-span of the invariant $H_K(t, y, z)$, and the span of the Jones polynomial. We prove that in all these cases, the quotient graphs are Gromov hyperbolic.

Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. Simulations with up to $10^5$ degrees of freedom confirm both predictions without adjustable parameters. Requiring neither tangent-space evolution nor prior specification of an order parameter for its computation, trajectory arclength provides a simple, quantitative link between microscopic Hamiltonian motion and collective thermodynamic criticality.

Both self-orthogonal codes and MDS codes are of great interest for coding and combinatorial theory. In this paper we consider the existence problem of self-orthogonal MDS codes, i.e, codes satisfying self-orthogonality and achieving the Singleton bound. More precisely, we investigate for which length $n$ and dimension $k$, there exist $q$-ary $[n,k]$ self-orthogonal MDS codes. We completely solve this problem for even prime power $q$ except for the case where $[n,k]=[q+2,3]$. For odd prime power $q$, we solve this problem for the cases where $n=q+1$, $n|q$ or $n|(q-1)$ except for two cases where (i) $[n,k]=[q+1, (q-1)/2]$; and (ii) $[n,k]=[q-1,(q-1)/2]$ and $q\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. Furthermore, we conjecture nonexistence of self-orthogonal MDS code for the first case. For odd $q$, we also show existence of self-orthogonal MDS codes for some other cases. Note that in general a self-orthogonal MDS code can not be derived from self-dual MDS codes (see the detailed discussion in Section 1). Our technique is to make use of the language of algebraic geometry codes. An advantage of using the language of algebraic geometry codes is that the Euclidean dual code of a functional algebraic geometry code is a differential code which can be turn into a functional code again. Thus, by choosing an appropriate differential, one can give an explicit construction of self-orthogonal MDS codes.
The response field approach to path integral control

This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. The response field is found to play an analogous role to the backward adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. In particular, the gradient of the optimal cost-to-go at the initial time, which is proportional to the optimal control, is given by the average of the response field at the initial time. In contrast to the case of non-equilibrium dynamics, the response function is found to be acausal in the control setting. The linear-quadratic case of path integral control is studied, confirming it as the free theory, meaning that solving the control problem is equivalent to completing the square and determining the propagator for a two point boundary value problem. The developments presented here are a necessary prelude to applications based on field theoretic approximation, for both path integral control and their dual inference problems.
Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing
Theshani Nuradha; Sujeet Bhalerao; Christoph Hirche; Mark M. Wilde; Mingze Xu

The hockey-stick divergence is a fundamental distinguishability measure in quantum information theory. It characterizes quantum differential privacy and determines the optimal error probability of binary quantum hypothesis testing with arbitrary priors. We study how it behaves on tensor-product states. To this end, we consider the noncommutative minimum $m(A,B):=(\mathrm{Tr}[A]+\mathrm{Tr}[B]-\|A-B\|_1)/2$ of positive semidefinite operators, which reduces to $\sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}$ when $A$ and $B$ commute, and we prove that it is super-multiplicative, i.e., $m(A\otimes C,B\otimes D)\ge m(A,B)\,m(C,D)$. As a consequence, we establish a sub-additivity property of the hockey-stick divergence on product states, in which the parameters of the individual systems are multiplied, and no additional prefactor appears. We show that this bound is tight, also for noncommuting states, and that it is strict for faithful states whenever at least two of the divergences are positive. Using this, we obtain sub-additivity of the Datta-Leditzky divergences, a parallel composition theorem for quantum differentially private channels under product neighboring inputs with at most linear degradation of the privacy parameters, and a sharp sub-additivity property of the hypothesis-testing relative entropy normalized by the acceptance probability. Finally, we apply the same tools to symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing. We determine the exact prefactor of the quantum Chernoff bound for every pair of noncommuting states satisfying mild conditions including a nonlattice condition and, under a quantitative version of this condition, the full asymptotic expansion to every fixed order in $1/n$, with explicitly computable coefficients. As a consequence, we determine the sample complexity of symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing up to one sample, as the error probability tends to zero.
CSI-Agnostic End-to-End Neural Decoding of LDPC Codes under Synchronization Errors
Yi Kuang; Shu Liu; Ningning Wang

Correcting synchronization errors (insertions, deletions, and substitutions) in concatenated coding schemes, typically comprising an inner marker code and an outer Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) code, poses a significant challenge. Traditional algebraic decoding fails entirely under sequence misalignment. While recent neural pipelines attempt to resolve this, they typically demand exact channel state information (CSI) for inner synchronization and suffer from error propagation caused by premature syndrome binarization before outer decoding. In this paper, we propose ASDecoder, a data-driven, CSI-agnostic end-to-end neural decoding architecture specifically designed for LDPC codes over insertion-deletion-substitution (IDS) channels. ASDecoder features a CNN-Transformer front-end that implicitly aligns variable-length sequences and fuses multi-read redundancies without requiring explicit CSI. Tightly integrated into this pipeline is a novel \emph{syndrome-free} BiDecoder back-end. By mapping continuous soft features directly into a sparse-masked graph attention network, it strictly avoids intermediate hard decisions and effectively captures topological constraints. Experiments demonstrate that a single universal ASDecoder outperforms the BCJRFormer baseline, providing consistent error correction across highly asymmetric channels. Furthermore, it generalizes robustly to real-world deployment scenarios, including the industrial CCSDS $(128,64)$ QC-LDPC standard and non-linear DNA biological constraints.
On the extension of non-faithful and non-normal traces of von Neumann algebras to their affiliated operators

Let $τ$ be a positive tracial functional on a finite von Neumann algebra ${\mathcal{M}}$, not necessarily normal. For a positive self-adjoint operator $A$ affiliated with ${\mathcal{M}}$ we define ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}τ(A(\mathrm{I}+hA)^{-1})\in[0,\infty]$. We show that $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(A)=\sup_Rτ(\min(A,R \mathrm{I}))$. We prove that ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is additive on positive affiliated operators, by a form--resolvent comparison valid for arbitrary positive traces. As a consequence, $τ$ has a positive linear extension to the span $\mathscr D_τ$ of the positive affiliated operators of finite extended trace, and $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(T^*T)$ defines a pre-Hilbert structure for every positive trace. For every trace, $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S+T|)^{2/3}\le τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S|)^{2/3}+τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)^{2/3}$; hence the operators $T$ with $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)<\infty$ form a ${\mathcal{M}}$-bimodule $\mathscr L_Y^1$, on which the linear extension is defined and cyclic. It turns out that $\mathscr L_Y^1=\mathscr D_τ$; $d(S,T)={τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(|S-T|)^{2/3}$ is a translation-invariant pseudometric on $\mathscr L^1_Y$ and is a metric iff $τ$ is faithful. On the approximation side, a Chernoff family in ${\mathcal{M}}$ forces affiliation of its generator. Trace defects of Chernoff families need not converge to ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)$, even for faithful normal traces, while two-sided resolvent comparison suffices. For faithful normal traces, ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is the canonical extension and the associated space $\mathscr L_Y^p$ coincide with the classical $L^p({\mathcal{M}},τ)$ as well as their norms ($1\leq p<\infty$).
Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
Yeyuan Chen; Mahdi Cheraghchi; King-Siong Si; Zihan Zhang

This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah--Guruswami--Li (SODA 2024), where achieving the generalized Singleton bound in the list-decoding setting also necessitates exponential alphabet size.
An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem

We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every integer $t\geq2$, \[ N(G,K_t)\leq \frac1n\sum_{v\in V(G)}Z_t(n,c(v)). \] Equality holds if and only if $G$ is $K_t$-free or $G\cong T_s(n)$ for some $t\leq s\leq n$. Moreover, the coefficients $Z_t(n,s)$ are pointwise best possible among all bounds of this form. Our result strengthens the previous vertex-localized bound \[ N(G,K_t)\leq n^{t-1} \sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{\binom{c(v)}{t}}{c(v)^t} \] by accounting for the integer part sizes of Turán graphs. The comparison between the two upper bounds is strict precisely when some vertex $v$ satisfies $c(v)\geq t$ and $c(v)\nmid n$. As consequences, we recover the exact Zykov and Turán bounds without divisibility assumptions.
Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
Jingying Hu; Jiao Li; Yufeng Xu; Jinyong Ying

Being able to find multiple solutions of a semilinear elliptic equation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing. In this paper, fully taking the advantages of randomized neural networks, we propose a new efficient and accurate method for identifying potentially as many solutions as possible. The new method is constructed from three aspects--initialization, optimization, a technique for acceleration and improving accuracy, two of which are innovative developments. Firstly, based on the basis functions of a randomized network and the sampling points, a characteristic matrix is introduced so that its singular value decomposition can be used to determine weakly variant search directions, followed by a newly developed algorithm to generate effective initial candidates. Then the good deflated Gauss-Newton method [see {\em A. Riley, et al., SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47~(5) (2025) A2963-A2987}] using an exponential deflation operator is adapted as the optimization to search for all multiple solutions. Local error estimate of a particular solution under some proper condition is given in terms of the neurons in the hidden layer and the sampling points for this newly designed method. Furthermore, to accelerate the computation and improve the solution accuracy, a new multilevel method based on hierarchical networks is designed. Without using any {\em a priori} information, several numerical tests show together with the multilevel method, the new method can not only accurately find multiple solutions with relative errors reaching $10^{-16}$ only in less than one-tenth computational cost for the best case, but also preserve the inherent symmetries of multiple solutions.
Tableau Consequence under Positive Contexts: A Reconstruction of Walukiewicz's Completeness Proof

We establish a positive-context lifting theorem for tableau consequence in the modal $μ$-calculus: under explicit syntactic hypotheses, $\mathcal T_B\Rightarrow\mathcal T_C$ induces $\mathcal T_{A(B)}\Rightarrow\mathcal T_{A(C)}$. The proof orders instances of the given relation by birth time and assigns overlapping formula occurrences to the oldest supporting instance. A corollary gives bidirectional replacement by automaton normal form inside positive contexts. Together with a separate unfolding consequence lemma and ANF bisimulation, the lifting theorem yields a self-contained reconstruction of Walukiewicz's completeness proof for Kozen's axiomatisation and makes its least-fixpoint step more transparent. We also give a finite parity-game proof of regular-refutation existence and a two-sided transfer from tableau consequence to thin refutations.
Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent

Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches between human players and an adaptive bot.
Statistically Optimal and Near Linear Time Hypothesis Selection
Satyen Kale; Amirreza Shaeiri; Kunal Talwar

In hypothesis selection we are given $n$ distributions $q_1,\dots,q_n$ on a countable domain $\mathcal{X}$ and samples from an unknown distribution $p$. The goal is a distribution $q$ with $\mathrm{TV}(p,q)\leα\min_i\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)+ε$. The factor $α=2$ is optimal for algorithms using a number of samples from $p$ that is independent of $|\mathcal{X}|$, and in general only improper learners achieve it. We give a learner that achieves $α=2$ with $O(\log(n/δ)/ε^2)$ samples of $p$, with probability at least $1-δ$. This matches the sample complexity of Yatracos's factor-$3$ estimator, and it removes the logarithmic factors in the factor-$2$ bound of Bousquet et al. (FOCS 2021). The learner accesses the $q_i$ only through sampling and pointwise comparisons. We measure its running time by its oracle complexity, the number of oracle calls. In expectation it makes $O((nε^{-2}+ε^{-4}\log(1/ε))\log(n/δ))$ oracle calls, independent of $\mathcal{X}$. It runs multiplicative weights over the constraints $\mathrm{TV}(q,q_i)\le\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)$ and uses at most one sample of $p$ per round.
A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
Ku-Yu Fan; Hau-Yi Lin; Jinbo Yu

In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^nζ(\{1,3\}^n)=ζ(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.
Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values

We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.
Sampling with graph wavelet kernels: optimality and adaptivity to regularity and geometry
Pranav Gupta; Hoang-Son Tran; Subhroshekhar Ghosh

We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. These samplers satisfy the same variance reduction for linear statistics of $s$-Hölder observables and yield conditionally unbiased estimators of empirical averages with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$, using at most $2n$ function evaluations. In both settings, the rates are governed by the intrinsic dimension $m$ and the regularity $s$ of the observable.
Min Gao; Zizhou Tang; Wenjiao Yan

The main theorem of the present paper is that $S^4\times P$ admits a complex structure whenever $P$ is the fibre product, over a compact complex manifold, of the unit circle bundles of an even number of holomorphic line bundles. This theorem has lots of significant applications. For example, $S^4\times G$ admits a complex structure for every compact Lie group $G$ of even dimension. The same holds for $S^4\times V_{2s}(C^n)$ and $S^4\times V_{2s}(H^n)$ when $n\geq 2s\geq2$, and for $S^4\times V_{4s}(R^n)$ when $n\ge4s\ge4$. The theorem also gives complex structures on the product of $S^4$ with any even number of odd-dimensional spheres. Moreover, complex structures exist on $S^4$ times some moment-angle manifolds, including certain connected sums of sphere products. The construction uses a holomorphic $(C^*)^2$-action on $S^4 \times T^2$ endowed with the complex structure we constructed in [Gao-Tang-Yan, arXiv:2610.06067v1] and a smooth splitting equivariant under the compact torus.
Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices

Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $φ\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.
Self-similar solutions to the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane

We classify the self-similar solutions of the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$. Using hyperbolic numbers, the self-similarity condition becomes a linear ODE system, and all solutions are obtained in closed form with explicit smoothness and completeness criteria. Translating solitons occur in three causal types, and dilation--rotation solitons are governed by the discriminant $Δ=a^2-4(b-1)$, as in the Euclidean case. When $a^2=b^2$ the translation cannot be eliminated, owing to the zero divisors of the hyperbolic numbers, and a genuinely Lorentzian class of mixed solitons arises, whose complete smooth members form a one-parameter family. The planar classification is then extended to translationally invariant solutions in $\mathbb{R}^{n,1}$, and rotationally invariant solutions are reduced to an explicit ODE system.
Global existence and large-time behavior of classical axisymmetric solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Saint-Venant equations and related models
Xiangdi Huang; Muxi Lei; Weili Meng

In this paper, we study a two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity in a disk, subject to the no-slip boundary condition. We consider both the symmetric viscous stress and the stress written in terms of the full velocity gradient. In each case the coefficients satisfy the BD relation $μ(ρ)=ρ^α$ and $λ(ρ)=2(α-1)ρ^α$. For every $1/2<α\le1$ and $γ>1$, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for arbitrarily large axisymmetric initial data with strictly positive density and possibly nonzero tangential velocity. Moreover, the density has upper and positive lower bounds independent of time, and the solution converges to the constant equilibrium. The two stresses give the same radial momentum equation, but require different estimates of the tangential velocity. The endpoint $α=1$, $γ=2$ includes the viscous shallow-water equations.
Space-Time Covariance with Screening Effects, Markov Property, and Long-Range Dependence

Constructing space-time covariance models is an essential task to account for spatio-temporal dependence. However, there is a lack of practical guidance for constructing new covariance constructions. This paper focuses on studying the interplay among three statistical properties: screening effect, Markov property, and long-range dependence for constructing desirable parsimonious space-time covariance functions. While these properties imply seemingly conflicting statistical practice, it is shown in this paper that closed-form parsimonious covariance functions that simultaneously possess all these properties could be constructed and may be desirable for understanding space-time dependence. To examine these properties, this paper first shows that the confluent hypergeometric (CH) covariance function has asymptotic screening effect even in long-range dependent regime. Then this paper provides theoretical characterizations on Markov property for the hierarchical mixture construction including a necessary and sufficient condition. To account for more practical structures, this paper constructs a flexible Lagrangian CH model with the time-lag varying smoothness and tail decay parameters via a hierarchical mixture approach. These properties are illustrated via simulation studies. The practical performance under these models is evaluated for the Irish wind data and the sea surface temperature data.
Jingmin Huang; Wei Zhao; Renjie Zhong

This paper studies the sale of supplementary training dataset to improve predictive model. The buyer not only has private knowledge of its own dataset, but also can choose the way to merge these two datasets. This flexibility imposes a new constraint on the menu, requiring the buyer's total net utility be monotonic in the Blackwell order on private datasets. Given that, we show that a single posted price for a fully informative dataset is optimal in hypothesis testing, under differential virtual-value condition. The result extends to multi-class classification in which private datasets share a clean component but differ in how their labels are contaminated.
A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form

In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. Ikramov, On the Symplectic Eigenvalues of Positive Definite Matrices. Moscow Univ. Comput. Math. Cybern., 42(2018)1-4]. As an application, we present another proof of Williamson's diagonal form for positive-semidefinite matrices with symplectic kernels.
Division rings of fractions of LV-algebras
Huynh Viet Khanh; Vo Hoang Thanh

Let $K$ be a field and let $A=L_K(E,ω)$ be an LV-algebra of a row-finite weighted graph. We prove that $A$ embeds in a division ring if and only if $E$ has one vertex and its ordered loop weights satisfy $w_n=n$ and $w_j>j$ for $1\le j<n$. Under these conditions, $A$ has a universal division ring of fractions, which we identify with the free field on $2\sum_{j=1}^n w_j-n^2$ generators over $K$. We construct a free generating set explicitly by factoring the matrix of generators. We classify the resulting division rings over $K$ and bound the stabilization required to recognize invertible matrices. These results include mixed weights, for which the LV-algebra need not be a semifir.
Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
Guowei Dai; Yingxin Sun; Yong Zhang

In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area. We prove the higher-dimensional conjecture in dimensions four and five by establishing a sharp comparison between the first clamped-plate eigenvalue and the square of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on the same domain. The proof uses a nonlinear transformation built from the ball eigenfunctions. A local identity keeps all terms of the Hessian. Exact coefficient inequalities and bounds for the infinite remainders establish positivity, while a weak formulation handles sign changes and critical sets. We characterize equality in the volume inequality and identify an obstruction to this transformation in dimension six.
Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature II: Multiplicity One

Let \(M_t^n\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}\) be a smooth mean curvature flow of closed embedded hypersurfaces, with \(n\ge3\), and let \(T\) be its first singular time. If the integral of \(|A|^n\) is uniformly bounded for \(t<T\), every nonzero tangent flow at time \(T\) has multiplicity one. At each singular point the tangent flow is unique, and the rescaled flow converges locally smoothly to a closed self-shrinker.
From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems

Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. We then construct higher-dimensional systems by coupling these low-dimensional building blocks through masked and multi-head attention mechanisms. We discuss the persistence of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds under weak coupling and investigate how the coupling architecture influences the resulting dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal the emergence of additional expanding directions, including a 60-particle system in which 26 of the 40 computed Lyapunov exponents exceed 0.01. These results demonstrate the richness of the dynamical behavior possible in simplified self-attention systems and motivate further investigation of the invariant structures organizing their high-dimensional dynamics.
Levi Dynamics and Largest Domains of Discontinuity on Flag Manifolds
Ángel Cano; Marlon M. López-Flores; José Seade; Andrew Shaw

Divergent sequences in a semisimple Lie group have a bounded Levi part that is invisible to Cartan projections and limit flags. We show that this Levi part is a genuine dynamical invariant and determines much of the large-scale behaviour of discrete groups on flag manifolds. For every real flag manifold, we compute the complete moving-source destination relation of a divergent sequence, including the Levi contribution. This yields a stratified convergence principle, a boundary compactification encoding the relation, and an exact properness criterion. For discrete groups the relation organises the classical limit sets into a single flag, from Quint's limit set through the recurrent and Kulkarni sets to the Myrberg set, the complement of equicontinuity. Sequences with coalescing limit flags satisfy a diagonal formula, which gives a recurrence criterion for the largest domain of proper discontinuity. For compact twists of Kleinian groups, the criterion becomes an exact incidence condition on the twist closure on every Grassmannian and Lagrangian Grassmannian. Two strongly irreducible subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(8,\mathbb{C})$ with identical marked Cartan projections, limit flags and destination relations on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^7$ are distinguished on $\operatorname{Gr}(4,\mathbb{C}^8)$ alone. We also show that marked boundary data recover the compact twist while unmarked data recover only its orbit partition. Further applications treat critical projective dynamics, cusped Hitchin groups and symmetric powers.
Several families of linear codes via weight functions of three-weight codes

Recently, Huang et al. proposed a general framework for deriving new linear codes from a given code by applying weight functions to the set of codewords with a prescribed Hamming weight in [A structural theory of linear codes from weight functions: constructions, geometry and applications, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, DOI:10.1109/TIT.2026.3742840, 2026]. While this method was systematically developed for two-weight codes and yielded several families of projective two-weight codes, extending it to codes with more weights remains an interesting and challenging problem. In this paper, we generalize this construction to three-weight codes by employing a well-known family of ternary three-weight cyclic codes. By determining the weight distribution of every codimension-one subcode, as well as the distribution of fixed-weight codewords across these subcodes, we completely characterize the behavior of the weight-function construction on this family. As a result, we obtain three classes of linear codes with four nonzero weights and explicitly determine their parameters. Furthermore, the results show that these obtained codes are self-orthogonal and minimal.
First-Order Information from Noisy Comparison Oracles
Qipei Chen; Katya Scheinberg; Zikai Xiong

We study stochastic and deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization problems where neither the functions nor their derivatives can be computed or estimated and the only information about the objective is available via pairwise comparisons. We focus on a specific model of smooth comparison oracles, as in the Bradley-Terry and Thurstone models, in which the probability of a correct comparison depends smoothly on the function-value gap. We investigate what first-order information can be obtained from such comparisons in deterministic and stochastic settings, and how many comparisons are needed to estimate it. We show that the first-order information that such comparisons provide is a fixed positive multiple of the gradient of the objective. We propose a random-direction estimator of the comparison gradient and analyze its bias and variance. It reaches mean-squared error $\varepsilon^2$ with $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-4})$ comparisons when the sample functions have Lipschitz gradients, and $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-3})$ when their Hessians are also Lipschitz. We prove lower bounds of the same order in $d$ and $\varepsilon$ for all comparison-based estimators, so these numbers are necessary and our estimator is optimal in $d$ and $\varepsilon$. As an application, we use it in a stochastic gradient method to find a point that is approximately stationary with respect to comparisons. We also extend the estimator to nonsmooth objectives, for which it estimates a smoothed comparison gradient.
Stabilized Isogeometric Topology Optimization on Trimmed Geometries
Haoyu Su; Giuliano Guarino; Xiaodong Wei

This paper presents a novel stabilized isogeometric topology optimization method for complex design domains represented by trimmed geometries. Minimum compliance is taken as the model problem, where a generalized Cahn-Hilliard model, a time-dependent fourth-order partial differential equation, is solved and its steady-state solutions yield the optimized structures. This approach does not require sensitivity analysis and can naturally accommodate material constraints and complex topological changes. To impose Dirichlet boundary conditions and solve the instability issue caused by trimming, Nitsche's formulation with minimal stabilization is proposed for the high-order problem. Moreover, the immersed boundary-conformal method is extended to handle complex non-design domains, allowing material-void interfaces to be treated in a unified manner. Finally, a three-dimensional biharmonic problem and several two-dimensional topology optimization examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness, stability, and flexibility of the proposed method in dealing with complex design domains.
Space-time almost periodicity for the defocusing NLS hierarchy via local Toeplitz operators

We study the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger hierarchy for reflectionless initial data with Dirac spectrum $E$. Under a gap moment condition of order $m$ and the assumption that $E$ is homogeneous, we prove existence and space-time almost periodicity of a global classical solution through order $m$ for every such initial datum. More generally, it suffices that $\mathbb C\setminus E$ be a Dirichlet regular Widom domain satisfying the direct Cauchy theorem and that the gap maxima of a weighted Green potential be summable, in addition to the gap moment condition. We obtain the frequencies by summing the upper and lower boundary values of the corrected powers $z^r$ on each gap and use local Toeplitz operators to reconstruct the potential from the gap phases. We also prove uniqueness under bounds on the spatial derivatives.
Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs

We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent. We resolve an open problem of Ponomarenko by proving that the maximum degree is asymptotic in probability to $\log n/\log(3/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain the probability generating function and a CLT for the number of edges crossing the boundary of $[n]$ in the infinite limit. We also study the $K$-nearest-predecessor graph, in which each new vertex attaches to its $K$ nearest earlier vertices without regard to side. For every fixed $K\geq1$, we construct the infinite limit, prove almost sure quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence, and show that it is almost surely connected, one-ended, and recurrent, as well as nonplanar when $K\geq2$.
Blow-up phenomena and ill-posedness for the 2D Euler-Poincaré equations
Wei Luo; Zhaoyang Yin; Pei Zheng

In this paper, we study finite-time blow-up and critical norm inflation for the Euler--Poincaré equations on $\mathbb R^2$. We consider a class of momentum fields admitting the div--curl decomposition with radial scalar potentials. The potentials satisfy a nonlocal transport system. By virtue of the conservation law and the finite propagation speed property, we obtain a growth estimate for the potential, which yields a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up. Furthermore, combining a multiscale construction of the initial data with a blow-up criterion formulated in terms of the Besov norm of the deformation tensor, we establish norm inflation at the zero initial datum in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$, thereby proving ill-posedness in this critical Sobolev space.
Orthogonal lifting and amenability in ultrapowers
Minghui Ma; Wenming Wu; Yifeng Ye

Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor and let $ω$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. We prove that any two orthogonal separable amenable von Neumann subalgebras in the ultrapower $\mathcal{M}^ω$ admit orthogonal finite-dimensional lifts. In particular, two independent unitary operators in $\mathcal{M}^ω$ admit independent finite-spectrum representatives. We also show that the orthogonal lifting can fail whenever one of the subalgebras is nonamenable and Connes-embeddable.
Schur decomposition with logarithmic precision in cubic time up to logarithmic factors

How much arithmetic precision is needed to compute a Schur decomposition to a prescribed tolerance? Let $A$ be a complex matrix of order $n$ with spectral norm at most one, let $0<δ<1/2$ be the tolerance, and let $0<p<1/2$ be the requested failure probability. Our randomised floating-point algorithm uses $O(\log(n/(δp)))$ mantissa bits per real component and $O(n^3\log^2(n/(δp)))$ arithmetic operations on every execution, with universal constants. It returns $Q$ and an exactly upper triangular $T$. With probability at least $1-p$, both $\|A-QTQ^*\|_2$ and $\|Q^*Q-I\|_2$ are at most $δ$. We sample a small perturbation using finitely many bits and use Gaussian estimates to bound the eigenvector conditioning and eigenvalue gap. A single contour estimate bounds the effect of a rounding error through any number of remaining Newton steps. At each subdivision level, the full matrix is unitarily similar to a small perturbation of the regularised input. This allows us to bound the conditioning of each diagonal block directly from that input and to use the same precision throughout.
Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems

Andrei Vlad Nicula; Kalp Shah; Robert-Stefan Sofroni; Mihnea Andrei Bârsan; Agneya Bhardwaj; Jan Jelínek; Chris Hoes; Remco Hogerwerf; Finn Govers; Storm Koper; Gerrit Janssen; Stef de Wildt; Alejandro Valverde Mahou

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations by penalizing their residual, but this formulation can be difficult to optimize for solutions with singular behaviour. We focus specifically on the two-dimensional Laplace equation, whose strong analytical structure allows the governing equation to be enforced directly in the neural representation. We compare a hybrid harmonic-neural model with a holomorphic neural network whose output is harmonic by construction and therefore requires only boundary training. We further enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions chosen according to the interior angle and boundary conditions at each junction of boundary segments. On six singular benchmarks, the enriched model is the most accurate of the neural models we compare. On the four with a closed-form solution, however, that solution lies in the span of the enrichment terms, and a least-squares fit of these terms alone is exact to rounding error. On Motz's problem and the cracked beam, the neural core reduces the relative error of the recovered leading singular coefficient from about $10^{-2}$, for a least-squares fit with the same four terms, to about $10^{-6}$, and on four variants whose solution has a smooth part outside the span, the network is $4\times10^{4}$ to $2\times10^{7}$ times more accurate than a fit of its singular terms alone; classical least-squares fits with more singular terms, or with harmonic polynomials and rational poles, are more accurate still. Our results demonstrate how exploiting problem-specific analytical structure can provide an alternative to base and residual PINNs for challenging scientific computing problems.
Carlos García Meixide; David Ríos Insua

The answer to a causal question often admits several translations in terms of observed data. These may differ in adjustment sets, comparison groups, instruments, mediators, cutoffs, eligibility occasions, or data sources. We describe the resulting collection of analyses by three structures: the causal target that each analysis identifies under its assumptions, the assumptions that the analyses share, and the sampling dependence among their estimates. A single decomposition separates identification discrepancies from differences in causal targets, and we make both terms explicit in fourteen examples spanning adjustment, comparative panels, proxies, mediators, instruments, discontinuities, staggered adoption, sequential trials, and source combination. Comparisons within a collection can reveal differential violations of assumptions but not a bias common to all analyses; agreement is therefore evidence about the assumptions that differ, not about those that are shared. Averaging retains a causal interpretation in three ways: efficient combination of analyses that identify one target, a projection of a causal curve with a declared approximating family and weighting measure, and inference under weaker premises such as validity of at least one analysis or a known sign of its bias. Precision weights, regression-implied weights, and hierarchical models do not supply these interpretations by themselves. We relate this account to triangulation, overidentification, marginal treatment effects, transportability, and recent methods for inference under model uncertainty, and distinguish identification multiplicity from multiple testing.

In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix. Thus, our construction provides a categorical generalization of Kashaev's construction.
The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number

We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.
Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
Jie Fan; Xiangdi Huang; Muxi Lei

In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $λ(ρ)=ρ^β$. For $β>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-Lü (arXiv:2611.20264, 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $β>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $β=1$, for every $γ>1$ and arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum.
On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus

We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.
Parking Functions inspired by board games
Alexander Clifton; Pamela E. Harris; Maryam Khaqan

We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $π$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $π$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $π$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.
Logarithmic Potential and its Applications in Conformal Geometry

We establish an intrinsic characterization of the end invariants $ν_i$ in the Chern--Gauss--Bonnet formula for complete, simply connected, locally conformally flat 4-manifolds with non-negative scalar curvature and $Q$-curvature non-negative outside a compact set. For each end $M_i$, we show that $ν_i$ is the cube root of its normalized asymptotic geodesic-ball volume growth: \[ ν_i=\left(\lim_{r\to\infty} \frac{V_g(B_r(p)\cap M_i)}{(π^2/2)r^4}\right)^{1/3}. \] This characterization uses only the Riemannian distance and volume of $g$; it is independent of the base point $p$, the choice of compact truncation of the end, and any conformal coordinates. The proof is based on asymptotic radial symmetry of the logarithmic potential outside a sparse $\mathscr{E}$-set, inspired by Hayman's work \cite{hayman1960slowly}, together with comparisons of radial lengths and geodesic distances.
G-Wave: Bit-to-Waveform Generation for Adaptive Wireless Communications
Hanwen Zhang; Yunfang Leng; Zheng Shi; Bo Yuan; Zhenlin An; Haijian Sun

Wireless waveforms are traditionally hand-designed for general propagation conditions, rather than adapted to each specific environment. Existing neural transceivers seek such adaptation, but often rely on relatively simple architectures with limited long-range modeling capability. More expressive Transformer-based generative architectures are difficult to apply directly because wireless communication demands extremely accurate bit recovery, often with BER below 0.1%, while providing no ground-truth waveform supervision. To address these limitations, we introduce G-Wave, a channel-conditioned generative transceiver that directly synthesizes environment-adaptive physical time-domain waveforms from bits. G-Wave consists of Transformer-based transmitter and receiver models equipped with a multiscale architecture that combines long-range sequence modeling with fine-grained signal synthesis to meet the stringent precision required for communication. The two models are jointly optimized end-to-end using only bit-reconstruction error, allowing the waveform itself to be discovered without waveform labels. Across diverse 3GPP wireless environments, G-Wave achieves lower BER than the SOTA neural transceiver (DeepOFDM) and a strong conventional baseline (OFDM) under estimated channel information, reducing mean BER by 42.4% and 72.6%, respectively.
Explicit Response Formulae and Request Problem for Smooth Expanding Endomorphisms
Jianyu Chen; Na Zhang; Yufeng Zhang

In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. The proof is based on the elegant Keller-Liverani-Gouëzel perturbation theory of transfer operators. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.
Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature

Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.
Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings

We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.
Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases

In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.
Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees

Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+δ$; furthermore, for edge processes, $δ> 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.
Global classification and local asymptotics for a Monge-Ampère obstacle problem
Tianling Jin; Connor Mooney; Aranya Sen; Xushan Tu; Jingang Xiong

Let $n\geq2$ and $0<q<n$. We prove that every nontrivial convex entire solution of $$\det D^2v = v^q, \quad v \geq 0, \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n$$ with bounded (possibly empty) coincidence set $\{v=0\}$ is affine equivalent to a radial solution. Together with the classification for unbounded coincidence sets by Jin-Tu-Xiong \cite{JTX2025}, this completes the classification of nontrivial nonnegative convex entire solutions. The proof uses an affine-invariant monotonicity formula extending the two-dimensional formula in Mooney-Sen \cite{MooneySen2026}. Combining this global classification with level-set parametrization and spectral analysis, we also obtain precise asymptotics of local solutions at isolated zeros, settling the remaining case, namely, a singleton free boundary, in the regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère obstacle problem studied in \cite{JTX2025}.
Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension

The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles to vanish, and for the type of signature (2,2,2,2,8,8) it is empty. We show that five of the nine and the empty type never occur as Delaunay triangulations, and that the other four occur only as triangulations of non-trivalent Delaunay decompositions. For the ten full-dimensional types every facet x_e = 0 lies at an edge where the Whitehead move is admissible, though not conversely, and the move identifies the facets of the two polytopes; these identifications pair the facet orbits of the ten cells under their automorphism groups. The free unfolding of the gluing grows at rate about 7.093. All finite statements are checked by an independent program, and the rank, infeasibility, forced coordinates, dimensions, vertices and facets are verified in Lean 4.
Second Moment Penny Packings via Rolling Spaces

We solve the unrestricted minimum second moment problem for six unit disks in the plane by proving that the minimum is \(29/3\) attained uniquely up to isometry and relabelling by one disk together with five of its six neighbours in the triangular lattice. The realised contacts themselves define the space of admissible motions, while the directions preserving those contacts to first order define the rolling space consisting of motions whose relative velocities have zero normal component at every realised contact. Together, these spaces lead to an exact tangent cone formula and to a criterion by which a strictly positive centroidal contact balance, combined with rolling rigidity, implies strict local minimality modulo Euclidean motions. Our method recovers the classical five disk minimum \(34/5\) of Graham and Sloane, previously the largest unrestricted case known exactly. Geometric reductions and a graph census reduce the global search to finitely many contact graph classes. Exact analysis and validated interval arithmetic then exclude competing configurations, establishing the global bounds and uniqueness. Our method allows us to pass from putative lattice extremisers to unrestricted optimality.
Besicovitch Pseudo Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes and Their Applications to Delayed Stochastic Neural Networks
Yongkun Li; Yuwei Cao; Bing Li

The Besicovitch almost periodic concept is a generalization of the Bohr, Stepanov, and Weyl almost periodic concepts and, in a certain sense, has broader coverage and weaker conditions. However, the concept of pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes in the Besicovitch sense has not yet been systematically proposed, which limits the characterization of the complex oscillatory behavior of a broader class of stochastic non-autonomous systems. This paper proposes the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes. As an application of this concept, we study the existence of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic solutions in distribution for a class of stochastic delayed neural networks in which all parameters except the time delays are pseudo almost periodic and establish stability criteria for such solutions in the $p$-th mean sense. The work of this paper fills the gap caused by the lack of the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes and provides a new conceptual tool and analytical approach for characterizing the complex oscillatory behavior of stochastic differential equations and stochastic neural network systems.
A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice

All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
Ameer Qaqish; Sudipto Banerjee; Didong Li

Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Matérn kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Matérn kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Matérn kernel parameters. Since parameter identifiability depends critically on the dimension of the observation domain, we characterize the estimable parameters and establish their convergence rates across different dimensions. We introduce a coupled scaled Dirichlet distribution for paired compositions that may have different dimensions. Building on the matched Gamma-sharing construction of Trick, Rothkopf, and Jäkel (2023) for ordinary Dirichlet vectors, we allow scaled Dirichlet margins and extend the construction to include crossed sharing between non-corresponding latent components. We propose a signed coupling parameter whose sign selects matched or crossed sharing and whose magnitude controls the strength of sharing. We then develop a time-varying extension in which observed covariates determine this parameter. The model can therefore switch between matched and crossed sharing over time while preserving both scaled Dirichlet margins. We derive the joint mixed moments and use them to estimate dependence after fitting the margins separately. The moments can be evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation or by two-dimensional numerical quadrature, regardless of the dimensions of the compositions. Simulations show that the estimator generally recovers the sharing pattern, although weak crossed sharing is harder to detect. In an application to four U.S. equity-index futures, the time-varying model modestly improved the held-out energy and variogram scores for the trading-volume and intraday price-range compositions relative to the static-dependence model.

Pólya (1923) proved the celebrated result that if $\sqrt{2}X_1 =^L X_1+X_2$ then $X_1$ is normally distributed. Pólya's theorem has been extended in many ways, e.g., to the case of random coefficients $R_1,R_2$ such that, under certain regularity conditions, if $(R_1^2+R_2^2)^{1/2}X_1 =^L R_1X_1+R_2X_2$, then $X_1$ is normally distributed.
