Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
Satoshi Naito; Khanh Nguyen Duc; Daisuke Sagaki

We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.
The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs

A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 23 (1977), 127--138] proved that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge6$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(3|V(G)|-6)/2$, and this bound is sharp for every even order at least 6. Fabres, Kothari and Carvalho [J. Graph Theory 96 (2021), 490--509] proved that every minimal 2-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge12$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(5|V(G)|-20)/2$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (2026), 559--606] characterized minimal matching covered bipartite graphs $G$ with $|E(G)|=(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ in terms of special trees. They also conjectured that, for every integer $k\ge1$, there exists an integer $N_k\le4k^2+2k$ such that every minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge N_k$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(2k+1)(|V(G)|-2k)/2$. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for $k\ge3$ and prove that the upper bound is sharp for every even order at least $6k$ ($k\ge3$).
A near-quadratic bound for critical sets of harmonic functions

Let $u$ be a nonconstant harmonic function in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 3$. Denote by $N$ the doubling index of $|\nabla u|$ in $B_1$. Let $\mathcal{C} := \{ x\in B_1: \nabla u(x) = 0 \}$ be the critical set. We show that $$\mathcal{H}^{n-2}(\mathcal{C} \cap B_{1/2}) \le C_n N^2 \log^2(N+2).$$ This estimate is sharp up to a squared logarithm loss.
Combinatorics of equivariant blowups of spherical varieties

We explicitly describe the colored fan of the blowup of a smooth spherical variety $X$ along a smooth irreducible $G$-stable subvariety $Y$. The answer is expressed in terms of the colored cone of $Y$ and the localization of the valuation cone at $Y$, and generalizes the star subdivision of fans of toric varieties. We also consider several examples illustrating the main result.
An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
Xinyao Ren; Yisai Xue; Ai Yang

Thomassé conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.
Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$

We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $α$ can be chosen with $[P,α,α]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $α$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,α,α,α]=1$, and with $[P,α,α]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.
Asymptotics for Riesz means of integrable polygons
Amanda Criner; Gustav Mårdby; Jacob Shapiro

We prove complete asymptotic expansions for Riesz means of order $γ> 0$ for the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on integrable polygons. The coefficients of the first three terms are the familiar ones involving the area, perimeter, and corner angles of the polygon. The coefficients of the lower-order terms are given by convergent trigonometric series. The proof is based on heat trace identities for integrable polygons, together with large-argument asymptotics for Bessel functions.
On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $σ$-permutable subgroups

Let $σ=\{σ_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $σ$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $σ_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $σ$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.
The norm axiom and factor hyperfields

Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form $\mathcal{H}_ρ(K)$: a valued field $K$ read up to relative error $ρ$. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient $K^\times/T\cup\{0\}$ of a field, the norm axiom forces $T=1+\mathfrak{m}_ρ$ for a valuation on $K$. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group $\mathbb{Z}$ we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.
Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds
Sirui Liu; Zongpeng Li; Baochun Li

Graphs represent objects as vertices and relationships as edges; positive edge weights define shortest-path metrics. Metric embeddings leverage target-space geometry to analyze distances. Foundational results target linear spaces: Nash embedded Riemannian manifolds isometrically into Euclidean space, and Bourgain embedded $n$-point metrics into Hilbert space with $O(\log n)$ distortion. By contrast, the manifold hypothesis places high-dimensional data near low-dimensional smooth manifolds, making such manifolds themselves target spaces. What distortion is needed to embed a finite graph metric into such a manifold with its intrinsic distance? Although the star $K_{1,3}$ cannot embed isometrically into any complete Riemannian manifold, we prove almost-isometric embeddings always exist: for $\varepsilon>0$ and any finite connected positively weighted graph, we construct a smooth connected closed orientable surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting a noncontractive $(1+\varepsilon)$-embedding of its vertices, with $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small and independent of graph parameters. This construction transfers communication schemes between graphs and surfaces. For independent unicasts, fractional routing splits flows across paths while network coding lets relays combine messages. Space information flow permits relays anywhere, charging bandwidth times distance. Whereas coding advantage (optimal routing over coding cost) equals one in Euclidean space, we prove coding advantages on finite positively weighted undirected graphs transfer to smooth closed surfaces within factors approaching one. Counterexamples to the multiple-unicast conjecture and amplification yield smooth closed surfaces with unbounded coding advantage. Conversely, coding advantage is at most $C\log(g+2)$ on finite undirected graphs of orientable genus $g$ and smooth closed orientable surfaces of genus $g$, for absolute $C$.
A generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for Gaussian rough paths

In this paper, we establish a generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for the canonical rough path lift of a $2n$-dimensional centered Gaussian process with independent, identically distributed components. The formula extends the identity obtained by Aihara, Akahori, Fujii and Nitta [1] for Brownian motion. We compute the expectation of the exponential of a functional involving stochastic areas and quadratic forms in the terminal values. The result is expressed in terms of spectral data of a Hilbert--Schmidt operator associated with the stochastic area and an $n \times n$ determinant. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for absolute integrability in terms of the covariance at the terminal time and the symmetric part of the quadratic form in the terminal values. As examples, we discuss the cases of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $1/4<H<1$, Brownian motion and the Brownian bridge. In particular, we recover the formula in [1] under the exact condition for absolute integrability.
An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations

Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of turbulence (K41) predicts that the rate of kinetic energy dissipation in a turbulent flow can remain positive as viscosity tends to zero. In 2023, Bruè and De Lellis used quasi-self-similar mixing to construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations exhibiting anomalous dissipation. In this paper, we show that anomalous dissipation can still occur for a flow with spiral geometry in an annulus. In the horizontal plane, we wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral and then apply alternating shears. After each pair of shears, the image of the segment shares a subarc of positive length with the original spiral. We compare the vertical velocity with sine profiles whose angular period halves with each pair. After the horizontal flow stops, diffusion damps the final profile. By embedding this planar construction into the $(2+\frac{1}{2})$-dimensional framework, we obtain smooth solutions of the three-dimensional equations with the same smooth initial datum. For a sequence of viscosities tending to zero, their dissipation over a fixed subannulus and one vertical period has a uniform positive lower bound, and their forces converge in $C^α$ uniformly in time for every $0<α<1$. We use this spiral construction to produce solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations that exhibit anomalous dissipation.
On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4

A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable. Our proof combines Rofa's algebraic graceful labeling at the root with complementary labelings, an end-to-end leg-reversal construction placing $0$ at a leaf, and a two-leg reflection permutation placing $0$ at distance $2$ from the root.
Scaling cores and dust-free layered sets

We study Hausdorff-box dimension gaps in compact sets of finite positive Hausdorff measure. At each scale, the points of low local measure form a scaling core that carries all covering growth above the Hausdorff dimension. This gives gap criteria for both box and intermediate dimensions. We construct dust-free layered sets, in which every neighbourhood of every point has positive measure. Their dimensions are determined by the layer dimension and a product core formed from a horizontal limit set and a sequence of heights. Under a suitable approximation-rate condition, the volume remaining after subtraction of the product tube grows linearly with radius, with coefficient twice the total layer measure. Every compact null horizontal set admits such a construction. Cantor approximants, homogeneous cube constructions and Bedford-McMullen carpets illustrate the results.
Controlled nonstationary G-diffusions: dynamic programming, weighted Harris contraction and entrance risk

We study controlled nonstationary \(G\)-diffusions in a canonical-law formulation of covariance uncertainty. The principal structural result is an abstract weighted Harris--oscillation contraction theorem for translation-covariant nonlinear evolution families. A Lyapunov estimate for a dominating terminal-perturbation bound and a local space--time oscillation estimate for differences imply exponential contraction in a weighted quotient norm, without positive homogeneity, subadditivity or convexity. For elementary sample-and-hold feedback controls and a rectangular family of martingale laws, we construct a measurable controlled state map and prove deterministic- and stopped-time dynamic programming principles for the robust lower value. Under uniform ellipticity, differences of Bellman values belong to a common parabolic Pucci class; a local Harnack argument and an all-policy Lyapunov estimate verify the abstract hypotheses. For zero running cost, the contraction yields a unique tempered entrance nonlinear expectation and exponential attraction. With running cost, it yields a unique normalized nonstationary corrector and an additive cocycle, together with exponential convergence of relative values. Subtracting a scalar primitive of the cocycle gives an all-time viscosity solution of the backward Bellman--Isaacs equation. Autonomous and periodic coefficients yield additive eigenpairs, stationary and periodic ergodic equations, and convergence of long-time average costs. The results provide a long-time theory for optimally controlled dynamic risk evaluation under nonstationary covariance uncertainty.
Analytic continuation of the T- and S-matrices to unphysical sheets in a multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model
Mikhail V. Kremenetsky; Alexander K. Motovilov

We consider a matrix multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model. First, we formulate conditions on the kernels of the potential matrix that guarantee for the T-matrix (and then for the S-matrix) the existence of analytical continuation to unphysical energy sheets. We also obtain explicit representations for the analytically continued T- and S-matrices on unphysical sheets in terms of these matrices themselves, but only taken in the physical sheet. From the explicit representations obtained, it follows that the resonances on a certain unphysical sheet are nothing but the points at which the corresponding truncation of the scattering matrix in the physical sheet has an eigenvalue of 0.
Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
Xi Chen; Yuze Chen; Baichuan Mo; Jie Ying; Yuan Zhou

Designing simple inventory policies becomes increasingly difficult as operational features and system configurations expand. We develop an Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System based on explicitly defined simple operational formula (SOF) policy and template classes. Large language models (LLMs) revise symbolic structures, while a numerical engine fits parameters separately for each instance and evaluates the induced policies. Multicriteria parent selection, state-specific operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs guide structural evolution. A three-stage progression develops shared templates across instances and configurations with varying state dimensions. Experiments on 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions cover lead times, perishability, their combination, and lead times with limited customer patience. The discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated SOF benchmarks and are competitive with policies requiring more elaborate online computations. For a lost-sales system with a three-period lead time, we develop an average-cost decomposition and prove that, under specified demand and cost conditions, a capped dual-shortfall specialization of a discovered policy strictly outperforms every policy in the considered capped base-stock benchmark class. This analysis links the performance advantage to the discovered replenishment mechanism. Together, these results highlight the potential of agentic discovery to generate simple inventory policies with strong empirical performance and identify operational mechanisms amenable to rigorous theoretical analysis.
Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps

Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Lattès families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.
Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension

An integration system is a triple $(X,L,I)$: a set $X$, a Riesz subspace $L$ of $\mathbb{R}^X$, and a continuous positive linear functional $I$ on $L$. We introduce the category Int whose morphisms are pullbacks along maps of the base spaces. The main result is that the Daniell extension defines a functor from Int to DInt and is left adjoint to the inclusion of the full subcategory DInt of Daniell closed systems, those with $L^1=L$, usually called complete. So DInt is reflective and the Daniell extension is its reflector. The content lies in a decomposition: a system is Daniell closed if and only if it satisfies the monotone convergence theorem and is closed under modification on null sets, and neither can be dropped. The second corresponds to completeness of the measure. The decomposition is a real-valued phenomenon: for extended-real-valued functions the second condition follows from the first. Daniell closedness of the codomain cannot be omitted. The inclusion of the category of systems satisfying the monotone convergence theorem also has a left adjoint, but its reflector is not the Daniell extension. Under the Stone condition that second reflection consists of the integrable functions measurable for the $σ$-algebra generated by $L$. For an arbitrary system, $L^1$ splits as the sum of that part and the functions supported on null sets, so the gap between the two reflections is exactly the completion of the measure. Finally, if morphisms are replaced by positive linear maps between Riesz spaces, they see only the quotient of $L$ by the null functions, where the Daniell extension gives the Banach completion. So the distinction between an abstract completion and a concrete realization survives as categorical structure only where morphisms are maps of base spaces. In sum: the Daniell counterpart of the completion of a measure space, in categorical language.
William Chan; Sandra Müller; Farmer Schlutzenberg; Benjamin Siskind

Gandy-Harrington forcing is an important tool in descriptive set theory, first developed by Gandy and later used by Harrington to give a simple proof of Silver's dichotomy theorem. In this paper, we develop a new version of Gandy-Harrington forcing higher up in the projective hierarchy, under an appropriate local determinacy hypothesis. Using this new forcing, we prove a reverse mathematics result at the level of $Δ^1_2$-Determinacy as well as new inner-model-theoretic basis theorem for $Σ^1_3$ sets.
Prescribing finite first singular sets of mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^3$

For any $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and any sufficiently small positive time, we construct a smooth mean curvature flow of embedded mean-convex tori whose first singularities occur precisely at those points at that time.
Sharp tails for arguments of Dirichlet $L$-functions

Let $t$ be uniform on $[T,2T]$, let $χ$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, and set $X=\Im\log L(1/2+it,χ)$ and $Q=\sum_{p\le T,\,p\nmid q}1/p$. For fixed $K,θ_0>0$, uniformly in $q\le T^{θ_0}$, $χ$, and $0\le V\le KQ$, each signed tail $\Pr\{\pm X>V\}$ has order $\sqrt Q\,(V+\sqrt Q)^{-1}\exp(-V^2/Q)$. In particular, for $S(t)=π^{-1}\argζ(1/2+it)$ and $0\le V\le K\log\log T$, each tail $\Pr\{\pm S(t)>V\}$ has order $\sqrt{\log\log T}\,(V+\sqrt{\log\log T})^{-1}\exp(-π^2V^2/\log\log T)$. For $|v|\le KQ$, the probability that $X$ lies in a fixed-width interval centered at $v$ has order $Q^{-1/2}\exp(-v^2/Q)$ whenever the width is sufficiently large. The upper bound holds for every fixed positive width. We also obtain matching bounds of order $\exp(k^2Q)$ for the means of $\exp(\pm2kX)$ for fixed $k>0$. The proof begins with a one-sided polynomial bound for each sign, using Alpöge's zero-location theorem at the primitive inducing conductor. A weighted comparison with a sum over primes controls departures from the target interval, and a signed polynomial gives its lower bound.
Global Flows for the KdV Hierarchy with Initial Conditions Having No Restriction on Schrödinger Spectra
Xiangshuo Kong; Shinichi Kotani; Shuo Zhang

When one of the authors constructed the KdV flow for a broad class of initial data, he imposed a restriction that the underlying Schrödinger operators with the initial data as potentials were bounded from below. We remove this restriction and establish the flow on a space of initial data that are bounded from above and possibly unbounded from below.
Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
Fabio Deelan Cunden; Paolo Facchi; Roberto La Scala; Marilena Ligabò; Karol Życzkowski

We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that retains the full unitary class and is a convex combination of at most four classical grids. This measurement map embeds the five-square model into a seven-dimensional polytope whose vertices are the twelve classical Sudoku.
Principal subspaces of affine vertex algebras at admissible levels

We classify generic principal subspaces of admissible affine vertex algebras for all simple Lie algebras. The nongeneric cases occur precisely at denominator two in types $B,C,F_4$ and at denominator three in type $G_2$. The proof uses geometry of nilpotent orbits combined with positive root null vectors. Surprisingly, null vectors needed for our classification are explicitly known and already studied in the literature. We then study the exceptional principal subspaces at the level of their $C_2$-algebras and arc algebras. For $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ at level $-\frac12$ and $G_2$ at level $-\frac53$, we prove classical freeness and obtain product character formulas. In type $C_n$ at level $-\frac12$, classical freeness fails for $n\ge4$. For $n=3$, we combine the functional model method of Feigin and Stoyanovsky, and a flat degeneration of the explicit realization of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ to prove a product character formula, while classical freeness in this case remains conjectural. The principal subspace of $L_{-5/2}(F_4)$ is also conjecturally classically free.
The mean orders of even and odd permutations

We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the larger sum from degree four on.
Universal Extra-Gradient Method for Stochastic Variational Inequalities
Abhishek Chakraborty; Anton Rodomanov; Sebastian U. Stich; Angelia Nedić

We study the stochastic Extra-Gradient Method (EGM) for solving a stochastic variational inequality (VI) over a compact convex set. The main assumption is $(δ, L)$-continuity of the VI mapping, which includes Hölder mappings and their linear combinations. We develop new adaptive, line-search-free step-size rules for stochastic EGM. These rules can be interpreted as enhanced AdaGrad-type updates and require no prior knowledge of either the continuity modulus of the VI mapping or the variance of the stochastic oracle. The resulting methods are universal and attain the best complexity bound among the admissible continuity regimes. We prove convergence guarantees in terms of an expected residual function that upper bounds the relevant accuracy measures for several important problem classes, including the dual gap for monotone VIs, and the primal-dual gap for saddle-point and optimization problems. For Hölder-continuous mappings, our bounds recover the optimal dimension-independent complexity of first-order methods.
Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
Ran Li; Jiaohui Xu; Dingshi Li; Tomas Caraballo

We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced. This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique. Moreover, we prove the existence of invariant measures by the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov approach, and further establish the regularity of invariant measures by virtue of a control argument.

An {\it axial algebra} is an algebra generated by a set $X$ of semisimple idempotents satisfying a prescribed set of fusion rules. Some axial algebras (such as primitive axial algebras of Jordan type $1/2$) have a Frobenius form, in which case one can define the radical $Rad(A)$ of the Frobenius form. Recently, Mamontov, S.~Shpectorov, and V.~Zhelyabin defined a radical $R(A;X)$ as the largest ideal not containing any axis of $X$, which is always contained in $Rad(A)$, and proved that $R(A;X) = Rad(A)$ when the Frobenius form is anisotropic. In this case they also proved that $A/R(A;X)$ is semisimple, yielding an elegant structure theory for primitive axial algebras with an anisotropic Frobenius form. Our objective is to recover these results, removing the assumption of a Frobenius form. We provide alternative characterizations of the radical, including a Jacobson-type radical (not the same as their Jacobson radical). We also replace the Frobenius form by a more general notion of orthogonality. Finally, we introduce a Baer-type radical and compare it to $R(A;X)$ and $Rad(A)$.
Prescribed matrix size for UHF Brauer classes on suspensions

Let \(Y\) be a connected finite CW complex, \(L=M_{l^\infty}\) for \(l\geq2\), and \(k\) a positive integer coprime to \(l\). Stable \(L\)-twists on \(ΣY\) have normalized clutching invariants \(1+x\) in \(K^0(Y)[1/l]\). We prove that such a twist is the stabilization of a unital \(M_k(L)\)-bundle exactly when \(kx=0\) additively. For each admissible size we construct a representative from two trivial \(M_k(\C)\)-bundles and a span of embeddings into \(M_{kl^N}(\C)\) on their overlap. Every \(N\geq0\) with \(2l^N\geq\dim Y\) suffices. For \(Y=S^{2m-1}\cup_p e^{2m}\), \(m\geq2\), and a prime \(p\geq m\) coprime to \(l\), a generator has least unital size \(p\) and least overlap exponent \(\lceil\log_l m\rceil\) at that size. In dimension five the least size is \(q\) and the least exponent is one for every Moore space \(S^4\cup_q e^5\) with \(q>1\) coprime to \(l\). Over \(Σ\RP^{2d}\), a twist of period two has least unital size \(2^d\) whenever \(l\) is odd.
Fixed-Time Heat Kernel Integrals on Flat Tori: a Finer Invariantthan the Heat Trace

Let \[T^n = \mathbb{R}^n/Λ\] be a flat torus and let \[k_t\]be its heat kernel. For a primitive lattice vector \[λ_0 \in Λ\] let \[ γ_{λ_0}(s) = sλ_0/|λ_0|, \qquad s \in [0, |λ_0|], \] and \[ I_t(λ_0) = \int_{0}^{|λ_0|} k_t(0, γ_{λ_0}(s)) \, ds. \] The integral \[I_t(λ_0)\] combines spectral data (the heat kernel) with geometric data (a choice of closed geodesic), and is a strictly finer invariant than the heat trace \[ K_t = \int_{T^n} k_t(x, x) \, dx. \] We prove the following. (i) For n = 1, \[I_t(λ_0) = 1\] for every t > 0 and every primitive \[λ_0\]; the fixed-time data carry no geometric information. (ii) For n = 2, for any fixed t_0 > 0 the multiset \[ \mathcal{D}_{t_0} = \{I_{t_0}(λ_0) : λ_0 \text{ primitive}\}/\{\pm\} \] determines \(Λ\) up to isometry, and hence the length spectrum, the volume, and the isometry class of T^2. (iii) For n = 16, the fixed-time data distinguish Milnor's isospectral non-isometric tori \[ \mathbb{R}^{16}/(D_8^+ \times D_8^+) \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{R}^{16}/D_{16}^+ \] for all \[t_0 > 0\] outside a countable set, although their heat traces agree at every t > 0.
On fourteen problems in the theory of composites

We study fourteen questions of Milton on the effective properties of composites. For one scalar potential every effective tensor of two fixed planar phases has a laminate representative. Two coupled potentials suffice for failure. In space, dyadic resistor networks characterize the isotropic conductivity closure, and some laws in it have no finite-perimeter periodic representative. We construct intervals on the single-pole absorption arc and hole-free planar inclusions realizing optimal double-coating laws. For a solid with void or perfectly rigid inclusions we characterize the two- and three-dimensional tensor closures. Porous solids can approach full shear at vanishing bulk in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. Prescribing a finite planar shortening gives a sharp loss of initial shear. We give the complete shear interval at each bulk for a polycrystal. For two positive elastic phases, changing only the bulk moduli can reverse which dimension admits a shear common to every attainable bulk.

In this paper, we establish upper bounds for shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-function over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one under the generalized Riemann hypothesis. The result is used to derive bounds for moments of angular Hecke character sums.
Explicit exponent bounds for sums of consecutive powers

Let $x^k+(x+1)^k=y^n$, where $x,y,k,n$ are positive integers with $k\ge2$ and $n\ge3$. We prove that $n<52k^2\log(2k)\log^2(50k)$ for odd $k$ and $n<216k\log^2(2500k)$ for even $k$. For odd $k$, an exact valuation formula reduces the problem to a linear form in two real logarithms. For even $k$, we use factorization in $\mathbb Z[i]$ and a bound of Yamada. When $k=5$, we prove that the original exponent $n$ is one of the 34 primes between $23$ and $181$, inclusive. Every solution satisfies $2x+1=u^n$ with $u>10^{1000}$. A gap between successive rational approximations to $2^{-4/n}$, together with the Thue--Siegel principle, gives at most four solutions for each of $n=23,29$ and at most three for each larger prime in this range. Thus there are at most 104 positive integer triples $(x,y,n)$ in the quintic case. All bounds are unconditional.
Extremal adjacency and distance spectral radii of graph powers
Joyentanuj Das; Anto Jerrin Ashni R; Sangeetha C

Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, \[ ρ(G^k)\geq ρ(P_n^k) \qquad\text{and}\qquad ρ_D(G^k)\leq ρ_D(P_n^k), \] where $P_n$ is the path of order $n$, and $ρ$ and $ρ_D$ are the adjacency and distance spectral radii, respectively. If $n\geq k+2$, equality in either inequality holds precisely when $G\cong P_n$. If $n\leq k+1$, every connected graph of order $n$ has complete $k$-th power, and both inequalities are equalities. The adjacency bound is proved by transferring a terminal vertex between pendant paths and applying a reflection rearrangement to a Rayleigh quotient. For the distance bound, a transfer of an entire pendant path is required; a Schur-complement comparison and estimates for the antisymmetric subspace of a path-power distance matrix yield the result. We also give examples showing why the two adjacency arguments do not extend directly to the distance spectral radius.
Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
Junpeng Ren; Zheng-Gang Wu; Mengzhen Zhu

Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(Δ(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually Gorenstein if and only if $A$ and $B$ are.
Stable-like Operators related to Bernstein Functions in weighted Lebesgue spaces: Boundedness, Regularity, Embedding, and Martingale Problem
J. -H. Choi; J. Kang; D. Park

We study variable-coefficient nonlocal operators associated with a Bernstein function $ϕ$ satisfying global weak scaling conditions. Let $j_d^ϕ$ denote the radial Lévy density of the corresponding subordinate Brownian motion. The kernels may be nonsymmetric, and the coefficients are measurable in the jump variable and satisfy a prescribed uniform modulus of continuity in the spatial variable. In the critical scaling regime, we impose an annular cancellation condition. For jump profiles satisfying $0\le V(y)\le Cj_d^ϕ(|y|)$, we prove that the operator $\mathcal L_V^a$ is bounded from $H_p^{ϕ,2}(w)$ to $L_p(w)$ for every $1<p<\infty$ and $w\in A_p(\mathbb R^d)$. The parabolic coefficients may be merely measurable in time. We also obtain elliptic resolvent estimates in weighted $L_p$ spaces for sufficiently large resolvent parameters. Under suitable integrability conditions, we prove a weighted Sobolev--Hölder embedding with an explicit local modulus of continuity in space and time. The modulus depends on $ϕ$, the integrability exponents, and the Muckenhoupt indices of the weights. Finally, we prove global well-posedness of the time-dependent martingale problem. For the resulting time-inhomogeneous strong Markov family, we derive a Krylov-type estimate in weighted mixed norms. Its local normalization involves the weighted measures of an intrinsic time interval and a spatial ball.
A thermodynamically consistent variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines
Junkai Wang; Ting Xiao; Qiaolin He

In this paper, we present a variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines. Based on the dynamic van der Waals theory with gradient contributions and surface thermodynamics, the governing equations and hydrodynamic boundary conditions are derived from a generalized Hamilton's principle for nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Two equivalent variational formulations based on internal energy and Helmholtz free energy are developed, using entropy density and temperature, respectively, as the primary thermal variable. Using the resulting weak forms, compatible spatial operators and discrete thermodynamic chain rules, we construct two thermodynamically consistent fully discrete finite element schemes. We rigorously prove the following properties for both fully discrete schemes: mass conservation, bound preservation for the number density, positivity of the temperature, an exact total energy balance incorporating external work and heat exchange, and a temperature-weighted weak entropy inequality with nonnegative bulk and boundary entropy production. A transitive $C^{1+α}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
Let $0<α\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.
On the Number Theory of the Greeks. II. Gauss's Lemmas and Riesz Domains

In the second part of our article on Euclid's four number theorem we start from the notion of incommensurability and take a closer look at irrationality proofs for algebraic numbers. Along the way we encounter Gauss's Lemma, integral closure and Dedekind's Prague theorem, and finally we arrive back at the four number theorem.
Gaussian Belief Propagation and Periodic Jacobi Matrices on Trees: Spectral Curve, Antibound Poles, and Fixed Points

Diagonal Green functions of a periodic Jacobi operator on a universal covering tree satisfy the scalar Gaussian belief propagation covariance equations on the finite connected loopless base multigraph. At cycle rank at least two, the Green functions continue to simple antibound poles at both Perron values for arbitrary real potentials and nonzero real weights. This proves the conjecture of Christiansen, Simon and Zinchenko. For positive weights the pole result includes self-loops. On loopless graphs the lower pole is the walk-summability threshold. Each energy strictly between it and the spectral bottom has at least two fixed points with positive definite local beliefs. On a connected simple graph, some coefficients yield a compact component of positive solutions exactly when the graph contains two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. The covariance curve is generically irreducible, with one sheet per edge subset with no vertex of degree one. For cycle rank at least two and generic real coefficients, the diagonal Green functions, infinite half-tree $m$-functions and the density-of-states Stieltjes transform all have this degree, answering a question of Avni, Breuer and Simon. Then all eigenvalues of the signed Jacobi matrices are antibound poles. Signed principal submatrices classify finite points with nonzero residue of $(\sum_i V_i) dz$, where $V_i$ are the vertex variances. We give a genus formula. Near zero potentials and unit weights on $K_4$, independently varying the coefficients leaves the cover spectrum an interval. This refutes Avni, Breuer and Simon's conjecture on the density of parameters with all gaps open. In block models, generic irreducibility and a uniqueness criterion extend, and at uniform dimension $p$ the degree can exceed $L^p$ for scalar degree $L$. Part of the scalar theory is formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
On the number theory of the Greeks. I. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic

In this article we present Euclid's fundamental theorem of number theory and give evidence for the claim that this theorem, which is largely unknown today, was as familiar to number theorists before Gauss as the Gaussian version of the fundamental theorem is to us.
On mesh transfers and time error estimation in adaptive finite element methods for parabolic problems

In space and time adaptive finite element methods, the discrete solution is transferred onto a different mesh whenever the spatial mesh changes. Refinement is commonly regarded as harmless, since nodal interpolation then reproduces the discrete solution exactly. However, we show that for the implicit Euler method applied to the heat equation, the transferred solution and time derivative, in general, violate the discrete equation on the new mesh. Unless the resulting transfer residual vanishes, the corresponding time error estimator overestimates the local error, for small time steps, by a factor inversely proportional to the time step size. To address this issue, we propose transfers based on the elliptic reconstruction, which significantly reduce the transfer residual or even remove it. In numerical experiments, we confirm the analysis and demonstrate the advantages of the proposed transfers in a space and time adaptive example.
Five-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel
Charif Bourzik; Othmane Dani; Mehdi Nabil
In this paper, we show that 5-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel.
Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space

This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.

We extend Jones' Baxterisation, which produces solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation directly from the generators of an algebra, to quantum spin chains with medium-range interactions. The key ingredient is an extended Yang-Baxter equation for R matrices that are built from the generators attached to two neighbouring sites. Together with the accompanying Lax operator, it gives rise to transfer matrices that are in involution up to boundary terms, exactly as in Jones' construction. We find a solution to the extended Yang-Baxter equation, of non-difference form, in terms of the generators of the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring, and obtain from it two families of medium-range lattice Hamiltonians. Thus, each representation of the algebra provides a medium-range solvable model. Using the relation between the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring and the fusion category $\mathrm{Rep}(S_3)$, we construct four such representations. They reproduce the folded XXZ model and the hard-rod deformed XXZ model, and give new medium-range models of a three-state antiferromagnet and of a Rydberg-blockade ladder. Two of the four models possess non-invertible symmetries.

For a commutative Ding--Chen ring $B$, we prove that Gorenstein and Ding injectivity coincide over $R=B[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ if and only if injective $B$-modules generate the unbounded derived category of $B$. We construct a commutative von Neumann regular ring $B$ whose unbounded derived category is not generated by its pure injective objects. For this $B$, the coherent ring $R$ admits a strongly Gorenstein injective module $G$ which is not Ding injective. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $G_{\mathfrak p}$ has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. The ring $R$ can be chosen to have cardinality $\aleph_ω$, the least possible among coherent rings over which Gorenstein and Ding injectivity differ.
The fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian is a function in dimensions 1 and 2

We show that the fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian in dimensions $1$ and $2$ is a locally integrable function. Together with earlier work of the first author, this resolves a conjecture of Chen and Véron. The key step is that the inverse Fourier transform of the high-frequency part of $1/\log(|ξ|^2)$ behaves like $|x|^{-d}(\log(1/|x|))^{-2}$ near the origin.
A new upper bound for the Erdős--Szekeres conjecture
Yifan Hu; Guokuan Shao; Guozhen Shen

Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}. \] In this article, we further improve the upper bound by showing that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{1/3})}. \]

We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(π_qX)\Longrightarrowπ_{p+q}\LH X \] where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.
Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results

A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $χ_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $χ_o(G)$ are known. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on $χ_o(G)$ for several graph classes. In particular, we obtain the following results: 1. For every block-cactus graph $G$, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq \max \{5,ω(G)+1\}$, where $ω(G)$ denotes the clique number of $G$. 2. For block graphs and proper interval graphs, we establish the bounds $ω(G) \leq χ_o(G) \leq ω(G)+1$. 3. For a bipartite circle graph, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq 6$. This settles an open question asked by Davis et al., 2026. 4. For every biconvex bipartite graph $G$, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq 5$. 5. For $C_4$-free cographs $G$, we establish the bound $χ_o(G) \leq ω(G)+1$. Moreover, we characterize block graphs, proper interval graphs, and cactus graphs based on their odd chromatic number.
Stability of Viscous Shock Waves of the Compressible Navier-Stokes System with Large Initial Perturbation

We show in this paper that viscous shock waves of the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations are time-asymptotically nonlinear stable with large initial perturbation. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. As far as we know, only under a class of large initial perturbations, the asymptotical stability of weak viscous shock wave was derived. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem for weak viscous shock wave. The key idea involves combining the $a$-contraction with shifts theory with a time splitting method to obtain the weighted $L^2$ estimates, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on the specific volume. Our method can be also applied to proving the nonlinear stability of composite waves.
Mass- and energy-preserving low-regularity integrators for nonlinear Schrödinger equations

The nonlinear Schrödinger equation is a fundamental model of dispersive wave phenomena, possessing a rich geometric structure that includes the conservation of mass and energy. Preserving these conservation laws at the level of numerical discretisation remains challenging, particularly for solutions of low regularity. In particular, combining the favourable convergence properties of low-regularity integrators with the exact preservation of fundamental conservation laws has remained an open challenge. In this work, we introduce, to the best of our knowledge, the first mass- and energy-preserving low-regularity integrators for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. We establish the well-posedness and convergence of the proposed schemes and demonstrate how ideas from projection methods can be used to ensure the simultaneous preservation of mass and energy. Our rigorous analysis (the first for mass- and energy-preserving schemes) is supported by extensive numerical experiments highlighting the favourable convergence and structure-preserving properties of the methods, including for rough solutions.
Comparable Overrings of Marot Rings II

Let $R$ be a Marot ring. We study comparable overrings of $R$ that are integral over $R$, generalizing results of Ayache for integral domains. We show that such an overring has at most two regular maximal ideals. When $R$ has a unique regular maximal ideal, we study the three possible types and give characterizations of comparability and minimality in the first two cases. In the case of two regular maximal ideals, we describe the integral closure of $R$ as an intersection of two valuation overrings. We also obtain comparability criteria using normal pairs and finite chain conditions. Finally, we construct counterexamples giving negative answers to two conjectures posed by Ayache.
Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar Hölder domains

Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar Hölder domain has no interior critical point. The Hölder condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing Hölder-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.
Sharp Volume Contraction of a Centrally Cut John Ellipsoid

For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ in positive dimension, let $w(K)$ be the volume of its maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid. For a closed halfspace $H$ whose boundary passes through the center of that ellipsoid, we prove \[ w(K\cap H)\le R_nw(K),\qquad R_1=\frac12,\qquad R_n=\frac12\left(\frac n{n-1}\right)^{(n-1)/2}\quad(n\ge2), \] with equality attained in every fixed dimension. This refines the optimal dimension-independent bound from the author's earlier work on [Khachiyan's ellipsoid conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28447). We characterize the full equality family, including nonsimplex extremizers, and establish an exact volume-deficit identity that yields dimension-independent stability of the new ellipsoid and its weighted contact geometry in John coordinates. The proof reduces the problem to finite John contacts and constructs an explicit conic certificate by a transformation of contact directions and a common polar rotation. Its determinant is controlled by a nonnegative contact defect. The sharp contraction theorem, equality classification, stability estimates, and supporting results have been formally verified in Lean 4 using mathlib.
Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems

We prove memory/query-complexity tradeoff lower bounds for the feasibility problem, where the goal is to find a point within an $ε$-ball hidden in the unit $d$-dimensional ball, with access to a separation oracle. This problem admits three regimes: the low-accuracy regime $ε\geq 1/\sqrt d$ where memory does not play a role, the medium-accuracy regime $1/\sqrt d\geq ε\geq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ where prior works identified strong memory/query-complexity separations, and the high-accuracy regime $ε\leq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ for which much less is known. In this regime, low-memory algorithms with significantly faster convergence rates than gradient descent have been developed in [BZJ24]: for accuracy $ε$ and any $δ\in[0,1]$, these require $d^{1+δ}\ln \frac1ε$ memory bits and use $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{O(d^{1-δ})}$ oracle queries. In comparison, gradient descent uses the same memory for $δ=0$ but requires $1/ε^2$ oracle queries. On the lower-bound side, no non-trivial memory/query-complexity tradeoff was known: the best lower bound remained the historical memory-independent bound $Ω(d\ln \frac1ε)$ from [NYD83]. We make progress towards characterizing the memory landscape in this high-accuracy regime by showing that for any $δ\in[0,1]$, any algorithm with $d^{1+δ}\ln\frac1ε$ bits of memory uses at least $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{\widetildeΩ(d^{(1-δ)/8})}$ oracle calls. This result justifies the seemingly peculiar exponential-in-$d$ dependence of oracle complexity for the aforementioned low-memory algorithms. In particular, our result shows that for high-accuracy feasibility problems, insufficient memory does result in an exponential price in the dimension for the query-complexity.
Learned spatial opportunity cost admission for ride-hailing with calibrated thresholds
Baichuan Mo; Yuan Zhou; Qixin Zhang; Hai Yang

Ride-hailing operators must decide whether to accept a request before observing future demand. Serving a ride earns revenue and changes where and when the vehicle can serve again. We develop learned spatial opportunity cost admission for a centrally managed fleet. The policy estimates demand from past requests and solves a rolling mean-demand plan. Dual prices account for using a vehicle at its origin and returning it to service at its destination. With positive regularization, the policy accepts a request when its planned service fraction reaches a common threshold. We fix the regularization parameter and select the threshold using validation revenue. For one vehicle on a single route, we derive the exact range of thresholds that attain optimal expected revenue. When several origins share return demand at a hub, the best common threshold can lose revenue in proportion to fleet size. Independent validation bounds the revenue loss relative to the best candidate threshold. At a fixed threshold, under Poisson arrivals and a margin condition, the revenue gap between using estimated and true mean demand has a tight inverse-square-root bound in the number of historical days. We evaluate the policy on 60 synthetic instances across six demand families and on ten New York workdays across 25 taxi zones and three fleet sizes. With two validation days, calibration improves mean paired revenue over the default threshold by 4.93% in the synthetic study and 7.08% in New York. In New York, the policy earns 1.24% to 2.54% less than the best-performing benchmark in mean paired comparisons and takes about one-eleventh as long per decision. Calibration gains are largest for the smallest New York fleet. In the synthetic study, gains over accepting every feasible request are largest under commuting demand.
Directional short-time special affine Fourier transform of distributions
Ilir Berisha; Astrit Ferizi; Katerina Hadzi-Velkova Saneva

In this paper, we introduce and study the directional short-time special affine Fourier transform (DSTSAFT) in the multidimensional setting. Motivated by the need to combine localized time-frequency analysis with directional sensitivity and the flexibility of the special affine Fourier transform, the DSTSAFT provides a unified framework that encompasses established directional transforms as particular cases. We establish Parseval's identity and derive an inversion formula for the DSTSAFT. Furthermore, we prove that both the DSTSAFT and its synthesis operator are continuous mappings between the corresponding spaces of test functions. Building on these continuity results, we extend the DSTSAFT and its synthesis operator to the corresponding spaces of tempered distributions via duality. We also establish an important relationship between the DSTSAFT and the special affine Fourier transform (SAFT) and derive a desingularization formula. The resulting framework provides an analytical basis for studying directional and localized properties of tempered distributions within the SAFT setting.
A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture

We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.

It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.
Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series

We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

Together with geometric arguments, these reductions establish that $\mathsf{Y}$, $\mathsf{X}$, and $\mathsf{Cheq}$ are pairwise incomparable, while each lies strictly between $\mathsf{PL}$ and Medvedev logic. In particular, we show that it is decidable whether a finite poset is isomorphic to a finite convex hull frame, and that the logics determined by configurations of a bounded number of points are decidable. Finally, we extend our study to infinite convex hull frames. We show that inclusion yields $\mathsf{KC}$, whereas reverse inclusion yields $\mathsf{IPC}$. For the latter result, we use the Cantor set to construct $p$-morphisms onto arbitrary finite rooted frames.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. More precisely, given a local $D_{p^2}$-action on $k[[z]]$, we construct an action on $R[[Z]]$ by $R$-automorphisms whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ is the given action, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring finite over the Witt ring $W(k)$. We prove that the action lifts if $u_i\equiv-1\pmod{2p}$ for every $i$. When $p=3$, we also prove lifting under the hypotheses $u_i\equiv5\pmod6$ for $2\leq i<n$ and $3\nmid u_n$.
Differential equations for Macdonald's hypergeometric series via Dunkl operators of type A

We solve an eigenvalue problem for a family of trigonometric Dunkl operators depending on a parameter, extending the result of Ref.[16] to the case of a general parameter. We introduce families of nonsymmetric W-type operators closely related to Dunkl operators and analyze their algebraic structure, various representations and symmetrization. We then use these operators to characterize non-symmetric Macdonald's hypergeometric series introduced in Ref.[5] and recover several known results. These results suggest a direct connection between Macdonald's hypergeometric series and Dunkl operators.
Systems of quadratic BSDEs with unbounded terminal data
Shengjun Fan; Ying Hu; Shanjian Tang

The paper is devoted to global solution of multidimensional backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with non-convex quadratic generators and unbounded terminal data. The generators of some individual BSDEs of the system are allowed to have interactions among their second unknown variables and can be non-Lipschitz continuous with general growth in the first unknown variable $y$ and non-convex/non-concave in the second unknown variable $z$. We extend the results of the authors' previous paper [JDE, 2023] by incorporating both the no convexity/concavity of the generators and the interaction among the second unknown variables of individual BSDEs, and update the assumptions of Theorems 2.10 and 2.27 stated in the authors' previous paper~[EJP, 2025] so as to fill in a gap in the original proofs.
Circular von Neumann-Jordan Constants in Complex Banach Spaces
Haiying Li; Yijia Zhao; Yongjin Li

Replacing \(y\) by \(ty\) does not refine the classical von Neumann--Jordan constant; we instead average over unimodular phases before optimization to define upper, lower, and balanced circular constants for complex Banach spaces. The upper and lower constants are the squared norm and squared minimum modulus of a Fourier synthesis operator, linking them to optimal two-term Steinhaus type and cotype constants. We also obtain quantitative comparisons with complex convexity and smoothness moduli. Complex interpolation improves the dimension-free upper bound for finite-dimensional \(\ell_p\)-spaces, \(2<p<\infty\). A James constant estimate yields the sharp uniform-nonsquareness threshold \(1+2/π\) and a sufficient condition for the fixed point property of nonexpansive mappings.
An explicit BGG-type resolution of the spin/oscillator module for osp(2m+1|2n)

We construct an explicit resolution of the spin/oscillator representation of the Lie superalgebra osp(2m+1|2n) by parabolic Verma modules. The resolution appears as the Chevalley-Eilenberg chain complex of the Lie algebra of quadratic operators in the universal Heisenberg algebra of the vector superspace C^{m|n}. In particular, its differentials are given by unified linear algebra formulas and all have degree 2 with respect to the standard grading of Verma modules.
Finite-Dimensional Internal Stabilization of Steady States of the Gray-Scott System

In this article, we establish the local exponential stabilization of every steady state of the Gray-Scott system with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, other than the trivial state $(0,1)^{\top}$, at any prescribed decay rate by finite-dimensional feedback controls supported in an arbitrary nonempty open subset of the domain and acting only on the first equation of the system. Our approach does not require the steady state to be spatially constant and accommodates non-self-adjoint linearizations with variable coefficients. The proof combines unique continuation, a nonvanishing property of the steady-state coupling, the Fattorini-Hautus condition, and Riccati-based feedback.
Persistence and Breakdown of the Initial Gaussian Rate Function for 1D Quasi-Periodic Cubic NLS

We study rare events for the spatial supremum of the solution amplitude in the 1D cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with weak nonlinearity and Gaussian quasi-periodic initial data. Under suitable polynomial decay assumptions in Fourier space and a Diophantine condition controlling small divisors arising from spatial quasi-periodicity, we prove that the initial Gaussian rate function persists uniformly on the \emph{critical logarithmic correction time scale} with a \emph{small enough} prefactor. Using the \emph{Akhmediev breather}, we obtain that the same Gaussian rate function \emph{fails} to hold uniformly on this time scale with a \emph{large} prefactor. This also implies that the initial Gaussian rate function cannot, in general, persist uniformly on arbitrarily long polynomial time scales.
Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity

This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), with \(γ>1\), and \(λ(ρ)=ρ\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. Combined with weighted estimates, pressure estimates, and the analysis of the effective viscous flux and vorticity, this method yields the density bound required to close the global continuation argument. Cylindrical Ricci flows and the PDE-ODI principle

We derive precise asymptotics for ancient asymptotically cylindrical Ricci flows. We establish a dichotomy in which the leading deviation from the cylinder is either linear or quadratic in the axial variables. In the linear case, we show that the flow is exponentially asymptotic to a Bryant soliton times a Euclidean factor. For $κ$-solutions, we further show that the flow is isometric to such a product, up to parabolic rescaling. In the quadratic case, we obtain higher-order asymptotics governed by a finite-dimensional invariant. We also establish propagation of cylindrical regions and uniqueness of cylindrical tangent flows.
