We make use of a relatively recent convex integration result from Lewicka and Pakzad and geometrical approximations (similar to the ones using origami maps) to find an upper bound for the scaling of the elastic energy as h	o 0. Through the interplay of the stretching and bending components of the energy we can attain a scaling of order h^{5/3} for the upper-bound of a positional constraint problem. Furthermore, in doing so we will provide some new C^0 approximation results for vK short maps through piecewise affine vK solutions.
Júlia Komjáthy; Marco Seiler; Daniel Valesin

Empirical studies show that communities such as households and workplaces strongly influence how an infection spreads and how long it persists in a population. To understand this effect, we study the contact process (SIS epidemic model) on random intersection graphs and their local weak limit. In the contact process, infected vertices recover with rate $1$ and transmit the infection to each of their neighbours with rate $λ$. The random intersection graph is defined on a finite population; each individual belongs to a random number of communities (captured by a membership distribution), and each community has a random size (captured by a community size distribution). Communities are all taken to be complete graphs. The local weak limit of the random intersection graph, called the branching community tree, has complete graphs arranged in a tree structure. Letting $M$ have the membership distribution and $K$ have the community size distribution, we prove that if either $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]=\infty$ for all $c > 0$ or $\mathbb E[e^{cK\log K}] = \infty$ for all $c > 0$, then for all $λ> 0$, the infection on the finite graph survives for exponentially long with high probability, and on the local limit graph, it survives forever with positive probability. On the other hand, if for some $c > 0$ both $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[e^{K\log(cK)}]<\infty$ hold, then the process with small $λ$ dies out in the local limit graph. We compare these findings with known results on the behaviour of the contact process on a "community-free" random graph with similar degree distributions, to highlight the impact of communities.
Elementary length of polynomial automorphisms in dimension at least three

Let $\mathrm{E}(K,n)$ be the group generated by the elementary automorphisms of $K[X]$, $X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$, the maps which add to one coordinate a polynomial in the other coordinates. It is the group of tame automorphisms with Jacobian determinant $1$. We study the word length $\ell$ on $\mathrm{E}(K,n)$ with respect to the elementary maps, for $n\ge3$ and in comparison with the plane, where the Jung-van der Kulk amalgam provides a normal form. The decompositions of $F$ of length $\#\mathrm{supp}(F)$, the number of coordinates moved by $F$, are determined by $F^{-1}$, and $\ell(F\times\mathrm{Id}_r)=\ell(F)$ whenever $\ell(F)\le\#\mathrm{supp}(F)+2$. Vasyunin's quadratic automorphism of $K[X_1,\dots,X_5]$ has exactly six minimal decompositions, which differ in the degrees of their factors, and its dynamical degree is $\sqrt2$. In characteristic zero a map $X+H\in K[X_1,X_2,X_3]^3$ with $H(0)=0$ and nilpotent Jacobian matrix is Pascal finite if and only if the components of $H$ are linearly dependent. Over every field the Anick automorphism $A$ of $K[X_1,\dots,X_4]$ is not a product of fewer than $7$ elementary maps, while $\ell(A\times\mathrm{Id}_1)=6$. The lower bound rests on Cohn's theorem on $\mathrm{GL}_2(K[X_3,X_4])$, and the decomposition of length $6$ is a polynomial form of the commutator identity which places Cohn's matrix in $\mathrm{E}_3(K[X_3,X_4])$.
Elementary Factorization For Continuous Orthogonal Matrices
Gaofeng Huang; Phan Quoc Bao Tran

We prove that every nullhomotopic continuous map, from a finite-dimensional normal topological space X to the complex special orthogonal group, is a product of elementary orthogonal matrices with entries in the ring of continuous functions. The number of factors is bounded by a constant depending only on the size of the matrices and the covering dimension of X. The same factorization result holds for nullhomotopic special orthogonal matrices with entries in a unital commutative Banach algebra.
Compactness from fractional momentum bounds and weak solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations

We consider the barotropic Navier--Stokes equations on ${\mathbb R}^3$ with constant viscosities, finite mass and finite energy. For every $γ>1$, a local bound on the momentum $m=ρu$ in $L^2_tH^{-1+σ}_x$, $σ>0$, gives strong local convergence of the densities under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1. For $γ>9/8$ we prove, uniformly along the approximations, $$ \|I_{1-α}m\|_{L^2(I\times{\mathbb R}^3)}\leq C_{I,α} \qquad\text{for some }α>0,\quad I\Subset(0,\infty).$$ Here $I_s$ is the spatial Riesz potential. Together with tightness of the energy at spatial infinity, this gives a global finite-energy renormalized weak solution.

We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
An arithmetic theory of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra

We show geometric and dimensional properties of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra for both $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$ using the projective cocycle steering method, which we introduce. In particular, we show the existence of a simultaneous Hall ray for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, a simultaneous Hall interval for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$, regimes of full and positive Hausdorff dimension, a scaling law, empty low spectra in certain cases, a compact set of full Hausdorff dimension in $(2Q\sqrt 3 - \varepsilon, 2Q\sqrt 3)$ where $Q$ is a common denominator of the finite set of rationals giving the translations, and the density of Lagrange equality sets in $\mathbb{R}$ for Lagrange constants in the Hall ray or Hall interval, respectively. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equality set for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, for a finite set of rational translations, is thick but, for the set of all rational translations, is empty. Likewise, we bound the Hausdorff dimension of the Lagrange equality sets for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$ in every nonempty open interval of $\mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $Q$, our result on the Hall interval, the density result, and the dimension bounds for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$ hold for all sufficiently small $δ>0$. Both emptiness results (low spectra and the Lagrange equality set under all rational translations) hold for every $δ>0$.
On coherence of enveloping algebras of infinite-dimensional Lie algebras

We investigate when the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{g})$ of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is coherent. We show that if $\mathfrak{g}$ is the loop algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$ then $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is coherent exactly when $\mathfrak{h}$ is nilpotent. As a consequence, we show that $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is not coherent if $\mathfrak{g}$ is complex, simple, $\mathbb{Z}$-graded, of polynomially bounded growth, and not isomorphic to the Witt algebra $W = \mathrm{Der} \mathbb{C}[t,t^{-1}]$ or its one-sided version. We also demonstrate that the homomorphic image of $U(W)$ used to prove non-Noetherianity of $U(W)$ in previous work of the first author and Walton is not coherent. On the other hand, we establish that two closely related connected graded rings are graded coherent. Finally, we prove that any exhaustively filtered ring is coherent if its Rees ring is graded coherent.

Let $D$ be a $k$-edge weighted VEW graph and $I=I(D)$ be its edge ideal. In this paper, we characterize the irredundant irreducible decomposition of edge ideal $I$. Also, we study the Cohen-Macaulay property and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of different classes of $k$-edge weighted VEW graphs.
No roughening transition for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 4$

Consider the Ising measure $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}$ on $Λ_n:=([-n,n]^{d-1}\times[-n,n-1]) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ at inverse temperature $β$ with all plus boundary condition at heights $z \geq 0$ and all minus boundary condition at heights $z<0$. Let $β_c(d)$ be the critical inverse temperature. For every $d \geq 4$ and $β>β_c(d)$, we prove that $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}(σ_0)$ has a positive lower bound independent of $n$. As a consequence, any Dobrushin state (i.e., a subsequential limit of $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}$) is not translation invariant for those $(d,β)$, and thus there is no roughening transition when $d \geq 4$.
Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)

We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology. To approach those $G$ that escape the net of previously known cases, for an inclusion of reductive $k$-groups $M \subset L$, we develop a new method based on the Rost invariant for transferring $R$-equivalence on $L/M$ to $R$-equivalence on $L$. To find homogeneous spaces to which our method fruitfully applies, we use the theories of prehomogeneous vector spaces and of special symplectic representations: concretely, for a $32$-dimensional half-spin representation $V$, we argue that the vectors in its unique open orbit $O \subset V$ admit unique up to interchange decompositions into sums of two pure spinors, and show that various double covers of $O$ built from such decompositions are rational varieties over any base field.
Brownian Twins of Fractional Diffusion Models

We study generative diffusion models in which the Brownian motion driving the noising dynamics is replaced by fractional Brownian motion or by a Markovian approximation of it. In the standard linear-Gaussian setting, we show that the memory of the noise acts only through the noise schedule. To every such model we associate a Brownian twin, a classical diffusion model with the same drift and an explicit variance schedule, and prove that everything the reverse-time process knows about the data is contained in one linear statistic which follows the reverse-time equation of the twin. Consequently, the denoising score matching losses of the two models coincide for every network, and access to the full path or to the augmented state does not reduce the loss. Moreover, we characterize when the reduction degenerates and describe where the reduction ends.
Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus

We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fifteen-node quotient. Applying a rational Kuga-Satake criterion, we establish abelianity of Chow motives for explicit infinite arithmetic subfamilies of all three Garbagnati-Sarti lattice types, including their Picard-rank specializations. Finally, we prove a square-Franchetta theorem for the ten-dimensional family of double-cubic K3 surfaces.
Rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration

We apply proof mining methods developed by Kohlenbach and the second author to compute uniform rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration studied by Kanzow and Shehu. As special cases, we obtain rates of metastability for the Halpern and modified Halpern iterations, as well as for the Tikhonov-Mann iteration. Furthermore, convergence results are obtained as immediate consequences of our quantitative results.
Energy-preserving Bayesian model reduction: closed-form structured posteriors and probabilistic stability certificates for quadratic operator inference
João Victor Galvão da Mata; Mengwu Guo

Bayesian operator inference learns reduced-order models (ROMs) with polynomial structure from state data and returns a closed-form Gaussian posterior over the reduced operators. That posterior is unconstrained, so it gives positive probability to operators with unbounded dynamics, and current practice controls this only through finite-horizon simulation tests on a few samples. We show that energy preservation of the quadratic operator is a set of linear equality constraints, which can be imposed exactly inside the Bayesian formulation without losing the closed form. In particular, the constrained posterior follows from one Kalman-type update of the unconstrained one, and its samples are obtained exactly, by the same correction applied to unconstrained draws. Under this structure, global boundedness for all initial conditions and bounded inputs reduces to a linear matrix condition on the symmetric part of the linear operator. The simulation test is then replaced by a probabilistic stability certificate: the posterior probability that the ROM is globally bounded, estimated with exact confidence bounds; the posterior restricted to certified models is then sampled exactly by rejection. For energy-conserving systems, the linear part can be constrained to be skew-symmetric as well: every draw then grows at most linearly in time, and conserves energy exactly when unforced. On a forced viscous Burgers' equation, the Korteweg-de Vries equation and a two-dimensional viscous Burgers' equation, every sample of the constrained posterior integrates to a bounded trajectory, where up to all unconstrained draws diverge, and beyond the observation window the former is also the more accurate of the two.

In this paper, we show that for every sufficiently large positive integer $t$ and every integer $n \ge t$, every $K_t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs on vertex set $[n]$ has size at most $2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}$. Furthermore, when the equality is attained, $\mathcal{G}$ must consist of all graphs on $[n]$ that contain some fixed copy of $K_t$. Our result settles a conjecture of Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut for sufficiently large $t$. We also present a short proof for the odd-cycle-intersecting case, slightly different from the existing proofs in the literature.
$L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
Norman El Fartass; Lampros Gavalakis; Ioannis Kontoyiannis

We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.
Elliptic regularization for anisotropic mean curvature flow
Carlo Alberto Antonini; Antonio De Rosa; Massimiliano Morini; Salvatore Stuvard

We develop an elliptic regularization scheme for anisotropic mean curvature flow in arbitrary dimension, with general norms serving as surface tension and mobility. Starting from a non-fattening set of finite perimeter, we prove that the vertically rescaled minimizers and translating solitons converge in the Kuratowski sense to the unique generalized level-set motion, and locally in BV to the flat flow. Furthermore, by implementing a restarting and matching procedure prior to curvature identification, we establish for the limit flat flow a coupled phase-transport and surface-energy dissipation balance valid for arbitrary, possibly crystalline, anisotropies. When the surface tension is continuously differentiable (away from the origin) and strictly convex, we further prove that the flat flow is a BV flow and that its reduced boundary defines a unit-density anisotropic Brakke flow. To our knowledge, this is the first construction of unit-density anisotropic Brakke flows valid for every strictly convex differentiable surface tension, in arbitrary dimension and for prescribed non-fattening initial data, without assuming perimeter convergence.
Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets

Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.
On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
Yangyang Cheng; Stefan Glock; Andrew Lane

A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. We prove a minimum degree version of this result. Note that a necessary condition for a $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices to admit a decomposition into perfect matchings is that $G$ is vertex-regular and $k\mid n$. We show that, if this is satisfied and, in addition, $G$ has minimum $(k-1)$-degree at least $(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n$, then it indeed decomposes into perfect matchings. The constant $1/2$ is optimal, as below this threshold, $G$ might not even contain a single perfect matching. This settles a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2021.
Complex chaotic Boltzmann machines as deterministic representations of quantum states

Neural networks and tensor networks have opened new ways to explore quantum systems by parameterizing families of wave functions through the structure and parameters of a network. Here we extend this perspective to a dynamical representation: we introduce a complex chaotic Boltzmann machine that assigns a deterministic system to a pure quantum state. We extend Suzuki's construction to incorporate both Born probabilities and relative phases. The probabilities set the trajectory velocities in a hypercube, while the phases define a complex field that lifts its Poincare sections. The evolution is determined by the network parameters and initial conditions, without random choices during flights or configuration changes. Our analysis of two qubits and study of three-qubit families show how relations between probabilities organize regular curves, islands, and unstable regions, and how phases distinguish states that share the same Born dynamics. This architecture turns a wave-function parameterization into a geometry of trajectories, providing a tool to explore probabilities, phases, and symmetries together across families of states.
A sharp dimension barrier for uniform Gaussian approximations

We establish a universal dimension barrier for Gaussian approximations based on $n$ i.i.d. random vectors $X_1,...,X_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Fix $m\in(2,\infty)$ and consider mean-zero distributions with coordinate variances bounded from below by a fixed positive constant and coordinatewise $m$th absolute moments bounded from above by a fixed constant. We show that \begin{equation*} \log d=o\left(n^{(m-2)/(3m-2)}\right) \end{equation*} is necessary for any sequence of statistics to admit a Gaussian approximation to its distribution uniformly over this distribution class and all hyperrectangles. Here, the centered Gaussian target is required to have the covariance or correlation matrix of the observations. The obstruction includes randomized procedures and already holds for coordinate maxima. Conversely, for $m\in(2,4]$, we establish that this growth condition on $d$ is sufficient for the distribution of a vector of centered and scaled quantile-winsorized means to obey a Gaussian approximation with covariance target without further restrictions on the covariances of the observations or knowledge of $m$. Thus, the dimension barrier is sharp in this moment range. For $m\in(4,\infty)$, the same statistic attains the barrier up to a power of $\log n$.
Riemannian Curvature Functionals for de Rham Spectral Triples

We compute mixed Clifford residue functionals for the Hodge-de Rham operator in even dimensions. A symbol-composition calculation recovers the Riemann and Einstein tensors and yields two ordered curvature functionals with the same classical limit. For specified truncation products on warped collars, we evaluate all five boundary cases and prove that the curvature-recovering antisymmetrizations have no boundary correction. We extend the constructions to spectral data equipped with two one-form actions. Explicit noncommutative torus and finite-direction examples distinguish the functionals and exhibit failures of module balancing and Riemann symmetries. A conformal example shows that a naive exterior lift need not recover classical curvature. The additional structures and limitations of each extension are stated explicitly.
Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four

A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $η(2z)^{4}η(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and level $8$. The proof reduces the counts by elementary means to a twisted second moment of the Legendre family of elliptic curves, which is a value of a hypergeometric function over $\mathbb{F}_q$ evaluated by Ahlgren and Ono for primes. As consequences, the number of factorizations whose three pairwise resultants lie in one square class is a polynomial in $q$, with proportion $1/4+3/(4q^{2})+O(q^{-4})$. When the quotient is a product of two elliptic curves conjugate over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, we prove that the splitting of the factors $u,v,w$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ decides which points of order two of the elliptic factor are divisible by two.
On the fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic quenching problem

We study the fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic free boundary problem $$|Du|^κF(D^2u)-u_t=u^{γ-1} \qquad \textrm{in} \quad \{u>0\},$$ where $κ>0$, $0<γ<1$, and $F$ is a convex or concave uniformly elliptic operator with $F(0)=0$. We establish the existence of a nonnegative viscosity solution with prescribed continuous nonnegative boundary data and prove its optimal upper growth along the free boundary, together with matching non-degeneracy estimates in parabolic cylinders adapted to the scaling. Our approach combines a weak Bernstein estimate with barrier arguments to obtain local compactness and boundary attainment. To obtain the optimal growth rate, we further use persistence of positivity for limits with vanishing absorption coefficients to identify the homogeneous equation across the zero set, and then combine the optimal spatial regularity estimate of \cite{LLYZ25} with an iteration argument.
Stochastic Extragradient Methods Beyond Lipschitz Continuity
Konstantinos Oikonomidis; Jan Quan; Mathijs Schuurmans; Panagiotis Patrinos

Stochastic variational inequality problems have received significant attention due to their ability to model large-scale machine learning tasks. Typically, the operators involved are assumed to be globally Lipschitz, with only a handful of works extending beyond the standard setting to the so-called $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. In this work, we propose a novel stochastic past extragradient algorithm for variational inequality problems under a broad regularity assumption that is even less restrictive than $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz continuity and provide convergence guarantees under bounded variance of the stochastic oracle. More precisely, we show a.s. convergence with suitable stepsize schedules and obtain convergence rates in expectation and in probability for fixed horizons. Finally, in numerical simulations we compare our proposed algorithm against standard methods.
Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization

One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. Of the many consequences of this lack of conditional expectation, we consider the problem of defining the quantum conditional relative entropy, i.e., the relative entropy between two quantum states conditioned to a sub-region or sub-algebra. We discuss how, when the conditional expectation map is not defined, there are multiple, non-equivalent ways to define a quantum conditional relative entropy quantity, and we present some of their properties. Classical conditional relative entropy has played a fundamental role in many applications to spin systems, and in particular in proving logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. A key feature of conditional relative entropy that intervenes in these results is its quasi-factorization or approximate tensorization property: informally, the relative entropy is almost super-additive over weakly-dependent sub-algebras. It is then not surprising that the key to obtaining similar applications in the quantum setting, such as quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities in spin systems, has been to obtain approximate factorization results for the quantum conditional relative entropy, with the added complication that there is not a unique definition of conditional relative entropy to work with. We review the recent results regarding quasi-factorization of the quantum conditional relative entropy, in strong and weak forms.
Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
Shengzhi Jin; Xin Sun; Baojun Wu

We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.
Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation

For $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ count Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and $c$ above it, and let $D_{k,n}=\det\bigl(a_{i+j,k}(x,c)\bigr)_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. T. Yu proved Cigler's conjecture $D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2$ $(n\ge2k+2)$ by writing $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant of Chebyshev polynomials modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$. Using a linear map found by Yu, we show that the recurrence is a reduction of the Hirota-Miwa equation for Casorati determinants. This gives a second proof, and the recurrence holds for $n\ge2k+2+\max(0,N-\lfloor k/2\rfloor)$ for the Hankel determinants of $n\mapsto L(X^n(U_k-xU_{k-1}))$ whenever the moment functional $L$ has the recurrence coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials above height $N$. For any monic polynomial in place of $U_k-xU_{k-1}$ the Hirota-Miwa equation gives an identity with a free parameter between symplectic characters, and Yu's identity for rectangular characters follows from it by fixing the parameter and restricting to a line. On the curve $xc+x^2+1=0$ we express the Hankel determinants of the sequences shifted by $2$ and $-1$ through the $D_{k,n}$. There the recurrence becomes the Desnanot-Jacobi identity, which gives a third proof, and a recurrence for the Hankel determinants of odd convolution powers of Narayana polynomials, shifted backward by $k$. We also prove identities that Cigler stated as observations, an analogue of odd orthogonal type, and a factorization for paths with a weighted return step.
An Asymptotic One-Sample Surrogate for Non-Gaussian ERM with General Convex Regularization
Tianjian Zhang; Cosme Louart; Malik Tiomoko; Zhenyu Liao

We study convex empirical risk minimization (ERM) with non-Gaussian features and nonsmooth penalties through a surrogate driven by a single Gaussian vector. The surrogate preserves the penalty and calibrates its coefficients using the actual joint law of the feature-label model. We prove that this population calibration exists and is unique. We prove a Gaussian approximation for fresh prediction scores when the data satisfy a Poincaré inequality. Together with regularity conditions on the losses, this approximation yields agreement between the ERM minimizer and its surrogate in normalized means and prediction variances, as well as formulas for prediction and classification risks. The result covers general uniformly strongly convex penalties and pure Lasso under projection anti-concentration. The core proof relies on a cavity Hamilton-Jacobi argument that compares the main statistics of the two minimizers without differentiating the penalty.
Invariant rings of Frobenius polarization operators and normal cores of subgroups

For a proper subgroup $H$ of a finite group $G$, we determine the common kernel, or invariant ring, of the Frobenius polarization operators corresponding to the elements of $G\setminus H$. We show that the invariant rings defined by the left and right polarization operators coincide and depend only on the normal core $N=\operatorname{Core}_G(H)$. We construct polynomials $P_Ω$ indexed by the orbits of the conjugation action of $G$ on $\widehat N$ and prove that they form an algebraically independent generating set for the invariant ring. We also show that inclusion of these invariant rings as subrings of $\mathbb C[\mathbf{x}]$ is equivalent to inclusion of the corresponding normal cores. For an arbitrary subgroup $H$, we give a factorization of the group determinant in terms of these polynomials. This factorization generalizes Frobenius' group determinant theorem and reduces to its factorization when $H=G$. When $G$ is abelian, each $P_Ω$ is a specialization of the group determinant of the quotient group $G/H$. Finally, we establish a Capelli identity for each $P_Ω$ and compute the coefficient polynomial obtained by applying a constant-coefficient differential operator to its powers.
Solvers for a Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations

We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. Under our assumptions we derive two solvers: a martingale solver (inspired by the deep FBSDE solver studied in recent literature), and a min-max solver leveraging a Hilbert space orthogonality condition to enforce the martingale property. We obtain a posteriori error bounds for both solvers. The min-max solver avoids the need to approximate the class of square integrable martingales directly (which in practice is usually done by parameterizing a stochastic integral representation), at the expense of weakening the topology with respect to which one should expect convergence of an approximate solution.
Weakly competing bubbles for a critical elliptic system in higher dimensions

We overcome this obstruction with a variational reduction in the spirit of Bahri and Rey, in which the infinite-dimensional correction is obtained by constrained minimization and is only required to depend continuously on the parameters. The resulting finite-dimensional problem is then solved by a degree argument. In this way, for every $n\ge5$ and every integer $k\ge2$, we construct nonnegative finite-energy solutions in the weak-competition regime $β\to0^-$: the first component is close to a standard bubble, while the second concentrates at the $k$ vertices of a regular polygon. The concentration scale is $d_*\varepsilon(1+o(1))$, with $d_*$ explicit and $\varepsilon^{(n-4)/2}=|β|\,|\ln\varepsilon|$, and we give precise expansions of the amplitudes and of the remainders.
Exponential decay of the quasilinear Maxwell system caused by conductivity on a collar

We study the anisotropic, quasilinear Maxwell system on a bounded domain $Ω$ with perfectly conducting boundary conditions. It is damped via a conductivity $σ$ which is strictly positive on its support containing a collar of the boundary. We prove that solutions exist globally and decay exponentially to $0$ if there are no magnetic charges on $Ω$, no electric charges off the support of $σ$, and the initial fields are small. Our approach relies on a splitting of the solution via adapted Helmholtz decompositions and an observability-type estimate for a related system without charges, shown by means of Morawetz multipliers. Moreover, one has to control the space derivatives of the solution by its time derivatives, exploiting the structure of the system. Distributed Optimization of $M$-Convex Functions Subject to Linear Constraints via Continuous Relaxation and Shapley-Folkman Decomposition

$M$-convex functions from discrete convex analysis admit tractable minimization and convex extensions that agree with them at integer points. We study the minimization of a separable collection of $N$ $M$-convex functions subject to $m$ linear coupling constraints. Our two-stage algorithm first solves the convex relaxation and then reconstructs an integer solution through local Carathéodory decompositions and an LP purification step. We prove polynomial value-oracle evaluation of the $M$-convex extension and give both an exact value-oracle-polynomial implementation and a distributed consensus-ADMM implementation under a proximal oracle. We also establish proximity and additive envelope-gap guarantees when Stage~1 uses a strongly convex extension. On an inventory placement problem with up to about $10^6$ products, both guarantees hold on every run, and the method is faster than exact integer-programming benchmarks by a factor that grows with the number of regions.
Boundary of the Lagrange and Markov spectra near Hall's ray

The Lagrange and Markov spectra, denoted by $L$ and $M$, respectively, are closed subsets of the real line with intricate fractal geometry related to Diophantine approximations. In 1975, Freiman proved that both spectra contain the ray $[c_F,\infty)$, where $c_F=4.527829566\dots$, and that this ray is optimal, as both spectra avoid a tiny interval $(ν_F,c_F)$. Using renormalization techniques and the thickness of Cantor sets, we prove that the boundaries $\partial L$ and $\partial M$ have positive Hausdorff dimensions arbitrarily close to $ν_F$. Furthermore, in connection with Berstein's conjecture, which predicts that $[4.1,4.52]\subset L$, we exhibit a gap in $L$ near $4.08$, the first known gap in the region $L\cap[3.945,4.52]$. We also prove that the boundaries of both spectra have positive Hausdorff dimension near $4.5213$ and $4.08$.
Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions

Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. The benchmarks also demonstrate that when $Q$ is the physical energy, the constrained models are less accurate than EDMD and can exhibit significant structural bias.

We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.
Projectively Flat Spherically Symmetric Sprays of Constant Curvature

In this paper, we study projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays of constant curvature. We derive a system of equations that is equivalent to the constant-curvature condition for such sprays and solve it to obtain a complete classification of the projective factor \(p(r,s)\) into four explicit families. We further show that the sprays induced by projectively flat spherically symmetric Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature \(K=0\), \(K=-1\), and \(K=1\) are all special cases of our classification, thereby confirming that the sprays induced by these constant-flag-curvature Finsler metrics are fully contained in our framework.

The vanilla method in bilevel programming is to reformulate it as a single-level mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCC), via the KKT conditions of the lower-level. This method seemed to work only for optimistic formulations. However, in (Zeng, 2020), B. Zeng presented a general method to reduce pessimistic bilevel problems to optimistic ones. In this note, we study how to apply the MPCC approach to the pessimistic counterpart through Zeng's reformulation (Zeng, 2020). While we show that it cannot be applied directly since constraint qualification can be destroyed by the reformulation, it still can be used to solve natural relaxations, in the spirit of (Wiesemann,2013),(Loridan & Morgan,1989), (Loridan & Morgan,1996).
Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally

Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].

This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology. In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a subscheme of a certain projective variety. Varying the hopping-rate parameter $p$, we give a one-parameter family $S$ of the solution sets. We show that, for the ASEP with $n$ sites and $m$ particles, the fiber $S|_p$ with generic $p$ contains $\binom{n}{m}$ points with multiplicity, which equals the expected number of admissible Bethe roots to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equation.
Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control

Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Recently, Chen et al. introduced the $k$-th binding number $β^k(G)$. Anderson [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1971] proved that every graph $G$ of even order with $β^1(G)\ge\frac43$ contains a perfect matching, and that the bound $\frac43$ is best possible. For $k\ge2$, Chen et al. proved that $β^k(G)\ge1$ guarantees a $k$-factor whenever $kn$ is even, and that the bound $1$ is best possible. The above facts reveal a fundamental distinction between the higher-order binding number and the classical binding number. This distinction makes extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number particularly intriguing. For positive integers $n,$ $k$ and $r$, we in this paper determine the maximum size and spectral radius among all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $β^k(G)<r$, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs, respectively. In particular, when $k=1$, our results imply the corresponding extremal results of Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin., 2024] and Liu, Chen and Fan [Electron. J. Combin., 2026]. Our proofs develop a structural framework that relates higher-order neighborhood inequalities to the structure of the complements of graphs. This framework may provide an approach to Turán-type problem involving the $k$-th binding number, and the approach may be of independent interest.
Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean-Field Games

We study second order variational mean-field games with quadratic Hamiltonian. In analogy with entropic optimal transport, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and the second author recently proposed an entropy-minimization formulation of the problem, which could be interpreted as the Lagrangian counterpart of the classical Eulerian approach. We investigate the small-noise $Γ$-limit for the Lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation and establish $Γ$-convergence of second order mean-field games towards their deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into another (dynamical) proof of the convergence of the Schrödinger problem to optimal transport. Moreover, we study the original Eulerian problem and prove a first order energy expansion, which establishes a selection principle for minimizers of the deterministic problem.
Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading

A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.
Dynamics of a spherical ferromagnet on a non-conducting incline in an external magnetic field
Rasmus C. Raschke; Tim Matthies; Roland Wiesendanger; Elena Y. Vedmedenko

Magnetic particles of various shapes and sizes are used in biomedical applications, robotics, nanomagnetism, electrotechnology, and education. Yet despite years of study, a theoretical description of the rolling motion of a solid magnetic sphere still eludes us. One of the reasons is that coupling magnetic fields with mechanical degrees of freedom creates a highly non-linear motion with non-holonomic constraints, which makes modeling these systems analytically or by simulations non-trivial. The Lagrange-d'Alembertian approach to holonomic systems remains one of the most versatile methods to prove central theorems and solve problems in analytical mechanics and electrodynamics. While non-holonomic systems are not accessible by the original theory, recent developments generalize the principle to certain dissipative systems. Here, we present a successful application of these developments to a simple mechanical system comprising a magnetic solid sphere on an incline within an external magnetic field. Using numerical simulations, we characterized how the system depends on its initial parameters. Furthermore, our findings are in line with recent experiments, demonstrating that even very weak magnetic fields can cause unexpected motion of ferromagnetic objects. The simplicity of this example also makes it a promising candidate for undergraduate physics education where the treatment of non-holonomic variational principles is still widely uncommon.
Linear support bounds for supercuspidal matrix coefficients of p-adic groups
Itay Glazer; Erez Lapid; Zhengyu Mao; Mark Shusterman

Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. For any standard congruence tower $K_{\bullet}=(K_n)$ in $\mathbf{G}(F)$, supercuspidal matrix coefficients between $K_n$-fixed vectors are supported in an adjoint ball of radius $an+b_{K_{\bullet}}$, compact modulo the center, with $a$ depending only on $F$ and $\mathbf{G}$. When $\mathbf{G}(F)$ is non-compact modulo its center, the linear dependence on $n$ is optimal. In algebraic families we obtain a uniform radius $An+Bk+C+\operatorname{val}_{F}(N)$, where $k$ bounds the logarithmic height of the parameter. We deduce a sharp linear bound for the exponent in Bernstein's stabilization theorem. For quasi-split classical groups, we also remove the dyadic level restriction in the limit multiplicity theorem.
Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
Shiqi Li; Jiawei He; Jianhua Huang

We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(μ\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_μ\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_μ\) is upper semicontinuous at \(μ=0\) almost surely.
Proximity and Remoteness in Trees with given Segment Sequence
Imran Allie; Brandon Du Preez; Zion Hefty; Sonwabile Mafunda

The average distance of a vertex $v$ of a connected graph $G$ is the arithmetic mean of the distances from $v$ to all other vertices of $G$. The proximity $π(G)$ and the remoteness $ρ(G)$ of $G$ are the minimum and the maximum of the average distances of the vertices of $G$, respectively. A segment $S$ of a tree is a path-subtree whose terminal vertices are either branching or pendant vertices, and all internal vertices have degree $2$. The segment sequence $(\ell_{S_1}, \ell_{S_2},\ldots,\ell_{S_m})$ of T is the non-increasing sequence of the lengths of all segments of T. In this paper, we characterise trees with a given segment sequence that minimise proximity and those that maximise remoteness. For trees that minimise remoteness, we establish sufficient conditions under which the tree is starlike and conjecture that a remoteness-minimising tree is always either starlike or a ($Δ,2$)-tree. For trees that maximise proximity, we derive a collection of necessary conditions that any tree maximising proximity must satisfy.
On the Role of Fisher Information, Variance and Asymptotics in Statistical Inference

Bahadur's \emph{Lectures on the Theory of Estimation} close with a chapter on asymptotics: asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimator, Fisher's bound on its asymptotic variance with Hodges's counterexample, and local asymptotic normality. A companion paper read the earlier lectures with one modification, replacing the point estimator by a generalized estimator---Fisher's continuum of significance tests---assessed by information rather than variance. This paper reads Chapter 8 the same way. At each of its three parts the classical statement is an approximation about a point estimator, while the corresponding statement about the score is exact at every sample size. Superefficiency does not arise, because information is bounded by the Fisher information at every $n$; Hodges's estimator, computed exactly, is fully efficient at the origin and loses information only where its mean square error is worst. The information of a generalized estimator is argued to be Fisher information: the mean rate at which a continuum of tests responds to the parameter, standardized by its variance. The resulting Fisher upper bound differs geometrically, not merely algebraically, from the Cramér--Rao lower bound. The extension is not empty: the $t$-test continuum loses about half an observation's worth of the information in $\bar X$ at every $n$.
Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares

Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near typical service. Thus one-time power distributions alone do not determine reliability.
A Higher-Dimensional Extension of the Laugesen--Siudeja Lower Bound

We prove a higher-dimensional analogue of the lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture, using a covariance normalization of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. We give a covariance-dependent lower bound for every bounded convex domain. From this bound we obtain the optimal constant for convex planar domains and for simplices in every dimension \(d\geq2\). If the simplex covariance inequality stated in a 2026 preprint holds, the same constant is optimal over all bounded convex domains in dimensions \(d\geq3\). In each of these cases, the infimum is approached by compressing a regular simplex in the direction of an edge and is unattained.
Approximation of the Nonautonomous Maxwell System with an Interface

To obtain higher-regularity solutions for nonautonomous Maxwell systems with an interface, we approximate the initial data and coefficients by smoother counterparts. To preserve compatibility conditions of the approximations, required to obtain solutions to the Maxwell systems, we systematically adjust the approximating sequence of initial data. While the existing well-posedness theory in [14] guarantees more regular solutions, standard a-priori estimates fail to ensure convergence in the desired norm. We overcome this by a mollification argument and a div-curl estimate from [4] and [7].
Global existence and scattering of large solutions of the cubic Dirac equation
Timothy Candy; Sebastian Herr; Kenji Nakanishi

We construct global dispersive solutions to the massive cubic Dirac equation (Soler Model) for initial data with large critical Sobolev norm. Because of a lack of a coercive energy in the Dirac equation, the only previously known large solutions are solitons (which are non-dispersive) and Majorana-solutions (which are in fact solutions to a linear equation). Here, the new strategy is to exploit the non-relativistic limit, which connects the Dirac equation to a system of Schrödinger equations with cubic nonlinearities, and then to develop a scattering theory for this limiting system.

Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. We show that a single pretrained Transformer can deliver efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass, without deriving efficient influence functions or estimating nuisance functions. Pretrained on simulated data with the true parameter as the only label, the Transformer learns the posterior mean and covariance of the queried estimand and hence returns an estimate and a Wald-type confidence region. Theoretically, we prove that, for locally flat pretraining priors of slowly growing complexity, the posterior mean is efficient for every queried estimand. The Transformer inherits this efficiency with asymptotically exact coverage, in probability over evaluation populations and queries, even under distribution shift. We also reveal that the guarantee places much higher demands on pretraining when the data-generating distribution is fixed, as in classical frequentist inference. Experiments on causal inference, partial linear regression, and survival analysis show that the pretrained model generally achieves the lowest estimation error among competing methods, with nearly nominal coverage, at a computational cost of only about 0.02 seconds per dataset.

We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.
A Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations

We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. We obtain existence and uniqueness results for arbitrary finite time horizons.
Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones

We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

Unlike the Gröbner method of Sam and Snowden, this criterion requires no ordering compatible with the morphisms.
Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning

Generative models transform simple random inputs into samples that resemble observed data. For a finite training set, a central question is how its geometry shapes the terminal dynamics and the probabilities assigned to individual samples. We address this question for flow matching with linear interpolation between independent Gaussian and empirical samples. The squared distance to the training set generates explicit paths contracting exponentially toward the nearest sample. At ties, the Clarke subdifferential characterizes the graphical limit of the rescaled velocity field. This geometry motivates two learning methods: fitting the distance potential with value and gradient supervision, and fitting velocities along explicit contraction paths. These results connect flow matching and score-based diffusion through a common limiting geometry and show how asymptotic analysis can inform the design and evaluation of generative models.
Emergent Causality of Macroscopic Transport and Equilibration in Long-Range Quantum Systems

Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent $α\in(D,D+1)$ in $D$ spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with $α\in (1,3/2)$, whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.
Essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees

We establish characterizations of the essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. As direct applications of our main results, we obtain compactness criteria for such composition operators.
On the prime index elements graph of finite groups

For a finite group $G$, the prime index elements graph $\G(G)$, introduced by Anitha and Rajkumar, has vertex set $G$, two distinct elements being adjacent if the cyclic subgroup generated by one has prime index in that generated by the other. We show that $\G(G)$ is a bipartite blow-up of a weighted graph $\Hq(G)$ on the cyclic subgroups of $G$, which is a cartesian product of trees when $G$ is nilpotent, and use this to study several graph invariants. We characterize the groups for which $\G(G)$ is a star, a cograph, a chordal graph, or has a perfect code. We compute the sharp bounds for the independence and domination number. We give an exact formula for the strong metric dimension, bound the metric and strong metric dimensions in terms of the quotient graph, show that the upper bounds for the strong metric dimension are attained for cyclic p-groups, and all upper bounds for groups whose prime index elements graph is complete bipartite, and determine the groups attaining the lower bounds: the strong metric dimension attains it only for $\Z_p$ with $p$ odd, and we give a criterion for the metric dimension, which we solve completely for cyclic groups. For nilpotent $G$ we give necessary conditions for $\G(G)$ to be Hamiltonian, in terms of the numbers of covers of cyclic subgroups in the Sylow subgroups, and prove that they are also sufficient when all Sylow subgroups but one are cyclic. We also show that a nilpotent group with a Hamiltonian path is $\Z_3$ or of the form $K\times\Z_2$ with $|K|$ odd, and that in the abelian case above a Hamiltonian path exists exactly when a Hamiltonian cycle does. Finally, we characterize the finite groups $G$ for which $\G(G)$ is planar, toroidal or of genus two.
Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
Péter Naszvadi; Marcell Tukora; Roman Kužel; Mátyás Koniorczyk

Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.
The Global Solutions to Nonlinear Thermoelastic Systems under a Null Condition

We study the Cauchy problem for a class of homogeneous, isotropic nonlinear thermoelastic systems in three space dimensions. Under a null condition for purely elastic part of our system which is different from those considered by Sideris, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global classical solutions with smallness assumptions on the initial data. We use Klainerman--Sideris weighted energy estimates and time-weighted energy estimates for the heat equation to establish global existence. Moreover, we improve upon the global existence result of Ponce and Racke, who assumed that the purely elastic nonlinear terms vanish.
Generalized Markov numbers and plane lattices

We give new explicit constructions of lattice rules in the two-dimensional square and torus. It is well-known that uniformly distributed lattices (in the sense of low-discrepancy) arise from continued fractions with bounded partial denominators. We demonstrate how integers solutions of the generalized Markov equation $x^2+y^2+z^2 = kxyz-k+3$ give rise to such lattices.
Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
Roman Kužel; Mátyás Koniorczyk; Janez Povh

We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.
Local well-posedness for generalized inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equations

We consider the initial value problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} i\partial_t u+Δu=a(x)|u|^αu, \end{equation*} where $a(x)$ is a spatially dependent coefficient. We study a general class of coefficients that includes the usual inhomogeneous nonlinearity $a(x)=λ|x|^{-b}$ and coefficients with multiple singularities. We establish local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for both the $H^s$-subcritical and $H^s$-critical cases under suitable assumptions on $a(x)$. We also extend a fractional difference estimate of Fujiwara to Lorentz spaces.
Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates

In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $μ_0$ and the first moment $μ_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $μ_0$, $μ_1$ and the second moment $μ_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $μ_0$ and $μ_1$ on its own. This condition defines at once a vector space which is studied via barycentric coordinates and elementary exterior algebra, thereby yielding families of equilibrium equations for systems with any consistent number $n$ of particles and dimension $d$. As before, the present equilibrium equations are homogeneous as well as invariant by oriented isometries (for interactions depending only on mutual distances). Our method also develops and extends the approach by A. Albouy from central configurations of codimension $c=(n-1)-d$ equal to one, the so-called Dziobek configurations, to equilibria of systems of interacting particles of arbitrary codimension. Despite the similar appearance, our generalized Albouy equations constitute new equilibrium equations when $c$ is greater than one, even in the case of central configurations. The paper closes with applications to central configurations, with specific results for $n=5,6$ in dimension $d=2$.
The Boolean completion of $\mathsf{S}(L)$: a refinement of localic mereology
M. Andrew Moshier; Imanol Mozo Carollo

We construct and study the Boolean completion of the coframe $\mathsf{S}(L)$ of sublocales of a frame $L$. Realizing $\mathsf{S}(L)$ as a basis for an Alexandroff topology on $L$ and passing to the regular elements of the associated frame, we obtain a complete Boolean algebra $\mathsf{P}(L)$ whose elements are certain subsets of $L$ generalizing sublocale sets; we call them the \emph{parts} of $L$. We show that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ embeds into $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the left adjoint of a Galois connection and that the canonical embedding of $L$ into $\mathsf{S}(L)$ extends to $\mathsf{P}(L)$. From a mereological standpoint, this completion is motivated by universalism: after proving that mereological sums and exact joins coincide for separative posets, we identify $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the sum-completion (equivalently, the exact-join-completion) of $\mathsf{S}(L)$, thereby supplying the mereological sums that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ lacks. Finally, we single out several distinguished parts of a frame: the pointless part, which extends Ball's construction beyond the $T_1$ setting, together with the part of merely points and the topological glue, the former of the two having no counterpart in the classical theory of sublocales.
Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields

We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria. Notably, the exceptional components of an $F$-pure surface singularity are geometrically reduced unless the singularity is a rational double point.

For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length $N$, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary reaches $M$; this random `lifetime' comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity $M$, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to $M$ on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of $N$ and $M$; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem, for one scaling regime in the case of a ball, and conjectures on the behaviour in general domains.
Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices

We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.
Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?
Jaemin Oh; Jerome Darbon; George Em Karniadakis

Trunk-basis (TB) preconditioners build the coarse space of a two-level Schwarz preconditioner from the trunk functions of a trained deep operator network (DeepONet), restricted to subdomains. Their effectiveness has been attributed to spectral bias since networks learn low frequencies first, complementing a smoother that removes the high-frequency error. Spectral bias, however, is a property of training, whereas a randomly initialized trunk with a smooth activation is already smooth. We therefore ask whether TB preconditioners need training. In one dimension, we prove that on each subdomain the span of untrained trunk functions is close to the space of low-degree polynomials under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerically, for the Poisson equation and three-dimensional linear elasticity with constant coefficients, untrained TB and piecewise polynomial coarse spaces of equal dimension yield close conjugate gradient iteration counts, while training with the standard \(\ell^2\) loss sometimes increases them. Training can improve iteration counts when high-contrast coefficients make the low-energy modes non-smooth, and if the loss measures the error in the energy norm. For the Poisson equation with contrast \(10^5\), energy-trained TB coarse spaces need fewer iterations than piecewise polynomials of equal dimension, whereas \(\ell^2\)-trained ones do not. For a topology-optimized elastic cantilever with contrast \(10^6\), the energy-trained TB space enriched with the rigid-body modes gives the fewest iterations at larger coarse dimensions. This suggests that for neural operator-based hybrid solvers, a network's inductive bias and training objective should match the solver.
A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions

For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq. (18) of arXiv:2309.15557 and MathOverflow question 456683). As a by-product we obtain an expression of $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant built from Chebyshev polynomials reduced modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$, together with a bilinear identity for these $k\times k$ determinants that holds for all integer shifts. We also give a proof of Cigler's companion conjecture that $D_{k,n}(x,c)$ equals the determinant of an explicit matrix $H_{k,n}(x)$ with entries $0$, $1$ and powers of $x$, and in particular does not depend on $c$; this statement has recently been proved by V. Jandhyala, and our proof was found independently. The proofs use Chebyshev polynomials, a model of $\mathbb{Q}(x)[X]/(U_k-xU_{k-1})$ by antisymmetric Laurent polynomials, a lemma on complementary minors, and a three-term Plücker relation.
Regular quadratic lattices are rare over real quadratic fields

We show that a positive definite regular quadratic lattice of rank at least 4 over a totally real number field contains a regular sublattice that represents precisely the totally positive integers lying in an ideal. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis and a conjecture on class numbers, it follows that, for each $m$, real quadratic fields admitting a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and $m$ have density 0. Unconditionally, only finitely many real quadratic fields of narrow class number 1 admit a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and 7.
Incentive-Based Regulatory Mechanism for Tariff Design in District Heating and Cooling Networks
Hossein Hesamzadeh; Wicak Ananduta; Eric Dumont; Zacharie De Greve

Low-temperature district heating and cooling networks exchange heat bidirectionally at near-ambient temperatures. When one supplier owns the shared loop, it controls both the tariff and the network temperature that sets every user's conversion efficiency. Existing price-cap and cost-based rules leave this non-price instrument unregulated and reach neither the first-best dispatch nor an explicit division of gains. This paper proposes a two-part, incentive-based tariff that anchors the supplier's lump-sum fee, per building and hour, to an audited outside alternative and divides the participation gains through one regulated share. We model a mixed-integer bilevel Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets hourly tariffs and the temperature regime, anticipating the buildings' co-optimization of electricity and thermal exchange.
