Centralized model predictive control (MPC) exploits network-wide traffic information to obtain the optimal solution of the network-level control problem, but its computational burden grows rapidly with network size. Iterative distributed MPC reduces the size of local optimization problems, but requires repeated information exchange and coordination within each control update. To address these limitations, this paper proposes information-region MPC (IR-MPC), which approximates the first control input of centralized MPC using limited real-time data without iterative coordination. Based on historical traffic data, we quantify how perturbations at other intersections affect the centralized first control input of each intersection and use these couplings to construct a compact information region for every intersection. At each control update, each intersection then solves a local IR-MPC problem once using current data only from its information region. SUMO simulations on a real 28-intersection network show that IR-MPC with one processor per intersection computes its control inputs 9 times faster than centralized MPC and 15 times faster than a representative iterative decomposition-based distributed MPC method. IR-MPC reproduces 85% of the centralized control inputs exactly at the implemented one-second resolution, keeps 99.3% within 2s, and increases mean delay by only 0.03%.
Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game

A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.
Perturbation Algorithm and Iterative Realization of a Four-Layer Semi-Discrete Scheme for an Evolutionary Problem with a Variable Operator
David Gulua; Jemal Rogava; Zurab Vashakidze

In a Hilbert space, we consider the Cauchy problem for an evolutionary equation with the operator $A+B(t)$, where $A$ is a self-adjoint positive definite operator and $B(t)$ is a bounded operator depending on time. By means of the perturbation algorithm, the purely implicit four-layer semi-discrete scheme of the third order of approximation (the three-step backward differentiation formula) is reduced to three two-layer schemes, whose solutions are used to construct an approximate solution of the original problem. In each two-layer scheme, the term containing $B(t)$ is moved to the right-hand side, and the resulting equation is solved by an iterative method, so that only the time-independent operator $I+τA$ has to be inverted; the convergence of the iterations at the rate of a geometric progression with a ratio of order $τ$ is proved. A priori estimates for the two-layer and four-layer schemes are obtained by means of a discrete analogue of Gronwall's lemma. An estimate of order $τ^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.
Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity

Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq δ^2+4δ+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq δ-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq δ-1$ and completely remove the order restriction. Specifically, we prove that $$ q(G) \leq q(B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}), $$ with equality if and only if $G \cong B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$, where $B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n-δ-1} \cup K_{δ+1}$ by adding $k$ edges joining a single vertex of $K_{n-δ-1}$ to $k$ distinct vertices of $K_{δ+1}$.
Asymptotic efficiency comparison of explicit Dirichlet shape estimators

In this study, we compare the asymptotic efficiency of three closed-form estimators of the Dirichlet shape parameters. We start by proving that, in the beta distribution, the score-adjusted moment estimator (SA) has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than the usual moment estimator (M1) for both parameters. We then introduce a new moment estimator (M2) that combines the marginal moment equations to obtain a common estimate of the total concentration. M2 coincides with M1 in the beta case and has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances for every positive shape vector in three or more dimensions. We then show that SA is asymptotically more efficient than M2 when all shape parameters are equal; if at least two parameters differ, each estimator has smaller asymptotic variance than the other for some linear combination of the parameters. Furthermore, SA has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than M2 when all shape parameters are at least 1. Finally, we show that this ordering can reverse if a parameter becomes too small, and obtain relevant mathematical and computational bounds. Overall, the study shows that, for the Dirichlet distribution and under a broad range of parameter settings, score-adjusted estimation outperforms the classic moment estimation and identifies the limits of that advantage.
On Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski sums and products of convex domains

For Minkowski p-sums of convex domains, we establish Brunn-Minkowski-type inequalities for the full sequence of Gutt-Hutchings capacities. We also obtain explicitlower bounds for the Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski p-products. Our proof uses Matijevic's formula for Gutt-Hutchings capacities in terms of the Clarke dual-action functional and the Fadell-Rabinowitz index. By the equality of Gutt-Hutchings and Ekeland-Hofer capacities on star-shaped domains, the same inequalities hold for Ekeland-Hofer capacities.
Rational multisections and unirationality of supersingular K3 surfaces

We prove that every supersingular K3 surface of Artin invariant at most nine is unirational, confirming the question of Artin, Rudakov, Shafarevich and Shioda outside the generic case of Artin invariant ten. In odd characteristic, we reduce the question to Artin invariant nine and sweep out the K3 surface by Abel--Jacobi images of rational multisections of its Artin--Tate twists which vary along the supersingular twistor line.
Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight

We study the multiplicity of positive solutions of the following Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \begin{aligned} \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' +a(t)g(u)&=0,\quad t\in(0,T),\\ u'(0)=u'(T)&=0, \end{aligned} \] where $a$ is a two-step sign-changing weight with negative mean. We establish a multiplicity criterion for positive solutions, give a negative answer to the uniqueness question raised by Boscaggin, Feltrin and Zanolin, and prove the existence of infinitely many positive solutions for a fixed weight. The proofs are based on the shooting method and uniform asymptotic estimates.
Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope

Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $°g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope. We show that the Kozlov simplex $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$ is a lecture hall simplex and that every point of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ has a unique chained decomposition into points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$. Hence the lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ are exactly the sums of shifted lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$, the polytope has the integer decomposition property, every lattice point is a Hilbert function when $n\le 3$, and lattice-point counts and Ehrhart polynomials are products of transfer matrices of the kind used in Part II. We determine the codegree of every Kozlov polytope and show that none is Gorenstein for $n\ge 3$. Finally we compare discrete and continuous invariants: the number of Hilbert functions against the volume and the lattice-point count, where we prove Kupreyeva's observed limit for the fraction of lattice points that are $f$-vectors and extend it to every rank. We also compare the centroid and second moments of the Hilbert functions with those of the polytope.
Regularity transfer for the Ritz projection
Lars Diening; Julian Rolfes; Abner J. Salgado

Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex polytope in arbitrary dimension $n\geq 1$, and consider the Ritz projection on quasi-uniform triangulations of $Ω$. We prove a new pointwise estimate in terms of the sharp maximal function and use it to establish stability in weighted Lebesgue, Orlicz, and Lorentz spaces. We then introduce discrete higher-order smoothness spaces based on oscillations and a smooth companion construction, and prove discrete analogues of classical embedding and compactness results. Finally, we establish stability of the Ritz projection in these discrete spaces, together with localized estimates. These results provide a framework for transferring higher-order regularity through the Ritz projection. As part of our analysis, we also study approximation properties of the Scott-Zhang projection in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models
Emilio González-Zamora; Pierre Tandeo; Laurent Debreu; Said Ouala

Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation through time (BPTT), whose computational and memory costs grow with the length of the training window. This limits the duration and resolution of hybrid-model training, a major bottleneck for realistic geophysical applications. Approaches like truncated BPTT reduces memory use by discarding sensitivities across truncation boundaries, introducing gradient bias and neglecting long-range dependencies. We propose a class of gradient approximation methods that preserve the adjoint recurrence over the full trajectory while approximating only the pullback operators within it. Exact pullbacks are computed by automatic differentiation at sparse anchor states only. Between anchors, sensitivities propagate either through the identity (Zero-order) or through a reused, frozen pullback (Pullback Reuse). This approximation makes the parameter pullback constant within each chunk, allowing the gradient sum to factorize so that a single evaluation per chunk replaces one per time step. We evaluate both on three systems of increasing complexity, an incomplete Lorenz-63 model, a large-eddy closure for two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence, and bias correction in a multilayer quasi-geostrophic ocean model. Peak memory falls by up to an order of magnitude and runtime up to fourfold, with Pullback Reuse staying closest to the exact gradient direction. In all three cases, approximate gradients support hybrid-model training at comparable accuracy, showing that effective online learning does not require exact gradients.
Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras

We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra. We construct a nontrivial topological post-Hopf structure on $U_\hbar(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and determine its semiclassical limit. For the standard Lie bialgebra structure on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we classify all compatible post-Lie products up to isomorphism and show that the nontrivial class admits a quantization. Finally, we formulate the general quantization problem for post-Lie bialgebras.
Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
Roberta Raineri; Mengbin Ye; Lorenzo Zino

Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems. Then, we focus on the problem of controlling such a coevolutionary model. In particular, we present two distinct approaches: i) introducing a committed minority in the population, and ii) broadcasting information to some target individuals. For both of these methods, we discuss their implementation and provide theoretical guarantees on their performance. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods on different case studies, illustrating their implementation on simple academic examples, as well as exploring their performance in realistic scenarios using network structures inferred from real-world data. In summary, this chapter provides an overview of the mathematical approaches developed to model a population of individuals with coevolving actions and opinions, providing effective tools to study and, ultimately, control this complex socio-technical system.

We prove that a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with irreducible local holonomy which is $r$-th order recurrent, $\nabla^r R=t^{(r)}\otimes R$, is locally symmetric, for every $r\ge1$. Without any assumption on the holonomy, we show that such a manifold is either locally symmetric or, locally, a flat extension $Σ^2\times\mathbb R^{n-2}$ of a surface: the only possible exceptions to local symmetry are essentially two-dimensional.
Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition

Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.
Preconditioning for quadratic matrix optimization via constraint reshaping

We study quadratic optimization over orthogonality or symplectic constraints, a problem arising in eigenvalue computation, subspace analysis, and reduced-order modeling. Ill-conditioned problems have a wide positive Hessian spectrum at a minimizer, which slows first-order Riemannian methods. Existing preconditioned-metric approaches choose a Riemannian metric, which determines the resulting Hessian spectrum. We instead redesign the problem itself to find the narrowest possible spectrum. We reshape the constraints into equivalent formulations that preserve the optimal value and the solution set, giving a family of preconditioned problems parametrized by positive constraint weights. We derive a closed form for the positive Hessian spectrum in terms of these weights. Minimizing the condition number then reduces to a linear program (LP) in the logarithms of the weights. The LP attains a globally optimal design within the paired equal-block family, and its strong duality gives matching lower bounds on the condition number. On tested instances, the optimized formulation substantially reduces the local condition number, with returned spectra matching predictions on both orthogonal and symplectic instances. We also benchmark the design against Lagrangian and left-right preconditioned metrics. The method thus provides an exact, optimization-based alternative to heuristic preconditioned metrics.
Mahler measures and a cubic Dedekind zeta value in three dilogarithms

A general formula evaluates a three-variable Mahler measure at Heegner points of fundamental discriminant $-d$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod8$, using CM modular forms and ray class $L$-values. Together with the case $d=27$, it proves six identities conjectured by Zheng. The parameter at $d=163$ also occurs in a cubic Ramanujan-Sato series for $1/π$. For $C=\mathbb Q(a)$, where $a^3+2a-2=0$, an exact hyperbolic volume argument expresses the Dedekind zeta derivative $ζ_C'(-1)$ in three Bloch-Wigner dilogarithms. The analogous identity for $C(\sqrt5)$ remains conjectural and is reduced to one explicit Bloch-group equality.
Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Channel Prediction in Satellite-Mounted Metasurface Reflection Communication Networks
Aolin Sun; Ruihong Jiang; Jincong Mo; Yangbo Guo; Zhuangzhuang Cui

Satellite-mounted metasurfaces (MS) provide a low-power programmable paradigm for 6G satellite-terrestrial networks, effectively compensating for severe free-space path loss under stringent payload constraints. However, accurate channel prediction for such systems remains fundamentally challenging due to the coupling of dynamic orbital topology, stochastic user geometry, and hardware-imposed phase quantization. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework that embeds the physics of wireless communication, including monotonicity constraints and asymptotic decay properties, into a deep neural network for outage probability (OP)-aware channel prediction. We construct a realistic system model incorporating spherical user distribution, Spherical Poisson Point Process-based satellite constellation, and practical metasurface quantization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves over 0.99 prediction accuracy with physically consistent outage trends under varying geometric configurations, constellation densities, and quantization resolutions.
Twisted Verlinde formulas for cyclic orbifolds and the order-two simple current of a vertex operator superalgebra

Let $V=\Vev\oplus J$ be a simple vertex operator superalgebra with $\Vev$ simple, rational and $C_2$-cofinite, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic group acting faithfully on $\Vev$. For arbitrary twisted $V$-modules we prove: (1) for $G$ of arbitrary order, a twisted Verlinde formula for $\Vev$; (2) unitarity of the orbifold $S$-matrix block in generating sectors; (3) as a consequence, a formula for $N^{X_3}_{X_1,X_2}\pm N^{J\boxtimes X_3}_{X_1,X_2}$ as sums over $J$-orbits of $G$-stable untwisted modules, in which $J$-fixed points enter with weight two and in the minus sign, with a parity selection rule (read in $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$) and a dimension sum rule; (4) simplicity of $V^G$. These results concern the $G$-graded fusion category of $\Vev$ together with the order two invertible object $J$ with $θ_J=-\dim_qJ$. The statements are tested numerically on six examples (odd and even orders up to $15$, both signs of $\dim_qJ$, $J$-fixed modules).
Exponential generating functions of multiple polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices

We give an explicit formula expressing any finite product of depth-one polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices as a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of shuffle-type multivariable multiple polylogarithms. The proof starts with an exponential generating function. For any fixed positive multi-index $\mathbf{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$, the substitution $z_i\mapsto z_i\exp(x_1+\cdots+x_i)$ in the corresponding shuffle-type multiple polylogarithm yields the exponential generating function for the functions at indices $\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{k}$, where $\mathbf{k}$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^r$. We combine this identity with the shuffle product for iterated integrals at positive indices and compare coefficients to obtain the product formula. The appendix gives an alternative proof using the Euler differential operators $z_i\partial/\partial z_i$.
Double determinants of quaternion matrices in the P-generalized determinant framework with applications

Building on the P-generalized determinant over quaternions, we introduce the double determinant of arbitrary square quaternion matrices. We then apply the double determinant to obtain a determinant representation for the inverse of any invertible quaternion matrix, without the Hermitian restriction. Furthermore, we establish Cramer's rule for the unique solutions to the quaternion linear equations Ax=b and xA=b, as well as to the quaternion matrix equations AX=B, XA=B, and AXB=C. As an application, we use the determinant representation of the unique solution to AXB=C to design a color image encryption-decryption scheme. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the encryption algorithm effectively conceals the contour and color information of the original image, while the decryption algorithm restores the original image almost perfectly, thereby confirming the effectiveness and practical potential of the proposed scheme.
A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
In-Jee Jeong; Guolin Qin; Kwan Woo

We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.
Sharp minimax rates and adaptive estimation of latent proportions in bivariate Poisson mixtures

We study estimation of the mean latent composition in a bivariate Poisson mixture. Conditional on an unobserved intensity S and proportion U, two counts are independent Poisson variables with respective means SU and S(1-U). The mixing law is unrestricted on the Cartesian product [a,b] x [0,1], where a and b are finite constants satisfying 0 < a < b, and dependence between S and U is allowed. Although the mixing distribution is identifiable, the usual ratio of mean counts estimates an intensity-weighted proportion and may be biased for theta = E[U]. We construct polynomial estimators based on factorial moments and establish the exact leading exponent of the minimax squared-error risk on the logarithmic scale, without claiming an exact multiplicative minimax constant. We also derive the sharp logarithmic separation exponent for testing zero latent covariance and construct an adaptive estimator achieving parametric squared-error risk on the zero-covariance submodel while retaining the optimal full-model logarithmic minimax exponent. Simulations illustrate the bias-variance trade-off, the role of polynomial regularization, and the distinction between theoretically guaranteed and empirically calibrated adaptation.
Optimal Beurling-Hörmander-type uncertainty principles and nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces

We study how rapidly a nonzero function $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{f}$ can simultaneously decay. For each suitable weight function $ω$, we construct a convex weight function $\varpi$ and establish the existence of a threshold $Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)} \in (0, \infty)$, where $\varpi^*$ denotes the convex conjugate of $\varpi$. For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[ \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. Similar results are also established in higher dimensions. We characterize the weights $ω$ for which $\varpi$ is equivalent to $ω$ and use this to determine when the Beurling-Hörmander uncertainty principle is optimal. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.
An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven

Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973). Nevertheless, for more than sixty years this lower bound has not been substantially improved beyond an additive constant. For $k\geq 3$, i.e. girth at least $7$, the best general bound was $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)+2$, due to Bannai and Ito (1981). We show that for fixed girth $7$ and growing degree $d$ we have $n(d,3)\ge m(d,3)+(1-o(1))d/8$. Furthermore, for girth $11$ we have $n(d,5)\ge m(d,5)+Ω(d^{3/5})$. In particular, the excess $n(d,k)-m(d,k)$, for $k\in\{3,5\}$, tends to infinity with $d$ and is therefore generally unbounded, which answers a question of Bollobás from 1978. For the degree/diameter problem we obtain similar bounds. A graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $3$ or $5$ has at most $m(d,3)-Ω(\sqrt{d})$ or $m(d,5)-Ω(d^{3/10})$ vertices, respectively. This answers a question of Bermond and Bollobás from 1981: for every constant $c$ there are $d$ and $k$ such that every graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $k$ has at least $c$ fewer vertices than the Moore bound.
Stars and paths in oriented graphs
Xuanrui Hu; Hanyi Wang; Yuefang Sun; Bo Deng

Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Turán number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Turán number to oriented graphs. In this paper, we investigate the supersaturation results for the directed path $P_k~(k\geq 2)$ and all oriented stars $\overrightarrow{S}_{p,q}~(0\leq p\leq q$), and all oriented paths of order at most four.

Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$. We prove this conjecture.
On the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders and their apparent contours

We study the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders $S^1(r) \times \mathbb{R}^2$. We relate the contact type to the singularities of the corresponding parallel projections along the direction of the axes of the toroidal cylinders, the geometry of the apparent contours under these projections, and the geometry of the original surfaces.
Conditional propagation of chaos for systems of particles with polynomial interactions

We consider N interacting particles taking values in the real numbers and evolving in discrete time with time step 1/n. Each particle follows an individual dynamics, driven by its own noise, which depends on the total configuration via a polynomial interaction. Moreover, all particles receive the same collective perturbation. This perturbation is given by a multilinear homogeneous sum of order $ m \geq 2$ of independent centered random fields which are evaluated at the current positions of the particles. We show that, as N and n tend to infinity, the system converges to the solution of a conditional McKean-Vlasov equation which is driven by an additional Brownian motion which emerges in the limit from the collective perturbations. Moreover we give explicit bounds for the Wasserstein-2-distance. Our proof combines the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz (2010), the CLT for Wiener chaoses in the Wasserstein-2-form of Ledoux, Nourdin and Peccati (2015) and a conditional law of large numbers for weighted U-statistics proven in this paper.
The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface

We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.
High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves

We propose a class of high-order area-preserving Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the surface diffusion flow of curves, a curvature-driven geometric flow that decreases the perimeter while conserving the enclosed area. By coupling the parametric finite element approximation of the classical BGN formulation with symplectic RK time discretisation, we rigorously prove that the fully discrete scheme unconditionally conserves the enclosed area of curves. This conservation arises solely from the intrinsic symplectic structure of the RK methods, without introducing any additional constraints, auxiliary variables, or Lagrange multipliers to enforce structure preservation. To attain high temporal accuracy, we adopt $q$-stage Gauss RK methods, which are symplectic and yield order $2q$ (e.g., $q=1,2,3$). The resulting fully implicit, strongly nonlinear system is solved efficiently via an equivalent discrete formulation combined with a monolithic damped Newton iteration. Extensive numerical tests on various evolving curves validate the theoretical findings, confirming exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, while the Newton iteration count rapidly decreases to fewer than 8 per step, demonstrating the robustness of the tailored solver.
Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
Xuezhang Chen; Jiaxue Gan; Yalong Shi

For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.
Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces

We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.
A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries

A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.
Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond

Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.
Rational maps with at most three critical values have no Herman rings
Yuming Fu; Weiwei Su; Fei Yang
We prove that any rational map with at most three critical values has no Herman rings. This generalizes previous results of Shishikura and Milnor on bi-critical rational maps.
Two-Timescale Channel Estimation and Port Selection for Fluid Antenna Systems With Limited Port Observations
Xusheng Zhu; Kai-Kit Wong; Jiajian Wang; Songling Zhang; Shihao Fan

Port selection in fluid antenna systems (FAS) requires instantaneous channel state information, but a single radio-frequency chain can probe only a few ports in each coherence block. Existing FAS channel estimators, even with learned or generative priors, work within a single block and are limited by its few probes, which cannot resolve several propagation paths. To overcome this limitation, we propose a two-timescale channel estimation and port selection scheme that exploits the slow variation of the path angles. Specifically, a sequential Monte Carlo filter accumulates the angle posterior over blocks, while the fast-fading path gains are integrated out in closed form. Furthermore, a Fisher information analysis reveals that a single probe per block carries no angle information, whereas two or more spread-out probes accumulate it linearly over blocks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme approaches the selection with known angles after about twenty blocks and, with four probes per block, matches memoryless schemes with eight.
The Csisz{á}r order for ranking the importance of input random variables
Cristina Butucea; Jean-François Delmas; Anne Dutfoy; Antoine Schoonaert

Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$, defined as the $f$-divergence between the joint distribution of a general random couple $(X,Y)$ and the product of its marginal distributions, are widely used to quantify dependence between the input variable $X$ and the output variable $Y$. We show that the ranking of two input variables $X$ and $X'$ in terms of their importance w.r.t.\ the output variable, given by the comparison of the Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$ and $S\_f(X',Y)$ depends on the choice of $f$. We introduce the Csisz{á}r order of input variables as the uniform ordering of Csisz{á}r indices over all proper convex functions $f$. We give a sufficient condition to prove Csiszár order of two input multivariate random variables. We fully characterize it in two cases: when $(X,X',Y)$ is a Gaussian vector (in the one-dimensional case this amount to compare the square of their correlation); and when $X$, $X'$ and $Y$ are Bernoulli random variables. Finally, motivated by sensitivity analysis, we show that, when $(X,X',Y)$ is a three-dimensional Gaussian random vector, thresholding $X$, $X'$, and $Y$ either preserves the Csisz{á}r order or makes the input variables incomparable; in particular thresholding never reverses the ranking.
Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance

The toroidal distance naturally describes the geometry of codes over \(\mathbb Z_q\), where distances are measured modulo \(q\). In this paper, we study asymptotic bounds for codes in \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) under the toroidal metric. We first derive an explicit asymptotic lower bound from the classical Gilbert--Varshamov bounds for the Hamming and Lee metrics, which serves as a baseline for comparison. We then develop a saddle-point approach for the toroidal metric, which yields an asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov lower bound and an asymptotic Hamming-type upper bound. For \(3\mid q\), we embed ternary Hamming codes into \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) and obtain another asymptotic lower bound for the toroidal metric. In addition, we derive an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes. We compare these lower bounds with the baseline and prove that they are nontrivial in the corresponding parameter ranges. Finally, we compare the asymptotic bounds numerically.
Two Knuth orbits of order 256 without primitive semifield coordinatizations
I. F. Rúa; E. F. Combarro

We exhibit two Knuth orbits of semifield planes of order 256 in which every coordinatizing semifield is nonprimitive on both the left and the right. Each orbit consists of two isotopy classes. The first orbit contains 168 isomorphism classes of unital semifields and the second contains 32. We give binary multiplication matrices for a representative of each orbit and an exhaustive computation that verifies nonprimitivity and the counts directly from these matrices.
$p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps

We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.
Uniform Bounds of $F$-Signature and Effective Ideal Containments

We establish inequalities between numerical invariants and ideal containments in local rings containing a field. We prove the positivity of $F$-signature for klt-type algebras essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ under prime characteristic reduction and resolve the Uniform Symbolic Topology Problem effectively for both $F$-finite strongly $F$-regular rings of prime characteristic and klt type algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Consequently, letting $s(R)$ denote the $F$-signature and $d$ the Krull dimension, if $d\geq 2$ then $I^{\left(\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq \overline{I^{n}}$ and $I^{\left(d\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq I^n$ for every ideal $I \subseteq R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ in these settings.
Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope

Let $c(n,k)$ denote the coefficient of $r^{(n-1)^2-k}$ in the Ehrhart polynomial of the $n\times n$ Birkhoff polytope. For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that $c(n,k)/c(n,0)\sim n^{3k}/(2^k k!)$ as $n\to\infty$, confirming a conjecture of Stanley.
A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
Serena Dipierro; Giorgio Poggesi; Jack Thompson; Enrico Valdinoci

In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients. As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.
PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
Sunoy Sanyal; Canberk Demir; Metin Türkay; Erdal Aydın

Neural networks represent nonlinear process systems accurately, but embedding them in optimization is difficult because smooth activations introduce nonlinear, nonconvex constraints. PWLNet is a Python framework for building optimization-compatible neural surrogates through exact and piecewise-linear reformulations. It combines baseline and physics-informed training, optimization-aware pruning, and Pyomo embeddings based on ReLU mixed-integer linear models, exact tanh nonlinear models, PWL-tanh formulations, and binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP. PWL-native training uses the same activation in training and embedding, avoiding extra linearization error. It is evaluated on Boston housing, the Williams-Otto process, the Van de Vusse reactor, and a hydroformylation semi-batch reactor. On Boston housing, SOSX training gave the best common-architecture model (test MAE 1.984, R2 = 0.925). On Williams-Otto, pruning 15% of hidden neurons reduced MILP solution time 6.5-fold while preserving the selected operating point. For the Van de Vusse reactor, a physics-informed ReLU RNN pruned from 32 to 12 hidden units enabled tractable exact MILP embedding and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy, while terminal-aware shrinking-horizon prediction reached 99.7% of the direct-shooting reference. For the hydroformylation reactor, one-step exact-tanh IPOPT reached 99.2% of the certified reference product with peak pressure 20.002 bar (limit 20 bar) and 14.36 s total solve time over 280 moves; ReLU and PWL-native controllers achieved comparable recovery, with ReLU fastest. Longer horizons and physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results. Overall, compact linearized neural surrogates enable accurate, tractable optimization in steady-state and dynamic applications, with constraint fidelity identified as a key direction for improvement.
Feedback-Free FDD Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Sparse AP Activation and Dual-Mode Precoding

This correspondence enables practical frequency-division duplex (FDD) operation in cell-free massive MIMO via two mechanisms. Sparse access-point (AP) activation reduces downlink pilot overhead to enable coherent detection, while angle-reciprocity precoding steers beams using only uplink-estimated angles, eliminating channel feedback entirely. A load-adaptive dual-mode optimizer further enhances performance: closed-form signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio precoding for high-load rate boosting, or semidefinite relaxation for low-load power minimization. Simulations verify its superiority over existing feedback-free FDD solutions in spectral and energy efficiency, and its robustness to angle errors, reciprocity mismatch, and multipath.
Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics

We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.
Schubert Calculus in the Eye of the Storm
Neil J. Y. Fan; Peter L. Guo; Changzheng Li; Rui Xiong

We introduce new combinatorial objects, called storm diagrams, to study the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of complete flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/B$. We consider the quantum product of an arbitrary Schubert class with a modified Hirzebruch $λ_y$-class of a tautological subbundle. We show that its Schubert expansion coefficients are given by the total weights of storm diagrams. As applications, we establish Pieri rules for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of partial flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/P$. Our storm diagrams provide the first combinatorial model for a manifestly positive multiplication formula for partial flag varieties beyond the Chevalley case, with restrictions imposed on only one of the two Schubert classes.

The principles of rational parafermi algebra of Mersenne order $p=2^n-1$, developed in an earlier work, are recapitulated in the introduction: A Continued Kronecker Square-root process (CKS) dispenses with irrational numbers.The process creates two types of lower triangular square matrices, called of $G$-type and $J$-type, whose elements decompose Catalan numbers in particular ways. Trilinear relations, which have the lower-left matrix part interact with a suitably chosen block-diagonal part, are only semi-conservative in that $G$-type and $J$-type elements are preserved but appear in an operational context showing different direction of rotation. The second section begins with an examination of the immersion effect, a tendency of LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p')})$ (for $G$-like lower-left part at order $p'\hspace*{-0.8mm}:=2^{n+1}\hspace*{-0.5mm}-\hspace*{-0.5mm}1$) to adopt pecularities of LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$: a semiprime in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(15)})$ leads to a semiprime in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$; diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$ prompt diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(63)})$. After translating opposing directions of rotation to differently directed paths that emerge when the ordinal number of the second factor of a semiprime with first factor 3, 7 or 11 is varied, a rulebook is formulated which reveals that paths associated with LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$ are not only aimed differently; they occur five times as often as paths associated with LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$. The coincidence of the frequency ratio ${\cal G}^{(p)}/{\cal J}^{(p)}$ with the mass ratio of conventional matter over dark matter is commented upon at the close.
A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions

We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.
On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
Xiao-Min Li; Jun Wang; Hong-Xun Yi

In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

We investigate Euclidean self-orthogonality and the generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) property for coefficient-vector codes generated by a monic polynomial $g$ and its shifts $xg,\ldots,x^{k-1}g$, of length $n=r+k$ and dimension $k$, where $°g=r$ and $3\le k\le r$. We give a complete classification, over any algebraically closed field, of the generators for which these codes are both self-orthogonal and GRS. Such generators have either distinct roots in a geometric progression satisfying explicit order and scalar conditions, or a single repeated root in certain positive characteristics. In particular, only finitely many generators occur for fixed $r$, $k$, and characteristic. We determine their maximal self-orthogonal lengths, show that the corresponding maximal-length codes are cyclic or negacyclic, and obtain exact generator counts over finite fields, together with the least fields of definition. In contrast, when $3\le k<r$, we prove that every algebraically closed field supports infinitely many pairwise monomially inequivalent self-orthogonal non-GRS maximum distance separable (MDS) codes in this family. Consequently, arbitrarily many such codes can be realized over a common finite extension of any prescribed finite field, while remaining inequivalent and non-GRS over its algebraic closure.
Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
Kumpei Tsuji; Ciara Galvin; Hiroyuki Omura; Naoto Mitsume; Mitsuteru Asai

This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.
Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems

This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. Under sparsity and bounded-parameter assumptions, storage and per-step cost of CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$ both scale as $O(N_s)$, excluding preprocessing. Numerical results agree well with conventional TDBEM and semi-analytical reference solutions. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}$, the storage requirement for a sphere with $N_s=20,480$ is reduced from approximately 349.0 GB to 1.6 GB, with a speedup of approximately $45.4\times$. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$, simulations with up to $N_s=1,310,720$ are performed in the low-frequency, long-wavelength regime. A million-degree-of-freedom underwater-vehicle model is also analyzed. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework for large-scale 3D transient acoustic analysis using TDBEM.
Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations

We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

Quasi-orthogonality is one of the key ingredients for proofs of optimal convergence rates for adaptive mesh refinement methods (Carstensen, Feischl, Page, and Praetorius, arXiv:1312.1171). The work of Feischl (arXiv:2008.12198) proposed a relaxed quasi-orthogonality that follows directly from the inf-sup stability of the underlying problem discretization. The proof uses an intricate connection to the stability of $LU$-factorization of matrices. Recently, Gantumur (arXiv:2609.16265) presented a vastly simplified argument based solely on Hilbert space arguments. Building on this idea, we show that quasi-orthogonality is a purely geometric property of a set of points. This property is checked for a large class of Petrov-Galerkin methods for monotone, non-linear equations.
Material optimization of optical properties of particulate products by transition matrix method and sequential global programming
Nico Nees; Lukas Pflug; Michael Stingl

Material optimization of nanoparticle assemblies, such as structurally coloured photonic crystals, attracts increasing interest. We combine the transition matrix method (TMM), which avoids spatial discretization of particles and surrounding medium, with sequential global programming (SGP) to optimize optical properties of particulate products by iteratively assigning predefined catalogue materials to individual particles. We derive exact separable models, reproducing the fully coupled objective under single-particle material changes, and computationally accessible first-order correct approximations for general continuously differentiable objectives. These approximations aim to capture the nonlinear, potentially nonconvex dependence on individual material variables beyond their local first-order behaviour. Within SGP, globally minimizing the particle-wise subproblems can yield substantial improvements in few outer iterations, including steps away from unfavourable stationary points, as previously demonstrated for discrete dipole approximation-based SGP. The construction exploits the decomposition of the TMM system matrix into a material-dependent block-diagonal and a material-independent coupling matrix, while the state and adjoint problems remain fully coupled. Applications include extinction, scattering quantities, and colour objectives. In a 35-particle extinction minimization problem, the objective decreases by 31.0% in 13 iterations. A fine-grid evaluation of the fully coupled objective shows that no tested single-particle material change improves the final design. For a 627-particle photonic crystal, chroma increases by 58.4-122.1% for different particle diameters in 17-42 iterations. The optimized designs favour absorbing material in layers away from the incident light, consistent with experimental findings.
The Scott sobriety on countable Frechet-Urysohn dcpos and locally compact meet-continuous dcpos

In this paper, we focus on the Scott Sobriety of countable dcpos and locally compact dcpos. Recently, Chen, Kou and Yang proved that every countable dcpo with its Scott topology first-countable is sober endowed with the Scott topology. A natural question is whether a countable dcpo whose Scott topology is a Frechet-Urysohn sapce must be sober. We show that a countable dcpo with condition FG is Scott sober if its Scott topology is Frechet-Urysohn. Besides, a countable Scott non sober Frechet-Urysohn dcpo is constructed. He and Zhang gave two sufficient conditions for the open problem whether every locally compact dcpo is Scott sober. One of their sufficient conditions is that any locally compact meet-continuous coherent dcpo is Scott sober. We further prove that each locally compact meet-continuous dcpo is always sober with respect to the Scott topology.
Auslander bounds under recollements and arrow removal

Auslander bounds measure uniformity in the eventual vanishing of extension groups and are closely related to homological conjectures, including the Auslander-Reiten conjecture and finitistic dimension conjecture. We study global and finitistic Auslander bounds of finite-dimensional algebras under recollements and arrow removal. For a recollement induced by an idempotent $e$ of an algebra $Λ$, we establish inequalities comparing the bounds of $Λ$ with those of the quotient algebra $Λ/ΛeΛ$ and the corner algebra $eΛe$. We also establish comparison results for cleft extensions and deduce that arrow removal preserves finiteness of both the global and finitistic Auslander bounds. Finally, we construct radical-square-zero algebras with $\findim(Λ_n)=0$ and $\mr{fab}(Λ_n)=\mr{gb}(Λ_n)=n$ for every $n\geq1$, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between finitistic Auslander bounds and finitistic dimensions.
A very robust Ramsey theorem for hypergraph matchings

A fundamental result in Ramsey theory due to Alon, Frankl and Lovász gives an exact formula for the $q$-colour Ramsey numbers of matchings in $r$-uniform hypergraphs: if $n\ge\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})=(r-1)\|\mathbf{t}\|_\infty+1+\sum_{j=1}^q(t_j-1)$ then in any $q$-edge-colouring of $K^r_n$ there is some colour $j$ with a matching of size $t_j$. We show that a very weak quasirandomness assumption suffices for this Ramsey property: we can replace $K^r_n$ by any $r$-graph $H$ on at least $\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})+o(n)$ vertices that is a sublinear connector, meaning that it has no balanced $r$-partite holes of linear size. This generalises the result for $r=2$ (ordinary graphs) that we proved previously using a compression algorithm based on Gallai-Edmonds decompositions. This structure theory is unavailable in the hypergraph setting, so we combine two other proof methods, namely (a) simultaneous optimisation in all colours by clustering vertices using fractional cover weights from LP duality, and (b) local-to-global structure via random sampling and Kahn's matching theorem.
An A $\infty$ -algebra structure for enriched Morse complexes

We construct a homotopy coherent product structure extending the Chas-Sullivan product on chains of the free loop space of a manifold. Our construction uses the framework of Morse homology with DG coefficients and perturbed Morse gradient trees. We define an operad given by moduli spaces of Morse gradient trees with a twisted differential. This Morse tree operad receives a map from a suspended A$\infty$-operad and in turn acts on Morse homology with DG coefficients associated to a fibration over a manifold with a fibrewise monoidal structure.
Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity

For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $α$ satisfying the condition \[ \{g^{a_0}\cdotα(g)^{a_1}\cdotsα^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $ι(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.
Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
Can Atacan; Noah Aygün; Yong-Woo Lee

We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.
Higher-order magnetic hopfions in uniaxial chiral magnets
Vladyslav M. Kuchkin; Nikolai S. Kiselev

Chiral magnets host hopfions, but their experimentally observed configurations are largely limited to hopfion rings, heliknotons, and their clusters. Here, we show that uniaxial anisotropy stabilizes a diverse family of knotted and linked hopfions with zero and arbitrary positive Hopf indices. We identify their stability regions in the anisotropy -- field parameter space and introduce a systematic construction based on mapping skyrmion braids into three-dimensional magnetic textures. We find that the minimum energy of stable hopfions increases approximately linearly with the Hopf index.
A proof of the Lyons-Pemantle-Peres monotonicity conjecture for high offspring laws

We prove the Lyons-Pemantle-Peres conjecture for high enough offspring laws, that is we show that the speed satisfies $\ell'(λ) < 0 $ for the entire transient regime of the bias $λ\in (0, m)$ in the special case that the number of children $Z$ in the Galton-Watson tree satisfies $Z \geq 4$ almost surely.
Shrinking Limit for the Stationary Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation on Cross-Shaped Infinite Domains

We study the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a planar, cross-shaped infinite domain and in the shrinking limit. For any fixed thickness, we establish the existence of solutions through a variational approach. To overcome the loss of compactness inherent to the unbounded geometry and bypass the regularity obstructions caused by the re-entrant corners, we constrain the minimization problem to a cone of symmetric and monotonic functions. We then establish the resolvent-preservation property, ensuring the constrained minimizers are stationary solutions. As the transverse width vanishes, we establish a transverse collapse phenomenon, that is, the two-dimensional solutions flatten across the central junction and become purely one-dimensional along the infinite branches. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.
On the trajectories of the ID algorithm
Ivano Lodato; Simran Hiranandani; Aditya Varna Iyer

The ID algorithm decides whether an interventional distribution can be computed from observational data and, when it can, returns a formula in which products, ratios and summations of conditional probabilities are nested inside one another. We study these formulas by following the trajectories of the calls of the algorithm, each of which ends with a tail (an alternation of lines 7 and 2) and an exit, and we derive two main results. First, line~4 and the exit lines fix the single outer summation of the output, while the tail forms everything inside it, both the inner summations and the ratios. Second, a ratio keeps a summation in its denominator only when a repetition of the tail is entangled, and a test of ancestry in the original graph decides, before any formula is computed, whether a topological order can be chosen so as to avoid it. We also derive a bound on the nesting depth of the output, and show a simple ``dimensional'' count that every output has to satisfy. Ordering Is Not Deciding: Towards Preference-Consistent Multi-Objective Design--Decision Optimisation
E. Özer; A. R. M. Wolfert

In integrated design and group decision-making, Pareto filtering identifies non-dominated alternatives but does not determine which design best fits actors' preferences. Applying those preferences after filtering does not guarantee that the best-fit solution will be found: the filter may already have excluded the alternative with the highest aggregated preference, even when all combinations of fixed performance-improvement directions are considered. We compare Pareto--based selection with Integrative Maximisation of Aggregated Preferences (IMAP) on constructed multi-objective design--decision problems, using identical feasible solution spaces and actor preferences for both methods. The problems involve two system performances and up to four preference functions elicited from up to two actors. They cover independent and interdependent relationships between feasible performance values, monotonic and non-monotonic preference functions, and conflicting preferences for the same performance. In some cases, Pareto filtering excludes the best-fit solution, whereas IMAP identifies it. These counterexamples show that Pareto optimality does not guarantee a preference consistent decision, even in problems much simpler than real-world design and group decision-making problems. Pareto analysis can support ordering and exploration in performance space. IMAP instead models and aggregates actor preferences before optimisation and maximises the resulting aggregate preference over the full feasible and acceptable solution space.
X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework
Bjørn André Aaslund; Johannes Berge; Ayoub Haida; Ying Ni; Rita Pimentel

We propose X Hedging, an alternative to the Deep Hedging framework that addresses computational and explainability limitations of neural-network-based hedging strategies. Deep Hedging leverages neural networks to learn flexible hedging policies but relies on opaque models and typically requires large training datasets, which can complicate interpretation and limit its effectiveness in data-constrained settings. X Hedging takes a step toward addressing these limitations by replacing neural networks with tree ensemble methods, specifically LightGBM, to estimate hedging strategies. This design provides a computationally efficient alternative while preserving strong hedging performance and moving toward more user-centered explainability. To integrate LightGBM into a reinforcement-learning-style hedging framework, we introduce an optimization approach that sequentially trains tree-ensemble models while introducing stochasticity through random training orders. In controlled experiments, X Hedging achieves performance comparable to Deep Hedging while offering greater user-centered explainability, improved computational efficiency, and substantially higher robustness when training data are limited. The numerical results demonstrate that tree-ensemble methods provide an effective computational alternative to neural networks for data-driven dynamic hedging.
Full Rank and Stable Sampling of $\tanh$ Networks

We study the recovery of feedforward $\tanh$ networks of fixed architecture with $P$ parameters from finitely many point evaluations. First, we characterize the set of parameters where the differential of the realization map has full rank and show that it coincides with the regular parameters in the sense of Vla{č}i{ć} and B{ö}lcskei (2021). Second, we make use of this characterization to prove that almost every tuple of $2P+1$ sampling points yields uniform-norm Lipschitz stability on compact subsets of this parameter set. Third, we prove that for exact observations, projected gradient descent and projected Gauss--Newton converge locally from sufficiently close feasible initial guesses. The same evaluations also determine the realized function for arbitrary parameters and identify parameters in the characterized set up to permutations and sign changes of hidden neurons. Finally, we develop a general framework for real-analytic networks that highlights the role of full rank in stability and local reconstruction.
Inference in High-Dimensional Linear Mediation Models
Samriddha Lahiry; Rajarshi Mukherjee; Pragya Sur

Mediation analysis plays an important role in psychology, epidemiology, and genomics. Al- though high-dimensional mediation has been studied extensively, existing inferential methods typically rely on sparsity assumptions that may be difficult to justify when many individually weak mediators collectively produce a substantial effect. We study inference for both the over- all indirect effect and the effect transmitted through an individual mediator in a proportional high-dimensional regime, where the number of mediators and the sample size grow at compa- rable rates, without imposing sparsity on the mediator effects. Standard debiasing procedures for high-dimensional inference commonly rely on design-covariance information or additional structural assumptions on precision-matrix directions. In mediation models, however, the full outcome-design covariance depends on unknown mediator-model coefficients, creating an addi- tional challenge when such information or structure is unavailable. To address this challenge, we introduce an approximate debiasing procedure based on partial ridge regression and show that the resulting estimator is asymptotically bias-corrected and Gaussian. We also develop a cross-fitted estimator with a smaller asymptotic variance than its sample-split counterpart. In addition, we construct consistent estimators of the limiting variances of both the sample-split and cross-fitted estimators. Together, these results provide feasible inferential procedures for global and pathwise mediation effects.
A note on the learning coefficient of exceptional singularities

We compute the learning coefficient of a polynomial neural network at a point of its neurovariety all of whose real parameters are good, and show that it equals $d/2$, with multiplicity one, where $d$ is the difference between the dimension of the parameter space and the dimension of the group of symmetries of the architecture. This is the value attained at a generic point of the neurovariety; consequently, exceptional singularities are invisible to the pair $(λ,θ)$ whenever all real parameters in their fibre are good. By contrast, at a full parameter in the interior of the parameter domain whose differential has non-maximal rank we show that $λ<d/2$. The two statements together give a statistical reading of the geometric distinction between nodes and cusps.
Optimal Impure $(r,δ)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes with Explicit Minimum Localities

The minimum locality of a qLRC is the least $r$ such that it has $(r,δ)$-locality. We then construct impure qLRCs as CSS codes from nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes. In this way, we obtain four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure $(r,δ)$-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, and determine their minimum localities and the recovering sets attaining them for every admissible $δ$, except for a partial range of $δ$ in one family. In particular, two of the families contain GKT-optimal impure subfamilies of CSS codes CSS$(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})$ with $(r,δ)$-locality for some $r<n-δ+1$ at values of $δ$ for which $\mathcal{C}$ has no classical $(r',δ)$-locality for any $0<r'<n$, where $n$ is the length of $\mathcal{C}$.

Every planar graph admits exponentially many proper colorings for any assignment of lists of five allowed colors to its vertices.
