For every assignment of lists of size five to vertices of G, following this algorithm in all possible ways guarantees that at least $2^{|V(G)|/7}$ different proper colorings of G are produced (and at least one color choice is guaranteed to be available in each step). We also show that this result has the following consequence: for every planar graph G, there exists a set $R\subseteq V(G)$ of size at least 0.06|V(G)| such that G can be properly colored from any assignment of lists of size four to vertices in R and lists of size five to the rest of vertices of G. Moreover, these statements remain true even in stronger settings, such as for correspondence coloring.

We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerdà's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?
Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$

Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.
Taylor expansions for first-passage time distributions of Brownian motion with moving boundaries

We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-Itô chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.

We estimate the probability that a vector of U-statistics lies within $C/n$ of a target in the range of typical fluctuations. For sufficiently large $C$, we prove a lower bound of the typical Gaussian order under finite variance, and a matching upper bound for bounded kernels. We show that under finite variance alone, stronger concentration may occur, and find the best possible asymptotic upper bound. Our proof is algorithmic, estimating probabilities by counting successful modifications produced by a random algorithm. We apply this result to settle a question of Beniamini, Lavee and Linial (2025), who asked if there exist permutations with $k$-order sub-pattern counts at most $O(n^{k-1})$ away from one another for $k>4$. We prove not only existence, but enumerate these permutations up to a constant factor, showing that there are $Θ(n!n^{-(k-1)^2/2})$ such permutations of size $n$.

We study Wolff-type ideal problems in $H^\infty(\mathbb B)$, the algebra of bounded slice regular functions on the quaternionic unit ball. We construct $f,f_1,f_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|f|^2\le |f_1|^2+|f_2|^2$ such that $f^{\ast N}\notin\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ for every integer $N\ge1$, where $\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ denotes the right ideal generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$. We also construct intrinsic functions $a,a_1,a_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|a|\le |a_1|+|a_2|\le1$ and $a^{\ast2}\notin\mathcal I(a_1,a_2)$. For intrinsic data satisfying $|f|\le\sum_{\ell=1}^n|f_\ell|$, the cube $f^{\ast3}$ has a representation in the generated right ideal with intrinsic coefficients. For general data, we obtain sufficient conditions for ideal membership under a fourth-order pointwise bound with a Dini factor. If the generators preserve a common slice, a quadratic bound with a Dini factor suffices.

In this paper, we will argue that the notion of computational trust can be understood as a form of fallible intuitionistic knowledge grounded in verification. This approach naturally captures a key aspect of trust: it involves vulnerability. Specifically, it validates the principle that verification leads to trust but does not validate the opposite principle that trust leads to verification. Thus, we can trust on good grounds that some program will perform according to its specification but the program might still fail. We present a simple logic for capturing this notion of computational trust based on constructive modal propositional logic extended with a trust modality, which will be specified in an inferential fashion and by utilizing the proofs-as-programs correspondence.
The distribution of greatest common divisors of binomial coefficients and their upper indices

For positive integers $n,d$, let $A_d(n)$ denote the number of integers $0\le k\le n$ such that $\gcd\bigl(n,\binom nk\bigr)=d$, and put $S_d(x)=\sum_{n\le x}A_d(n)$. We prove that, for each fixed integer $d\ge2$, \[ S_d(x)\sim\frac{d-1}{d}\,\mathfrak c\,\frac{x}{\log x}\qquad(x\to\infty),\qquad \mathfrak c=1.526453\ldots \] The key step is to extend the coprimality result of Ford and Konyagin to arbitrary fixed parameters $d\ge2$ and $1\le j<d$, obtaining \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=1\Bigr\} \sim\mathfrak c\frac x{\log x}. \] The zero set of the corresponding Kummer carry function is a finite union of intervals of total measure $1/2$. We combine this property with estimates for small prime factors, Selberg trigonometric approximation, and exponential sum estimates over primes to count simultaneous carry conditions. We further prove that, for every fixed integer $e\ge1$, \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=e\Bigr\} \sim\frac{\mathfrak c}{e}\frac x{\log x}. \]

We extend the kernel-compensated eigensolver developed in our previous work from Hermitian to non-Hermitian nonlinear eigenproblems arising in dispersive photonic crystals. A mimetic finite-difference discretization preserves the discrete curl--divergence complex, and three-dimensional discrete Fourier transforms provide matrix-free realizations of the curl and divergence blocks. The isotropic inverse dielectric coefficient is stored through the material-edge indices, so its value and derivatives can be updated without assembling a Maxwell matrix. Kernel compensation is characterized by a fixed unitary block diagonalization, which remains exact for the nonlinear problem. At each outer step, a right Generalized Davidson iteration solves the non-Hermitian linearized eigenproblem. The exact derivative of a simple eigenvalue branch is expressed through its left and right eigenvectors. To avoid a second eigensolve, we replace the left eigenvector by the available normalized right eigenvector and obtain a right-Rayleigh quasi-Newton update. We prove that the exact left--right Newton iteration is locally quadratically convergent at simple roots, whereas the proposed iteration with exact inner eigenpairs has an explicit linear error factor and is at least quadratic when the derivative defect vanishes. A spectral regularity estimate bounds the gradient appearing in the derivative defect.
Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns

Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Plücker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.
Quantitative approximations for finite-state mean-field configuration models

We establish quantitative approximations for the empirical measures of finite-state mean-field particle systems in a general framework. The scales of the empirical drift and covariance distinguish the ODE and critical diffusion regimes and determine the corresponding time rescaling. In the ODE regime, we obtain quantitative central limit approximations in the $1$-Wasserstein distance and a Bernstein-type concentration inequality. The concentration bound has no dimensional prefactor. Its explicit time dependence also identifies growing intervals on which the ODE approximation remains accurate. In the critical regime, we prove a quantitative nonlinear diffusion approximation in the $1$-Wasserstein distance. We apply our quantitative approximation results to noisy voter systems, Moran models with mutations and selections, heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the $p$-spin Curie--Weiss model, and autocatalytic reactions with mutations.

Writing $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)=\sum_q m_q\,t^{q/d}$, we show that $m_q-m_{2d-q}=n(f)_{q-3}-n(f)_{q+d-3}$ for every integer $q$, where $n(f)_k$ is the Hilbert function of the Jacobian module $N(f)$. For a free curve with exponents $(d_1,d_2)$ we give a closed formula: $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)-t^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}^1_P(f)$ depends only on $(d,d_1)$. We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. abla h$. Under a natural transversality assumption we determine the minimal free resolution of the Milnor algebra of such a curve: it depends only on $d$, $\mathrm{deg}\, g$ and $\mathrm{deg}\, h$, and the module of Jacobian syzygies is generated by $
abla g	imes

An institution must complete a portfolio adjustment, but traders who prepare inventory for it can choose whether to participate. The curvature of equilibrium cost as a function of the posterior target mean determines the value of information. In the scalar model, information benefits every fixed participation roster. Optional supply can reverse this ranking at entry, at full participation, and in a smooth interior with lognormal activation costs. For centered scalar targets, information weakly lowers cost relative to no information, strictly when the posterior mean is nonzero with positive probability. Centered Gaussian precision gains are always beneficial. An exact symmetric finite-population equilibrium identifies how information resolution and individual strategic size interact near entry. A portfolio extension gives a matrix criterion for the fixed-roster ranking, which can fail under general cross-impact. Even with isotropic execution, shared activation allows equally accurate signals about target magnitude and composition to have opposite execution values under one unchanged prior. Intraday ETF price data is used to characterize target uncertainty and trading conditions without identifying activation or institutional costs.
A note on a recent result by Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar, or the counterexample which I missed

Recently Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar showed, among others, that the inverse of an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup on a Hilbert space need not to be an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup. In this note we show that with the ingredients of that paper, the example can be constructed more directly. Furthermore, the author reflects on the reason why he did not construct this a decade ago.
Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle

This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.
Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
Erqiang Tang; Zixin Wang; Wei Guo; Shenghui Song; Jun Zhang; Khaled B. Letaief

Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.
The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction

The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.
Global well-posedness for the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system
Liening Qiao; Juntao Sun; Jiahong Wu; Fuyi Xu

This paper establishes the global well-posedness and nonlinear stability of the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system $\mathbb T^2$, for smooth initial data close to the equilibrium with constant density and temperature, zero velocity and background magnetic field $\mathbf e_2=(0,1)$. Neither the density nor the magnetic field is damped or diffused in this system. Here, we impose no Diophantine condition on the background magnetic field, no symmetry on the data and no special geometry on the domain. Our proof rests on two intrinsic stabilizing mechanisms hidden in the structure of the system. First, the background magnetic field generates damped wave structures which provide dissipation for the $x_2$-derivatives of the density and of the magnetic field. Second, we introduce a new good unknown $Φ$, an effective total pressure gradient that combines the density, the temperature with the magnetic pressure. Although none of its constituents is dissipative by itself, we show that the coupling of $Φ$ with the divergence of the velocity and with the temperature produces dissipation for $Φ$ in all directions, together with an extra regularization of the divergence of the velocity. Combining these two mechanisms with new anisotropic commutator estimates and a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, we prove that the system admits a unique global solution in $H^N(\mathbb T^2)$ for every $N\geq5$, and obtain a uniform-in-time bound on the highest-order energy as well as explicit algebraic decay rates. Even in comparison with the known result for the simpler isentropic counterpart, where the highest-order energy was only shown to grow at most algebraically in time for data in $H^{N}$ with $N\geq10$, our result removes the possible growth and lowers the regularity requirement to $N\geq5$.
Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron

We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular. Its atoms are the $n!$ permutations, and its elements of rank one, which we call pseudo-atoms, are the edges of the permutohedron. Describing ordered set partitions by chains of subsets, the cuts, we show that the rank is modular whenever the meet is above $\bot$, while the join of two distant atoms can have large rank, so that the rank of the join is a metric on permutations. An element has a unique representation as a join of atoms only up to rank one; above it, irredundant representations have sizes ranging from two to the rank, and the redundancy of an element is its number of atoms minus two. The Möbius function is that of an Eulerian lattice, the Whitney numbers are the face numbers of the permutohedron, and the characteristic polynomial has the alternating coefficients of the geometric case, but only $\bot$ and $\top$ are left-modular, so the lattice is not supersolvable. We show that it is CL-shellable, we exhibit EL-labelings for $n\le5$, and we compare the independent sets of Raz arXiv:2307.05005 (v3, Jan. 2026) with irredundant families and with the matroid of the vertices of the permutohedron. Replacing ordered set partitions by partial flags of subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ gives a $q$-analogue, whose Möbius function is $(-1)^{\mathrm{rk}+1}q^κ$, with $κ$ the number of pairs of elements in a common block at $q=1$, and whose characteristic polynomial and Betti numbers are polynomials in $q$.
Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds
Gayana Jayasinghe; Manousos Maridakis; Hadrian Quan; Alex R. Taylor; Xinran Yu

We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). We use this to construct Witten deformed subcomplexes of SUSY Hilbert complexes that categorify Morse polynomials and equivariant index formulae for a large class of operators. This allows us to prove equivariant index theorems for spin-c Dirac operators with Hamiltonian actions, and Holomorphic Morse inequalities in the Kähler case, in particular proving a new type of equivariant Riemann-Roch (ERR) theorem on singular spaces. We also improve on stratified Morse-Bott inequalities in the de Rham case, and review other applications including for the Kervaire semi-characteristic and the equivariant signature. We compute local cohomology groups for the Dolbeault complexes at both smooth and singular non-isolated fixed point sets which categorify the ERR numbers. In an Appendix joint with Alex R. Taylor, we give a broad overview of the relevance of SUSY to index theory on manifolds with boundaries and singularities, mainly focusing on the new insights and results related to N=2 SUSY that the authors have uncovered recently.
A generic construction of complex codebooks from functions over Abelian groups
Ziling Heng; Chenkun Xie; Jiantao Hu; Xiaoyan Jing

Codebooks with small inner-product correlation play a central role in direct spread code division multiple access communications, space-time coding, compressed sensing, and related areas because they improve system performance. This paper presents a generic construction and a modified construction of complex codebooks from functions on finite Abelian groups. By choosing perfect nonlinear functions, we systematically obtain several families of optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks with respect to the Welch or Levenshtein bounds. These constructions recover a number of known optimal codebooks and also yield new codebooks with previously unreported parameters.
Fourier Bases from Optimal Eigenfunctions of Paley Graphs of Square Order
Bart De Bruyn; Sergey Goryainov; Yilin Xie; Weihao Yan; Ferdinando Zullo

Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.
Compactness of branched conformal immersions with free boundary
Rui Gao; Zijun Wang; Miaomiao Zhu

We prove bubble tree compactness for branched conformal immersions with free boundary under uniform Dirichlet and Willmore energy bounds, with images in a fixed compact subset of \R^K and possibly degenerating conformal structures. In particular, we prove that the convergence satisfies the Dirichlet energy identity and the no-neck property. For smooth Lagrangian immersions in Kähler surfaces, we characterize the natural free boundary conditions for stationarity of the area functional under exact infinitesimal variations on the domain. We then prove bubble tree compactness for Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian (HSL) immersions in a complete Kähler surface under the orthogonal free boundary condition and the zero normal trace boundary condition for the associated mean curvature $1$-form. Finally, as applications of the bubble tree convergence results, we obtain Willmore energy minimizers for short free boundary annuli under a Steklov constraint and concentration of free boundary disk minimizers near maxima of the support mean curvature under a small area constraint. We also derive a Willmore energy lower bound under a calibration constraint and an intrinsic Willmore energy decomposition for free boundary HSL sequences in Kähler-Einstein surfaces.
Noncompactifiable Kähler threefolds with positive Ricci curvature

We construct a complete Kähler threefold $(M,ω)$ with positive Ricci curvature and infinite-dimensional third rational homology. It admits no analytic compactification, answering Yau's compactification question negatively (see \cite{Yau1992}, Problem~71, p.~304). The metric is obtained by solving a complex Monge--Ampère equation on an affine threefold and lifting the solution to an infinite cyclic cover. Its Ricci form $ρ_ω$ satisfies $\int_Mρ_ω^3=\infty$, disproving the top Yang--Yau conjecture.
Real Principal-Minor Detectors: Normal Forms and Regular Parity Lifts

Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ on a finite index set, and let $t$ be the column of diagonal entries of $A$, viewed over $\mathbb{R}$. A real detector of $A$ is a real matrix whose principal minors equal the integer $0/1$ representatives of the corresponding principal minors of $A$. We prove that $A$ has a real detector if and only if it has one of the form $K+tt^T$, with $K$ skew-symmetric and $\{0,\pm1\}$-valued. These conditions are equivalent to the existence of a principally unimodular skew-symmetric signing of the bordered lift matrix of $A$, and to regularity of the parity lift of its delta-matroid. If the graph on the nonempty index set of $A$, with edges given by its nonzero off-diagonal entries, is connected, every real detector of $A$ is diagonally similar to a detector of this form. The proof uses cut-transposes to preserve the prescribed symmetric part up to diagonal similarity, then applies feasible singleton pivots to a minimal counterexample. For ribbon bouquets, the characterization proves Whistler's conjecture. For every $A$ with a real detector, the feasible-set generating polynomial is Hurwitz stable, and the polynomial counting feasible sets of sizes $2i-1$ or $2i$ by $i$ has only strictly negative real zeros and ultra-log-concave coefficients.
A Sharp Nodal Measure Bound for the Mixed Clamped--Navier Biharmonic Eigenvalue Problem in Dimensions $n\ge 2$

We estimate the interior nodal set of real eigenfunctions of $Δ^2u=λu$ on a bounded connected Euclidean domain. Each boundary component is either of class $C^\infty$ with clamped conditions or of class $C^{2,α}$ and subject to Navier conditions. We obtain $\mathcal H^{n-1}(\{u=0\}\capΩ)\le C_Ωλ^{1/4}$ for $n\ge2$. A spectral inequality on auxiliary clamped collars supplies fixed-scale interior mass. On clamped patches we localize the Carleman estimates of Liu, Tian and Yang. On Navier patches a single harmonic function with trace $u$ controls the two boundary data required for subdivision at every spatial scale. Summing an index linear in local doubling and frequency gives the stated bound. An annulus with one component of each type realizes its order of growth.
Safeguarded Learning-Assisted Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Methods

A learning-assisted framework for Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient (NCG) methods is developed in which lightweight online prediction is used to support, rather than replace, the classical optimization process. The proposed approach retains the standard two-term NCG structure and introduces two independent online extreme learning machine models. The first model predicts an NCG coefficient during restart recovery or when persistent stagnation is detected, whereas the second model is used only after a line-search failure in finite precision arithmetic to propose a bounded correction to the deterministic fallback step size. Neural predictions are accepted only when they satisfy deterministic numerical safeguards, including descent, scale, and out-of-distribution requirements; otherwise, the corresponding deterministic recovery or fallback mechanism is retained. Both learning models are updated online using quantities already generated along the optimization trajectory and therefore require no additional function or gradient evaluations for training. These learning frameworks are applied to six well-known classical NCG methods, producing corresponding low-storage learning-assisted variants with deterministic safeguards. Numerical experiments on 480 CUTEst test problems show improved robustness for all six variants at broadly comparable evaluation costs. A PDE-constrained conductivity-identification example further illustrates the potential of the proposed approach to reduce evaluation costs and computational time for problems with expensive function and gradient evaluations. These findings suggest that restricted online learning can improve the robustness and computational performance of classical NCG methods while preserving their low-storage structure and deterministic optimization safeguards, and is particularly promising when function or gradient evaluations are expensive.
Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\)

In this paper, we study the following Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\): \[ \sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N}|u(z)-u(z-e_j)|^2 -C_H(n,m)\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ} \frac{|u(z)|^2}{d_Σ(z)^2} \geq\overlineκ_{m,n}\|u\|_{\ell^{2^*}(\mathbb Z^N)}^2, \quad u\in C_c(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ), \] where \(n,m\geq1\), \(N=n+m\geq3\), \(Σ=\mathbb Z^n\times\{0\}\), \(2^*=2N/(N-2)\), \(e_j\) is the \(j\)-th coordinate vector, \(d_Σ(z):=\inf_{ζ\inΣ}|z-ζ|\), and \(C_H(n,m)\) is the best constant for the Hardy inequality on \(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ\). Using the supersolution method and multilinear interpolation, we first prove that the best constant \(\overlineκ_{m,n}\) is positive if and only if either \(1\leq m\leq8\) and \(n\geq1\), or \(m=9\) and \(n\geq14\). Then, we show that \[ \overlineκ_{m,n}=\overline S_N \quad\text{if }m=2\text{ or }(m,n)=(1,2), \] where \(\overline S_N\) is the best constant in the critical Sobolev inequality on \(D^{1,2}(\mathbb Z^N)\). Moreover, for \(m\neq2\) and \(N\geq4\), we prove \(0\leq\overlineκ_{m,n}<\overline S_N\). Finally, using the equality \(\overlineκ_{2,n}=\overline S_{n+2}\), we prove that \(\overlineκ_{2,n}\) is not attained, while for \((m,n)=(1,2)\), we establish nonattainment of \(\overlineκ_{1,2}\) by developing a duality argument based on a comparison of Green functions.
Displaceability of monotone Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$

We show that the generalized Polterovich submanifold $L_{0, 2}^P$ in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and the Chekanov-Oakley-Usher Lagrangian $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ in the quadric $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$ are displaceable. Since $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ are in the zero level set of the moment maps of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-actions on $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$, the main idea is to construct Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms mapping $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ to nonzero level sets of the moment maps.
Yi Zhou; Jiaheng Zhuang; Shuguo Zhang

A Hausdorff space $Y$ is called rigid if, for every positive integer $k$, every continuous open $k$-to-one map $p:X\to Y$ from a Hausdorff space $X$ admits a partition of $X$ into $k$ open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto $Y$. We show that the Sorgenfrey plane is not rigid, giving negative answers in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ to Velichko's questions on finite products of rigid spaces and on strongly zero-dimensional spaces. For ordinal spaces, we prove in $\mathsf{ZF}$ that every regular uncountable cardinal with the tree property is rigid. In $\mathsf{ZFC}$, we obtain a characterization for arbitrary limit ordinals: a limit ordinal $α$ is rigid if and only if every coherent family $\langle f_ξ:ξ<α\rangle$, where $f_ξ:ξ\to\{0,1\}$, admits a uniformization. As a consequence, a limit ordinal is rigid if and only if its cofinality is rigid. The characterization also implies that $ω_1$ is not rigid in $\mathsf{ZFC}$, answering a question of Velichko.
A weakly singular Volterra integral equation and the fractional Lyapunov asymptotic stability theorem

We study the weakly singular Volterra integral equation V(t) = A - (1/Gamma(alpha)) int_0^t (t-s)^{alpha-1} h(|V(s)|) ds, t >= 0, where alpha in (0,1), A > 0 and h is a class-K function. This equation arises as the scalar reduction of fractional-order Lyapunov inequalities through the fractional variation-of-constants formula. We prove that it admits a unique global solution V with 0 < V(t) <= A, that V is non-increasing, and that V(t) tends to 0 as t goes to infinity, under the pure class-K hypothesis on h. If, in addition, h is locally Holder continuous on (0,infinity) with exponent beta > 1 - alpha, then the rescaled function W(t) := V(t^{1/alpha}) is of class C^1 on [0,infinity) and satisfies W'(t) <= 0. We determine the optimal regularity of the solution, which is alpha-Holder continuous with the sharp expansion V(t) = A - h(A) t^alpha / Gamma(alpha+1) + o(t^alpha) at the origin, and its sharp decay rate h(V(t)) ~ A t^{-alpha} / Gamma(1-alpha) as t goes to infinity. In the power case h(x) ~ kappa x^p one has V(t) ~ (A/(kappa Gamma(1-alpha)))^{1/p} t^{-alpha/p}. As an application, we give a complete proof of the fractional-order Lyapunov asymptotic stability theorem of Li, Chen and Podlubny (Theorem 11, Automatica 45 (2009), 1965-1969) under the general class-K hypothesis, a case not covered by the linear, power-law and convex arguments available in the literature. This theorem plays for fractional-order stability theory the role of Lyapunov's classical theorem for ODEs, and its proof closes a gap that has been open since the theorem first appeared. We further show that the Caputo inequality C_0D_t^alpha V(t) <= -c V^p(t) with 0 < p < 1 implies Mittag-Leffler stability of V, yet neither entails nor precludes finite-time decay to zero, in contrast with the integer-order criterion V'(t) <= -c V^p(t), which entails finite-time decay to zero.

We prove that, given a projective minimal model and a projective family of good minimal models, the subset of the base parametrizing fibers isomorphic (or birationally equivalent) to the given minimal model is constructible in the Zariski topology. Together with recent boundedness results for polarized log Calabi--Yau fibrations, this constructibility theorem provides new finiteness results predicted by the relative Kawamata--Morrison--Totaro cone conjecture.
Oisín Flynn-Connolly; José M. Moreno-Fernández; Fernando Muro

We introduce the determinant Massey product, a secondary operation on the cohomology of commutative dg algebras which is reminiscent of the classical Massey product. We prove some of the elementary properties of this product, compute several examples, and relate them to classical and matric Massey products. When 2 is invertible, a determinant Massey product is a matric Massey product, but over $\mathbb F_2$, it is not. In this case, we produce a finite-dimensional cdga whose Harrison cohomology does not inject into its Hochschild cohomology, and a divided powers algebra which is formal as an associative dg algebra, but not as a commutative one, with an explicit determinant Massey product witnessing the failure. Over $\mathbb Q$, we use determinant Massey products to construct a simply-connected coformal space with Koszul cohomology ring and vanishing ordinary Massey products of all orders, which is not formal.
Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
Phan Thành Nam; Toan T. Nguyen

We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.
Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees
Fulong Ye; Bofeng Huo; Yuxiang Liu; Ligong Wang

A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. When $l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_t=l$, we abbreviate these graphs as $S(t\cdot l)$ and $C_{t\cdot l}$, respectively. Previous results determined $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(t\cdot l))$ for $t\ge4$ [Graphs Combin. 42 (2026) 80] and for $t=3$, in each case for sufficiently large $n$. For $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$, the corresponding extremal graphs are known for $t=2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The sets $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{t\cdot l})$ were also determined for sufficiently large $n$ [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114673]. In this paper, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t))$ for sufficiently large $n$ when the branch lengths are not all equal. Our result for $t\ge4$ also includes equal branch lengths. As applications, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t})$ for arbitrary cycle lengths and sufficiently large $n$. We also determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ for certain linear forests $F=\bigcup_{i=1}^tP_{l_i}$ and sufficiently large $n$. Finally, we apply our main theorems to obtain the known results on outerplanar graphs forbidding matchings or theta graphs for sufficiently large $n$.
A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions

Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.
On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
Jiacheng Bao; Zhiqiang Yu; Ying Zheng

Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction inequality for Rademacher random variables.
Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
Michael Goldman; Lukas Koch; Dario Trevisan

We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.
Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
Wencheng Yan; Binrui Xu; Yihao Shen; Zhiyuan Jiang; Sheng Zhou

Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. The results show improved service satisfaction at a throughput cost and improved remote-control performance when random contention is replaced by distributed urgency-based arbitration. We finally discuss the open challenges in intent specification, evidence, hardware execution, interoperability, and lifecycle cost, and outline a staged path toward deployment.
Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons

We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.
Sharp box-dimension bounds for fractional integrals under unequal Hölder and anti-Hölder exponents

Let $0<h\le H<1$ and $0<σ<1$. Graph box dimensions are studied for fractional integrals of functions satisfying an $h$-Holder upper bound on increments and an $H$-anti-H lder lower bound on oscillation on a nondegenerate subinterval. For the Riemann--Liouville integral, the following inequalities hold: \[ \begin{aligned} \max\{1,2-H-σH/h\} &\le\lbdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1])\\ &\le\ubdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1]) \le\max\{1,2-h-σ\}. \end{aligned} \] The lower bound is obtained by balancing the truncation error of a Marchaud inverse against the oscillation of the input. For each $(h,H)$, a single sparse tent construction attains it for all $σ\in(0,1)$. The same bounds and their optimality are established for Hadamard integrals on compact intervals bounded away from zero and for left- and right-sided Liouville--Weyl integrals under explicit weighted tail conditions. Zero-mean periodic Weyl integrals with conditionally convergent tails are treated separately. For Hadamard integrals the bounds are transferred by a bi-Lipschitz logarithmic change of variables. For Weyl integrals the transfer relies on invariance of graph box dimensions under continuous perturbations of bounded variation. Local hypotheses and point-dependent anti-Hölder constants are also treated. The exact linear dimension law is recovered for equal exponents, whereas unequal exponents allow a strictly greater loss of graph dimension.
Nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with singular viscosity
Guanghan Zhao; Jingyu Li; Xiaowen Li; Changchun Liu; Ming Mei

We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. Under a vanishing--stress condition, we first establish the existence and uniqueness, up to a shift, of a monotone profile with an algebraic right tail. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We note that the existing approach for treating scalar conservation law with singular viscosity can not be applied to Navier--Stokes equations. We propose some new technique: after introducing an effective velocity and using an anti--derivative method, we establish unusual interactive--energy--estimates and thereby the expected energy estimates for velocity by coupling the two perturbation equations; furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary functional to eliminate uncontrollable terms. The artful weighted--energy estimates play a crucial role for treating singularity.
Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces with general weights

In this paper, we introduce a new family of function spaces of generalized smoothness that encompasses the classical Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, their weighted counterparts, as well as Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We provide a characterization of these spaces via the $φ$-transform in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth, and establish the corresponding Sobolev embeddings. Furthermore, we obtain smooth atomic and molecular decompositions for these spaces. Our approach relies on several new maximal inequalities.
Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7

Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Diţă's family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.
Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four

Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions. The proof combines the nilpotent flag with the geometry of the geometric generic affine fibers and the projective image surface. Line fibers are treated by homogeneous quasi-translations. For nonlinear fibers, three successive invariants constrain the directions at infinity, reducing the nonplanar image to a developable surface or a smooth quadric. Boundary, ruling, and trace identities exclude both alternatives. We further prove that $X+H$ is one-stably tame in every degree and tame in four variables through degree five.
Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons

We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.
Collineations of the diamond lattice in a Hilbert space

Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on $\mathscr{H}$ which maps $\mathscr{M}$ onto $\mathscr{N}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ onto $\mathscr{M}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.
Subfactor symmetries of real Hadamard matrices

Every Hadamard matrix gives rise to a {\it spin model commuting square} and a hyperfinite subfactor with finite Jones index. The standard invariant of this subfactor is comprised of quantum symmetries of the subfactor which can be viewed as ``non-invertible'' symmetries of the Hadamard matrix. We show that if the Hadamard matrix is real and has order greater than four and congruent to four modulo eight, the standard invariant is minimal, i.e. it consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Consequently, both principal graphs of the subfactor are $A_\infty$. In particular, this holds for every Paley type II Hadamard matrix. The proof uses a congruence for products of four rows and Jones's annular decomposition. More generally, we show that if an irreducible subfactor of finite index greater than four has bounded annular multiplicities along an infinite subsequence of degrees, then its principal graph is $A_\infty$.
Finitely supported mapping classes on infinite-type surfaces

We study the topological closure of the group of mapping classes group with finite-type support on an infinite-type surface. Since every such mapping class fixes each end which is not a puncture, we have that the closure is contained in the pointwise stabilizer of infinite-type ends. A natural question is therefore when this inclusion is an equality, and if it is not, what must be added to obtain the full stabilizer. We prove that finitely supported mapping classes are dense in the stabilizer precisely when there is at most one end accumulated by genus and at most one end accumulated by punctures. We show that if we remove either of these conditions, we need to add puncture and/or handle shifts to topologically generate the stabilizer.
Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of smooth solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}$
Zipeng Chen; Song Liu; Zhaoyang Yin

We study the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb T^d$ with $d\ge2$. For every $2<q\le\infty$ and every smooth mean-zero background solution $U$, we construct two distinct mild solutions with the same initial datum arbitrarily close to $U(0)$ in $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$, both belonging to $C([0,T];\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)) \cap C^\infty((0,T]\times\mathbb T^d)$. The time $T>0$ depends on the background solution but is independent of the prescribed tolerance for the initial data. This gives non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small initial data and density of non-unique initial data in the mean-zero divergence-free subspace of $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $2<q<\infty$. We also prove uniqueness in the same solution class for $1\le q\le2$, establishing the sharp threshold $q=2$ in this Besov scale. The uniqueness result extends to $\dot B^{-1+d/p}_{p,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $1\le p<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, under the same continuity and smoothness assumptions.
Operator generated topologies and the Krein property

Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.
Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations

This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincaré-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.
Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity

We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.
Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary of $C^{1, η}$ open sets
Soobin Cho; Panki Kim; Renming Song; Zoran Vondraček

We study the boundary behavior of nonnegative harmonic functions for a class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes in $C^{1,η}$ open sets $D\subset\mathbb R^d$. The jump kernels are allowed to blow up at the boundary of $D$ and the processes may have a critical killing potential. We identify the exact boundary decay exponent $p$, characterized by the coefficient of the critical killing potential. We establish a boundary Harnack principle which yields the comparability of $f(x)/δ_D(x)^p$ for nonnegative harmonic functions that vanish continuously on a portion of the boundary. The key ingredient of the proof combines estimates of the exact decay rate for the survival probability of the killed process with a modified box method and uses a regularized distance function to handle the limited boundary regularity.
k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
Zihao Geng; Ji-Ming Guo; Jongyook Park

The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.
Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
Nguyen Thu Hang; Truong Thi Hien; Thanh Vu

Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.
Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
Anlin Liu; Guowei Yan; Zhaojun Wang

This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space. We estimate the pricing errors in three steps: regress returns on the observed factors, extract latent factors from the lagged covariance structure of the regression residuals, and regress returns on both observed and estimated latent factors. The intercept from the final regression serves as the estimated pricing error. We construct Sum and Max tests based on the estimated pricing errors to detect diffuse and concentrated alternatives, respectively, and combine them using a Cauchy procedure. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the joint null distribution of the component statistics, their asymptotic independence, and their power against alternative hypotheses. We also propose a residual bootstrap and establish its first-order validity. Simulation studies examine the finite-sample performance of the tests under different pricing-error patterns and factor-number choices. An application to S\&P 500 stocks illustrates the use of the proposed framework in evaluating an observed-factor pricing model after latent-factor adjustment.
A new second-moment method for spectral measures of inhomogeneous non-Hermitian random matrices

We develop a second-moment method for the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of non-Hermitian random matrices $X_N=(\sqrt{s_{ij}}ξ_{ij})$ with a deterministic variance profile $S_N=(s_{ij})$. When the entries are independent and centered, the second moment of $\det(zI-X_N)$ is the permanent $\mathrm{per}(S_N+|z|^2I)$ of a diagonal shift of $S_N$, and the method approximates $\log|\det(zI-X_N)|$ by half its logarithm. For i.i.d. centered $ξ_{ij}$ of unit variance satisfying a Dini-type condition on their Lévy concentration function, we prove the circular law for every doubly stochastic profile whose largest entry tends to zero, however slowly. This condition holds for every law with a bounded density on $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We also allow the two entries $X_{ij}$ and $X_{ji}$ of each reciprocal pair to be correlated, with a nondegenerate joint law that has a finite mixed fourth moment. If the pairs and the diagonal entries also have bounded densities on their real linear supports, we prove an elliptic law for every symmetric doubly stochastic profile whose largest entry tends to zero. For i.i.d. $ξ_{ij}$ as above and general profiles with vanishing largest entry and bounded average row sum, we show that the ESD is asymptotically close to the Brown measure of the matrix $(\sqrt{s_{ij}}c_{ij})$ of free circular elements. The ESD converges weakly in probability if and only if $N^{-1}\log\mathrm{per}(S_N+qI)$ converges for every $q>0$, and these limits determine the radial distribution of the limit. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for convergence in terms of tree weights, characterize the radial laws that arise from profiles with uniformly bounded row and column sums, and show that the empirical distribution of the zeros of $\mathrm{per}(zI-X_N)$ is asymptotically close to the ESD.
Distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
Zihao Geng; Qian-Qian Chen; Ji-Ming Guo

The gem is obtained by joining a vertex to every vertex of a path on four vertices. A distance-hereditary split graph is a split graph containing no induced gem. In this paper, we characterize all connected distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1 and determine the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 1. Our result extends previous results on threshold graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1.

States with identical protected observations can admit different future interventions. Each transition specifies its successor, response increment, required initial reserve and net consumption. Composing these records in execution order distinguishes protocols with equal net consumption and different initial reserve requirements. At a fixed state, a weighted Gram operator determines the linear response ellipsoid and a quotient identifies directions attainable only through cooperation between blocks. Nonlinear systems with identical complete affine data can have incomparable finite-budget response sets. In regular charts, the first correction to quadratic minimum cost is a covariant cubic form involving the third derivative of cost and the Hessians of protection and response. At singular gates, sequential feasibility depends on the peak reserve along the path. A history-weighted operator detects responses outside the old channel's range closure. Controlled congruence characterizes exact reductions of deterministic labelled dynamics, and a two-cut value identity separates the effect of paid verification from that of subsequent action selection. On Qwen2.5-7B Base, two projected policies preserved 2,048 reference top tokens under a per-position KL ceiling of $2\times10^{-5}$. Over 200 arrivals they recovered 391 of 396 initial rejections. Each yielded over 1,200 times the held-out cross-entropy reduction of historical-channel-only AdamW. Under an expanded 2,560-position contract, fixed continuation and neutral renewal began on the same protected logit fiber in distinct structural strata. Both admitted all 200 subsequent writes. Fixed continuation yielded 1.74 times the held-out loss reduction per unit squared write cost. Renewal had a smaller KL excess on the first candidate tested at every arrival and used fewer full verification scans.
Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold

We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \] The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.
Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
Mengxiao Gao; Elly K. H. Hung; Yuchen Wu; Yi Yu

Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks. Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under $(α,β)$-differential privacy for $d$-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally $γ$-Hölder-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size $n$. The proposed estimator satisfies $(α,β)$-differential privacy, and achieves expected density-weighted squared error $\mbox{polylog}(n) \max(n^{-2γ/(d+2γ+2)},\,(nα)^{-2γ/(d+γ+1)})$. We also establish a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, thereby characterizing the privacy-accuracy trade-off for score estimation. As an application, we construct a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps. We show that, with an appropriate discretization scheme, the resulting diffusion model attains nearly minimax optimal expected total variation error among all private distribution estimators. We validate our theoretical findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group

The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.
Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
Saber Omidi; Momotaz Begum; Marek Petrik; Se Young Yoon

We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. This paper shows that stationary reach-avoid policies may be suboptimal and non-stationary policies may outperform them in reach probability by a margin arbitrarily close to one. To compute optimal non-stationary policies, we reduce the reach-avoid problem to a constrained average-reward Markov decision problem and propose an algorithm to compute lottery-based policies from a standard linear program formulation. We prove that the lottery-based policies are optimal and show that they are simple to compute, analyze, interpret, and implement. The numerical experiments confirm that the lottery-based policies can outperform state-of-the-art stationary policies even in complex domains.
Ryutaro Misawa; Masanori Sawa; Filip Špiranec

For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.
When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?

Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.
Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator

We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average. The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

For a perfect matching $M$ on $[2n]$, let $P_M$ be the interval order on its edges and let $\operatorname{Open}(M)$ be the set of smaller endpoints of its edges. For an opening set $O$ that occurs for some matching, put $S_O=\sum_{\operatorname{Open}(M)=O}X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_M)}$ and $H_O=ωS_O$. We give explicit Schur and power-sum expansions of $H_O$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and prove that $H_O$ is $h$-positive (equivalently, $S_O$ is $e$-positive). The Schur coefficients count standard tableaux of staggered skew shapes with prescribed entries in the left cells of distinguished dominoes. The Schur expansion follows from a Jacobi--Trudi sign-reversing involution on arrays with prescribed opener positions. For every partition $μ$ of $n$, a coefficient-transfer formula expresses $[h_μ]H_O$ as a positive scalar multiple of an elementary coefficient of the chromatic symmetric function of a clique blow-up of a path. This graph is a unit interval graph, so Hikita's theorem gives nonnegativity. The power-sum coefficients admit a cycle-type autocorrelation formula in terms of the restricted permutations from the Ferrers threshold model and an interpretation by alternating permutations with prescribed valley values and record partitions; we also obtain explicit threshold formulas. Further results include descent-set refinements, formulas for selected $h$-coefficients, and a rim-hook cancellation for the coefficient of $h_n$. These results refine the global matching identity of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.
Stein degree on birational log Calabi-Yau fibrations

We prove uniform bounds for the Stein degrees of boundary divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations of Fano type over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero. The main ingredient is the birational case for which we provide two approaches.
A Note on Spherical Images of Convex Hypersurfaces

A theorem of Wu states that the closure of the image of the Gauss map of an open convex hypersurface is geodesically convex, although the image itself may not be. We show that the general version of this theorem follows from a short proof for smooth hypersurfaces due to do Carmo and Lawson. We also show that all closed, geodesically convex subsets of spheres are attained as spherical images of convex hypersurfaces and give examples of convex surfaces whose spherical images cannot be attained as spherical images of smooth surfaces.
Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
Zijuan Gao; Qing Guo; Chengxiang Zhang

We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $β<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument.
