This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.
Andrzej Derdzinski; Sinhwi Kim; JeongHyeong Park

We call a Riemannian metric on a four-manifold, as well as the underlying conformal structure, conformally even/odd if its self-dual and anti-self- dual Weyl tensors acting on bivectors have, at each point, equal/opposite spectra. The term mixed parity refers to the simultaneous occurrence of both of these conditions, an obvious example being the conformally flat case. After listing various known classes of conformally even metrics, we construct examples of conformally odd ones which are not of mixed parity, as well as some metrics of mixed parity that are not conformally flat. The former examples are provided by left-invariant metrics on Lie groups, and realize uncountably many local conformal-equivalence types. The latter also include some arising from Lie groups, as well as certain 1+3 Riemannian products that are not locally conformally homogeneous.
Convex splitting by binary quantum hypothesis testing

How many independent quantum systems does it take to hide one system that is correlated with a reference? An observer can measure all the systems together with the reference to detect the correlation. We turn any such measurement into binary tests on a single system and the reference. For each test we bound the probability of declaring a signal when an independent pair was prepared. Averaging the largest signal acceptance probabilities allowed by these bounds controls the normalized trace distance in the convex-split lemma. A second bound gives a sufficient number of systems by minimizing the hypothesis-testing relative entropy over the state of the reference. Both bounds hold for density operators on separable Hilbert spaces. Comparing two distributions for the location of the hidden system gives one-shot bounds for private communication and one-way secret key distillation, including the public information available to an eavesdropper. For a fixed finite-alphabet model with separable quantum outputs and positive information advantage and variances, we recover the known Gaussian corrections to the attainable number of private or key bits from $n$ independent repetitions and bound the remaining loss by $\log_2 n+O(1)$ at fixed errors. The position-based key distillation protocol attains this bound with $O(n)$ public bits.
Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers II

For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. We show that a positive proportion of integers $n\leq x$ satisfy\begin{align*} P^+(n-1)<P^+(n)>P^+(n+1)<P^+(n+2)>P^+(n+3). \end{align*} The proof employs Selberg's upper-bound sieve and the multidimensional Selberg sieve developed in the Polymath8b work.
Invariance of Property (T) for Étale Groupoids
Xiangqi Qiang; Rui Liu; Chengjun Hou

We study topological Property (T) for locally compact Hausdorff étale groupoids under pullbacks, amplifications, and Morita equivalencen. We show that Kazhdan pairs for the regular representation family pull back along Haar system-preserving homomorphisms, and for general representation families we identify a constant-vector compatibility condition as the additional hypothesis needed. We also show that Property (T) for the regular representation family passes from a groupoid to its transformation groupoid with the same Kazhdan constant; under a natural restriction condition on representation families, the same holds for general families. Finally, we prove that Property (T) is invariant under ampliation for ample groupoids with compact unit spaces, both for all representations and for the regular representation family. Hence topological Property (T) is Morita invariant for ample Hausdorff étale groupoids with compact unit spaces, and likewise for the regular representation family.
Characterizations and Algebraic, Perturbation, and Topological Properties of $θ(H)$

Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $θ(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $θ(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $θ(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $θ(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.
Twisted enveloping algebras for permutation orbifolds

We formulate a topological formal calculus for continuous distributions with values in linearly topologized spaces. We apply it here to construct permutation-twisted fields directly from products and branch specializations. For a vertex operator algebra $V$, the key structural observation is that modes of tensors with at most one non-vacuum factor topologically generate the permutation-twisted enveloping algebra. Combining this observation with the calculus and $Δ_N$, we obtain an explicit isomorphism $\mathscr{U}_σ(V^{\otimes N})\cong\mathscr{U}(V)$ for an $N$-cycle $σ$, with grading and canonical filtrations rescaled by $N$. For arbitrary permutations, the cycle factors are rescaled before taking their degreewise completed tensor product.
Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing

We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size $d$ is to be identified among $N$ items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling $T=Θ(d\log N)$ for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime $d=Ω(\log^2 N)$. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with $T\le (1/\ln 2+\varepsilon)d\log N$ tests for any $\varepsilon>0$, in the admissible regime $N=q^k$ for some prime power $q = Θ(d)$ and integer $k \ge 2$. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap remains except in the sparse regime $d = N^{o(1)}$.
On the Type E case of the Brown Wemyss realization conjecture

We consider the remaining Type E case of the Brown-Wemyss numerical realization conjecture. The noncommutative splitting lemma and the Type A and D classifications of Brown and Wemyss leave two-generator cyclic potentials with cubic part $x^3$. For these remaining potentials, we construct geometric realizations under the hypothesis of radical growth dimension at most one. The construction combines marked ADE deformations and cyclic coordinate changes for lengths three, four, and six with a filtered finiteness argument in length five. Under the numerical growth hypothesis, cubic lower bounds exclude the other branches for every choice of formal tail. The resulting contractions have a regular source and a complete local cDV target. Finite-dimensional algebras are realized by threefold flops, and the sole growth-one algebra in this residual case is $\operatorname{Jac}(x^3+xy^3)$, for which we give a divisor-to-curve contraction.
DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
Jingyuan Li; Dawei Shi; Ling Shi

Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.
Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
Yin Liu; Shanshan Zhao; Didong Li

Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.
Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback

Analyses of error feedback bound the memory buffer through a compressor contraction constant -- $r/p$ for the best rank-$r$ approximation of a $p$-dimensional spectrum -- which survives into the rate. We show it need not appear at all. When the compressed momentum is re-injected into the pre-compression accumulator, the previous compressed momentum $β_1 M_{t-1}$ is an admissible competitor in the projection, and the buffer obeys $\|E_t\|_F \le (1-β_1)\|G_t\|_F + γ\|E_{t-1}\|_F$, free of the dimensions $m,n$ and of the rank $r$. The argument uses only that the compressor is a metric projection onto a closed cone, so it covers top-$k$ selection as well as truncated SVD, holds for every selection from the projection set with no condition on singular-value crossings, and in its trajectory-tracking form assumes nothing about the gradients. In the two-stage template of the standard analyses it replaces a Stage-2 constant of order $p^2/r^2$ by one of order $1$, against $Θ(p/r)$ for the sharpest contraction-based bounds. Transferring the full rate costs a leakage term, which we bound by the step-weighted gradient mass $\sum_{u\le t}η_u\|G_u\|_F$ and show tight up to a factor $\sqrt{2}$; the price is an additive $O(\log^2 T)$ floor, not a slower rate. On BERT fine-tuning at rank ratio $32/768$ the feedback decay costs under $0.008$ validation $F_1$.
A Faà di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products

We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.
Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories

We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.
Note on the random triadic process II

For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process. Korándi et al. proved a sharp threshold probability ${p}= \frac 12n^{ - \frac 12}$ for the propagation of the random triadic process.Tian and Yang complemented those results by considering the final size of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when ${p}=o( n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ α(3-r)} n)$ for any fixed constant $α> \frac 12$.In this note, we further consider the sharp threshold probability $\tilde{p}_r$ for the propagation of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when $r\geqslant 4$. We prove that $\frac 12 n^{- \frac 12}<\tilde{p}_r\leqslant c\, n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ \frac 12} n$ for some positive constant $c$, and conjecture that $\tilde{p}_r= c_r\, n^{ - \frac 12}$, where $c_r= \frac 12(r-2)!^{ \frac{1}{2r-4}}\bigl( \frac{2r-5}{r-2}\bigr)^{ \frac{2r-5}{2r-4}}$.
An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems
Xingwei Hu; Yaozhong Hu; Aiguo Xiao

A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.
Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk

Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.
A decoupled structure-preserving scheme for pressure-driven multispecies tumor growth

We propose an Onsager-based scheme for an $m$-species pressure-driven reaction--cross-diffusion system with a common homeostatic pressure. The scheme uses a modified scalar energy structure to update the total density, followed by compatible updates of the individual species. The global nonlinear problem remains scalar, and the species densities sum exactly to the updated total density. We establish unique solvability and show that the scheme preserves species nonnegativity, the pressure bound and total-mass monotonicity and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law without a time-step restriction. We further develop a predictor--corrector extension to improve temporal accuracy while retaining these structural properties. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the proposed schemes and demonstrate their computational efficiency.
A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line

We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.
Covering Location Optimization at GPU Speed

Large-scale covering location optimization often involves NP-hard combinatorial problems that pose substantial computational challenges in urban facility planning. This paper proposes a GPU-accelerated parallel search framework for the maximal covering location problem, combining device-resident multi-trajectory exploration with lightweight CPU-side coordination. Exploiting the structure of one-swap moves, exact incremental gains are evaluated through sparse coverage representations and tiled CUDA kernels. A hierarchical reduction identifies the best exchange without materializing the full swap-gain matrix, while GPU-resident destroy-and-repair and elite-guided restarts balance intensification and diversification. Computational experiments on nine real-world urban configurations demonstrate consistent improvements over GRASP, achieving a mean relative gap of 0.029\% against published best-known solutions (BKS) and reaching BKS in 50 of 90 independent runs. On the largest urban benchmark, Kings, with 7,730 candidate locations and a budget of 50 facilities, the proposed method reaches BKS in all ten runs using a consumer-grade NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti GPU, requiring only 45.2 seconds on average to obtain its final incumbent, compared with 99.5 seconds reported for AILS-PR in a high-performance computing cluster environment. The source code and benchmark reproduction scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/Yuntian-Zhang/GPU4CO
Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models

Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. A first-order term, present because regularized solutions are not stationary for the task loss, is not reduced in the same way. Experiments on an exact non-quadratic model confirm the budget and the ceiling, show the first-order term dominating for strong penalties, and find the curvature-guided penalty slightly better than an isotropic one. In a three-seed transformer study the functional is rank-correlated with merging degradation, but no more strongly than the Euclidean displacement norm.
Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy

Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; formality of the $d$-fold cyclic cover rules out such blocks at the $d$-th roots of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime; this is a formality property of cochains, as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. The complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, is Alexander formal exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1. We also show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Hence the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$, but not conversely. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows; the two conditions are incomparable, and all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.
Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules

We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.
Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools

This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

We prove convexity in the affine orbit of entropies associated to Gauss curvature flow for sub-affine powers. This allows the construction of an affine boosted Gauss curvature flow, which keeps the evolving hypersurface at the affine minimizer of the Gaussian entropy. The modified flow has bounded isoperimetric ratio, and after rescaling it converges along a sequence of times to self-similar solutions of the Gauss curvature flow. The construction also proves existence of new self-similar solutions to Gauss curvature flow in the sub-affine regime.
A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity

Equilibrium-based conic formulations of elastoplasticity and limit analysis provide statically admissible stress fields but generate large Newton systems whose sparse factorization limits three-dimensional computations. This work develops and analyzes a macro-element condensation tailored to the Newton systems arising from primal--dual interior-point methods. Exploiting four-tetrahedron macro-elements, the method eliminates stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers, yielding reduced systems that can be solved using positive-definite factorizations, with estimated reductions of approximately \(4\times\) in dimension and structural nonzeros relative to stress-only elimination. The validity of this elimination is established through global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions. Local nonsingularity is independent of the yield criterion in elastoplasticity, whereas in limit analysis it holds directly for Rankine and is ensured for von Mises through trace-bound augmentation. Numerical results show that, relative to stress-only elimination, the proposed condensation achieves CPU speedups of up to approximately \(2\times\) and reduces peak linear-solver memory by up to \(66.5\%\). We further develop a CUDA Fortran implementation that exploits uniform macro-local blocks through batched routines and uses cuDSS for the reduced sparse solve. This implementation achieves speedups of up to \(13.5\times\) over its CPU counterpart and up to \(87.5\times\) over MOSEK, while successfully solving the largest tested 3D problems that exceed the device-memory capacity of the GPU solver CuClarabel. For elastoplasticity, we also propose a preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver that reduces device-memory requirements relative to the direct GPU solver, at the expense of increased solution time.
Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
Xiaoxue Hu; Jiangxu Kong; Yu Xue

The strong chromatic index $χ_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $θ(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $θ(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $χ_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $θ(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.
Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains

Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.
The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice

Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.
A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture

We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $π_K\hookrightarrowπ$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[ H_i(\mathfrak u,π_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H_i(\mathfrak u,π). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π),\ \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,π),C^j(\mathfrak u,π)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.
Generalized Covering radii and Deep Holes of a Family of Antiprimitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes in Even Characteristic
Ketong Ren; Bing Liu; Cuiling Fan; Haode Yan

This paper determines the generalized covering radii, deep holes, and complete coset leader weight distribution of the antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH code of length \(q+1\) and designed distance \(3\) over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q=2^m\) and \(m\geq 2\). We establish the complete generalized covering-radius hierarchy: the covering radius is \(3\), whereas the \(t\)-th generalized covering radius is \(4\) for every \(t\geq 2\). Using the covering radius, we then derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a received word to be a deep hole by reducing the syndrome representations to conditions involving roots of an associated cubic polynomial. An explicit parametrization yields complete, nonredundant representatives of all deep-hole cosets. Enumerating these representatives gives closed-form expressions for the numbers of deep holes and determines the complete coset leader weight distribution, with distinct formulas according to the parity of \(m\).
Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
Jiaoyang Huang; Shengjing Xu; Yulei Xu

We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge. More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals. The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.
Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$

For every $0<β\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,β}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under Hölder regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.

In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1, \dots, n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the records published before this work; one of them, the optimal formula for $π$ with 1-9 (error $2.81 \cdot 10^{-14}$), was found independently by M. Verheyen, and we prove it optimal. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size

Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.
On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems

In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent
Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
Kota Kaneko; Kohei Motegi; Jun Sato

We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $Λ=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $τ=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions $\operatorname{Ki}_3$. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.
A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension

Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $δ\|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $δ$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.
Andrés R. Moreno; José L. Ramírez

In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.
Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
Ritwik Chakraborty; Inhyeok Choi; Biswajit Nag

Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.
Gaussian Quasi-Likelihood Estimation for Nonsynchronously Observed Lévy processes

We study parametric inference for a two-dimensional simple Lévy process observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon, where the two components are sampled in a possibly non-synchronous manner. Combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimation for Lévy SDEs with the non-synchronous quasi-likelihood methodology, we construct a Gaussian-type quasi-likelihood based on the covariance structure of non-synchronous increments, and we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. The convergence rates coincide with those in the synchronous setting, while the asymptotic variance depends essentially on the sampling design and becomes more complicated under non-synchronicity. To handle the different moment structure of pure-jump Lévy processes, we introduce an additional convergence assumption and provide tractable sufficient conditions linked to the observation scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators.
Kakutani equivalence of higher rank unipotent abelian actions I
Adam Kanigowski; Philipp Kunde; Kurt Vinhage; Daren Wei

We study Kakutani equivalence of higher-rank abelian unipotent actions. We construct a Kakutani invariant for general $\mathbb{R}^n$-actions and establish a quantitative vanishing criterion. By this criterion, we prove that ergodic abelian horocyclic actions on finite-volume quotients of connected semisimple Lie groups are loosely Kronecker. We also include a proof of the Abramov entropy formula for time changes of Rn-actions, following the strategy developed by Nadler.
Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III

We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.
Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
Leonardo Colombo; María Emma Eyrea Irazú; David Martín de Diego; María Daniela Sánchez; Marcela Zuccalli

We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.
Painlevé transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions

We consider the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions \begin{align*} &iq_t+ q_{xx}-2\left(|q|^2-1\right)q +i\left(q_{xxx}-6|q|^2q_x\right)=0,\\ &q(x,0)=q_0(x)\to\pm 1, \quad x\to\pm\infty, \end{align*} which can be characterized using a Riemann-Hilbert problem through the inverse scattering transform. With the $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method and double scaling limit technique, we derive the long-time asymptotics of the solution in two transition regions \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}_{a} :=\left\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}: \left| {x}/{t}-a\right|t^{2/3}<C\right\}, \quad a\in\{-4,-8\}, \end{align*} where $C>0$ is a constant. It is shown that the asymptotic expansions in two transition regions can be expressed in terms of the Hastings--McLeod solution of the Painlevé II equation in the generic case and Ablowitz--Segur solutions in the non-generic case.
Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction with Sparse Field Measurements
Lang Ming; Longhui Wang; Yazhou Sun; Xi Chen; Jian Wang; Yu Wang

Field measurements are essential for evaluating radio map reconstruction under real-world conditions, but their acquisition is costly. This letter proposes a simulation-assisted parameterized-background data-weak (SA-PBDW) method that combines propagation simulations with sparse field measurements, which jointly estimates background coefficients and a spatial correction to account for discrepancies between simulated and measured power distributions. Dense field measurements are collected for multiple transmitter positions at an urban site. Evaluations on the collected data and RadioMapSeer demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and structural fidelity over benchmark methods at reduced sampling rates.

We prove a new combinatorial interpretation for Fishburn numbers, in that they count the number of homogeneous games; specifically homogeneous games without dummy players, which we show extends to homogeneous games via the partial sums of Fishburn numbers. In doing so, we settle two conjectures commented in the OEIS A189359 entry, and finish off by providing some immediate consequences on homogeneous game counts; including an asymptotic formula and congruences.
Every friend of 10 has at least eleven distinct prime factors

A friend of $10$ is a positive integer $N\neq 10$ such that $σ(N)/N=σ(10)/10=9/5$. Whether one exists is an open problem. Thackeray proved that a friend of $10$ has at least $10$ distinct prime factors. We describe a computer-assisted proof that it has at least $11$. The proof is an exhaustive search over sets of primes, carried out by a recursive certifier written in PARI/GP, which extends the open-source project caioross/solitary10. The new ingredients are a split of ``almost tight'' nodes that avoids enumerating the smallest unknown prime, a treatment of nodes with three or more unknown primes by a saturation dichotomy, a counting rule for unfactored cofactors of cyclotomic values, and the correction of a soundness gap in the earlier closure rule. The certification run for $ω=10$ visited $157{,}210{,}962$ nodes in $11.4$ hours on $12$ threads. As a consequence, a friend of $10$ would be larger than $10^{38}$.
Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions

In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).
Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions

We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Barański, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpińska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{λz} + Be^{-λz}$, where $ABλ\neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.

This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.
Saksham Aggarwal; James Nichols; Katharine Turner

Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.
Pointwise Minmax Representations for Total Variation Denoising on Graphs

Total variation denoising (TVD) is a fundamental method in image denoising, signal processing, and nonparametric regression. We establish exact pointwise minmax/maxmin representations for TVD on arbitrary finite graphs, extending recent one-dimensional results. Under squared loss, fitted values are expressed through corrected local averages over nested connected vertex sets. The correction is a signed boundary count: edges leaving the inner set contribute +1 if they remain within the outer set and -1 otherwise. To the best of our knowledge, this representation is new even for two-dimensional TVD. We show that Brunk's classical minmax formulas for isotonic regression on every finite directed acyclic graph arise as special cases of our graph TVD representation. The exact reduction proceeds through asymmetric TVD and nearly isotonic regression, which coincides with isotonic regression above a finite penalty threshold. We further extend the representations to arbitrary finite separable convex losses, assuming coercivity of the full objective, but without requiring differentiability or strict convexity. For nonunique solutions, the possible fitted values at each coordinate form a compact interval. Its lower and upper endpoints admit maxmin and minmax representations, respectively, through scalar local optimization problems and are attained simultaneously at all coordinates by two extremal solutions. This yields exact representations for quantile TVD on arbitrary graphs and unifies TVD, nearly isotonic regression, and isotonic regression within a single pointwise framework for general separable convex losses.
Interacting framework for the free magnetic dynamics

This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.
Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
Armando Gutierrez Terradillos; Lois Omil-Pazos; Óscar Rivero

The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.
Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes

If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface. Further, for each integer $n\geq 2$, we construct automorphisms of $A^{[n]}$ not preserving the big diagonal for an abelian surface $A$.
Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform

It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.
DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware

Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.
On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
Alan Filipin; Yasutsugu Fujita; Ana Jurasić

We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.
Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
Tim Kunt; Thorsten Koch; Hyejun Park

We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.
Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations

Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.
Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture

Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.
Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II

We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.
A fast iterative solver for lopsided Sylvester matrix equations

A generalization of the factored alternating direction implicit algorithm is introduced that makes use of type $(p, q)$ Zolotarev rational functions to apply unequal numbers of left and right shifts. Convergence properties of the algorithm are discussed, as well as a method for computing shift parameters. Several applications are highlighted where the generalized method is useful, including in the solving of a collection of shifted linear systems, for discretizations that involve left and right operators that are not equally amenable to inversion, and for Sylvester matrix equations with differently-sized, differently-structured, or differently-conditioned coefficient matrices.
A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products

The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.

In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or Hölder assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,β}$ for some $1-2/k<β<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^α$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,α}$ for $0<α<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.

Many problems in statistics, combinatorics, econometrics, and other fields are expressible in terms of the upper probability of all copulas. We formally study this capacity, which we call the upper copula capacity, as a mathematical object. In particular, we examine the capacity of given sets and integration with respect to this capacity. For two-dimensional convex sets, the upper copula capacity equals the smaller of the two coordinate projection lengths. We also give an exact formula for the capacity of lower-tail events for positively weighted sums in any dimension and characterize when the upper Choquet integral equals the supremum of expectations over all copulas. Various problems in different fields can be formulated via the upper-copula capacity, and we discuss how known and new results connect to offer new perspectives on these problems.

We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.
Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons

We prove that complete expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in complex manifolds, provided their closures admit neighborhoods with holomorphic immersions into Euclidean space. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler--Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.
The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms

We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.
The geometry and classification of positive frames
Shankhadeep Mondal; Deguang Han; David Larson; Ursula M. Molter

We investigate the geometric and operator-theoretic structure of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with particular emphasis on positive linear dependence, redundancy, and convex geometry. Building on the classical theory of positive spanning sets, we characterize equivalence classes of positive frames through the kernels of their synthesis operators and obtain parametrizations in terms of the relative interior of a standard simplex and suitable subsets of Grassmannians. We establish that every redundant frame admits a positive dual, regardless of whether the original frame is positive, and provide an explicit construction through a rank-one perturbation of the canonical dual. Furthermore, we investigate the affine and topological structure of positive dual frames, proving their relative openness in the space of all duals and the absence of extreme points. We characterize dual frames satisfying prescribed positive relations and derive criteria for the existence of positive-basis duals. We also examine semi-positive frames and their boundary behavior, together with connections between positive spanning, balancedness, and finite group representations. Finally, we study the convex geometry of nonnegative relation spaces and establish a directional characterization of positive-spanning robustness under arbitrary vector erasures. These results provide a unified geometric framework for understanding positive frames, their dual systems, and the role of redundancy in constrained reconstruction.
Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
Nikita V. Gordeev; Manuel Mota; Elena B. Yarovaya

We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota (2024), our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.
On generalizations of the Cohen structure theorem

The Cohen structure theorem is an important tool in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. Recent work of Caviglia, Goswami, and Mesiti addresses the related question of which unital rings admit a maximal ideal for which the natural projection admits a section; for such rings, they prove a structure theorem in terms of semidirect products of rings. In this paper, we extract the underlying mechanism of their structure theorem to address when unital rings admit a nonzero proper ideal whose associated projection map has this property. We also address other settings involving ideals with conditions which are determined by ring theoretic properties of the corresponding quotient.
Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
Jeremy Miller; Urshita Pal; Peter Patzt

We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.
A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties

We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.
The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121

We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus.
