We sample a flow from a suitably random family, together with a base point $p$ chosen uniformly at random on that flow's domain. For a smooth observable $f$, we show that the centered Birkhoff integral $\int_{0}^t f(ϕ_s p)\,ds-t\bar f$, where $\bar f$ is the spatial mean of $f$, normalized by $(\log t)^2$, converges in distribution to the product of two independent random variables. Using special representation of locally Hamiltonian flows, we reduce the problem to studying ergodic sums of functions with logarithmic singularities over circle rotations. Then, we prove a Cauchy limit theorem for such ergodic sums, which is a result of independent interest.
Cwikel and Kato-Seiler-Simon estimates for commutators

We prove that the commutator $[a(X),b(-\mathrm{i}
abla)]$ belongs to the weak Schatten class $\mathcal{S}^p_{m weak}$ provided $
abla a\in L^p$ and $
abla b\in L^p_{m weak}$ for $\max\{1,2d/(d+2)\}<p<\infty$. This is an analogue of Cwikel's estimate, with a larger range of exponents. We also prove analogues of the Kato-Seiler-Simon and Birman-Solomyak-Simon estimates. Counterexamples show the necessity of the lower thresholds and the failure of the Lipschitz endpoint estimate.

Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $ψ$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $ψ$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $ψ$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).
Trickle groups on a complete graph are linear

Trickle groups were recently introduced by Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris, as generalizations of both cactus groups and right-angled Coxeter and Artin groups. We construct a representation of any trickle group $\mathrm{Tr}(Γ)$ with complete graph $Γ$ on a space having a basis in bijection with the vertex set $V(Γ)$, and show that it is faithful. This in particular shows that trickle Garside groups are linear. It also allows one to realize every finite trickle group as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_{|V(Γ)|}(\mathbb{C})$. We do not use the results of Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris; instead we rather show that several properties of trickle groups that they obtained (and also some new ones) can easily be proven in the particular case of a complete graph using our representation. This includes the normal forms, the embedding of the trickle monoid inside the group in the case where $μ(x)=\infty$ for all $x\in V(Γ)$, and the absence of torsion of the latter. In this last case we give a second proof of faithfulness in the spirit of Krammer-Hée, which explains how to read Garside-theoretic information from the representation.
Stafford's conjecture on cyclicity of torsion modules
Christopher Albert; Johanna Moser; Maximilian Philipp

We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero $A_n(k)$, every nonzero $d\in A_n(k)$ admits $F,R,S\in A_n(k)$ such that $1=dR+FdS$, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right $A_n(k)$-module is cyclic. The proof maps $d$, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form $\tilde d$ and shows that the cyclic module $Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))$ vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by $x_1$ is surjective on $Q$. A comparison of lengths of localized modules over the associated graded ring then gives $\operatorname{gr}Q=x_1\operatorname{gr}Q$, so that the characteristic variety of $Q$ is disjoint from the hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$. Finally, Gabber's involutivity theorem together with an argument about conormal directions at infinity from algebraic geometry shows that such a characteristic variety must be empty and therefore, $Q = 0$.
Volume growth and gap Theorem for manifolds with non-negative complex sectional curvature

The combined work of Liu, Ni, and Ni-Tam established that a complete Kähler manifold with positive bisectional curvature has Euclidean volume growth if and only if its curvature decays quadratically on average. In this work, we use the approximation scheme developed by Cabezas-Rivas and Wilking to establish the Riemannian analogue under the assumption of nonnegative complex sectional curvature. As an application, we prove an optimal gap theorem for manifolds with nonnegative complex sectional curvature. These results generalize the authors' earlier work.
The number of cycles in a random 2-factor of a random regular graph

We study the number of cycles $X$ in a uniformly random 2-factor $F$ of a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices (in the pairing model) for any fixed $d\ge 3$. When the pairing $P$ and the 2-factor $F\subseteq P$ are chosen uniformly at random together, the probability generating function of $X$ is $Γ(n+\tfrac u2)Γ(\tfrac12)/\bigl(Γ(n+\tfrac12)Γ(\tfrac u2)\bigr)$, which does not depend on $d$. Consequently, $X$ has mean $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$ and variance $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$, satisfies a central limit theorem, and equals $1$ (so that $F$ is a Hamilton cycle) with probability $Θ(n^{-1/2})$. Using an exact formula for the second moment of the cycle generating polynomial together with small subgraph conditioning, we transfer these results to a uniformly random 2-factor of a fixed random regular graph.
Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
Beniamin Bogosel; Dorin Bucur; Ilaria Fragalà

We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya and Szegö: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the partition cells, and with an angular concavity property of this functional on the class of isosceles triangles.
An asymptotic ball algebra with countably determined spectra and a nonseparable character space

Let $X=\partial\mathbb B_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the restrictions to $X$ of functions in the ball algebra $A(\overline{\mathbb B_2})$. The unital uniform Banach algebra \[ \mathcal A=\{(f_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X)):\mathrm{dist}_{C(X)}(f_n,\mathcal R)\longrightarrow0\} \] is inverse-closed in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X))$. Consequently one countable family of evaluation characters generates the spectrum of every element of $\mathcal A$. Nevertheless $Δ(\mathcal A)$ contains continuum many pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets and is therefore nonseparable. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Ohrysko, Wojciechowski and Graham.
Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one

We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $χ=χ(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2χ+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2χ+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.
Jordi Daura Serrano; Jordi Garriga Puig; Ioannis Gkeneralis

We study smooth actions of quaternionic tori $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$ on closed, connected smooth manifolds, establishing sharp bounds for $r$ in terms of the dimension of the manifold when the action is either effective, effective almost-free, or almost-effective. In particular, we prove that an almost-effective $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$-action on an $n$-dimensional manifold satisfies $r\leq \lfloor2n/3\rfloor$, and we classify up to diffeomorphism all simply connected manifolds attaining the maximal possible rank. This gives a quaternionic counterpart of the maximal symmetry rank conjecture without any curvature assumption. We also establish the bounds $r\leq n/3$ for effective and effective almost-free quaternionic torus actions, and we compute the exact value for spheres, quoric manifolds, or manifolds of the form $(S^3)^a\times (S^1)^b$.
Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
Lenka Kopfová; Matthew Kwan; Richard Montgomery; Kalina Petrova

We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).
Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients

We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.
Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime
Leonardo Galli; Daniela Angela Parletta; Andrea Paudice

In this paper, we study stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime, where the population objective shares a common minimizer with the sample losses. In contrast to prior work, which has largely focused on in-expectation analysis, we obtain high-probability convergence guarantees under the same assumptions. In the convex case, we prove a fast rate of order $\log(β^{-1}) \cdot n^{-1}$ after $n$ iterations, with failure probability at most $β$. In the strongly convex case, we derive a family of moment-based bounds of order $β^{-p} \cdot \exp(-\mathcal{O}(p \cdot n))$ for $p \in (0,1]$, and complement them with a matching lower bound showing that the corresponding deterioration in the exponential rate is essentially unavoidable. In both settings, our theoretical results are unified across a broad class of step-size schedules. Building on this analysis, we extend our results to a low-noise regime and to nonconvex objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
A Local False Discovery Rate Framework for Compound p-values
Jierui Zhu; Rina Foygel Barber; Nikolaos Ignatiadis

Compound p-values relax individual p-value validity to an average condition across the null hypotheses. This flexibility, however, need not protect particular rejections, especially when paired with an average error criterion such as the false discovery rate (FDR). In this work, we introduce "density-compound p-values," a concept that connects compound p-values and the frequentist local FDR paradigm. Under independence, we establish boundary FDR (bFDR) guarantees for the support-line (SL) procedure, with nominal-level control for weighted and compound-e-weighted p-values. For general density-compound p-values, our bounds depend on a tractable null-distribution parameter, and we show that without further restrictions on this parameter, the bFDR can substantially exceed its nominal level. Our theory extends to discrete compound p-values constructed by pooling permutation tests. Applications illustrate the method in low-resolution testing problems, where individually valid permutation p-values are too coarse to yield discoveries after multiplicity correction.
A Trajectory-Based Mathematical Framework for Wildfire Front Propagation in Heterogeneous Landscapes

We present a mathematical formulation based on trajectories for modeling the propagation of wildfire fronts in heterogeneous landscapes and apply it to the Brazilian Pantanal. The formulation is made up of a direction-dependent propagation law and Finsler orthogonality along a moving boundary. This results in a nonlinear local system for outward fire front trajectories. We provide a strictly convex translated ellipse representation at each point of the evolving boundary which guaranties uniqueness and existence of the chosen outward velocity. The effective propagation coefficients that are dependent on space and the hourly wind forcing permit the perimeter to evolve irregularly without imposing a fixed global front geometry. Computed trajectories were georeferenced and isotropically spatially registered with VIIRS active-fire observations. ERA5 wind and ERA5-Land vegetation data were used to describe the environmental forcing and landscape heterogeneity. The full-run Dice coefficients for the observation-guided spatial comparisons for the exploratory experiments for September 3-5, 2020 are 0.578, 0.571, and 0.467 respectively. One-at-a-time sensitivity perturbations of the spatial propagation coefficient, wind speed magnitude and rate-law exponents quantify the governing influence of the environmental forcing and parameter variations on the spatial extent of the calculated fire advance. These observed patterns also guided calibration and, in the absence of exact timestamps of satellite acquisition, the results show within-event spatial agreement rather than independent predictive validation. The framework provides a mathematically rigorous basis for subsequent uncertainty quantification, independent validation over multiple events and prospective sector-wise assessments of simulated fire spread.
Further simulations between tropical and linear programming

Propositional proof systems that apply various kinds of cuts to linear inequalities (such as Cutting Planes [CCT87] and Lift&Project [BCC93,Pud99,Das05]) or operate with disjunctions of linear inequalities (such as Res(CP) [Kra98] and Res(LP) [HK06]) have been in the focus of research for the past 30 years. Recently, tropical proof systems were introduced [AGH25]; they resemble the latter systems but differ from them in important respects. The relations between the traditional systems and the new tropical systems have remained largely unknown, and exponential lower bounds for tropical systems were limited to non-CNF examples. In this paper we prove several new polynomial simulations between these systems. To this end, we introduce Thr-Res (Threshold Resolution), a new natural daglike proof system operating on threshold conditions over the Boolean literals: lines asserting that at least s literals of a given multiset are true. Its main difference from CP is that the rounding rule (without it CP is incomplete) is replaced by a weaker rule that allows one to perform "resolution" steps with linear combinations beyond Boolean clauses; also, in its addition rules, Thr-Res resembles input resolution [Cha70]: a derived line is combined with an input clause or an axiom, whereas CP can add up any two derived lines. By varying the maximum value of s, one obtains systems ranging in strength from Resolution to MP-NSR, the static tropical (min-plus) proof system introduced in [AGH25]. As a consequence, we prove that MP-NSR is polynomially simulated by CP and L&P (even by their unary versions), which automatically yields exponential lower bounds on the size of MP-NSR proofs for formulas in CNF. We complement it with simulations in the converse direction: binary daglike MP-PCR (a dynamic version of MP-NSR) polynomially simulates L&P; it also polynomially simulates CP when division axioms are added.
Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
Vida Dujmović; Robert Hickingbotham; Pat Morin; David R. Wood

We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $Δ$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $Δ$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumović, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $Δ$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.
Restoring Power Fairly: Equitable Resource Allocation in Post-Disaster Grid Recovery
Jie Mao; Saharnaz Mehrani; Samin Aref; Payman Dehghanian

Post-disaster power restoration requires allocating limited repair and power resources across affected communities, creating a fundamental tension between restoring service efficiently and providing equitable access to electricity. We develop an optimization framework incorporating horizontal fairness, which promotes comparable service across affected communities, and vertical fairness, which accounts for differences in community vulnerability. The framework integrates repair-crew scheduling with an approximation of power-system operations, including distributed generation and solar-plus-storage resources. It supports vulnerability-aware prioritization while protecting specified fractions of bus-level service under a horizontal-fairness reference plan and limiting the increase in restoration cost. Structural results characterize when the two fairness benchmarks can be attained simultaneously in an aggregate allocation model and provide a sufficient condition under which improving vertical fairness requires changing discrete decisions in the full restoration model. Using the IEEE 33-bus test system, we show that equitable restoration operates through two interconnected mechanisms: reconnecting isolated areas and allocating limited power within connected areas. In the tested setting, selected vulnerability-aware solutions attain both fairness benchmarks at a lower cost than their horizontal-fairness reference plan. The results also show that stronger emphasis on horizontal fairness can yield lower efficiency losses than intermediate fairness settings, with an identical-demand comparison illustrating the role of demand heterogeneity. The framework helps decision makers identify the operational sources of service disparities and evaluate how repair priorities, power allocation, and allowable cost increases affect the opportunities to reduce them.
Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology

Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement.
A unified Sobolev framework for long-wave limits of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation

We present a unified justification of the KdV, Airy, inviscid Burgers, and Whitham approximations for the one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation in Sobolev spaces. Using energy estimates for its Madelung formulation, we establish quantitative error bounds on the natural time scales of the respective approximations. The analysis covers different long-wave scaling regimes within a single framework.
Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem

We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.
New Heuristics for Large-Scale Joint Order Selection, Allocation, Batching, and Picking

Manual order picking in warehouses plays an important role in modern e-commerce fulfillment. In this work, we consider a warehouse fulfillment model recently introduced by researchers at Zalando, a leading fashion e-commerce company. It simultaneously models the hierarchy of decision stages in a very large-scale setting with a semi-online order set, where only a certain number of items have to be fulfilled in each time interval. For their base model, we present both new and improved algorithms together with comprehensive performance evaluation. We further extend the model to a setting with multiple phases, which more closely represents the situation observed in real warehouses, and adapt the algorithms to this setting, including new variants that incorporate multi-phase specific features. We demonstrate that this extension allows us to model, control, and optimize for certain parameters such as order age which play an important role in managerial considerations with the growing importance of next or even same day delivery.

We study free products of vector lattices and their relation to free products of Banach lattices. We characterize the Archimedean vector lattices whose vector lattice free product with every Archimedean vector lattice is again Archimedean: these are precisely those whose finitely generated sublattices are projective. For finitely generated lattices, this connects the free-product property with polyhedral geometry through Baker--Beynon duality. We also show that the Banach lattice free product is the completion of the Archimedean vector lattice free product under the largest lattice norm making the canonical maps contractive. For finitely many factors, the Archimedean vector lattice free product is order dense in the Banach lattice free product. Moreover, it is shown that bounded families of injective lattice homomorphisms also induce injective homomorphisms between Banach lattice free products. Finally, in analogy with the theory of separably injective Banach lattices, we study relative injectivity and universal disposition for the class of vector lattices with countably many proper prime ideals. Every vector lattice embeds into one of universal disposition for this class, while ordered ultrapowers of the real line provide relatively injective examples of cardinality continuum.
Hull variation of algebraic geometry codes under divisor twists
Erik Mendoza; Sihem Mesnager; Luciane Quoos

The hull $\mathrm{Hull}(\mathcal{C})=\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp}$ of a linear code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ interpolates between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes, with trivial hull, and self-dual codes. Its dimension is preserved by coordinate permutations but not by scalings $\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathcal{C}$, $\mathbf{x}\in(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^n$. This governs the complexity of Sendrier's support-splitting algorithm and decides whether an equivalence class contains LCD codes. We study this hull-variation problem, formalised by Chen, for algebraic geometry codes $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ over a function field $\mathcal{F}/\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g>0$, where scalings are twists of $G$ by principal divisors; as a natural relaxation, we allow twists $G\mapsto G+L$ by arbitrary divisors. Writing $\mathcal{C}(D,G)^{\perp}=\mathcal{C}(D,H)$, with $H=D-G+W$, $W$ canonical, a twist acts by $(G,H)\mapsto(G+L,H-L)$. Whenever $\gcd(G+L,H-L)$ is non-special, the hull dimensions of $\mathcal{C}(D,G+L)$ and $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ differ by exactly $\frac12(\mathrm{deg}|G-H|-\mathrm{deg}|G-H+2L|)$. For a genuine scaling, $L=-(z)$, this variation is bounded by $2[\mathcal{F}:\mathbb{F}_q(z)]$. Under the same hypothesis, we obtain an upper bound on the hull dimension depending only on $D$ and $W$, and characterise exactly when it is attained by a scaling of it. These bounds shed new light on Chen's maximal hull dimension; explicit scalings on Kummer extensions show that the first is sharp. We construct explicit twists that raise, respectively lower, the hull dimension by prescribed amounts, one unit at a time, and apply them to two classical families. Starting from known LCD codes, we reach every hull dimension in an explicit range; starting from a self-dual code ($q$ even) or a code of maximal hull dimension ($q$ odd), we descend to $0$, yielding LCD codes of various dimensions.
A counterexample to Molchan's orthant persistence conjecture

We refute Molchan's conjecture that the persistence probability of the isotropic fractional Brownian field on $[0,R]^d$ satisfies $p_{d,H}(R)=R^{-d(1-H)+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$. We prove $$ \limsup_{d\to\infty}\limsup_{R\to\infty} \frac{-\log p_{d,H}(R)}{d\log R} \le 1-\frac{49}{48}H+o(H), \qquad H\downarrow 0. $$ Thus the conjecture fails for every sufficiently small fixed Hurst parameter in all sufficiently large dimensions. A finite-step Gaussian interpolation inequality on the exact positive sphere is proved in an appendix.
Failure of the $L^p$ Neumann problem in bi-Lipschitz images of a ball
Mihalis Mourgoglou; Carmelo Puliatti; Xavier Tolsa

For every $n\geq 2$ we construct a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}$, which is the image of the unit ball under a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, and a bounded Neumann datum $g$ with zero mean such that the variational solution $u$ of the Neumann problem with datum $g$ satisfies $\mathcal N(\nabla u)\notin L^1(\partialΩ)$. In particular, the $L^p$ Neumann problem is not solvable in $Ω$ for any $1<p<\infty$, although $Ω$ is a two-sided chord-arc domain whose boundary supports a weak $(1,1)$-Poincaré inequality, and although in this class of domains the Dirichlet and the regularity problems are solvable for some exponents. This answers in the negative a question of C. Kenig, and it also shows that, unlike the solvability of the Dirichlet problem, the solvability of the $L^p$ Neumann problem for some $p\in (1,\infty)$ is not invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously. For seventeen colors, the residue class singled out by Kiming and Olsson carries no congruence, and we show that its generating function is $y f(y^{19})^{2}/f(y)$ modulo $19$. Along the way, we recall, with proofs, such exact relationships known for all these congruences. O'Brien's cubic relation is a Weierstrass equation for $X_{0}(19)$ in Kolberg's coordinates; we prove the existence of a doubling automorphism of the theta functions, fixing the cubic, which acts on both dissections by explicit scalars. All proofs are by hand.
Wegner model in high dimension: singular continuous spectrum from U(1) symmetry breaking and AAT self-consistency

We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuous type for the disordered model at the Anderson transition. The key mechanism that leads to a singular continuous spectrum is a novel scenario of spontaneous symmetry breaking, intimately connected to the non-compactness of the global symmetry group of the field theory. While that symmetry breaks down to a compact subgroup in the metallic phase, it spontaneously breaks down to a nilpotent subgroup at criticality. We describe the symmetry-breaking extremal states approximately, by applying the self-consistent theory of localization due to Abou-Chacra, Anderson, and Thouless. The thrust of our work is to provide a field-theoretical foundation for disorder phenomena associated with singular continuous spectra.
About the occurrence of Akhmediev breathers in dispersive systems

Akhmediev breathers are spatially periodic solutions of the NLS equation which are localized in time. We prove a new NLS approximation result for dispersive wave systems, showing that there are solutions to these systems where Akhmediev breathers in the lowest order approximately modulate the underlying wave packet. Since the solutions of the original wave system are quasi-periodic in space, the main challenge is to find an appropriate function space to estimate the approximation error.
Katona's Shadow Equality Persists under Bounded VC-Dimension

Katona's intersecting-shadow theorem states that every $t$-intersecting $r$-uniform family has size at most that of its $(r-t)$-shadow, with equality precisely for complete $r$-uniform families on $2r-t$ points. We prove that both the shadow inequality and its equality classification remain valid under the substantially weaker assumption that the VC-dimension is at most $r-t$. By contrast, bounded VC-dimension and $t$-intersection do not, in general, yield the same extremal bounds in the corresponding cardinality problem.
A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees

Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric. By introducing an auxiliary tree statistic dual to $\mathrm{eoc}$, we give a bijective proof of this symmetry. Our proof composes a recursive bijection on strict binary trees, a bijection to alternating André permutations, and the reverse-complement involution on permutations.
Open Homomorphisms between $m$-step Solvable Galois Groups of Number Fields

Let $K,L$ be number fields, and let $m \geq 2$ be an integer. In this paper, we prove that an open homomorphism $ϕ_{m+2}: G_K^{m+2} \to G_L^{m+2}$ induces an open homomorphism $ϕ_m$ that arises uniquely from a field embedding $τ_m:L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. We first establish a sharper version of the $m$-step solvable cyclotomic compatibility criterion by Mao and Saïdi: if $ϕ_{m+2}:G_K^{m+2}\to G_L^{m+2}$ is compatible with the cyclotomic characters, then the induced map $ϕ_m:G_K^m \to G_L^m$ arises uniquely from a field embedding $L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. Then we apply the strategy of OpenAI's (together with Tsujimura's recent explanation of OpenAI's work) proposed proof of Uchida's conjecture to show that every open homomorphism $ϕ_4:G_K^4 \to G_L^4$ is automatically compatible with the cyclotomic characters.
Shape-Derivative Moment Approximation for a Reduced Time-Harmonic Biot Poroelastic System with Random Interfaces
Yongle Hao; Fuchang Huo; Jingzhi Li; Kai Zhang

We develop first- and second-moment approximations for a reduced time-harmonic Biot poroelastic interface system with random material interfaces. The model retains mixture inertia, quasi-static Darcy discharge, and explicit storage and coupling coefficients. The interface separates two media, each with constant Lamé parameters and hydraulic mobility. We use shape calculus to analyze random perturbations normal to the interface. We derive the first shape derivative in a total-traction and normal-flux formulation, establish a Taylor expansion on a fixed function space under a non-resonance assumption, and prove error bounds on fixed observation regions. The mean approximation is second-order accurate, and the covariance and variance approximations are third-order accurate. We estimate the variance error directly. Applying pivoted Cholesky compression to the covariance matrix of the coefficients in a fixed basis of smooth interface modes reduces the computation of the leading covariance to deterministic sensitivity solves. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions examine perturbation rates, low-rank truncation, coupled statistics, and computational cost.
A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem

We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent. Our proof follows the strategy of Kurano and Shimomoto and makes essential use of Česnavičius' Macaulayfication theorem.
The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
Minhui Li; Shumin Zhang; Junhao Qu

An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $ι(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. We prove that if $T$ has order $n$ and at least two edges, then $ι(T)\le\lfloor n/(2r-1)\rfloor$, where $r\ge3$. Moreover, the bound is attained for every admissible order. Furthermore, we characterize all hypertrees attaining it by a construction using six types of marked hypertrees of orders $2r-1$, $3r-2$ and $4r-3$. For connected graphs of order $n$ with at least two blocks, all of which are triangles, we obtain the sharp bound $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ on the cycle isolation number and characterize the graphs attaining it.
Convergence of replicator-mutator particle systems via bounded Wasserstein distance

Interacting particle systems with selection and mutation mechanisms arise in biological modeling, evolutionary optimization, and particle filtering methods. In this work we will consider the paradigmatic replicator-mutator PDE, which combines a diffusive component with a source term that depends on an external potential. We derive quantitative error estimates for the distance between the empirical measure of an unweighted particle system and the solution of the PDE. The proof uses a Wasserstein-1 distance with a bounded ground cost, which allows us to treat unbounded potentials on an unbounded state space. The key tools are the optimal coupling of newly resampled particles and, for the time-continuous limit, the use of a discrete-time killing resampling.
Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake

We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\mathscr{C}$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.
Asymptotic Error of the Euler--Maruyama Scheme for McKean--Vlasov SDEs Driven by $α$-Stable Processes

We study the continuous-time Euler--Maruyama error for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by symmetric $α$-stable noise, $1<α<2$. We assume globally Lipschitz coefficients, a bounded jump coefficient, and bounded Lipschitz state derivatives and law-derivative kernels. The error normalized by $(n/\log n)^{1/α}$ converges jointly with the original driver in the multivariate Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, and hence stably relative to the driver's path. The limit solves a linear SDE driven by the original noise and an independent symmetric $α$-stable process. Conditional centering removes both law-derivative terms from the limiting equation. For $1\leqslant p<α$, the Euler schemes based on the numerical and exact marginal laws differ by $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$ in the $L^p$ norm of the path supremum. Their normalized errors have the same limiting $p$th moment of the path supremum, which is positive if $σ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\partial_xσ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\ne 0$. For test functions in $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$, the fixed-time weak error is $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$.
Michael Joswig; Kevin Kuehn; Bernd Sturmfels; Mathieu Vallée

We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.
Conditional Mean-Field Type Linear Quadratic Optimal Control Problem for Regime-Switching Diffusions with Indefinite Coefficients
Zhongbin Guo; Guangchen Wang; Shupeng Wang

We study a conditional mean-field type linear quadratic optimal control problem for regime-switching diffusions with indefinite weights. The dynamics and cost depend on conditional expectations of the state and control given the history of the Markov chain. Under standard definiteness conditions, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the optimal control and derive its feedback representation and optimal cost through two sets of coupled Riccati equations and a linear backward stochastic differential equation driven by the Markov chain. To treat the case of indefinite weights, we extend the equivalent cost functional approach to this setting using regime-dependent quadratic adjustments for the conditional mean of the state and its deviation from that mean. When the transformed weights in the equivalent cost functional satisfy standard definiteness conditions, this construction yields unique solvability of the original Hamiltonian system and a feedback representation of the unique optimal control. The proposed results also provide an effective method for establishing the solvability of fully coupled linear conditional mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations that do not satisfy certain existing monotonicity conditions. We further apply the results to conditional mean-variance portfolio selection with exogenous liability in an incomplete regime-switching market and derive the optimal investment strategy.
An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs

Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.
(Non-)existence of complex structures on $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras
María Laura Barberis; Andrei Moroianu; Alejandro Tolcachier

In this paper we determine which $8$-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent real Lie algebras admit (integrable) complex structures. We construct explicit examples on $40$ out of the $43$ isomorphism classes, and show that there are obstructions to the existence of complex structures on the remaining three isomorphism classes. These obstructions are related to the set of elements of rank $2$ in the pencil defining the Lie algebra structure. We also show that for any even-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$, the direct sum $\mathfrak{g}:=\mathbb{R}^2\oplus \mathfrak{h}$ (and also some other, more general, extensions of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by $\mathfrak{h}$) admits a complex structure if and only if $\mathfrak{h}$ admits a complex structure. In particular, this allows us to construct the first examples of $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras in every even dimension $2n\geq8$ which do not admit complex structures. Finally, we show that every even-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebra with $2$-dimensional center admits a complex structure.
Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$. For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change. For a finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $K$ with abelian coradical over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the largest Hopf ideal contained in $J(K)$ is determined. $K^*$ is generated by its coradical if and only if $J(K)$ contains no nonzero skew-primitive elements. For liftings of quantum linear spaces and standard liftings of finite Cartan type, this condition is expressed in terms of the deformation parameters of $K$.
A unified approach to the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator via point transformations and Lie symmetries

We revisit the time-dependent harmonic oscillator (TDHO) in quantum mechanics based on the notion of equivalence transformations and Lie point symmetries. Within this framework, we give the most general point transformations depending on seven parameters which map from the TDHO to the usual harmonic oscillator (HO) and the other way around. As a byproduct we reconstruct the Schrödinger propagator (Mehler's kernel) for the time-independent harmonic oscillator. We demonstrate, without recourse to the Lewis--Riesenwert (LR) invariant, how Lie algebraic methods enable alternative derivation of the normalized wave functions of the TDHO by constructing solutions invariant under some specific subgroup of $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ combined with the gauge group. We further show that, on the relevant $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$-invariant solution family, the Lewis--Riesenfeld operator defines a compatible second-order differential constraint, thereby clarifying its relation to the Lie symmetry structure of the TDHO.
Asymptotics of linear normal lambda terms: WKB structure, Airy turning point and a positive recurrence

Let a n be the number of closed linear $λ$-terms in $β$-normal form with n variable occurrences. We prove is the large-order constant of the Riccati-Airy sequence K m attached to the turning point of the WKB expansion. We show that the K m are exactly rescaled coefficients of the formal logarithmic derivative of the Airy asymptotic series, and deduce $κ$ $\infty$ = 1/(2$π$) from the explicit Airy coefficients. Hence The proof combines four further ingredients: (i) the WKB coefficients are polynomials with nonnegative coefficients in v = (1 -4w) -1/2 and satisfy an explicit positive recurrence; (ii) the linearisation of the WKB equation has a combinatorial meaning ($λ$-chain terms) and is a translation in the action coordinate s, whose singularity sits at the instanton action A 0 = ln 2 -1 2\,; (iii) an exact identity shows that, after conjugation by the transported WKB prefactor $μ$ = r/(1+r) 2 , the remaining non-linear terms are either negative or of relative size O(m -2 ); (iv) under the conjugated linear dynamics the depth profile is dominated by its top coefficient. A finite bound on an explicit ratio sequence is obtained by exact computer arithmetic (the program is given in an appendix); it also yields a n $\le$ 1.14736 f '' n (1) for all n, with f '' n (1) $\sim$ 5 144 (n -1)!$λ$ n .
An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6

An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.
Worst-case bias of the independence assumption for functions of two ordinal variables

Let ordinal grades $X$ and $Y$ be obtained by cutting a pair of random variables with copula $C$ at arbitrary thresholds, and let $g$ be a function of the grades. We study the largest error $S_C(g)$, over all thresholds, that is, over all marginal laws, made when the mean of $g(X,Y)$ is computed as if the grades were independent. This is the counterpart of the classical dependence-uncertainty problem: the copula is fixed and the discretisation is free. The error is caused entirely by the interaction of the inputs, measured by an index $ρ(g)$, the largest absolute $g$-volume of a rectangle of grades, which vanishes if and only if $g$ is additive. For every copula, $S_C(g)$ lies between $ρ(g)$ times the largest deviation of $C$ from the independence copula and $ρ(g)$ times half the total variation of their difference, and the factor one half cannot be improved. For the Gaussian copula with correlation $λ$ we prove that $S_C(g)$ equals $|λ|ρ(g)/(2π)$ to first order, with a sharp constant and an explicit remainder. The same first-order law holds for copula families whose first-order departure from independence is a product of unimodal factors, including the Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern, Ali-Mikhail-Haq, Frank, Clayton and Plackett families, and we characterise the Archimedean families with this property. An application to the TNM staging of colon cancer, with data from a clinical trial, compares the bounds with the actual error of the independence computation.
Global well-posedness and decay estimates of strong solutions to a non-conservative compressible two-fluid model in $L^p$ critical framework
Zhiwen He; Shiyu Li; Jiayan Wu; Ting Zhang

We investigate the global existence and long-time behavior of solutions to a general multidimensional non-conservative compressible two-fluid model satisfying the algebraic capillary pressure relation \(P^{+}(ρ^+)-P^{-}(ρ^-)=f(α^{-}ρ^{-})\) in the $L^p$ critical framework. Our main contributions are twofold. First, under the sharp stability condition \(-\frac{s_{-}^{2}(1,1)}{α^{-}(1,1)}<f^{\prime}(1)<0,\) we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions for small perturbations around a linearly stable constant equilibrium. In particular, our result removes the additional negativity assumption required in Evje--Wang--Wen [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 221:1285--1316, 2016]. Second, assuming in addition that the low-frequency of the initial perturbation is small in a lower-regularity Besov space, we derive optimal decay rates for the solution.
Induced matching treewidth in classes with a forbidden structure
Valia Mitsou; Paweł Rzążewski; Giannos Stamoulis

Induced matching treewidth is a tree-decomposition based parameter where we bound the size of an induced matching whose every edge intersects a single bag of the decomposition. It is known that many computational problems can be solved efficiently in graphs of bounded induced matching treewidth. In this paper we are interested in understanding what classes of graphs have bounded induced matching treewidth. We provide dichotomy theorems for all classes defined by excluding a single graph with respect to six basic containment relations: (induced) subgraph, (induced) topological minor, and (induced) minor. Furthermore, we study the case where the input graph has minimum degree at least 2, as well as the more restrictive case where it is 2-connected. This can be assumed without loss of generality for many computational problems. It turns out that for classes excluding some graph as an induced minor, this restrictions yield some new cases of bounded induced matching treewidth. As a consequence, our results imply new algorithmic results, as well as the existence of balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices in the considered classes. This confirms some special cases of two conjectures of Gartland and Lokshtanov.
Rational v. Radical: Trajectory Properties of Iterated Bayesian Updates
Clive Cenxin Aw; Lynette Zhong Ling Wang; Peter Sidajaya

Iterating Jeffrey's update on fixed evidence gives a maximum-likelihood estimate under suitable support conditions. What is less clear would be how the trajectories are organized, and what happens when we trace them in reverse. For a fixed strictly positive, invertible classical channel and full-support evidence, reverse iteration corresponds to repeated prior hacking. Almost every interior prior then approaches certainty in one possibility while each nontrivial step worsens agreement with the evidence. We call this limiting behavior radicalization. Priors that approach the same pure state form a Bayes phase. In the phase diagrams, the separating trajectories instead approach facet fixed points determined by M-projections. We also ask whether one can choose evidence that brings every interior prior to the same conclusion. For a strictly positive, invertible channel this is always possible, although one cannot always prescribe which conclusion it will be
The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions

We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.

In this work, we study semilinear representations of groups acting on degree two Galois extensions. Our results include a classification of irreducible semilinear representations, which generalises Dyson's Tenfold Way. Using this, we completely describe the semilinear representation theory of certain groups, such as symmetric groups, and of finite groups over cyclotomic fields. We also prove many results concerning semilinear representations over $\mathbb{C}$, which includes an induction theorem which simultaneously generalises Brauer's Induction Theorem and Serre's Induction Theorem. We are also interested in applications of our classification theorem to crystallography, and include a detailed study of the semilinear representation theory of magnetic wallpaper groups.
Optimal Stability for Bivariate Weighted Fourth-Order Inequalities

In this paper, we prove sharp stability estimates for a two-component radial weighted fourth-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality in the two radial regimes for which the scalar optimizers are explicitly known and the corresponding spectral non-degeneracy holds. These regimes are \(4-N<α<2,\ \ell=-α\), and \(2<α<N,\ \ell=4(α-2)(N-2)/(N-α)-α\). Let $N\ge 3$, $p=2(N+\ell)/(N-4+α)>2$, \(μ_1,μ_2\geq0\), \(κ>0\), and $r,s>1$ satisfy $r+s=p$. For radial pairs $(u,v)\in X_{\mathrm{rad}}\times X_{\mathrm{rad}}$, we determine the sharp constant $S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ}$ in the coupled inequality \[ S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ} \left(\int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\ell\big(μ_1|u|^p+μ_2|v|^p+pκ|u|^r|v|^s\big)dx\right)^{2/p} \le \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^α\big(|Δu|^2+|Δv|^2\big)dx . \] The sharp constant is expressed through the scalar sharp constant and the minimum of an explicit one-dimensional ratio function. We also characterize all extremals and prove sharp quantitative stability estimates. The stability exponent is determined by the degeneracy of the ratio minimizers: it is quadratic in the non-degenerate case and becomes square-root type in the degenerate case.
On a conjecture of Elie Cartan concerning the Gauss equation of a flat submanifold

We study exteriorly orthogonal (or flat) symmetric bilinear forms on $\R^n$ with values in $\R^p$, continuing the work initiated by Élie Cartan in 1919 and 1920. In particular, we describe the second fundamental form of an $n$-dimensional flat manifold isometrically immersed in $\E^{n+p}$. Depending on the values of $n$ and $p$, Cartan's results either can be extended to this setting or fail.
On the thermal behavior of composites embedding extended general interfaces
Soheil Firooz; Kashish Veda Eluri; Ali Javili; Paul Steinmann

In heterogeneous materials, surface roughness, chemical incompatibility, mechanical mismatch or manufacturing defects result in imperfect bonding between the constituents. Such imperfections introduce a finite-thickness interphase zone between the constituents that possess a graded or inhomogeneous micro-structure. It is virtually impossible to resolve the behavior of such interphases. Instead, a well-established approach is to replace the interphase by a zero-thickness interface endowed with its own energetic structure. Conventional interface models define the interface temperature as an average of the temperatures of the surrounding bulk phases. However, this assumption is only adequate to represent uniform homogeneous interphases and it fails to accurately capture the behavior of graded or inhomogeneous interphases. In this work, we address this limitation by allowing for unequal contributions of the surrounding bulk phases to the interface temperature. We systematically revisit the resulting balance equations and present the computational framework for the finite element implementation of the model. We further incorporate the proposed model within the homogenization framework and derive closed-form analytical expressions for the effective thermal conductivity of fiber- and particle-reinforced composites, accouting for the influence of the extended general interface. Finally, through a series of numerical examples, we demonstrate the capabilities of the proposed model and investigate the influence of its parameters on the size-dependent thermal behavior of composites.

The paper studies universal operators and $n$-tuples of operators on Banach spaces. In the Hilbert-space setting, sufficient criteria for universality, concrete examples, and spectral properties are well established. We investigate extensions of these results to Banach spaces. In particular, we discuss the link between universality and the invariant subspace problem: this leads us to define a stronger notion of universality which is the notion of hereditarily universal operators. We give sufficient conditions for an operator to be hereditarily universal and provide some examples. We also study $n$-tuples of operators by generalizing Vladimir Müller's results to the Banach setting. Finally, we obtain a result on the essential spectrum of a universal $n$-tuple of operators on $\ell_p$.
Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
Boris Bermúdez-Cárdenas; Christian Sadel; Amal Taarabt

We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.
On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$

Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.
Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves

Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigurðardóttir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.
Mesh Sensitivity of Different Boundary Treatments in High-Order Compact Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Hypersonic Heat-Flux Prediction
Xingyi Jiang; Jiawang Zhang; Junlei Mu; Xing Ji

Accurate wall-heat-flux prediction in hypersonic flow depends on both the wall treatment and the available near-wall resolution. This work compares three complete implementations of a gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) for Mach~8.03 laminar flow over an isothermal circular cylinder: a linear Green--Gauss scheme (GG), a compact ghost-cell scheme (GC), and a pointwise one-sided compact scheme (POS). In POS, the stationary isothermal-wall conditions are imposed at the two Gaussian points used by the kinetic wall-flux quadrature. A reference mesh and six meshes in the uniform reduction (UR), log-layer unpacked (LLU), and log-layer packed (LLP) families are used to assess heat-flux sensitivity. At 24 digitized experimental angles, GG has the lowest root-mean-square difference on the reference, UR, and LLP families, whereas POS is closest on the two LLU meshes; GC is not the lowest-RMS scheme on any tested mesh. Hence no treatment is uniformly superior. On the present high-aspect-ratio cylinder grids, GG is the more robust choice except under LLU node redistribution, for which POS is preferable. Uniform reduction produces the largest heat-flux response for all three implementations. The comparison concerns complete schemes and does not isolate the pointwise constraints from differences in reconstruction and geometry representation.
Numerical integration of non-local master equations for renewal shot noise with drift and state-dependent amplitude

The probability density of a system driven by a drift and a renewal train of kicks with state-dependent amplitude obeys a master equation that is non-local in space, because the kick operator $\hat{p}(i\partial_x I(x))$ is of infinite order, and, for non-exponential waiting times, non-local in time, with a memory kernel containing the propagator of the drift. Its solutions contain quasi-singular components, the never-kicked mass, which collapse onto the attractors of the drift. We present an accurate numerical method for such equations. The kick operator is a push-forward along the Marcus flow; in the Lamperti variable it becomes a translation, whose exact cell-to-cell weights follow from the cumulative distribution of the kicks, without quadrature. The drift is integrated by a conservative semi-Lagrangian step exact in time. The memory is represented by a sum of exponentials whose auxiliary fields are advected by the drift, at a cost linear in the number of steps. The never-kicked mass is transported exactly. For each ingredient we quantify the errors of simpler alternatives. The method is verified against exact solutions and event-driven Monte Carlo simulations with exact flow maps, from which it is statistically indistinguishable with $10^8$ trajectories. Parameters tuned for Gaussian kicks carry over unchanged to other kick distributions, and near a zero of the coupling, where the density vanishes faster than any power, the solution follows the known asymptotic law down to densities of order $10^{-37}$, far beyond Monte Carlo reach. As an application we compare the exact equation with its local and Poissonian approximations: in the range explored, the local equation deviates by up to 8% of the density width, also for waiting times with finite mean, consistently with an error estimate predicting larger deviations for slow drifts at long times. A Fortran implementation is available.
Phase factors and optimal seminorms for polynomial averages of commuting transformations

For invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1, \ldots, T_\ell$ on a standard probability space, we study polynomial averages along both integers and primes. We provide a rank-based criterion ensuring that, even when the polynomials are linearly dependent, finite-order phase factors are characteristic factors. For polynomials with integer coefficients and zero constant terms, it suffices that the dimension of the space spanned (over $\mathbb{Q}$) by any nonempty subfamily of $k$ polynomials exceeds $k/2$. These phase factors are generated by polynomial phases associated with positive integer powers of the individual transformations and may be strictly smaller than the corresponding Host-Kra factors of the same order. The required order depends only on the number of polynomials and their maximum degree. A four-term example involving a totally ergodic Heisenberg nilsystem shows that this criterion may fail if the equality $k/2$ is permitted. For a family of three polynomials, this criterion is equivalent to the condition that the polynomials are pairwise linearly independent. Consequently, it applies to the family $t, t^2, t^2+t$, where the third polynomial is the sum of the first two. For this specific family, we prove that the optimal orders for the phase factors and the Host-Kra factors are $4, 2, 2$, respectively--a result that holds for both integers and primes. The corresponding optimal seminorms are $U^5(T_1)$, $U^3(T_2)$, and $U^3(T_3)$, which provides an answer to a question posed by Kuca.

We study the multiplicative $C-$lattices generated by principal elements in which every proper element is a finite product of $k-$absorbing elements. We prove that such lattices have Krull dimension at most one. In the modular case, a finite direct product decomposition theorem is obtained.
Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality

Let \(1<p\le2\). We prove that the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant has supremum \(p\), already over finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. This settles the sharpness question of Areshidze~\cite{aresh}, who improved the bound \(π/\sqrt{2}\) of Ivanisvili et al.~\cite{ivv} to \(p\). We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] If \(p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] Uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For the exponents in (a), as the modulus of roundness \(ν_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}
Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
Lassaad Aloui; Moez Khenissi; Julien Royer

We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.
Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
Ali Ulaş Özgür Kişisel; Ozcan Yazici

Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_α(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $ν(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $α\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_α(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.
Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors

We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.
Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces

We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zsák in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable renorming of the ambient space.
Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
Zefu Feng; Yinghui Wang; Jiahong Wu

We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.
Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
Leevan Ling; Shu Ma; Yizhong Sun

Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.
Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras

We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number
Complete monotonicity of Laplace transform ratios: Density criteria for self-decomposability and additive decomposition

We prove a complete monotonicity (CM) theorem for ratios of Laplace transforms: if the denominator function is logarithmically convex and the quotient of the two functions is monotone, then the corresponding quotient of Laplace transforms (or, in the opposite monotonicity case, its derivative) is CM. As probabilistic consequences, we obtain density-level criteria for self-decomposability (SD) and additive decomposition (AD) of positive distributions, together with a short proof of the classical Steutel theorem concerning infinite divisibility (ID). These criteria reduce problems typically tackled via special function quotients or Lévy measures to elementary checks on the underlying densities. The main application is to the beta prime distribution and Tricomi's confluent hypergeometric function. In the log-convex range $a\le1$, we prove new cross-parameter additive decompositions and self-convolution additive factorizations for beta prime laws. Equivalently, we establish the complete monotonicity of several quotients of Tricomi functions, providing partial affirmative solutions to a problem of Ismail and Kelker (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 1979) and to two conjectures of Ferreira and Simon (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023). We also obtain additive factorizations for generalized inverse Gaussian (GIG) laws, expressed as complete monotonicity of ratios of modified Bessel functions. Further examples, including Whittaker-type and logarithmic beta families, illustrate the scope and limitations of the method.

It is shown that the maximum number of intersection points between the boundaries of a simple $m$-gon and a simple $n$-gon is $mn-(m+n)+3$ for any odd integers $m,n \ge 3$. The previous best upper bound was $mn-(m+n)+C$, for some huge constant $C$.
Sharp integral condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals
Jnaneshwar Baslingker; Daniel Spivak; Bálint Virág

We show that the necessary and sufficient condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals with nonnegative i.i.d. vertex weights in every dimension $q\ge2$ is the same criterion for linear growth of directed last-passage times. We also obtain two-sided finite-size estimates, up to dimension-dependent constants, for the mean maximal weights of directed paths, lattice animals, valid for every nonnegative weights. These estimates determine the order of mean growth even when growth is superlinear. Since every up-right path from the origin is a lattice animal, the lower bound follows from the corresponding last-passage bound. For the upper bound, we couple the lattice weights to a Poisson process and represent each animal by a polygonal route of length proportional to its size.
On the Critical Exponent for a Time--Space Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equation with a Slowly Varying Time-Dependent Source

We study the Fujita critical exponent for the Cauchy problem $\partial_t^αu+(-Δ)^{θ/2}u=h(t)u^p$ in $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N$, $u(0)=u_0\ge0$, where $α\in(0,1]$, $θ\in(0,2]$, $p>1$, $\partial_t^α$ is the Caputo derivative, and $h(t)\sim t^γ\ell(t)$ for large $t$, with $γ\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\ell$ slowly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata. For $α=1$ and every $θ\in(0,2]$ we obtain a complete classification. If $γ\le-1$, small data give global solutions for every $p>1$, so there is no Fujita threshold. If $γ>-1$, the critical exponent is $p_c(γ)=1+θ(γ+1)/N$: every nontrivial solution blows up for $1<p<p_c(γ)$, while small global solutions exist for $p>p_c(γ)$. At $p=p_c(γ)$ the slowly varying factor decides: blow-up occurs if $\int_1^\infty t^{-1}\ell(t)dt=\infty$, and small global solutions exist if this integral converges. Hence global existence may occur at the critical exponent, unlike the autonomous case. For $α\in(0,1)$, the memory of the Caputo derivative replaces $γ+1$ by $γ+α$. We prove small-data global existence for every $p>1$ when $γ\le-α$. When $γ>-α$, all nontrivial solutions blow up for $1<p<p_c(γ,α):=1+θ(γ+α)/(Nα)$. If $N<θ$, we also obtain global existence for $p>p_c(γ,α)$, so the classification is complete, and at $p=p_c(γ,α)$ the dichotomy is governed by the boundedness of $\ell$. If $N\geθ$, we obtain global existence for $p>1+(γ+α)/α$, which coincides with $p_c(γ,α)$ when $N=θ$. Finally, a second, purely local blow-up mechanism shows that for $N>θ$ and $γ>αθ/(N-θ)$, $p_c(γ,α)$ is not the Fujita exponent. Our results extend the theorems of Meier (1990) to the nonlocal setting.
Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations

We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=λ(1+t)^{-μ}$ with $0<μ<1$, $λ>0$, or $μ=1$, $λ>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative.
