We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-μ}$ for the derivatives $u_t$, $v_t$, and $v_x$, together with a pointwise estimate for $u_x$ involving the spatial coefficient $a(x)$. The main ingredient is a time-uniform $L^\infty$ estimate for an inhomogeneous coupled transport system with a non-small spatial coefficient. Combined with suitable transformations of the Riemann-invariant derivatives, this estimate allows us to control the nonlinear terms and establish global $C^1$ bounds.
Critical Gaussian Asymptotics for Directional Superoscillations: STFT and Gabor Consequences
Younis Ahmad Bhat; Sunit Ghosh; Jitendriya Swain

We study directional Aharonov--Berry superoscillations in $\R^d$ with widening anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. We prove that the rescaled total $L^2$ mass has a sharp transition governed by the matrix $D=Q-(a^2-1)vv^T$. At criticality, $D$ has a one-dimensional kernel, and the mass obeys an exact $N^{d/2+1/4}$ law with an explicit Gamma-function constant. After anisotropic rescaling, the intensity converges globally in $L^1$ to a transverse Gaussian times a longitudinal quartic exponential. Moyal's identity gives the corresponding total STFT-energy law, but does not imply a local phase-space concentration theorem. We compare these global statements with the earlier quartic critical-window analysis of Berry and Shukla for periodic superoscillations. Supporting results include quantitative fixed-Gaussian STFT expansions, entire-growth convergence with a critical-step obstruction, and conditional Gabor-frame and dual-window expansions. Weighted STFT estimates for polynomial electric-field evolution are obtained as applications. No claim of priority is made for quartic criticality, qualitative STFT supershift preservation, or polynomial electric-field persistence as such.
A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
Rommel Rabongue Real; Simon Schwab; Frank Werner

We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.
Global stability and nonlinear asymptotics for the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity
Zefu Feng; Guangyi Hong; Yinghui Wang; Jiahong Wu

We study the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity, a positive coefficient $λ+μ>0$ in the divergence term, and full heat conduction. Horizontal viscosity does not dissipate vertical shear derivatives, while thermal diffusion is coupled to the compressible variables. For small $H^2$ perturbations of a constant equilibrium, we construct global strong solutions. Additional spatial localization yields anisotropic decay through second order, convergence of the full $H^2$ norm, and horizontal Gaussian profiles determined by an effective velocity datum. The third-order behavior contains nonlinear contributions: horizontal viscous heating generates a differentiated Newton potential in temperature, while compressible transport slows the decay of the potential velocity. We prove the corresponding bounds with exponents $17/8$ and $2$; for each exponent, we construct a fixed datum in the corresponding class for which every larger exponent fails. For each fixed initial datum, however, the corresponding time-weighted norms tend to zero as $t\to\infty$. Smallness of the first vertical derivative of the initial velocity in the horizontal mixed norm improves the vertical decay estimates and restores the linear third-order temperature rate. Both the existence and decay results require only $H^2$ Sobolev regularity of the initial data.
Structure-Preserving Neural Approximation of Convex, Semiconvex, and Quasiconvex Functions

Input convex neural networks provide a natural way to enforce convexity globally through architectural constraints. We study how this structure-preserving approximation framework extends to semiconvex, quasiconvex, and convex transformable functions. For $C^{1,1}$ convex functions on compact convex domains, we establish the sharp $W^{1,p}$ minimax rate $m^{-1/d}$ under max-affine approximation with $m$ affine pieces, and show that every max-affine function admits an exact bounded-width ICNN representation with complexity linear in $m$. The same $W^{1,p}$ approximation rate extends to semiconvex functions through quadratic lifting and to convex transformable functions through monotone composition. For general Lipschitz quasiconvex functions, we develop a quantitative finite-probe approximation theory based on monotone responses to affine projections and obtain a structure-preserving IqCNN with an $L^\infty$ approximation guarantee. We further show that these approximation results extend to ReLU-transferable smooth activations, including Softplus and ELU. Numerical experiments on PDE-based approximation problems compare the proposed architectures with parameter-matched MLPs and validation-tuned shape penalties, demonstrating global structural validity without penalty tuning while maintaining competitive approximation accuracy. Overall, the results identify recoverable convex latent structure as the key mechanism enabling gradient-level structure-preserving approximation beyond convexity.
Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
Wojciech Bruzda; Domonkos Czifra; Ilona Nagy; Ferenc Szöllősi

In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary. We carry out this task for the case of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices, and using finite field techniques we show that none of these projections can be lifted up to form a Butson matrix. In particular, we show the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices for the first time.
The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
Jnaneshwar Baslingker; Daniel Spivak; Bálint Virág

We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam.
Homeomorphic Sobolev Extensions to Jordan Domains and the inner distance
Pekka Koskela; Chengxi Li; Xilin Zhou; Yizhe Zhu

Given a Jordan domain $Ω$, we characterize the situation where a given parametrization (or all parametrizations) $φ:\partial\mathbb D\to\partialΩ$ has (have) a homeomorphic $W^{1,1}$-extension $f_φ:\overline{\mathbb D}\to\overlineΩ$.
Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction

In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.
Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
Chuansen Peng; Hanning Tang; Xiaowei Yang; Xiaojing Shen

Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of topology and latent states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian: a flexible generative transition can absorb graph-induced changes of the conditional mean, whereas a Gaussian transition discards the information in the residual shape. We develop a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, and a frozen diffusion emulator represents the conditionally centered residual. First, a score--topology duality expresses edge-wise likelihood gradients as edge projections of the residual diffusion score, so topology learning requires neither transition densities nor differentiation through the sampler. Second, we prove identifiability from intermittent observations, invariance of the population minimizer across noise levels, and global strong convexity above an explicit smoothing threshold for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cramér--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

In this paper, we introduce the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Banach spaces and investigate its basic properties. We establish some inequalities which give the relationship between the $n$-th Zbáganu constant and two other constants, namely the $n$-th Von Neumann-Jordan constant and the $n$-th James constant. In addition, we determine the values of the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, and discrete Morrey spaces.
Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition

We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.
Two results on rich-neighbour $5$-colouring of subcubic graphs
Masaki Kashima; Mirko Petruševski; Jelena Sedlar; Riste Škrekovski

A rich-neighbour edge-colouring is a proper edge-colouring in which every non-isolated edge has an adjacent edge whose neighbours have pairwise distinct colours. Petruševski and Škrekovski conjectured that every connected subcubic loopless multigraph distinct from $K_4$ admits such a colouring with five colours. We prove the conjecture for two classes: claw-free subcubic loopless multigraphs and $2$-connected subcubic outerplanar loopless multigraphs. The bound is sharp in both classes, as witnessed by the diamond $K_4-e$.
A Well-Separated Pair Decomposition of Linear Size for Unit-Disk Graphs
Mark de Berg; Joachim Gudmundsson; Sampson Wong

We prove that every connected Euclidean-weighted unit-disk graph on $n$ vertices has a $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition of size $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. This resolves an open problem posed by Gao and Zhang in 2003. We also show that this bound is tight: there are connected unit-disk graphs for which any $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition has size $Ω(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log (1/\varepsilon))$.
Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops

We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.
Parameter estimation for discretely observed rough fractional interacting particle systems
Chiara Amorino; Augustin Puel; Radomyra Shevchenko

We study parametric inference for interacting particle systems driven by independent fractional Brownian motions, based on discrete observations of all particles over a fixed time horizon. Our goal is to estimate an unknown drift parameter in the joint limit as the number of particles increases and the observation mesh vanishes. For $H>\frac 12$, we construct contrast based estimators by extending the discrete time least squares approach of Neuenkirch and Tindel to the interacting setting. For the rough regime $H\in(\frac 14,\frac 12)$, we introduce a modified contrast and use the stochastic sewing lemma to handle the first order approximations available from discrete observations. Our analysis combines the propagation of chaos for the associated fractional McKean Vlasov equation with estimates controlling the temporal discretization error. When the Hurst parameter and the diffusion coefficient are known, we establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators. The asymptotic results reveal an interplay between the number of particles and the temporal discretization: the convergence rate with respect to the observation mesh changes at $H=\frac 34$, while the asymptotic normality holds in both regimes considered. We further develop a joint estimation procedure for the drift parameter, the Hurst parameter, and the diffusion coefficient, extending quadratic-variation methods for fractional Brownian motion to the interacting particle framework. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators.
A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights

We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\neΛ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(Λ)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.
A complete classification of isometries of quasihyperbolic domains

We classify all surjective quasihyperbolic isometries between arbitrary proper planar domains. Apart from Euclidean similarities, the orientation-preserving isometries are reciprocal maps on sectors or punctured planes and explicit complex-power maps on logarithmic spiral sectors. In particular, orientation-preserving planar quasihyperbolic isometries need not be Möbius. As consequences, we obtain similarity rigidity when either domain has finite inradius, for multiply connected domains other than punctured planes, and for $C^1$ domains other than half-planes. The $C^1$ conclusion strengthens Hästö's corresponding result for planar $C^3$ domains. Our planar classification, together with Richard's classification in dimensions $n\geq3$, completely solves the quasihyperbolic isometry problem between proper subdomains of $\mathbb R^n$ in every dimension $n\geq2$. As an application, we extend to dimension two the characterization of pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of quasihyperbolic domains obtained by Herron, Richard, and Snipes.
Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
Max J. van Horssen; Arno B. J. Kuijlaars

We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.
One more curious property of $1729$: The only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with prime $p$
Jean Lucien Randrianantenaina; Ali K. Uncu

Florian Luca recently proved that if $2^np^3+1$ is a Carmichael number for some prime $p$ and integer $n\ge1$, then $p=3$. Here we complete the cubic classification by proving that $1729$, Hardy--Ramanujan taxicab number, is the only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with $p$ prime and $n\ge1$. The proof identifies the unique possible multiplicatively dependent prime factor, sharpens the known bound on Fermat prime factors of $2^nk+1$ from $k^2$ to $2k$, derives the explicit bound $n\le2742$, and concludes with a short sieve requiring neither factorisation nor primality testing.
Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
Richard Eager; Kentaro Hori; Johanna Knapp; Mauricio Romo

We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important rôle in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.
Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
Huy The Nguyen; Artemis A. Vogiatzi

We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity. We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.
Mixed-integer programming formulations for the quadratic bin packing problem: linearization, hybridization, and enhancements
Fatih Burak Akçay; Maxence Delorme; Renata Sotirov

The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.
Counting shorter even cycles in graphs forbidding an even cycle

For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Turán number $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,F)$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices. Liu and Wu (2026) proved that, for fixed integers $k>\ell\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})=\left(\frac{(k-1)_\ell}{2\ell}+o(1)\right)n^\ell$, where $(k-1)_\ell=(k-1)\cdots(k-\ell)$. In this paper, we determine the exact value of $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize the unique extremal graph.
A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
Kaie Kubjas; Lilja Metsälampi; Milo Orlich

The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.
Functional Principal Component Analysis: Minimax Optimality from Sparse to Dense Designs and Beyond

Functional principal component analysis (FPCA) plays a central role as a dimension-reduction and representation tool in functional data analysis, but its minimax theory for diverging spectral indices under noisy discrete observation has remained open for over two decades. To fill this gap, we consider a sieve-based FPCA framework that pools discrete measurements across subjects and accommodates sampling frequencies ranging from sparse to dense under random designs. We begin by establishing new minimax rates for covariance estimation over general bivariate function classes beyond tensor-product low-complexity structures, thereby identifying the intrinsically two-dimensional optimal rate. Our central theoretical contribution is to establish minimax optimal rates for both individually labelled eigenfunctions with diverging indices and leading principal subspaces of increasing dimensions, under explicit growth and regularity conditions. To establish these results, we develop a general framework for sharp minimax analysis of FPCA under discrete observation, separating spectral approximation from stochastic perturbations and exploiting their distinct structures, thereby offering a new approach to a broad class of nonparametric spectral estimation problems. For both spectral targets, the optimal rates reveal two distinct statistical mechanisms, spectral identification and nonparametric reconstruction, whose interplay gives rise to either four or two sampling regimes. This yields, for the first time, a precise characterization of the impact of discrete sampling across the full range from sparse to dense designs. Finally, as a downstream application, we analyze FPCA-based functional linear regression and show that the FPCA-based estimator attains the minimax-optimal rates.
A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?

We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone. We propose this as the basis of a relativistically causal generally covariant gravitisation of relativistic quantum theory in $1+3$ spacetime dimensions. We derive the weak-field limit which exhibits the explicitly causal dynamical structure of the theory, and recover the Schrödinger-Newton (SN) system in the nonrelativistic limit. This proposal can thus be understood as a causal completion of the SN equation, a nonlinear extension to quantum theory. We analyze relativistic quantum measurements in this nonlinear setup, showing that these do not lead to superluminal signalling if quantum states update (only) in the future light-cone of the measurement region. We give explicit examples of quantum measurements on a spatial superposition and on entangled subsystems showing how, in the weak field limit, discontinuities in the expectation value of the stress-energy tensor can be consistent with distributional solutions to the (linearised) semiclassical EFEs. We also highlight that the theory allows non-standard measurements via its nonlinearities. These effective ``readout devices'' can approximately determine a quantum state without affecting it through the state's influence on the classical gravitational field and hence can implement approximate quantum state cloning. Nonetheless, the theory does not allow superluminal signalling, although it does violate the quantum no-signalling principle. We further show that the classical gravitational field is generally not locally causal in the sense of Bell. We present several paths to test the model against low-energy quantum gravity in tabletop experiments.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a $d$-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring, $d\geq2$ containing a field, and let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m^s$ be a parameter ideal with $s\geq2$, also, in the mixed case via some mild assumptions. We prove for that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)}\subseteq\overline{J}$, and that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)+1}\subseteq\overline{J}$ when $R$ is not regular. We show that Cohen--Macaulayness cannot be removed. We also prove the characteristic-free exact formula $g(J)=(d-1)(s-1)+r$ for parameter ideals of order $s$ with a level tangent cone, giving singular mixed-characteristic Gorenstein and non-Gorenstein examples in which the singular bound is attained.
The Fujita equation with time-integrable forcing: effective mass, mass annihilation and sharp lifespan

We study the Cauchy problem $\partial_t u-Δu=|u|^p+ζ(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, $p>1$, with sign-changing data and a forcing whose temporal profile $ζ$ is integrable on $(0,\infty)$, the model case being $ζ(t)=t^σe^{-t}$, $σ>-1$. For power-type profiles $ζ(t)=t^σ$ the forcing is known to raise the critical exponent above the Fujita exponent $p_F=1+2/N$ or to destroy global existence. We show that an integrable forcing leaves $p_F$ unchanged and acts only through the effective mass $M_{\rm eff}=\int u_0+(\int_0^\inftyζ)(\int w)$. Our central result is an exact mass-annihilation identity: if $1<p\le p_F$, every global weak solution lies in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty))$ and satisfies $\iint|u|^p=-M_{\rm eff}$. Hence, for $p\le p_F$, no global solution exists when $M_{\rm eff}\ge0$ and the data are nontrivial, and every global mild solution vanishes in $L^1$ as $t\to\infty$; examples show that $M_{\rm eff}<0$ neither excludes nor implies global existence. For $p>p_F$, every solution is dominated by a multiple of the linear forced flow under a single integral condition; this gives small-data global existence without sign restrictions and, if $ζ$ decays mildly, convergence to $m_\infty G_t$ with asymptotic mass $m_\infty=M_{\rm eff}+\iint|u|^p$. We also give a localized necessary condition valid for all $p>1$, showing that large or slowly decaying data blow up regardless of the forcing and that non-integrable forcings shift the threshold, and sharp lifespan estimates for small data with positive effective mass: $T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-2(p-1)/(2-N(p-1))}$ for $p<p_F$ and $\log T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for $p=p_F$.
On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families

Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$. We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $χ\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $π_{χ,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $π_χ=\operatorname{ind}_P^Gχ$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $χ$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $π_{χ,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $χ$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $Θ(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(Θ(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $αd$ coordinates, $0<α<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $Θ(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leqαd$, for fixed $r>1$ and $0<α<2/3$. Node counts exclude leaf computation. For three fixed masks, optimal joint conditional KL has order $d/\log d$ when $\ell\leq(\log d)^2$. Local cycle identities relate joint divergence to identifiable channel products and separate weak-channel recovery from density estimation. Factorized evidence preserves a planar zero-field Ising model: given local integrals, exact queries cost $O(d^{3/2})$ arithmetic operations and one root extraction.
Two-Scale Calculus for Riesz Fractional Gradients: Compactness, Realization, and Periodic Homogenization

We develop a two-scale calculus for the Riesz fractional gradient $\grads$, $0<s<1$, acting on functions that vanish outside a bounded open set $Ω\subset\R^N$. For bounded families in $H_0^s(Ω)$ we characterize the interior two-scale limits of the fractional gradients and prove, by a Fourier-multiplier estimate, that every limit of this form is generated by such a family; a periodic fractional Helmholtz decomposition identifies the microscopic potentials, and $\eps^s$ is the natural amplitude of the oscillations. For periodic fractional divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, uniformly elliptic, not necessarily symmetric coefficients, we identify the two-scale limit of the fractional gradients and the homogenized problem, whose coefficient is the classical homogenized matrix in $Ω$ and the cell average outside $Ω$, and we construct correctors in $H_0^s(Ω)$ that give strong convergence in $H^s(\R^N)$. The identification extends to parabolic problems with dual-space forcing.
Critical spectral weights on triangulated disk

We solve the common-positive-weight support problem at the local spectral threshold 1/2 for relative triangulated disks with interior degrees at most five and an empty or connected degree-five core. We characterize feasibility by a finite decomposition into three elementary pieces and a condition on the original boundary marking. The proof passes from spectral equality to a positive conjugate rectangle, then uses geometric reductions to obtain a serial presentation. The empty-face inequality holds for some common positive weights exactly when such a presentation has only old join endpoints. Whenever this condition holds, our construction yields weights with a positive definite empty-face matrix. Positive Schur responses establish sufficiency, and a uniform face-counting obstruction proves necessity. This gives a finite combinatorial criterion for critical spectral feasibility together with a constructive choice of common weights.
DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space

This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.
Large-Scale Tensor Trace-Ratio Problem: Randomized Algorithm and Sparse Multilinear Discriminant Analysis via Closed-Form Solution

Trace-ratio optimization problems from high-dimensional tensor data appear across numerous research domains including machine learning, signal processing, as well as pattern recognition. Up to now, analytical closed-form expressions remain unavailable for tensor trace-ratio tasks; prevailing techniques mostly adopt inner-outer iterative schemes to tackle such optimization tasks. However, when dealing with high-dimensional tensor data sets, existing multilinear discriminant analysis methods often encounter limitations such as heavy computational costs, insufficient memory space, and interference from redundant features. This paper yields two core contributions.First, we present a closed-form solution under the full row rank condition, and construct a randomized solver targeting large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization. In contrast to prior approaches, the devised algorithm achieves substantial computational speedup.Its core mechanism is to reformulate the original large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization into a tensor least-squares formulation, instead of the much more complicated (generalized) tensor eigenproblems. We derive theoretical error-bound results which verify the reliability of the newly developed algorithm. Second, we build a sparse multilinear discriminant analysis model leveraging the above closed-form result combined with tensor \ell_{2,0}-norm regularization, and propose a sparse multilinear discriminant method for tensor feature selection. The sparse method can identify key discriminative features from high-dimensional data and suppress redundant information. Comprehensive numerical evaluations are conducted over multiple publicly available real-world benchmarks.The proposed methods demonstrate significant advantages in computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale problems, while achieving competitive classification accuracy on some datasets.
Absence of uniform bounds for the boundary nodal count of Steklov eigenfunctions on Euclidean domains
Alberto Enciso; Angela Pistoia; Luigi Provenzano

We prove that for any $K,N\in\mathbb N$ there exist smooth bounded domains in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq 3$, homeomorphic to a ball, for which the first $N$ positive Steklov eigenvalues are simple and the boundary traces of the corresponding eigenfunctions have at least $K$ nodal domains. This provides a negative answer to the question of whether the number of nodal domains of Dirichlet-to-Neumann eigenfunctions satisfies a Courant-type bound in the Euclidean setting and complements the results of [6].
Variational Estimates for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs

We study edge variation estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on finite connected graphs. For $0<α<1$, we determine the optimal coefficient in the uniform estimate of the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge $p$-variation of the original function. We also obtain two-sided variation bounds involving the number of vertices and the diameter. On complete graphs, we prove that the sharp $(p,q)$ constant is $(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{1/q-1/p}$ for all $0<p\leq q\leq\infty$. On star graphs with $n\geq4$, we determine the sharp infinite-exponent constant and show that the sharp constant for $p=2$ equals $1-n^{α-1}$ if and only if $n^{α-1}\geq1/2$. Combining this with the known estimate for $p=1$, we also obtain sharp mixed estimates. Extremizers and counterexamples are given.
Note on parallel transport of IHS manifolds of Kummer type
We give a characterization of parallel transport operators for irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of Kummer type.
On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds

We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.
Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise
Arya Mazumdar; Prateeti Mukherjee; Harsh Vardhan

We revisit the classical problem of learning general Gaussian halfspaces in the presence of label noise, with particular focus on the large-bias regime, where information-computation gaps are conjectured in several standard label-noise models. Concretely, we present and analyze the rare-tail mean estimator, an extremely simple one-shot statistic that averages only the observed minority class. In the large-bias regime, classical Averaging (Servedio, 1999) and related global first-moment statistics are provably suboptimal, while the rare-tail mean estimator recovers the target halfspace direction at the information-theoretic sample rate (modulo log factors) under a broad class of label noise models, including probit noise and margin-dependent noise with very slow decay away from the boundary. Notably, our guarantees allow labels arbitrarily close to the decision boundary to be nearly random, while still giving strong directional recovery from a small number of samples. The estimator also cleanly interpolates between the noiseless and noisy regimes: without noise, it attains the same sample rate as classical separability-based methods for realizable halfspaces, and under low noise, or noise that decays away from the boundary, it keeps this rate even after linear separability has been destroyed. As an application, we consider a two-stage curriculum in which source samples, whose noise may be arbitrarily close to $1/2$ near the boundary and decay very slowly away from it, precede target samples, whose noise flips every label at the same rate, i.e., random classification noise (RCN). Since both stages share the same Bayes optimal halfspace, our estimator supplies the directional warm start needed by existing refinement routines, and together they learn the RCN target at the information-theoretic sample rate in the large-bias regime, up to log factors.
Variational Estimates for the Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs

We study edge variation for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on finite connected graphs. We determine the optimal uniform coefficient controlling the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge variation of the original function and derive two-sided estimates for the variational constant of an individual graph. These estimates involve point-mass tests, the diameter, and the number of edges. On star graphs, we determine the sharp constant for exponents greater than one and characterize all nonconstant real-valued extremizers for every exponent.
Linear Duality and Its Nonlinear Extension via Topological Covering Theorems

Linear programming duality and core existence theorems in cooperative game theory are closely related. For example, in the 1960s, Bondareva used linear duality to characterize when the core of a game with transferable utility is nonempty. Scarf later established a core existence theorem for balanced games with non-transferable utility. Shapley derived this result from his KKMS covering theorem, demonstrating how topological covering theorems yield core existence results. In this note we give a new KKM-type covering proof of linear duality. We then extend the argument to inequalities with continuous perturbations. Under some asymptotic growth assumptions on perturbations, we obtain a feasible point and balancing coefficients satisfying complementary slackness, a Lagrangian lower bound, and a Scarf-type feasibility criterion. The latter yields Scarf's theorem for normalized cooperative games with non-transferable utility. Using Musin's 2017 KKM-type theorems with boundary conditions and the author's 2026 results on cover degrees relative to point configurations, we also obtain a complementary slackness theorem for continuous functions on compact connected oriented manifolds with nonempty boundary.
Rigidity for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional in dimensions greater than four

We investigate rigidity properties of critical metrics for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional on Riemannian manifolds of dimension greater than four. This functional is the integral of the squared norm of the Riemann curvature tensor. On noncompact manifolds, criticality is understood with respect to compactly supported variations, without assuming finite total curvature energy. We prove that every complete noncompact critical metric with finite curvature energy is either flat or has strictly negative scalar curvature everywhere. We further show that every complete critical metric with concircular scalar curvature is flat. Here concircularity means that the Hessian of the scalar curvature is pointwise proportional to the metric. Consequently, every complete weakly Einstein critical metric with divergence-free Cotton tensor is flat. The latter two flatness results require neither noncompactness nor finite curvature energy. Finally, we construct a complete nonflat critical metric in dimension five with vanishing Cotton tensor, showing that the concircularity and weakly Einstein assumptions are essential in the respective flatness results.
Rough vector fields with vanishing Lie brackets

We consider two vector fields $X, Y \in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf L^\infty$ with bounded divergence. If $p \geq 2$, this paper shows that $DX \,Y - DY \, X = 0$ almost everywhere if and only if their Regular Lagrangian Flows commute. If instead $1 \leq p < 2$, we present an example of two divergence free locally Sobolev vector fields in $\mathbb R^2$ with vanishing Lie brackets whose flows do not commute. In the regime $2 \leq p < \infty$ this paper also yields a quantitative commutation result not depending on the Lipschitz constant for vector fields with $[X, Y] \neq 0$, which is new even in the smooth setting.
Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning in Nonlinear Resistive Networks with Monotone Elements
Henk J. van Waarde; Benjamin Scellier; Encho T. Nguyen

In the pursuit of energy-efficient hardware for machine learning, nonlinear resistive networks trained via local learning rules are emerging as promising alternatives to digital neural networks. Learning in these physical systems is often achieved with Equilibrium Propagation (EP), which compares a "free" state to a "nudged" target-driven state to perform gradient descent on an objective defined by an explicit cost function. In contrast, Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning (TCCL) "clamps" output nodes directly to exact target values, performing gradient descent on an implicit contrastive function - an objective whose properties have long remained unknown. Focusing on nonlinear networks composed of resistors with monotonically increasing current-voltage characteristics (such as Ohmic resistors and diodes), our contribution is twofold. First, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for TCCL. We prove that the contrastive function is convex for nonlinear resistive networks without hidden nodes, and demonstrate that this property does not hold in general for the objective function optimized by EP. For these networks, TCCL converges to a global minimum of the contrastive function under suitable assumptions on the learning rate. In the presence of hidden nodes, the contrastive function is not convex, but we show that TCCL still converges to a stationary point on a subsequence. We also reveal cases where such stationary points are global minimizers of the contrastive function. Second, we characterize the representational capacity of these circuits. We establish a novel function approximation theorem demonstrating that any continuous, monotonically non-decreasing, and shift-equivariant function can be approximated to arbitrary precision, proving that these properties are the sole limitations on the network's computational expressivity.
44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
Helga Boyer von Berghof; Daniel C. Mayer

We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.
Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Rings and Unimodular Lattices
Minjia Shi; Mengru Yang; Patrick Solé

We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.
Nearly Tight Almost Sure Convergence Rates for the Last iterate of SGD
Weiming Ou; Andrea Paudice; Xiao Wang

We study the almost sure convergence of the last-iterate optimization error of Stochastic (sub)Gradient Descent (SGD) for convex objectives. For smooth objectives, we establish convergence rates of order $k^{-1/3}$ when a stationary minimizer exists, and $k^{-1/4}$ otherwise, up to polylogarithmic factors, where $k$ denotes the iteration counter. We further show that the latter rate extends to nonsmooth convex objectives. All these rates are achieved by deterministic, anytime stepsize policies. Finally, we establish matching lower bounds showing that the exponents $-1/3$ and $-1/4$ are optimal, up to polylogarithmic factors, for the corresponding problem classes.
Wenhua Qian; Yuze Ren; Wenming Wu

We study surjective $L^p$-isometries on spaces of bounded idempotents in an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. On each fixed positive finite-rank stratum, every surjective $L^p$-isometry, $1\leq p<\infty$, is implemented by a unitary or antiunitary operator, possibly composed with adjunction; no separability is required. The same conclusion holds for the operator norm, viewed as the $L^\infty$-norm. On a separable space, operator-norm isometries of the infinite-rank, infinite-corank sector admit the additional complement operation, as do surjective $L^p$-isometries between individual $L^p$-perturbation classes for $1\leq p<\infty$. For the extended $L^p$-metric on all idempotents, implementations may be chosen independently on finite-distance classes, subject to an explicit compatibility condition for matching infinite-rank classes. The proofs use similarity coordinates and metric blow-ups, followed by tangent-space splittings, nearest projections at the $L^1$ endpoint, or sharp Fredholm-index distance estimates. We also establish uniqueness of standard implementations and use essential-spectral invariants to obtain continuum many perturbation-class isometry types.
Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras

This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem for their simple quotients under certain conditions. If $A$ is finite-dimensional, we prove that its orthogonal idempotent decomposition into local Artinian summands naturally induces a tensor product isomorphism of the corresponding vertex operator superalgebras. In addition, our general construction encompasses many vertex operator superalgebras, such as superconformal algebras and generalized $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ (super)algebras.
Large Deviations and Convexity Transition for the Multidimensional Elephant Random Walk

In this article we establish a weak large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the elephant random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, for every reinforcement parameter $p \in (0,1)$. We identify a qualitative change in the behaviour of the associated rate function between dimension $d=1$ and dimensions $d \geq 2$. In dimension $d=1$, the rate function coincides with the Donsker--Varadhan rate function of the simple symmetric random walk and is independent of the reinforcement parameter $p$. By contrast, in every dimension $d\geq 2$, the rate function differs from that of the simple random walk as soon as $p\neq 1/(2d)$. Finally, we prove that for all $d \geq 2$ the rate function is convex if and only if $p \leq 1/(2d)$. This allows us to identify a critical point in the large-deviation behaviour of the model which occurs strictly before the standard diffusive-to-superdiffusive crossover.
Non-bipartite spectral extremal graphs forbidding a three-chromatic color-critical graph
Bo Dong; Cunxiang Duan; Attila Sali; Ligong Wang

A graph is color-critical if it contains at least one color-critical edge. For every fixed three-chromatic color-critical graph $H$, we determine the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex non-bipartite $H$-free graph and characterize the unique extremal graph for all sufficiently large $n$. The extremal graph belongs to one of three graph families: $J_n(s,t)$, $\mathrm{ST}_2(n-1)$ or $L_n(s,t)$. Explicit conditions on $H$ determine the family and its exact parameters. This paper generalizes the results for books and theta graphs to all three-chromatic color-critical graphs. Furthermore, an three-chromatic example demonstrates that spectral extremal graphs are not necessarily edge-extremal, disproving a conjecture of Fang and Lin [J. Algebraic Combin., 2026].
Central limit theorem for linear eigenvalue statistics of random spatial networks
Christian Hirsch; Kyeongsik Nam; Moritz Otto; Anne Marie Svane

The random connection model provides a flexible framework for spatial networks in which connectivity is determined by both geometry and randomness. Its vertices form a Poisson point process, and pairs are connected independently, conditional on their positions, with distance-dependent probabilities. This generalizes the hard distance threshold of random geometric graphs and accommodates long-range connections. We also consider a weighted extension in which each vertex carries a positive random weight that influences its probability of connecting to other vertices. This combination of spatial structure and heterogeneous connectivity raises the question of whether spectral fluctuations exhibit Gaussian behavior on large scales. We address this question by studying linear eigenvalue statistics $\operatorname{Tr}[f(A_n)]$ of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of the random connection model in expanding windows $W_n$. For polynomial test functions, we establish a finite limit for the normalized variance and prove a central limit theorem under suitable connection-profile integrability and vertex mark moment assumptions. When the limiting variance is positive, the normalized statistics admit an $O(|W_n|^{-1/2})$ normal-approximation bound in both Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distance. Furthermore, under an exponential moment assumption on the vertex marks, we extend the central limit theorem to a general class of test functions $f$.
A Godunov-type in-cell discontinuous reconstruction shock-capturing method for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
Christophe Berthon; Marie Compain; Carlos Par{é}s; Ernesto Pimentel-Garc{í}a

The present paper is devoted to show the correct convergence of a numerical method based on Godunov and the in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic but never recasts in a conservation form. With ambiguous nonconservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. In a previous work the authors determine the simple waves of the nonconservative system studied here and they are able to construct the solutions of the Riemann problem of interest. These solutions are used to obtain a Godunov-type scheme and it is combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique to obtain the correct convergence to the exact solution even in the presence of shocks.
Second-Order Steady-State Approximation of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models

Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large stochastic systems, but second-order steady-state results are largely limited to homogeneous or fixed-dimensional population processes. This paper develops a second-order steady-state approximation for fully heterogeneous mean-field models. Conditioning on the realized agent parameters, we study fixed-dimensional weighted occupancies even though the dimension of the full heterogeneous mean-field system grows linearly with the number of agents $M$. We first establish an $O(M^{-1})$ bound on the mean-field approximation error for stationary expectations of twice continuously differentiable functions of these occupancies. We then characterize the leading term in this error in terms of the stationary mean bias and covariance of the weighted occupancies. A Lyapunov equation for the linearized dynamics yields an approximation to the stationary covariance of the unscaled weighted occupancy with error $O(M^{-3/2})$. Its solution, together with the drift derivatives at equilibrium, also gives an explicit $1/M$ correction to the mean-field prediction of the stationary mean. The corrected mean has error $o(M^{-1})$, which improves to $O(M^{-3/2})$ under a stronger bound on the drift remainder. The resulting covariance and mean-refinement equations have the same structure as the finite-time heterogeneous refined mean-field equations, but our results directly provide steady-state guarantees for weighted occupancies rather than marginal state probabilities of individual agents. The results are illustrated through a heterogeneous power-of-two load-balancing model with buffer size two.
Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
Camillo De Lellis; Guido De Philippis; Alessio Figalli

We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(Ω\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(Ω\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partialΩ\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(Ω\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partialΩ\setminusΣ\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminusΣ\), where \(Σ=\{κ=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partialΩ\). Also, at each point \(p\inΣ\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\). The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(Δv=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.
The inverse Littlewood problem for multiplicative functions

We formulate and solve the asymptotic inverse Littlewood problem in the class of multiplicative functions. That is, let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{U}\cup\{0\}$ be a bounded completely multiplicative function satisfying $\sum_{p:f(p)=0}1/p<\infty$. We show that \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα\ll\log x \] for all $x\ge3$ if and only if $f(n)=χ(n)n^{it}$ for some Dirichlet character $χ$ and some $t\in\mathbb{R}$.\\ More generally, we show that there is $\varepsilon_0>0$, depending only on the $\ell^2$-density of $f$ (that is, on $\prod_{p:f(p)=0}(1-1/p)$), such that under the weaker hypothesis \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα \ll x^{\varepsilon_0} \] for all $x\ge3$, there are a Dirichlet character $χ$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \[ \sum_p\frac{\left|f(p)-χ(p)p^{it}\right|}{p}<\infty. \] We give evidence for the sharpness of such classification, by constructing non-pretentious examples with $L^1$ norm $o(\sqrt{x})$ at every sufficiently large scale, but with ``wild" behavior at the intermediate scales.
AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
Regina Carla Sousa; Denis Vargas; Elizabeth Wanner; Joshua Knowles

We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.
A Euclidean Quasi-Newton Method for Matrix-Manifold Optimization via Almost-Global Coordinates
Ziang Tian; Jiang Hu; Zhigang Yao; Bingjie Li

We study smooth matrix-manifold optimization using objective values and first derivatives. Almost-global coordinates transform the manifold-constrained problem into an unconstrained pullback problem, to which we apply BFGS with a chart-restart strategy and a limited-memory implementation. We establish correspondence of first- and second-order stationary points and minimizers, together with conditional convergence and local q-superlinear convergence. The local rate follows from Euclidean full-memory BFGS theory once the chart is fixed, without the locking condition required by classical transported-gradient Riemannian BFGS analyses. Tests on 15 benchmark problems from Manopt and Pymanopt, with ten instances per problem, show that our limited-memory method solves all 150 cases, whereas Riemannian BFGS and Riemannian steepest descent solve 132 and 117 cases, respectively. On the 115 cases successfully solved by all three methods, our method takes roughly half the time of either baseline, measured by geometric-mean solve time.
A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange

Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.

For coassociatives, we give an explicit example on a torus showing that the Laplacian flow of closed $G_2$ structures coupled to mean curvature flow can fail to preserve coassociativity, even arbitrarily close to a flat structure. We circumvent this by adding a Lie derivative to the ambient equation, using an elliptic correction of minimum $L^2$ norm along the submanifold. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled flow from coassociative initial data, without any rigidity assumption. We also prove global existence and smooth exponential convergence for coassociative initial pairs sufficiently close to a torsion-free coassociative pair, with the ambient cohomology class fixed. For instantons, we propose a similar corrected coupled system by adding a torsion term and a nonlocal elliptic correction to Yang-Mills flow along prescribed coclosed ambient $4$-forms. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled system for connections nearby an acyclic $G_2$ instanton. We obtain global existence and smooth exponential convergence for the coupled corrected connection flow and the modified coflow of coclosed $G_2$ structures with parameter zero, near a torsion-free structure with an acyclic instanton. We prove a new result on the global existence and smooth exponential convergence near a torsion-free $4$-form in a fixed cohomology class for the modified coflow with $c=0$ which is a result of independent interest. We also give continuation criteria for both the coupled systems and construct compact examples with nonzero correction. Finally, for every positive coflow parameter, we exhibit a flat torus with a growing linear mode which shows why $c=0$ is the meaningful one.
Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.
Construction of Ternary Minimal Linear Codes with Dimension $n+r$ Via Index Codes and The Access Structures of Their Dual Codes

Recently, minimal linear codes have been extensively studied due to their applications in secret sharing schemes, secure two-party computations, and so on. Constructing minimal linear codes violating the Ashikhmin-Barg condition and then determining their weight distributions have been interesting in coding theory and cryptography. In this paper, we present a general construction of ternary linear codes of dimension $n+r$, where $n$ and $r$ are positive integers, and derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the resulting codes to be minimal. We first specialize the construction using index codes arising from spreads, with three classes of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters and weight enumerators of the corresponding minimal codes, and determine the access structures type of the secret-sharing schemes based on their dual codes. By the index codes from Krawtchouk polynomials, we then give a second specialization of the construction, with a class of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters of the resulting minimal codes, and determine the access-structure type of the secret-sharing scheme based on each dual code. Several constructed families of minimal codes violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

We prove that for $n\ge2$ the normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb S^n$, and that for $d\ge3$ Lebesgue measure is the only finitely additive measure on the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ which is invariant under orientation-preserving isometries and normalized on the unit cube. This answers the Borel version of the Ruziewicz problem. On $\mathbb S^n$ it suffices to assume invariance under a finite set of rotations with a spectral gap, and on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under two such sets of rotations about two distinct centres. The main step is a criterion for invariant finitely additive probability measures to vanish on null sets. For a finite nonempty symmetric set of homeomorphisms of a $σ$-compact metrizable space with a quasi-invariant Borel measure $m$ which is finite on compact sets, such as Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$, every invariant finitely additive probability measure on Borel sets vanishes on $m$-null sets if and only if there is $δ>0$ such that every countably additive Borel probability measure supported on an $m$-null Borel set is moved by some generator by at least $δ$ in total variation. Sufficiency is proved by constructing, for every invariant null Borel set, a bounded Borel field on the orbit graph, supported on the set and with divergence at least one there.
Long lived QNM for multiple black holes

We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.
Action-Dependent Policies for Multi-Agent Linear Quadratic Regulation
Yongjie Liu; Gangshan Jing; Long Wang

The linear quadratic regulation (LQR) problem over a multi-agent system usually requires a distributed feedback gain that is structurally constrained by the network topology, incurring an inevitable suboptimality gap. Existing studies either identify conditions on the system and topology that enable convex relaxation or seek a stationary point via policy gradient algorithms. In this paper, we reduce the suboptimality gap by adopting action-dependent policies (ADPs), where the control input of each agent depends on not only states of neighbor agents, but also control inputs of some other agents. We show that although exhibiting a distributed structure, ADP can enlarge the feasible set of feedback gains and even represent centralized optimal policies under suitable conditions. However, this comes at the price of losing coercivity of the cost function and possible failure of convergence for the projected gradient flow (PGF). To overcome this difficulty, we propose a partially regularized formulation, which guarantees convergence of PGFs, and forges a connection between standard multi-agent LQR and its action-dependent counterpart. Sufficient conditions for local convergence to globally optimal policies under PGFs regardless of regularization are also established. Finally, numerical examples are presented to validate the performance of ADP.
On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums

Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $σ$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.
Turán number of the odd-ballooning of odd prisms
Wenwen Chen; Longfei Fang; Yuke Zhang

The Turán problem for odd-balloonings has been studied for various classes of skeleton graphs, including stars, paths, cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, and certain 3-chromatic graphs. The Turán numbers and extremal graphs for odd prisms have also been determined. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the Turán problem for prescribed odd-balloonings of odd prisms. Let $k\geq1$ be fixed, and let $F^o$ be a prescribed odd-ballooning of the odd prism $C_{2k+1}\square K_2$, in which each edge is replaced by a cycle of prescribed odd length at least five. For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that $${\rm ex}(n,F^o)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\Big\rfloor+(k+1)n-3(k+1)^2.$$ Furthermore, the unique extremal graph is $K_{\,2k+2,\,\lfloor(n-2k-2)/2\rfloor,\,\lceil(n-2k-2)/2\rceil}$. Optimal local gradient estimate for gravity water waves and its application to the Stokes conjecture
Lili Du; Chunlei Yang; Fan Zhang

In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point. The conjecture was first proved by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. Their proofs rely on structural assumptions, including the isolation of stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the wave profile. In 2011, Varvaruca and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] introduced a novel geometric approach and gave a new proof of the conjecture without relying on the structural assumptions mentioned above, under a local gradient bound for the two-dimensional stream function.
